# REPUBLIC OF DJIBOUTI

REPUBLIC OF DJIBOUTI

Unity-Equality-Peace

NATIONAL ASSEMBLY

8th Legislature

Law No. 003/AN/18/8th L

Enacting the Civil Code

THE NATIONAL ASSEMBLY

CONSIDERING The Constitution of September 15, 1992;

CONSIDERING Constitutional Law No. 92/AN/10/6th L of April 21, 2010 revising the Constitution;

CONSIDERING Decree No. 2016-109/PRE of May 11, 2016 appointing the Prime Minister;

CONSIDERING Decree No. 2016-110/PRE of May 12, 2016 appointing members of the government;

CONSIDERING Circular No. 79/PAN of 5/04/2018 convening the second public session of the 1st Ordinary Session of the Year 2018; HAS ADOPTED, IN ITS second PUBLIC SESSION OF 09/04/18, THE LAW

THE TENOR OF WHICH FOLLOWS:

###### ARTICLE 1:

This Civil Code is adopted.

###### ARTICLE 2:

This law shall be published in the Official Journal of the Republic of Djibouti, upon its promulgation.

Mohamed ALI HOUMED saleban daher bileh

President of the Assembly Secretary of the Bureau of the Assembly the National Assembly

Article final

Dispositions transitoires générales

Code civil de la République de Djibouti

Titre préliminaire : De la publication, des effets et de l'application des lois en général

###### Article 1

Laws are enforceable in the territory of Djibouti by virtue of their promulgation by the President of the Republic, and come into force on the day they specify or, failing that, on the day following their publication in the Official Journal of the Republic of Djibouti.

Publication within the meaning of this text means the first publication in date carried out by the National Printing Office or by electronic means.

###### Article 2

The law only provides for the future; it has no retroactive effect.

###### Article 3

Public order and security laws bind all those who inhabit the territory.

Immovables, even those owned by foreigners, are governed by Djiboutian law.

Laws concerning the status and capacity of persons govern Djiboutians, even when residing in a foreign country.

###### Article 4

A judge who refuses to adjudicate, on the pretext of the silence, obscurity or inadequacy of the law, may be prosecuted as guilty of denial of justice.

###### Article 5

Judges are prohibited from ruling by way of general and regulatory provision on the cases submitted to them.

###### Article 6

One cannot derogate, by private agreements, from laws that concern public order and good morals.

## BOOK I: OF PERSONS

Title I: Of civil rights and the individual Chapter I: Of the enjoyment of civil rights

###### Article 7

The exercise of civil rights is independent of the exercise of political rights, which are acquired and retained in accordance with constitutional and electoral laws.

###### Article 8

Every person has legal personality.

###### Article 9

Everyone has the right to respect for their private life.

Judges may, without prejudice to compensation for damage suffered, prescribe all measures, such as sequestration, seizure and others, capable of preventing or stopping an infringement of the privacy of private life; these measures may, if there is urgency, be ordered in summary proceedings.

###### Article 10

Everyone has the right to respect for the presumption of innocence.

When a person is, before any conviction, publicly presented as being guilty of facts that are the subject of an investigation or judicial inquiry, the judge may, even in summary proceedings, without prejudice to compensation for damage suffered, prescribe all measures, such as the insertion of a correction or the dissemination of a statement, for the purpose of stopping the infringement of the presumption of innocence, and this at the expense of the person, natural or legal, responsible for this infringement.

###### Article 11

Every Djiboutian shall enjoy civil rights.

A foreigner shall enjoy in Djibouti the same civil rights as those granted by treaty to Djiboutians by the State of which the foreigner is a national.

The provisions of the Family Code form the ordinary law regime of the family (marriage, divorce, filiation, successions and liberalities) and fall under the Personal Status Court; the provisions of the Civil Code relating to family law fall within the jurisdiction of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance.

###### Article 12

A foreigner, even if not resident in Djibouti, may be summoned before the Djiboutian courts for the performance of obligations contracted by him in Djibouti with a Djiboutian; he may be brought before the courts of Djibouti for obligations contracted by him in a foreign country towards Djiboutians.

###### Article 13

A Djiboutian may be brought before the Djiboutian courts for obligations contracted by him in a foreign country, even with a foreigner.

##### Chapitre II : Du respect du corps humain

###### Article 14

The law ensures the primacy of the person, prohibits any violation of his dignity and guarantees respect for the human being from the beginning of his life.

###### Article 15

Everyone has the right to respect for their body.

###### Article 16

The human body is inviolable.

The human body, its elements and its products cannot be the subject of a property right.

###### Article 17

The respect due to the human body does not cease with death.

The remains of deceased persons, including the ashes of those whose body has been cremated, must be treated with respect, dignity and decency.

###### Article 18

The judge may prescribe all measures capable of preventing or stopping an unlawful infringement of the human body or unlawful acts concerning elements or products thereof, including after death.

###### Article 19

The integrity of the human body may only be interfered with in the event of medical necessity for the person or, exceptionally, in the therapeutic interest of another.

The consent of the person concerned must be obtained beforehand except in the case where their condition makes necessary a therapeutic intervention to which they are not in a position to consent.

###### Article 20

No one may interfere with the integrity of the human species.

Any eugenic practice tending to organize the selection of persons is prohibited. Any intervention aimed at giving birth to a child genetically identical to another living or deceased person is prohibited.

Without prejudice to research aimed at the prevention and treatment of genetic diseases, no transformation may be made to genetic characteristics for the purpose of modifying the person's descendants.

###### Article 21

Agreements having the effect of conferring a pecuniary value on the human body, its elements or its products are null and void.

###### Article 22

No remuneration may be allocated to a person who submits to experimentation on their person, to the removal of elements of their body or to the collection of products thereof.

###### Article 23

Any agreement relating to procreation or gestation on behalf of another is null and void.

###### Article 24

No information allowing the identification of both the person who donated an element or product of their body and the person who received it may be disclosed. The donor cannot know the identity of the recipient nor the recipient that of the donor.

In case of therapeutic necessity, only the doctors of the donor and the recipient may have access to information allowing their identification.

###### Article 25

The provisions of this chapter are of public order.

#### Title II: Nationality

Chapter I: General Provisions

###### Article 26

Djiboutian nationality is acquired according to the provisions set forth in this title subject to the application of treaties and other international commitments of the Republic of Djibouti.

###### Article 27

Djiboutian nationality by descent is that which an individual possesses, from birth, by virtue of the origin of their parents of Djiboutian nationality.

Djiboutian nationality by acquisition is that which an individual obtains after their birth, either by operation of law or by decision of the public authority.

###### Article 28

The acquisition of Djiboutian nationality is governed by the laws in force at the time of the act or fact to which the law attaches its effects.

##### Chapter II: Djiboutian nationality by descent

###### Article 29

A person whose father and mother are Djiboutian is Djiboutian.

###### Article 30

A person born in the Republic of Djibouti or abroad whose father or mother is Djiboutian is also Djiboutian.

###### Article 31

An individual born in the Republic of Djibouti whose parents are unknown is also Djiboutian.

They shall be deemed never to have been Djiboutian if, before reaching the age of majority, their descent is established with respect to a foreigner.

###### Article 32

An individual who is Djiboutian by virtue of the provisions of articles 29 to 31 is deemed to have been Djiboutian from birth, even if the existence of the conditions required by law for the attribution of Djiboutian nationality is established only subsequently. However, the establishment of Djiboutian status subsequent to birth does not affect the validity of acts previously acquired by third parties on the basis of the person's apparent nationality.

##### Chapter III: Djiboutian nationality by acquisition

###### Article 33

Djiboutian nationality may be acquired by decision of the public authority. It results from naturalization granted by decree and upon application by the person concerned.

###### Article 34

Marriage does not, automatically, have any effect on the nationality of the foreign spouse.

###### Article 35

The acquisition of a foreign nationality does not result in the loss of Djiboutian status, unless the individual renounces their Djiboutian nationality of their own free will.

###### Article 36

In case of naturalization, minor children born of the marriage are, by right, Djiboutian.

###### Article 37

The adoption of a child does not, automatically, have any effect on the nationality of the adopted child, except in the case of full adoption in which case the child is, by right, Djiboutian.

###### Article 38

A commission is established to give a prior opinion on all naturalization applications.

This commission, whose headquarters are at the Palace of Justice, comprises:

- a magistrate, president;
- a representative of the Ministry of the Interior, member;
- a representative of the Ministry of Health, member;
- the Director of Population, member;
- the prefect of the place of residence of the person applying for naturalization, member.

The commission is appointed by the President of the Republic. It meets upon convocation by its president.

###### Article 39

Subject to the exceptions provided for in articles 36 and 40, naturalization may only be granted to a foreigner demonstrating habitual residence in the Republic of Djibouti during the ten years preceding the filing of their application.

###### Article 40

The period provided for in article 39 is reduced to five years for individuals who have rendered or who can render, through their capacity and talent, important services to the Republic of Djibouti.

###### Article 41

No one may apply for naturalization if they have not reached the age of eighteen years.

###### Article 42

No one may be naturalized if they are not of good character and conduct or if they have been subject to a conviction referred to in article 45 of this code. Convictions pronounced abroad may be taken into consideration.

A medical certificate must attest that they are in good health.

###### Article 43

No one may be naturalized if they do not demonstrate their assimilation into the Djiboutian community, in particular, through sufficient knowledge of one of the languages used in the Republic of Djibouti.

###### Article 44

No one may acquire Djiboutian nationality if they are subject to an expulsion order or residence assignment not rescinded in the forms in which it was issued at the time of the fact or act likely to determine acquisition.

The same applies to an individual who has been subject to a decree opposing the acquisition of Djiboutian nationality.

###### Article 45

No one may acquire Djiboutian nationality if they have been subject either to a conviction for an act classified as a crime or offense against State security, or to a conviction not erased by rehabilitation for a fact classified as a crime, or to a conviction not erased by rehabilitation to a sentence of more than six months' imprisonment for one of the offenses provided for in articles 131 to 150 of the penal code and the offenses of theft, fraud, breach of trust, receiving, extortion and blackmail, forgery and use of forged documents, provided for in articles 485 to 498, 509 to 510, 520 to 521, 533 to 540, 499 to 508 of the same code.

###### Article 46

An individual who has acquired nationality enjoys, from the date of this acquisition, all the rights attached to the status of Djiboutian.

##### Chapter IV: Acts relating to the acquisition by naturalization of Djiboutian nationality

###### Article 47

Any application to obtain naturalization is filed and addressed to the Ministry of the Interior (Director of Population). A receipt for the filing of the application is provided. Any application must be registered. Mention of this registration is entered on this file.

###### Article 48

The applicant produces the civil status records, documents and titles requested of him, such as to: 1° Establish that his application is admissible in the terms of the law;

2° Allow the commission charged with giving a preliminary opinion on naturalization to assess whether the favor requested is justified, from the national point of view, particularly in light of the filiation, profession of the interested party and the duration of his stay in the Republic of Djibouti;

3° Establish that he has not been subject to any conviction in the Republic of Djibouti or in his country of origin; 4° Establish that the applicant is in good health by producing a medical certificate.

###### Article 49

In the event that the interested party is unable to produce the civil status records necessary for the admissibility of the naturalization application, these records may be substituted by certificates of notoriety issued by the judge designated in accordance with Article 62.

###### Article 50

Every naturalization application must be the subject of a police investigation. This investigation concerns the morality, conduct and loyalty of the applicant and the interest that the granting of naturalization would present from the national point of view.

###### Article 51

Within six months of the filing of the naturalization application, the Minister of the Interior must transmit to the president of the naturalization commission the complete file of the application as well as the results of the investigation and his reasoned opinion.

###### Article 52

The naturalization commission must be seized within two months following the receipt of the file by the president of the commission.

###### Article 53

Decrees granting naturalization to Djiboutian nationality are published in the Official Journal.

###### Article 54

If the application does not give rise to naturalization or if the application is deemed inadmissible by the president of the commission after its opinion, the Minister of the Interior notifies the rejection of the application. The notification pronouncing the rejection of the application need not be reasoned.

##### Chapitre V: Disputes concerning nationality

###### Article 55

The Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance has sole jurisdiction to hear disputes concerning nationality.

Questions of nationality are preliminary before any other administrative or judicial jurisdiction.

###### Article 56

Every person has the right to bring legal action to have it decided that he has or does not have Djiboutian status.

The Public Prosecutor and the Attorney General have the same right with respect to any person. The public prosecutor's office is a necessary defendant in any declaratory action concerning nationality. It must be made a party whenever a question of nationality is raised incidentally before a court empowered to hear it.

###### Article 57

The Public Prosecutor and the Attorney General are required to act if they are requested to do so by a public administration or by a third party who has raised the exception of nationality before a jurisdiction that has stayed its decision in application of Article 62. The third party applicant must be made a party.

###### Article 58

Judgments and rulings rendered in matters of Djiboutian nationality have effect even with respect to those who were neither parties nor represented therein.

However, any interested party is entitled to challenge them by third-party opposition on condition that the Public Prosecutor or the Attorney General be made a party, depending on the level of the jurisdiction to be seized.

##### Chapitre VI: Proof of nationality before judicial courts

###### Article 59

The burden of proof, in matters of Djiboutian nationality, falls on the person whose nationality is at issue.

However, this burden falls on the person who contests the status of Djiboutian of a third party who holds a certificate of nationality issued in accordance with Articles 62, 63 and 64 below.

###### Article 60

When Djiboutian nationality is attributed or acquired other than by naturalization, proof can only be made by establishing the existence of all the conditions required by law.

###### Article 61

Proof of the foreign status of an individual may be established by demonstrating that the interested party does not fulfill any of the conditions required by law to have Djiboutian status.

##### Chapitre VII: Certificates of nationality

###### Article 62

The president of the Court of First Instance of Djibouti, or a judge specially designated for this purpose by him, alone has authority to issue a certificate of Djiboutian nationality to any person proving that he has this nationality.

Before ruling on any application for a certificate of nationality, the file must be the subject of a police investigation and be sent to the Population Directorate for an opinion.

###### Article 63

The certificate of nationality indicates, referring to the articles of this code, the legal provisions under which the interested party is Djiboutian as well as the documents that made it possible to establish it. It constitutes evidence until proven otherwise.

###### Article 64

When the judge rejects the request and refuses to issue a certificate of nationality, the interested party may seize the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of Appeal who decides, after having conducted a new police investigation, whether or not to proceed with this issuance. The decision of refusal by the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of Appeal is subject to appeal before the Supreme Court.

#### Titre III: Civil status records

Chapitre Ier: General provisions

###### Article 65

Civil status records state the year, day and hour when they are received, the first names, surnames, professions and domiciles of all those named therein.

The dates and places of birth of the following persons are indicated in the civil status records, when they are known:

1° Of the father and mother in birth and acknowledgment records;

2° Of the child in acknowledgment records;

3° Of the spouses in marriage records;

4° Of the deceased in death records.

When the date of birth of the interested party is not known, the age of said persons shall be designated by their number of years, as shall be, in all cases, the age of the declarants. With respect to witnesses, only their status as adults shall be indicated.

###### Article 66

Civil status officers may not insert anything in the records they receive, either by note or by any statement whatsoever, other than what must be declared by the appearing parties.

###### Article 67

In cases where the interested parties are not required to appear in person, they may be represented by an agent equipped with a special and authentic power of attorney.

###### Article 68

Witnesses produced for civil status records must be at least eighteen years of age, relatives or others, without distinction of sex; they are chosen by the interested persons.

###### Article 69

The civil status officer reads the records aloud to the appearing parties, or to their agent equipped with a power of attorney, and to the witnesses; he invites them to take direct knowledge of them before signing them.

Mention is made on the records of the completion of these formalities.

###### Article 70

These records are signed by the civil status officer, by the appearing parties and the witnesses; or mention shall be made of the reason preventing the appearing parties and the witnesses from signing.

###### Article 71

Civil status records are entered, in each commune, in one or more registers kept in duplicate.

###### Article 72

The registers are numbered and initialed on each sheet by the president of the court of first instance or by the judge he shall appoint for this purpose.

###### Article 73

Acts are recorded in the registers immediately, without any gaps. Erasures and cross-references are approved and signed in the same manner as the body of the act. Nothing may be written by abbreviation, and no date shall be written in figures.

###### Article 74

The registers are closed and finalized by the civil status officer at the end of each year; and, within the month, one of the duplicates shall be deposited in the municipal archives, the other at the registry of the Court of First Instance.

###### Article 75

Powers of attorney and other documents that must remain annexed to civil status acts are deposited, after they have been initialed by the person who produced them and by the civil status officer, at the court registry, with the duplicate of the registers.

###### Article 76

Any person may obtain from the custodians of civil status registers extracts from these registers. Extracts issued in conformity with the registers and certified by the president of the Court of First Instance, or by the judge replacing him, are authentic until proven false.

###### Article 77

When registers have not existed, or when they are lost, proof may be received both by documents and by witnesses; and, in these cases, marriages, births and deaths may be proven both by registers and papers emanating from deceased fathers and mothers, and by witnesses.

###### Article 78

Any civil status act of Djiboutians and foreigners, made in a foreign country, is authentic if it is drawn up in the forms customary in said country.

###### Article 79

Any civil status act of Djiboutians in a foreign country is valid if it has been received, in accordance with Djiboutian laws, by diplomatic agents or by consuls.

A duplicate of the civil status registers kept by these agents is sent at the end of each year to the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, which ensures their custody and may issue extracts therefrom.

###### Article 80

In all cases where the notation of an act relating to civil status must be made in the margin of an act already recorded, it is made ex officio.

The civil status officer who has drawn up or transcribed the act giving rise to notation makes this notation, within three days, on the registers he holds, and, if the duplicate of the register where the notation must be made is at the registry, he sends a notice to the public prosecutor.

If the act in the margin of which this notation must be made has been drawn up or transcribed in another municipality, the notice is sent, within three days, to the civil status officer of that municipality and the latter immediately notifies, if the duplicate of the register is at the registry, the public prosecutor. If the act in the margin of which a notation must be made has been drawn up or transcribed abroad, the civil status officer who has drawn up or transcribed the act giving rise to notation notifies, within three days, the Minister of Foreign Affairs.

###### Article 81

Any violation of the preceding articles by the officials named therein shall be prosecuted before the Court of First Instance and punished by a fine of 20,000 Djibouti francs (FD) to 200,000 FD.

###### Article 82

Every custodian of registers is civilly liable for alterations that may occur therein, except for his recourse, if applicable, against the perpetrators of said alterations.

###### Article 83

Any alteration, any forgery in civil status acts, any recording of these acts made on a loose sheet and otherwise than on the registers intended for this purpose, gives rise to the awarding of damages in favor of the parties who are victims thereof, without prejudice to the penalties provided in the penal code.

###### Article 84

The public prosecutor is required to verify the state of the registers when they are deposited at the registry; he draws up a summary report of the verification, reports violations or offenses committed by civil status officers, and seeks against them conviction to fines.

###### Article 85

In all cases where the Court of First Instance hears matters relating to civil status acts, the interested parties may appeal against the judgment.

##### Chapitre II: Birth acts

###### Article 86

Birth declarations are made within three days of delivery, to the civil status officer of the place.

When a birth has not been declared within the legal time limit, the civil status officer may only record it on his registers by virtue of a judgment rendered by the court of the place in which the child was born, and a summary notation is made in the margin at the date of birth. If the place of birth is unknown, the competent court is that of the applicant's domicile.

In a foreign country, declarations to diplomatic agents or consuls are made within ten days of delivery. However, this time limit may be extended in certain consular districts by virtue of a decree of the President of the Republic which sets the extent and conditions of this extension.

###### Article 87

The birth of the child is declared by the father, or in the absence of the father, by doctors of medicine or surgery, midwives, health officers or other persons who attended the delivery; and when the mother has given birth outside her domicile, by the person at whose place she gave birth. The birth act is drawn up immediately.

###### Article 88

The birth act states the day, hour and place of birth, the sex of the child and the given names assigned to him, the given names, surnames, ages, professions and domiciles of the father and mother and, if applicable, those of the declarant. If the father and mother of the natural child, or one of them, are not designated to the civil status officer, no mention is made on the registers in this regard.

If the act drawn up concerns a natural child, the civil status officer gives, within the month, notice to the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance or to the judge delegated for this purpose. The judgment is rendered and published under the conditions provided for in Articles 129 and 131 of this code.

###### Article 89

Any person who finds a newborn child is required to report it to the civil registrar of the place where the child was found. If they do not consent to take charge of the child, they must hand it over, along with the clothing and other items found with it, to an approved center for the reception of abandoned children. If, on the other hand, they consent to take charge of the child, they must report it to the Public Prosecutor and initiate proceedings for placement or adoption.

A detailed report is drawn up which, in addition to the information provided for in Article 65 of this Code, states the date, time, place and circumstances of the discovery, the apparent age and sex of the child, any particularity that may contribute to his identification, as well as the authority or person to whom he is entrusted. This report is recorded on its date in the civil status registers.

Following and separately from this report, the civil registrar draws up a document serving as a birth certificate. In addition to the information provided for in Article 65, this document states the sex of the child as well as the given names and surname assigned to him; it sets a date of birth that may correspond to his apparent age and designates as place of birth the municipality where the child was discovered.

Such a document must be drawn up, upon declaration by the child welfare services, for children placed under their guardianship and lacking a known birth certificate or for whom secrecy of birth has been requested.

Copies and extracts of the discovery report or provisional birth certificate are issued under the conditions and according to the distinctions made in Article 88 of this Code.

If the child's birth certificate is found or if his birth is judicially declared, the discovery report and the provisional birth certificate are cancelled at the request of the Public Prosecutor or the interested parties.

###### Article 90

The deed of acknowledgment of a natural child is recorded in the registers on its date; it is noted in the margin of the birth certificate, if one exists, and notice thereof is given, within one month, to the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance.

###### Article 91

Every person is identified by his given name followed by his traditional or patronymic family name. The choice is made at the time of drawing up the birth certificate of the first child, subsequent children being identified in the same manner. In the absence of an expressed choice, the traditional family name system is retained.

The traditional family name is composed of the father's given name to which is added the paternal grandfather's given name.

The patronymic family name is the family name of the child's father, transmitted by filiation from generation to generation.

###### Article 92

Any person who demonstrates a legitimate interest may request to change his given name. The addition or deletion of a given name may likewise be requested.

When the request concerns a minor, the application is submitted by his legal representative. If the child is over thirteen years of age, his personal consent is required.

The request is brought before the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance at the application of the interested party or, in the case of a minor or an adult under guardianship, at the application of his legal representative. The request is communicated for opinion to the Public Prosecutor.

The decision to change a given name is recorded in the civil status register.

###### Article 93

Any person who demonstrates a legitimate interest may request to change his patronymic name. The request to change a patronymic name may have the purpose of avoiding the extinction of a name borne by an ancestor or collateral relative of the applicant up to the fourth degree.

The request to change a name may also have the purpose of abandoning the traditional family name in favor of a patronymic name, which will be transmitted by filiation from generation to generation.

The change of name is authorized by decree.

###### Article 94

Any interested party may file an objection before the Administrative Court to the decree changing a name, within two months from its publication in the Official Journal.

A decree changing a name takes effect, if there has been no objection, upon expiration of the period during which an objection is admissible or, otherwise, after rejection of the objection.

###### Article 95

The change of name extends by operation of law to the children of the beneficiary when they are less than thirteen years of age.

###### Article 96

Any change of name of a child over thirteen years of age requires his personal consent when this change does not result from the establishment or modification of a filiation link. However, the establishment or modification of a filiation link only entails the change of family name of adult children subject to their express consent.

###### Article 97

Any person who proves that a name is recorded in the civil status register of another State may request from the civil registrar holding his birth certificate established in Djibouti to change his name in order to bear the name acquired in that other State. When the person is a minor, the declaration is made jointly by both parents exercising parental authority or by the parent exercising parental authority alone, with his personal consent if he is over thirteen years of age.

The change of name is authorized by the civil registrar, who records it in the current birth register.

In case of difficulties, the civil registrar refers the matter to the Public Prosecutor, who may oppose the request. In this case, the interested party is notified.

Seized under the same conditions, the Public Prosecutor of the place of birth may himself order the change of name.

The change of name acquired under the conditions set out in the first four paragraphs extends by operation of law to the children of the beneficiary when they are less than thirteen years of age.

###### Article 98

Mention of decisions to change given names and surname is made in the margin of the civil status documents of the interested party and, where applicable, those of his spouse and children.

Similarly, decisions to change given names and surname lawfully obtained abroad are noted in the margin of Djibouti civil status documents, upon instructions from the Public Prosecutor. The provisions of Articles 130 and 131 are applicable to changes of given names and surname.

##### Chapitre III. Des actes de mariage

###### Article 99

Before the celebration of the marriage, the civil registrar makes a publication by way of a notice posted on the door of the town hall. This publication states the given names, surnames, professions, domiciles and residences of the future spouses, as well as the place where the marriage is to be celebrated.

The civil registrar may not proceed with the publication provided for in the above paragraph nor, in case of dispensation from publication, with the celebration of the marriage, until after each of the future spouses has submitted a medical certificate dated less than two months prior, certifying, to the exclusion of any other indication, that the interested party has been examined for the purpose of marriage.

The civil registrar who does not comply with the requirements of the preceding paragraph shall be prosecuted before the correctional chamber of the Court of First Instance and punished by a fine of 20,000 FD to 200,000 FD.

The civil registrar receives the declaration of the future spouses if they intend that their union be governed by the family code or by the provisions of this Code.

###### Article 100

The notice provided for in article 99 shall remain posted on the door of the town hall for ten days.

The marriage cannot be celebrated before the tenth day from and not including that of the publication. If the posting is interrupted before the expiration of this period, mention shall be made on the notice that has ceased to be posted on the door of the town hall.

###### Article 101

If the marriage has not been celebrated within the year, from the expiration of the publication period, it may only be celebrated after a new publication made in the form above.

###### Article 102

The acts of objection to the marriage are signed on the original and on the copy by the objectors or by their representatives equipped with a special and authentic power of attorney; they are served, with the copy of the power of attorney, on the person or at the domicile of the parties, and on the civil registrar, who places his visa on the original.

###### Article 103

The civil registrar makes, without delay, a summary mention of the objections in the marriage register; he also makes mention, in the margin of the registration of said objections, of the judgments or acts of withdrawal of which a copy has been delivered to him.

###### Article 104

In case of objection, the civil registrar cannot celebrate the marriage before the withdrawal has been delivered to him, under penalty of 100,000 FD fine, and damages.

###### Article 105

The copy of the birth certificate submitted by each of the future spouses to the civil registrar who is to celebrate their marriage is in accordance with the provisions of article 88 of this code, with, if applicable, the indication of the marital status of his father and mother or, if the future spouse is a minor, the indication of the acknowledgement of which he has been the subject.

This act must not have been issued more than three months previously.

###### Article 106

The future spouse who is unable to obtain this act may substitute it by producing a certificate of notoriety issued by the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance of the place of his birth or of his domicile.

The certificate of notoriety contains the declaration made by three witnesses of either sex, related or unrelated, of the first names, name, profession and domicile of the future spouse, and of those of his father and mother, if they are known; the place, and, as far as possible, the time of his birth, and the reasons preventing the production of the act. The witnesses sign the certificate of notoriety with the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance; and if any cannot or do not know how to sign, mention is made thereof.

###### Article 107

Neither the certificate of notoriety nor the refusal to issue it is subject to appeal.

###### Article 108

The authentic act of consent of the father and mother or grandfathers and grandmothers, or, in their absence, that of the family council, contains the first names, names, professions and domicile of the future spouses and of all those who participated in the act, as well as their degree of kinship.

Except in the case provided for by article 170 of the Civil Code, this act of consent is drawn up either by a notary, or by the civil registrar of the domicile or residence of the ascendant and, abroad, by Djiboutian diplomatic or consular agents. When it is drawn up by a civil registrar, it need only be legalized, except where international conventions provide otherwise, when it is to be produced before foreign authorities.

###### Article 109

The marriage is celebrated in the commune where one of the two spouses has his domicile or residence established by at least one month of continuous habitation at the date of the publication provided for by law.

###### Article 110

On the day designated by the parties, after the publication period, the civil registrar, at the town hall, in the presence of at least two witnesses or at most four, related or not to the parties, reads to the future spouses articles 220 (paragraph 1), 221, 222 (paragraph 1) and 223 (paragraph 1) of this code. However, in case of serious impediment, the public prosecutor of the place of the marriage may require the civil registrar to go to the domicile or residence of one of the parties to celebrate the marriage. In case of imminent danger of death of one of the future spouses, the civil registrar may go there before any requisition or authorization from the public prosecutor, to whom he must then, as soon as possible, inform of the necessity of this celebration outside the town hall.

Mention shall be made thereof in the marriage certificate.

The civil registrar calls upon the future spouses, and, if they are minors, their ascendants present at the celebration and authorizing the marriage, to declare whether a marriage contract has been made and, if so, the date of this contract, as well as the name and place of residence of the notary who received it. If the documents produced by one of the future spouses do not agree with each other as to the first names or as to the spelling of the names, he calls upon the person concerned, and, if he is a minor, his closest ascendants present at the celebration, to declare that the lack of concordance results from an omission or an error.

He receives from each party, one after the other, the declaration that they wish to take each other as husband and wife; he pronounces, in the name of the law, that they are united by marriage and he draws up an act on the spot.

###### Article 111

The marriage certificate states:

1° The first names, names, professions, ages, dates and places of birth, domiciles and residences of the spouses; 2° The first names, names, professions and domiciles of the fathers and mothers;

3° The consent of the fathers and mothers, grandfathers or grandmothers and that of the family council, in cases where they are required;

4° The first names and name of the previous spouse of each of the spouses;

5° The declaration of the contracting parties to take each other as spouses, and the pronouncement of their union by the civil registrar;

6° The first names, names, professions, domiciles of the witnesses and their status as adults;

7° The declaration made that a marriage contract has or has not been made and, as far as possible, the date of the contract, if it exists, as well as the name and place of residence of the notary who received it; 8° The option provided for in article 99 of this code.

In the margin of the birth certificate of each spouse, mention shall be made of the celebration of the marriage and of the name of the spouse.

##### Chapter IV. Death certificates

###### Article 112

No burial may be made without an authorization on plain paper and free of charge from the civil registrar, or from a doctor, who may only issue it after having gone to the deceased person, to verify the death.

If the circumstances reveal doubt as to the identity of the person or the causes of death, the doctor shall proceed as provided for in article 116 of this code.

###### Article 113

The death certificate is drawn up by the civil registrar of the commune where the death occurred, on the declaration of a relative of the deceased or of a person possessing the most accurate and complete information possible on his civil status.

###### Article 114

The death certificate states:

1° The day, time and place of death;

2° The first names, name, date and place of birth, profession and domicile of the deceased person; 3° The first names, names, professions and domiciles of his father and mother;

4° The first names and name of the other spouse, if the deceased person was married, widowed or divorced; 5° The first names, name, age, profession and domicile of the declarant and, if applicable, his degree of kinship with the deceased person.

All of the above, as far as can be known.

Mention is made of the death in the margin of the birth certificate of the deceased person.

###### Article 115

When a death has occurred elsewhere than in the commune where the deceased was domiciled, the civil registrar who drew up the death certificate sends, as soon as possible, to the civil registrar of the deceased's last domicile a certified copy of this certificate, which is immediately transcribed in the registers. In case of death in hospitals or other public establishments, the directors of these hospitals or establishments must give notice, within ten hours, to the civil registrar or to the person performing their functions.

The latter goes there to ascertain the death and draws up the certificate, in accordance with the preceding article, based on the declarations made to them and the information they have obtained.

A register is kept in said hospitals and establishments on which these declarations and information are recorded.

###### Article 116

When there are signs or indications of violent death, or other circumstances that give reason to suspect it, burial may not take place until a police officer, assisted by a doctor of medicine, has drawn up a report on the condition of the body and the circumstances relating thereto, as well as the information they have been able to collect on the first names, surname, age, profession, place of birth and domicile of the deceased person.

###### Article 117

The police officer is required to immediately transmit to the civil registrar of the place where the person died, all the information stated in their report, based on which the death certificate is drafted.

The civil registrar sends a certified copy to that of the domicile of the deceased person, if it is known: this certified copy is recorded in the registers.

###### Article 118

In case of death in a prison or a detention facility, notice is given immediately, by the head of the establishment, to the civil registrar, who goes there as stated in Article 115, and drafts the death certificate.

###### Article 119

When the body of a deceased person is found and this person can be identified, a death certificate must be drawn up by the civil registrar of the presumed place of death, regardless of the time elapsed between the death and the discovery of the body.

If the deceased cannot be identified, the death certificate must include their most complete description; in case of subsequent identification, the certificate is rectified under the conditions provided for in Article 129 of this code.

###### Article 120

May be judicially declared, at the request of the public prosecutor or interested parties, the death of any Djiboutian who disappeared in Djibouti or outside the country, in circumstances likely to endanger their life, when their body could not be found.

May, under the same conditions, be judicially declared the death of any foreigner who disappeared either in a territory under the authority of Djibouti, or abroad if they had their domicile or habitual residence in Djibouti.

The procedure for judicial declaration of death is also applicable when the death is certain but the body could not be found.

###### Article 121

The application is submitted to the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance. If several persons disappeared during the same event, a collective application may be submitted to them.

###### Article 122

When it does not emanate from the public prosecutor, the application is transmitted through them to the court. The case is investigated and judged in chambers. Legal representation is not mandatory and all acts of the procedure, as well as certified copies and extracts of said acts, are exempt from stamp duty and registered free of charge.

If the court considers that the death is not sufficiently established, it may order any additional investigative measure and request in particular an administrative inquiry into the circumstances of the disappearance.

If the death is declared, its date must be fixed taking into account the presumptions drawn from the circumstances of the case and, failing that, on the day of the disappearance. This date must never be indeterminate.

###### Article 123

The operative part of the declaratory judgment of death is transcribed in the civil status registers of the real or presumed place of death and, where applicable, in those of the place of the deceased's last domicile.

Mention of the transcription is made in the margin of the registers at the date of death. In case of collective judgment, individual extracts of the operative part are transmitted to the civil registrars of the last domicile of each of the disappeared persons, with a view to transcription.

Declaratory judgments of death serve as death certificates and are enforceable against third parties, who may only obtain their rectification, in accordance with Article 129 of this code.

###### Article 124

If the person whose death was judicially declared reappears after the declaratory judgment, the public prosecutor or any interested party may pursue, in the forms provided for in Articles 121 et seq., the annulment of the judgment.

They will recover their property in the state in which it will be found, as well as the price of those that have been alienated and the property acquired through the use of capital or revenues accrued for their benefit.

The matrimonial regime to which the declaratory judgment had put an end will resume its course. If there had been a liquidation of the spouses' rights that became final, the restoration of the matrimonial regime will not affect the rights acquired, on the basis of the apparent situation, by persons other than the spouse, heirs, legatees or holders of any rights whose acquisition was subject to the death of the missing person.

Mention of the annulment of the declaratory judgment will be made in the margin of its transcription.

##### Chapitre V : Civil status records concerning military personnel and sailors in certain special cases

###### Article 125

Civil status records concerning military personnel and sailors of the State are established as stated in the preceding chapters.

However, outside the territory of the Republic of Djibouti and in case of war, order maintenance and pacification operations or stationing of Djiboutian troops in foreign territory, these records may also be received by military civil registrars designated by order of the Minister of Defense.

In the territory of the Republic of Djibouti, the civil registrars referred to above may receive records concerning military personnel and non-military personnel, in parts of the territory where, as a result of mobilization or siege, the municipal civil status service is no longer regularly provided.

Birth declarations in the armed forces are made within ten days following the delivery. Death certificates may be drawn up in the armed forces by derogation from Article 112 above, even though the civil registrar could not go to the deceased person, and, by derogation from Article 113, they may only be drawn up there on the attestation of two declarants.

###### Article 126

Marriage publications of military personnel and employees attached to the armed forces are made at the place of their last domicile: they are furthermore posted, twenty-five days before the celebration of the marriage, in the order of the day of the army or army corps, for officers without troops, and for employees who are part of it.

###### Article 127

In the cases provided for in paragraphs 2 and 3 of Article 125, civil status documents are drawn up in a special register, the maintenance and conservation of which are regulated by order of the Minister of Defense. When a marriage is celebrated in one of the cases provided for in paragraphs 2 and 3 of Article 125, the publications are made, to the extent that circumstances permit, at the place of the last domicile of the future spouse; they are furthermore ensured, in the unit to which the person concerned belongs, under the conditions set by order of the Minister of Defense.

###### Article 128

Death certificates received by military authority, in all cases provided for in Article 125 above, or by civil authority for members of the armed forces, civilians participating in their action, on commanded service, or persons employed following the armies, may be subject to administrative rectification under conditions set by decree, in the periods and on the territories where the military authority is authorized, by said Article 125, to eventually receive these documents.

##### Chapitre VI. De la rectification des actes de l'état civil

###### Article 129

The rectification of civil status documents is ordered by the President of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance.

The rectification of documents drawn up or transcribed by diplomatic agents and consuls is ordered by the President of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance of Djibouti. This magistrate may also hear applications for rectification of documents of which one of the copies is deposited in the archives of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.

The rectification of declaratory or supplementary judgments of civil status documents is ordered by the court that rendered the judgment.

The president or court having territorial jurisdiction to order the rectification of a document or judgment also has jurisdiction to prescribe the rectification of all documents, even drawn up or transcribed outside its jurisdiction, which reproduce the error or contain the original omission.

The application for rectification may be submitted by any interested person or by the public prosecutor; the latter is required to act ex officio when the error or omission relates to an essential indication of the document or the decision that takes its place. When the application does not emanate from the public prosecutor, it must be communicated to him for opinion.

The public prosecutor may proceed with the administrative rectification of purely material errors and omissions in civil status documents; for this purpose, he gives useful instructions directly to the custodians of the registers.

###### Article 130

Any judicial or administrative rectification of a document or judgment relating to civil status is opposable to all.

###### Article 131

The operative part of the order, judgment or ruling providing for rectification is immediately transmitted by the public prosecutor to the civil status officer or to the custodian of the registers of the place where the reformed document is recorded; mention of this operative part is immediately made in the margin of said document. A copy of the document may no longer be issued except with the ordered rectifications, upon penalty of a fine of 20,000 FD to 200,000 FD pronounced by the Court of First Instance and of all damages against the custodian of the registers.

#### Titre IV : Du domicile

###### Article 132

The domicile of every Djiboutian, with regard to the exercise of his civil rights, is in the place where he has his principal establishment.

The place of exercise of civil rights of a person without stable domicile is that where he has made election of domicile. This election of domicile must be either with a communal center, or with an organization approved for this purpose, or with a notary or lawyer.

###### Article 133

The change of domicile shall take effect by the fact of actual habitation in another place, combined with the intention to fix one's principal establishment there.

###### Article 134

Proof of the intention shall result from an express declaration, made both to the town hall of the place that one will leave and to that of the place where one will have transferred one's domicile.

In the absence of an express declaration, proof of the intention shall depend on the circumstances.

###### Article 135

The husband and wife may have a separate domicile without thereby affecting the rules relating to community of life.

Any notification made to a spouse, even separated from bed and board, in matters of status and capacity of persons, must also be addressed to his or her spouse, under penalty of nullity.

###### Article 136

The separate residence of spouses, during divorce or separation from bed and board proceedings, automatically results in separate domicile.

###### Article 137

The unemancipated minor is domiciled with his father and mother.

If the father and mother have separate domiciles, he is domiciled with the parent with whom he resides.

###### Article 138

The adult under guardianship is domiciled with his guardian.

###### Article 139

Adults who habitually serve or work for others shall have the same domicile as the person they serve or for whom they work, when they reside with that person in the same house.

###### Article 140

The place where the succession shall open shall be determined by the domicile of the deceased.

###### Article 141

When a document contains, on the part of the parties or one of them, election of domicile for the execution of that same document in a place other than that of the actual domicile, the notifications, demands and proceedings relating to this document may be made at the agreed domicile, and before the judge of that domicile.

#### Titre V : Des absents

##### Chapitre I. De la présomption d'absence

###### Article 142

When a person has ceased to appear at the place of his domicile or residence without news having been received, the President of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance or the judge he delegates for this purpose may, at the request of interested parties or the public prosecutor, establish that there is a presumption of absence.

###### Article 143

The judge may designate one or more relatives or relatives by marriage, or, where appropriate, any other persons to represent the person presumed absent in the exercise of his rights or in any act in which he would be interested, as well as to administer all or part of his property; the representation of the presumed absent and the administration of his property are then subject to the rules applicable to guardianship of adults without family council, and moreover subject to the following modifications.

###### Article 144

Without prejudice to the special jurisdiction attributed to other courts, for the same purposes, the judge determines, where appropriate, according to the importance of the property, the sums that should be allocated annually for the maintenance of the family or for the charges of the marriage. He determines how provision is made for the establishment of the children. He also specifies how administrative expenses are settled as well as possibly the remuneration that may be allocated to the person responsible for the representation of the presumed absent and the administration of his property.

###### Article 145

The judge may, at any time and even ex officio, terminate the mission of the person thus designated; he may also proceed with his replacement.

###### Article 146

If the presumed absentee is called to a partition, the latter may be done amicably. In this case, the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance authorizes the partition, even partial, and designates, if necessary, a notary to proceed with it, in the presence of the representative of the presumed absentee or his replacement designated in accordance with Article 143, if the initial representative is himself interested in the partition. The liquidation statement is submitted for approval to the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance. The partition may also be done in court. Any other partition is considered provisional.

###### Article 147

The public prosecutor is specially charged with safeguarding the interests of presumed absentees. It is heard on all applications concerning them; it may require ex officio the application or modification of the measures provided for in this title.

###### Article 148

If a presumed absentee reappears or gives news of himself, the judge, upon his request, terminates the measures taken for his representation and the administration of his property; he then recovers the property managed or acquired on his behalf during the period of absence.

###### Article 149

Rights acquired without fraud, on the basis of the presumption of absence, are not called into question when the death of the absentee is established or judicially declared, whatever the date retained for the death.

###### Article 150

The preceding provisions, relating to the representation of presumed absentees and the administration of their property, are also applicable to persons who, as a result of remoteness, find themselves despite themselves unable to express their will.

###### Article 151

These same provisions are not applicable to presumed absentees or to the persons mentioned in Article 120 when they have left a sufficient power of attorney for the purpose of representing them and administering their property.

The same applies if the spouse can sufficiently provide for the interests at stake through the application of the matrimonial regime, and in particular through the effect of a decision obtained pursuant to Articles 225 and 227, and 1671 and 1674.

##### Chapitre II: Of the declaration of absence

###### Article 152

When ten years have elapsed since the judgment which established the presumption of absence, either according to the procedures set by Article 142, or on the occasion of one of the judicial proceedings provided for by Articles 225 and 227, and 1671 and 1674, the absence may be declared by the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance at the request of any interested party or the public prosecutor. The same shall apply when, in the absence of such a finding, the person has ceased to appear at the place of his domicile or residence, without news having been received for more than twenty years.

###### Article 153

Extracts from the application for a declaration of absence, after having been approved by the public prosecutor, are published in a journal authorized to receive legal publications and in a journal of the country of domicile or last residence of the person who has remained without giving news when the domicile or last residence is located outside the territory of the Republic of Djibouti. The Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance, seized of the application, may furthermore order any other publicity measure in any place where it deems useful.

These publicity measures are ensured by the party submitting the application.

###### Article 154

As soon as the extracts have been published, the application is transmitted, through the intermediary of the public prosecutor, to the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance which decides according to the documents and records produced and having regard to the conditions of the disappearance, as well as to the circumstances which may explain the lack of news. The Civil Chamber may order any supplementary information measure and prescribe, if necessary, that an investigation be conducted adversarially in any place where it deems useful.

###### Article 155

The application initiating proceedings may be filed as of the year preceding the expiration of the time limits provided for in Article 152. The judgment declaring absence is rendered at least one year after the publication of the extracts from this application. It finds that the person presumed absent has not reappeared during the time limits referred to in Article 152.

###### Article 156

The application for a declaration of absence is considered null and void when the absentee reappears or the date of his death is established, prior to the rendering of the judgment.

###### Article 157

When the judgment declaring absence is rendered, extracts from it are published according to the procedures provided for in Article 153, within the time limit set by the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance. The decision is deemed null and void if it has not been published within this time limit.

When the judgment has become res judicata, its operative part is transcribed at the request of the public prosecutor in the death registers of the place of domicile of the absentee or of his last residence. Mention of this transcription is made in the margin of the registers at the date of the judgment declaring the absence; it is also made in the margin of the birth certificate of the person declared absent. The transcription makes the judgment enforceable against third parties who can only obtain its rectification or annulment, in accordance with Article 129.

###### Article 158

The judgment declaring absence entails, from the transcription, all the effects that the established death of the absentee would have had. The measures taken for the administration of the property of the absentee, in accordance with Chapter I of this title, come to an end, unless otherwise decided by the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance. The spouse of the absentee may contract a new marriage.

###### Article 159

If the absentee reappears or if his existence is proven subsequent to the judgment declaring absence, the annulment of this judgment may be pursued, at the request of the public prosecutor or any interested party.

However, if the interested party intends to be represented, he may only do so through an attorney duly registered with the bar.

The operative part of the annulment judgment is published without delay, according to the procedures set by Article 153. Mention of this decision is made, upon its publication, in the margin of the judgment declaring absence and on any register that refers to it.

###### Article 160

The absentee whose existence is judicially established recovers his property and that which he should have collected during his absence in the state in which they are found, the price of those which would have been alienated or the property acquired in employment of the capital or income due to his benefit.

###### Article 161

Any interested party who has fraudulently caused a declaration of absence shall be required to restore to the absentee whose existence is judicially established the income from the property which it shall have enjoyed and to pay him the legal interest from the day of receipt, without prejudice, if applicable, to additional damages.

If the fraud is attributable to the spouse of the person declared absent, the latter shall be admissible to challenge the liquidation of the matrimonial regime which the judgment declaring absence shall have terminated.

###### Article 162

If the missing person reappears while his wife has not yet remarried, she becomes by right his spouse again. Whereas if she has remarried, she remains the spouse of the second husband.

#### Title VI: On Marriage

##### Chapter I. Qualities and Conditions Required to Contract Marriage

###### Article 163

Man and woman cannot contract marriage before the age of eighteen.

Nevertheless, the public prosecutor of the place of celebration of the marriage may grant age dispensations for serious reasons.

The civil registrar receives the declaration of the future spouses if they intend that their union be governed by the provisions of this code, failing which it will be governed by the family code.

###### Article 164

There is no marriage when there is no consent.

###### Article 165

A second marriage cannot be contracted before the dissolution of the first.

###### Article 166

Minors cannot contract marriage without the consent of their father and mother.

In case of disagreement between the father and the mother, this division implies consent.

In case of refusal by both parents and persistence of the matrimonial intention of the two minors, the marriage is authorized by the judge.

###### Article 167

If one of the two parents is dead or if they are unable to express their will, the consent of the other is sufficient.

It is not necessary to produce the death certificate of the father or mother of one of the future spouses when the spouse or the father and mother of the deceased attest to this death under oath.

If the current residence of the father or mother is unknown, and if they have not given news for a year, the marriage may be celebrated if the child and the one of their father and mother who will give their consent make a declaration under oath.

All of this shall be mentioned on the marriage certificate.

False oath taken in the cases provided for in this article and in the following articles of this chapter shall be punished by the penalties prescribed by article 266 of the penal code.

###### Article 168

If the father and mother are dead or if they are both unable to express their will, the grandfathers and grandmothers replace them; if there is disagreement between the grandfather and grandmother of the same line or if there is disagreement between the two lines, this division implies consent.

If the current residence of the father and mother is unknown and if they have not given news for a year, the marriage may be celebrated if the grandfathers and grandmothers as well as the child themselves make a declaration under oath. The same applies if, one or more grandfathers or grandmothers giving their consent to the marriage, the current residence of the other grandfathers or grandmothers is unknown and if they have not given news for a year.

###### Article 169

The provisions contained in articles 166 and 167 are applicable to legally recognized natural children.

If one of the two parents is dead or if they are unable to express their will, the consent of the other is sufficient. The provisions of paragraphs 3, 4 and 5 of article 167 are applicable to the minor natural child.

###### Article 170

If there is no father, mother, grandfather, or grandmother, or if they are all unable to express their will, minors under eighteen years of age cannot contract marriage without the consent of the family council.

The natural child who has not been recognized, and the one who, after having been recognized, has lost their father and mother or whose father and mother cannot express their will, may not, before the age of eighteen, marry without having obtained the consent of the family council.

###### Article 171

If the current residence of those ascendants of the minor under eighteen whose death is not established is unknown and if these ascendants have not given news for a year, the minor shall make a declaration under oath before the president of the Court of First Instance of their residence, assisted by their clerk, in their chambers, and this judge shall acknowledge it.

The president of the Court of First Instance shall notify this oath to the family council, which shall rule on the request for authorization to marry. However, the minor may take the oath directly in the presence of the members of the family council.

###### Article 172

Civil registrars who have proceeded with the celebration of marriages contracted by sons or daughters who have not reached the age of eighteen years without the consent of the father and mother, that of the grandfathers or grandmothers and that of the family council, in cases where it is required, being stated in the marriage certificate, shall, at the request of the interested parties or the public prosecutor, be condemned to a fine of 100,000 FD.

###### Article 173

In direct line, marriage is prohibited between all legitimate or natural ascendants and descendants, and relatives by marriage in the same line.

###### Article 174

In collateral line, marriage is prohibited between legitimate or natural brother and sister.

###### Article 175

Marriage is also prohibited between uncle and niece, aunt and nephew, whether the relationship is legitimate or natural.

###### Article 176

Nevertheless, the President of the Republic may, for serious reasons, lift the prohibitions provided:

- by article 173 on marriages between relatives by marriage in direct line when the person who created the alliance is deceased;
- by article 175 on marriages between uncle and niece, aunt and nephew.

##### Chapter II. Formalities Relating to the Celebration of Marriage

###### Article 177

The marriage shall be celebrated publicly before the civil registrar of the municipality where one of the spouses has their domicile or residence on the date of the publication provided for by article 99 and, in case of dispensation from publication, on the date of the dispensation provided for in article 178 below.

The man and woman may attend their marriage themselves or by proxy. The person who consents to the marriage of a minor may also do so by proxy. The guardian may also exercise their rights by proxy. The proxy must, under penalty of nullity, be established by authentic instrument and expressly include the designation of the two future spouses.

###### Article 178

The publication ordered in article 99 shall be made at the town hall of the place of marriage and at that of the place where each of the future spouses has their domicile or, in the absence of domicile, their residence.

###### Article 179

The public prosecutor may, for serious reasons, dispense with publication and any time limit or with the posting of the publication only.

They may also in exceptional cases dispense the future spouses or only one of them from submitting the medical certificate required by the second paragraph of article 99.

The medical certificate is not required from either of the future spouses in case of imminent danger of death of one of them, provided for in the second paragraph of article 110 of this code.

###### Article 180

A marriage contracted in a foreign country between Djiboutian nationals and between a Djiboutian national and a foreigner shall be valid if it has been contracted in the forms customary in that country, provided that it has been preceded by the publication prescribed by Article 99, under the title Of civil status records, and that the Djiboutian national has not contravened the provisions contained in the preceding chapter of this code.

The same shall apply to a marriage contracted in a foreign country between a Djiboutian national and a foreign national, if it has been celebrated by diplomatic agents or by the consuls of Djibouti, in accordance with Djiboutian laws.

A marriage contracted in accordance with the two preceding paragraphs is only enforceable against third parties in Djibouti if the marriage certificate has been transcribed in the Djiboutian civil status registers. In the absence of transcription, the marriage of a Djiboutian national, validly celebrated by a foreign authority, produces its civil effects in Djibouti with regard to the spouses and children. The request for transcription is made to the consular or diplomatic authority with jurisdiction over the place of celebration of the marriage.

###### Article 181

The President of the Republic may, for serious reasons, authorize the celebration of the marriage if one of the future spouses has died after the completion of official formalities unequivocally marking his or her consent.

In this case, the effects of the marriage date back to the day preceding that of the death of the spouse. However, this marriage does not entail any right of intestate succession for the benefit of the surviving spouse and no matrimonial property regime is deemed to have existed between the spouses.

##### Chapitre III. Objections to marriage

###### Article 182

The right to lodge an objection to the celebration of the marriage belongs to the person bound by marriage to one of the two contracting parties.

###### Article 183

The father, the mother, and, in the absence of father and mother, the grandfathers and grandmothers may lodge an objection to the marriage of their children and descendants, even if of legal age.

After judicial lifting of an objection to marriage lodged by an ascendant, no new objection lodged by an ascendant is admissible or may delay the celebration.

###### Article 184

In the absence of any ascendant, a brother or sister, uncle or aunt, or first cousin, of legal age, may only lodge an objection in the following two cases:

1° When the consent of the family council required by application, as the case may be, of Articles 170 or 171 has not been obtained;

2° When the objection is based on the state of insanity of the future spouse: this objection, for which the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance may pronounce an unconditional lifting, shall never be admitted except on condition that the objector institutes guardianship proceedings for adults and has a decision rendered thereon within the time limit to be set by the judgment.

###### Article 185

In the two cases provided for by the preceding article, the guardian or curator may, during the duration of the guardianship or curatorship, lodge an objection only insofar as he has been authorized to do so by a family council, which he may convene.

###### Article 186

Every act of objection shall state the capacity that gives the objector the right to lodge it and shall be signed, on the original and on the copy, by the latter or his agent holding a special and authentic power of attorney; it shall contain an election of domicile in the place where the marriage is to be celebrated; it must also contain the grounds for the objection and reproduce the text of the law on which the objection is based; all on pain of nullity and of temporary suspension of the bailiff who has signed the act containing the objection. The suspension is pronounced according to the procedure provided for by Ordinance No. 86-069/PR/J of 11 September 1986 relating to the discipline of bailiffs, auctioneers and notaries. The bailiff may, however, only be responsible for the formal regularity of the act and does not have to judge the capacity claimed by the objector or the accuracy of the facts alleged by him. The bailiff may, without incurring liability, refuse his services if the objector is not one of the persons enumerated by law, or if the objection is not based on a cause provided for by law. After one full year, the act of objection ceases to have effect. It may be renewed, except in the case referred to in the second paragraph of Article 183 above.

###### Article 187

The Civil Chamber shall rule within ten days on the application for lifting lodged by the future spouses, even if minors.

###### Article 188

The decision of the Civil Chamber may be referred to the Court of Appeal, which rules within the same period of ten days.

###### Article 189

If the objection is rejected, the objectors, other than ascendants, may be ordered to pay damages.

Default judgments and orders rejecting objections to marriage are not subject to opposition.

##### Chapitre IV. Applications for annulment of marriage

###### Article 190

A marriage that has been contracted without the free consent of both spouses, or of one of them, may only be challenged by the spouses, or by the one of the two whose consent was not free, or by the public prosecutor.

The exercise of duress on the spouses or one of them, including reverential fear towards an ascendant, constitutes a ground for annulment of the marriage.

If there has been an error as to the person, or as to essential qualities of the person, the other spouse may apply for annulment of the marriage.

###### Article 191

In the case of the preceding article, the application for annulment is no longer admissible after a period of two years from the marriage, or from the time the spouse acquired his or her full freedom or the error was recognized by him or her.

###### Article 192

A marriage contracted without the consent of the father and mother, of ascendants, or of the family council, in cases where such consent was necessary, may only be challenged by those whose consent was required, or by the one of the two spouses who needed such consent.

###### Article 193

The action for annulment may no longer be brought either by the spouses or by the relatives whose consent was required, whenever the marriage has been approved expressly or tacitly by those whose consent was necessary, or when two years have elapsed without any claim on their part, since they became aware of the marriage. The action for annulment may also not be brought by the spouse when two years have elapsed without any claim on his or her part, since he or she reached the age required to consent on his or her own to the marriage.

###### Article 194

Any marriage contracted in contravention of the provisions contained in Articles 163, 164, 165, 173, 174 and 175 may be challenged, within thirty years from its celebration, either by the spouses themselves, or by all those who have an interest, or by the public prosecutor.
