Nevertheless, a marriage contracted by spouses who had not yet reached the required age, or of whom one of the two had not reached that age, may no longer be challenged:

1° when six months have elapsed since that spouse or the spouses reached the required age; 2° when the woman who had not reached that age conceived before the expiry of six months.

The father, mother, ascendants and family who consented to the contracted marriage are not entitled to apply for its annulment.

###### Article 195

In all cases where, in accordance with Article 194, the action for annulment may be brought by all those who have an interest therein, it may not be brought by collateral relatives, or by children born of another marriage, during the lifetime of both spouses, but only when they have a vested and current interest therein.

###### Article 196

The spouse to whose detriment a second marriage has been contracted may request its nullity, even during the lifetime of the spouse who was bound to him or her.

###### Article 197

If the new spouses contest the nullity of the first marriage, the validity or nullity of that marriage must be determined beforehand.

###### Article 198

The Public Prosecutor, in all cases to which Article 194 applies, may and must request the nullity of the marriage, during the lifetime of both spouses, and have them condemned to separate.

###### Article 199

A marriage that has been celebrated in fraud of the law may be annulled at the request of the spouse acting in good faith or of the Public Prosecutor's office, filed within one year of the marriage.

###### Article 200

Any marriage that has not been contracted publicly, and that has not been celebrated before the competent public officer, may be challenged, within a period of thirty years from its celebration, by the spouses themselves, by the fathers and mothers, by the ascendants, and by all those who have a vested and current interest therein, as well as by the Public Prosecutor's office.

The period is reduced to fifteen years when there is possession of status of spouse during this period and when a certificate of celebration registered in the civil status register is produced.

###### Article 201

If the marriage was not preceded by the required publication or if the dispensations permitted by law were not obtained or if the prescribed intervals between publications and celebrations were not observed, the public officer and the contracting parties, or those under whose authority they acted, are liable to a fine of 20,000 FD to 50,000 FD.

###### Article 202

The penalties pronounced by the preceding article shall be incurred by the persons designated therein, for any contravention of the rules prescribed by Article 177, even if these contraventions are not deemed sufficient to pronounce the nullity of the marriage.

###### Article 203

No one may claim the title of spouse and the civil effects of marriage if he or she does not produce a certificate of celebration registered in the civil status register, except in the cases provided for by Article 77, under the title Of Civil Status Acts.

###### Article 204

Possession of status cannot dispense the alleged spouses who invoke it respectively from producing the certificate of celebration of the marriage before the civil status officer.

On the other hand, subsequent publicity cures prior or concomitant clandestinity to the marriage when possession of status of spouse exists.

###### Article 205

When there is possession of status, and the certificate of celebration of the marriage before the civil status officer is produced, the spouses are respectively not admissible to request the nullity of this certificate.

###### Article 206

If nevertheless, in the cases of Articles 203 and 204, there exist children born of two individuals who have lived publicly as husband and wife, and who are both deceased, the legitimacy of the children cannot be contested solely on the grounds of failure to produce the certificate of celebration, whenever this legitimacy is proven by a possession of status that is not contradicted by the birth certificate.

###### Article 207

When proof of a legal celebration of the marriage is acquired by the result of criminal proceedings, the registration of the judgment on the civil status registers ensures to the marriage, from the day of its celebration, all civil effects, both with regard to the spouses and with regard to the children born of this marriage.

###### Article 208

If the spouses or one of them died without having discovered the fraud, criminal action may be brought by all those who have an interest in having the marriage declared valid, and by the Public Prosecutor. The court ruling on the criminal matter must, in order to enter into conviction, recognize that the incriminated act resulted in suppressing the proof of a marriage actually celebrated.

###### Article 209

If the public officer is deceased at the time of the discovery of the fraud, the action shall be brought in civil court against his heirs by the Public Prosecutor, in the presence of the interested parties and upon their complaint.

###### Article 210

A marriage that has been declared null nevertheless produces its effects with regard to the spouses when it was contracted in good faith.

If good faith exists only on the part of one of the spouses, the marriage produces its effects only in favor of that spouse.

###### Article 211

It also produces its effects with regard to the children, even if neither of the spouses was in good faith.

Decisions regarding the exercise of parental authority are made as in matters of divorce.

##### Chapitre V. Des obligations qui naissent du mariage

###### Article 212

The spouses contract together, by the mere fact of marriage, the obligation to feed, maintain and educate their children.

###### Article 213

Children owe support to their father and mother or other ascendants who are in need.

###### Article 214

Sons-in-law and daughters-in-law likewise owe, and in the same circumstances, support to their father-in-law and mother-in-law, but this obligation ceases when the spouse who produced the affinity and the children born of his or her union with the other spouse are deceased.

###### Article 215

The obligations resulting from these provisions are reciprocal.

Nevertheless, when the creditor has himself seriously failed in his obligations toward the debtor, the judge may discharge the latter from all or part of the support debt.

###### Article 216

Support is granted only in proportion to the need of the person claiming it and to the fortune of the person who owes it.

The Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance may, even of its own motion, and according to the circumstances of the case, accompany the support payment with a variation clause permitted by the laws in force.

###### Article 217

When the person providing or the person receiving support is placed back in a state such that one can no longer give it or the other no longer needs it in whole or in part, discharge or reduction may be requested.

###### Article 218

If the person who must provide support justifies that he or she cannot pay the support payment, the Civil Chamber may, with knowledge of the cause, order that he or she will receive into his or her dwelling, that he or she will feed and maintain the person to whom he or she owes support.

###### Article 219

The Civil Chamber shall also judge whether the father or mother who offers to receive, feed and maintain in his or her dwelling the child to whom he owes support, shall in this case be dispensed from paying the support payment.

##### Chapitre VI. Des devoirs et des droits respectifs des époux

###### Article 220

Spouses owe each other mutual fidelity, relief, assistance.

Each of the spouses may bear, for use, the name of the other spouse, by substitution or addition to his or her own name in the order he or she chooses.

If one of the spouses complains of any act causing him or her prejudice on the part of the other spouse without being able to provide proof thereof, and if the judge cannot determine the responsible spouse, he must appoint two persons whom he gives the mission to conciliate the spouses. After having studied the situation, the conciliators must, to the extent possible, reconcile the spouses and, in all cases, report on their mission to the judge.

###### Article 221

The spouses jointly ensure the moral and material direction of the family. They provide for the education of the children and prepare their future.

###### Article 222

If the matrimonial agreements do not regulate the contribution of the spouses to the charges of the marriage, they contribute to it in proportion to their respective means.

If one of the spouses does not fulfill his or her obligations, he or she may be compelled to do so by the other in the forms provided for in the code of civil procedure.

###### Article 223

The spouses mutually commit themselves to a life together.

The family residence is at the place they choose by mutual agreement.

The spouses cannot, one without the other, dispose of the rights by which the family dwelling is secured, nor of the furnishings with which it is furnished. The one of the two who has not given his consent to the act may request its annulment: the action for nullity is open to him within one year from the day on which he became aware of the act, without ever being able to be brought more than one year after the matrimonial regime has been dissolved.

###### Article 224

Each spouse has full legal capacity; but his rights and powers may be limited by the effect of the matrimonial regime and the provisions of this chapter.

###### Article 225

A spouse may be authorized by the court to enter into alone an act for which the cooperation or consent of his spouse would be necessary, if the latter is unable to express his will or if his refusal is not justified by the interest of the family.

The act entered into under the conditions set by the court authorization is enforceable against the spouse whose cooperation or consent was lacking, without resulting in any personal obligation on his part.

###### Article 226

A spouse may give a mandate to the other to represent him in the exercise of the powers attributed to him by the matrimonial regime.

###### Article 227

If one of the spouses is unable to express his will, the other may be authorized by the court to represent him, in a general manner, or for certain particular acts, in the exercise of the powers resulting from the matrimonial regime. The conditions and scope of this representation are determined by the judge.

In the absence of legal power, mandate or court authorization, acts performed by one spouse in representation of the other have effect, with regard to the latter, according to the rules of management of affairs.

###### Article 228

Each spouse has the power to enter into alone contracts that have as their object the maintenance of the household or the education of the children: any debt thus contracted by one binds the other jointly and severally.

Joint and several liability does not apply, however, for manifestly excessive expenses, having regard to the standard of living of the household, the usefulness or uselessness of the transaction, the good or bad faith of the third party contracting. It does not apply either for obligations arising from installment purchases if they have not been concluded with the consent of both spouses.

###### Article 229

If one of the spouses seriously fails in his duties and thereby endangers the interests of the family, the president of the Court of First Instance may prescribe all urgent measures required by these interests.

He may in particular prohibit this spouse from performing, without the consent of the other, acts of disposition over his own property or that of the community, movable or immovable. He may also prohibit the removal of movables, except to specify those of which he grants personal use to one or the other of the spouses.

The duration of the measures provided for in this article must be determined. It may not, including any extension, exceed three years.

###### Article 230

If the order prohibits acts of disposition over property the alienation of which is subject to publication, it must be published at the initiative of the requesting spouse. This publication ceases to have effect upon the expiration of the period determined by the order, unless the interested party obtains in the meantime a modifying order, which shall be published in the same manner.

If the order prohibits disposing of corporeal movables, or moving them, it is served by the applicant on his spouse, and has the effect of making the latter responsible custodian of the movables under the same conditions as a debtor under seizure.

When the spouse brings the order to the knowledge of a third party, that third party, if he nevertheless contracts with the other spouse, is in bad faith.

###### Article 231

All acts performed in violation of the order are voidable, at the request of the requesting spouse, if they have been entered into with a third party in bad faith, or even in the case of property the alienation of which is subject to publication, if they are simply subsequent to the publication provided for by the preceding article.

The action for nullity is open to the requesting spouse for two years from the day on which he became aware of the act, without ever being able to be brought, if this act is subject to publication, more than two years after its publication.

###### Article 232

Each spouse may open, without the consent of the other, any deposit account and any securities account in his personal name.

The depositing spouse is deemed, with regard to the depositary, to have free disposal of the funds and securities on deposit.

###### Article 233

If one of the spouses appears alone to perform an act of administration, enjoyment or disposition over movable property that he holds individually, he is deemed, with regard to third parties in good faith, to have the power to perform this act alone.

This provision is not applicable to furnishings referred to in article 223, paragraph 3, nor to corporeal movables the nature of which creates a presumption of ownership by the other spouse in accordance with article 1651.

###### Article 234

Each spouse has the right to practice a profession without the consent of his spouse, and may always, for the needs of this profession, alienate and encumber alone his personal property in full ownership.

Each spouse administers, encumbers and alienates alone his personal property. The origin and composition of personal property are established both with regard to third parties and to the spouse, according to the rules of article 1649.

###### Article 235

Each spouse receives his earnings and salary and may dispose of them freely after having discharged the burdens of marriage.

###### Article 236

The creditors to whom a spouse has bound himself may exercise their claims against his personal property, even when the obligation has not been contracted by him in the exercise of his profession.

###### Article 237

The provisions of this chapter, in all points where they do not reserve the application of matrimonial agreements, are applicable, by the sole effect of marriage, whatever the matrimonial regime of the spouses.

##### Chapitre VII. Of the dissolution of marriage

###### Article 238

Marriage is dissolved:

1° By the death of one of the spouses; 2° By legally pronounced divorce.

##### Chapitre VIII. Of second marriages

###### Article 239

A woman may not contract a new marriage until three hundred days have elapsed since the dissolution of the previous marriage. The woman may however, before the expiration of this period of widowhood, contract marriage with her former spouse. The period is extended to four months and ten days elapsed from the death of the husband, for the widow, and from the judgment referred to in article 158 of this code, for the wife of the disappeared person.

This period ends in case of childbirth after the dissolution of the marriage. It also ends if the woman produces a medical certificate attesting that she is not pregnant.

The president of the Court of First Instance within whose jurisdiction the marriage is to be celebrated may, by order made upon simple application, shorten the period provided for by this article when it results clearly from the circumstances that, for three hundred days, the previous husband has not cohabited with his wife. The application is communicated to the public prosecutor. In case of rejection of the application, an appeal may be lodged.

#### Titre VII: Of divorce

##### Chapitre I. Of grounds for divorce

###### Article 240

Divorce may be pronounced in case:

- either of mutual consent;
- or of definitive breakdown of the conjugal bond;
- or of fault.

###### Section I: Divorce by mutual consent

###### § 1. Divorce upon joint petition of the spouses

###### Article 241

When the spouses jointly request divorce, they do not have to disclose the cause; they must only submit to the judge's approval a draft agreement that settles the consequences. The petition may be presented either by the parties themselves, or by their respective lawyers, or by a lawyer chosen by mutual agreement.

Divorce by mutual consent may not be requested during the first six months of marriage.

###### Article 242

The judge examines the petition with each of the spouses, then brings them together. He then calls the lawyer or lawyers, if one or both spouses have made such choice.

If the spouses persist in their intention to divorce, the judge informs them that their petition must be renewed after a reflection period of one month.

In the absence of renewal within three months following the expiration of this reflection period, the joint petition shall lapse.

###### Article 243

The judge approves the agreement and pronounces the divorce if he has obtained the conviction that the will of each of the spouses is genuine and that their consent is free and informed.

The judge may refuse approval and not pronounce the divorce if he finds that the agreement insufficiently protects the interests of the children or of one of the spouses.

###### § 2. Accepted divorce

###### Article 244

Divorce may be requested by one or the other of the spouses or by both when they accept the principle of the breakdown of the marriage without consideration of the facts at the origin thereof. This acceptance is not subject to retraction. Once it has been validly given, it can no longer be called into question, even by exercising a means of appeal.

###### Article 245

If he has obtained the conviction that each of the spouses has given his consent freely, the judge pronounces the divorce and rules on its consequences.

###### Section II: Divorce for permanent breakdown of the conjugal bond

###### Article 246

Divorce may be requested by one of the spouses when the conjugal bond is permanently broken down.

###### Article 247

The permanent breakdown of the conjugal bond results from the cessation of the community of life between the spouses, when they have lived separately for two years at the time of the divorce summons.

Notwithstanding these provisions, divorce is pronounced for permanent breakdown of the conjugal bond in the case provided for in the second paragraph of Article 251, as soon as the petition presented on this ground is filed as a counterclaim.

###### Section III: Divorce for fault

###### Article 248

Divorce may be requested by one of the spouses when facts constituting a serious or repeated violation of the duties and obligations of marriage are attributable to his spouse and make the continuation of the common life intolerable

###### Article 249

In the event of reconciliation of the spouses having occurred since the alleged facts, these facts can no longer be invoked as grounds for divorce. If this should nevertheless be the case, the judge would have the obligation to declare the petition inadmissible.

A new petition may however be filed by reason of facts that occurred or were discovered since the reconciliation, the old facts being then able to be recalled in support of this new petition. The maintenance or temporary resumption of common life are not considered as a reconciliation if they result only from necessity, from an effort at conciliation, or from the needs of the children's education.

###### Article 250

The faults of the spouse who initiated the divorce do not prevent examination of his petition; they may, however, remove from the facts he reproaches his spouse the character of seriousness which would have made them grounds for divorce.

These faults may also be invoked by the other spouse in support of a counterclaim for divorce. If both petitions are granted, the divorce is pronounced on the basis of shared fault. Even in the absence of a counterclaim, the divorce may be pronounced on the basis of shared fault of both spouses if the proceedings reveal faults on the part of each.

###### Article 251

If a petition for permanent breakdown of the conjugal bond and a petition for fault are concurrently presented, the judge examines first the petition for fault.

In this case, if he rejects the petition for divorce for fault, the judge rules without delay on the petition for divorce for permanent breakdown of the conjugal bond.

###### Section IV: Modifications to the ground of a divorce petition

###### Article 252

The spouses may, at any time during the proceedings, ask the judge to note their agreement to have the divorce pronounced by mutual consent by presenting to him an agreement settling the consequences thereof.

###### Article 253

The spouses may also, at any time during the proceedings, when divorce has been requested for permanent breakdown of the conjugal bond or for fault, ask the judge to note their agreement to have the divorce pronounced for acceptance of the principle of the breakdown of the marriage.

###### Article 254

If, in the context of proceedings initiated for permanent breakdown of the conjugal bond, the defendant counterclaims for divorce for fault, the plaintiff may invoke the faults of his spouse to modify the ground of his petition.

##### Chapter II: Divorce proceedings

###### Section I: General provisions

###### Article 255

The proceedings concerning the cause, the consequences of the divorce and the provisional measures are not public.

###### Article 256

In the case of divorce for fault, and at the request of the spouses, the court may limit itself to noting in the grounds of the judgment that there exist facts constituting grounds for divorce, without having to state the faults and grievances of the parties.

###### Article 257

If a petition for divorce must be filed in the name of an adult under guardianship, it is presented by the guardian with the authorization of the family council, after opinion of the treating physician.

The adult under curatorship exercises the action himself with the assistance of the curator.

###### Article 258

If the spouse against whom the petition is filed is under guardianship, the action is exercised against the guardian; if he is under curatorship, he defends himself, with the assistance of the curator.

###### Article 259

A special guardian or curator is appointed when the guardianship or curatorship had been entrusted to the spouse of the incapacitated person.

###### Article 260

If one of the spouses is placed under safeguard of justice, the petition for divorce may not be examined until after organization of the guardianship or appointment of a special curator.

###### Article 261

When one of the spouses is placed under one of the protection regimes provided for in Chapter II Legal protection measures for adults of Title XII Majority and adults protected by law(art. 565 et seq.), no petition for divorce by mutual consent may be presented.

###### Section II: Procedure applicable to divorce by mutual consent

###### Article 262

The petition for divorce is presented by the parties themselves or their lawyers. The spouses may be represented by a lawyer chosen by mutual agreement.

This petition takes the form of an initial application to which is annexed an agreement containing the provisional measures that the spouses will respect during the time of the proceedings, as well as a draft final agreement intended to settle the consequences of the divorce.

The judge examines the petition with each of the spouses, then brings them together. He then calls the lawyer or lawyers if they have made such choice.

###### Article 263

When the conditions provided for in Article 243 are met, the judge approves the agreement settling the consequences of the divorce and, by the same decision, pronounces the divorce.

###### Article 264

In case of refusal to approve the agreement settling the consequences of divorce, the judge may nevertheless approve the provisional measures envisaged by the parties under Article 262, paragraph 2, and take any measure provided for in Articles 272 and 273, until the date on which the divorce judgment becomes final, ensuring in particular that these measures are in accordance with the interest of the child or children.

A new agreement settling the consequences of divorce may then be presented by the spouses within a maximum period of three months.

###### Article 265

In the absence of presentation of a new agreement within the time limit set in the preceding article or if the judge refuses approval again, the application for divorce lapses.

###### Section III : Procedure applicable to other cases of divorce

###### § 1. The initial petition

###### Article 266

The spouse filing an application for divorce submits, himself or herself or through a lawyer, a petition to the judge, without indicating the grounds for divorce.

###### § 2. Conciliation

###### Article 267

The judge must organize a conciliation hearing. In case of failure, the conciliation attempt may be renewed and attempted at any time during the divorce proceedings which may be initiated by a spouse in accordance with Article 276.

The judge invites the spouses to consider renouncing the divorce and, if he observes their will to continue the procedure, the judge seeks to reconcile the spouses both on the principle of divorce and on its consequences.

###### Article 268

When the judge seeks to reconcile the spouses, he must meet personally with each of them separately before bringing them together in his presence.

The lawyers are then called upon to attend and participate in the meeting.

In the case where the spouse who did not file the application does not appear at the hearing or is unable to express his or her will, the judge meets with the other spouse and invites him or her to reflect.

###### Article 269

The conciliation attempt may be suspended and resumed without formality, allowing the spouses time for reflection within a limit of eight days.

If a longer period appears useful, the judge may decide to suspend the procedure and resort to a new conciliation attempt within six months at most. He orders, where appropriate, the necessary provisional measures.

###### Article 270

When the judge observes that the applicant maintains his or her application, he encourages the spouses to settle the consequences of the divorce amicably.

He requests that they present a draft settlement of the effects of the divorce for the trial hearing. For this purpose, he may take any provisional measure within the meaning of Articles 272 and 273 of this Code, until the date on which the divorce judgment becomes final, ensuring in particular that these measures are in accordance with the interest of the child or children.

###### Article 271

What has been said or written on the occasion of a conciliation attempt, in whatever form it may have taken place, may never be invoked for or against a spouse or a third party in the continuation of the proceedings.

###### § 3. Provisional measures

###### Article 272

Upon the appearance of the spouses in the case referred to in Article 244, or the non-conciliation order in other cases, the judge prescribes the measures that are necessary to ensure the existence of the spouses and children until the date on which the judgment becomes final.

###### Article 273

The judge may in particular:

1° Propose to the spouses a mediation measure and, after obtaining their agreement, appoint a mediator to proceed with it;

2° Require the spouses to meet with a mediator who will inform them about the purpose and conduct of mediation;

3° Rule on the terms of the spouses' separate residence;

4° Grant to one of them the enjoyment of the dwelling and household furniture, or share this enjoyment between them, specifying whether it is free of charge or not and, where appropriate, noting the spouses' agreement on the amount of an occupation indemnity; failing that, set this amount;

5° Order the return of clothing and personal items and, in case of dispute over the ownership of these goods, provisionally decide their allocation;

6° Fix the alimony and the provision for costs of proceedings that one of the spouses must pay to his or her spouse, designate which spouse or spouses must ensure the provisional settlement of all or part of the debts;

7° Grant to one of the spouses advances on account of his or her rights in the liquidation of the matrimonial regime if the situation makes it necessary;

8° Rule on the allocation of the enjoyment or management of common or undivided property other than that referred to in 4°, subject to the rights of each of the spouses in the liquidation of the matrimonial regime 9° Appoint any qualified professional with a view to drawing up an estimated inventory or making proposals regarding the settlement of the spouses' pecuniary interests;

10° Appoint a notary with a view to drawing up a draft liquidation of the matrimonial regime and formation of lots to be shared.

###### Article 274

If there are minor children, the judge rules on their custody, as well as on the right of visitation and accommodation. He sets the contribution due, for their maintenance and education, by the spouse who does not have custody.

Parental authority is exercised by the spouse to whom the court has entrusted custody of the child, except for the right of visitation and supervision of the other.

###### Article 275

The judge may take, from the initial petition, emergency measures.

He may, in this capacity, authorize the petitioning spouse to reside separately, if necessary with his or her minor children; the judge may then and where appropriate, determine, with the agreement of the spouses and failing that by decision, the financial arrangements between spouses in order to facilitate this separate residence.

The judge may also, to guarantee the rights of a spouse, order any conservatory measures such as the affixing of seals on common property. The provisions of Article 240 and the other safeguards established by the matrimonial regime remain applicable, however.

###### § 4. Del'introduction de l'instance en divorce

###### Article 276

After the non-conciliation order, a spouse may initiate proceedings or file a counterclaim for acceptance of the principle of breakdown of the marriage, for irretrievable breakdown of the marital bond or for fault.

However, when at the conciliation hearing the spouses have declared acceptance of the principle of breakdown of the marriage and the pronouncement of divorce on the basis of Article 244, the proceedings may be initiated only on that same basis.

###### Article 277

On pain of inadmissibility, the application initiating proceedings must include a proposal for the settlement of the spouses' pecuniary and patrimonial interests.

###### Article 278

When he definitively rejects the application for divorce, the judge may rule on the contribution to the expenses of the marriage, the residence of the family and the terms of the exercise of parental authority.

###### § 5. Des preuves

###### Article 279

The facts invoked as grounds for divorce or as defenses to an application may be established by any mode of proof, including admission. However, descendants may never be heard on the grievances invoked by the spouses.

###### Article 280

A spouse may not submit in the proceedings an element of evidence that he or she obtained by violence or fraud.

###### Article 281

Reports drawn up at the request of a spouse outside judicial proceedings are excluded from the proceedings if there has been a violation of domicile or unlawful interference with the privacy of private life.

###### Article 282

The spouses must communicate to each other and to the judge as well as to the experts appointed by him, all useful information and documents to set allowances and pensions and liquidate the matrimonial property regime.

The judge may have all useful searches carried out with debtors or those who hold assets on behalf of the spouses without professional secrecy being invoked. Any contravention of the judge's order shall be prosecuted before the Court of First Instance, and punished by a fine of 20,000 to 200,000 FD.

##### Chapitre III: Consequences of Divorce

###### Section I: The Date on Which the Effects of Divorce Occur

###### Article 283

The decision granting divorce dissolves the marriage on the date on which it acquires the force of res judicata.

###### Article 284

To enter into a new marriage, the woman must observe the period of three hundred days as provided for in Article 250.

If the spouses have been authorized to reside separately during the proceedings, this period begins to run from the day of the decision authorizing separate residence or approving, in the case of a joint application, the temporary agreement made in this regard.

The woman may remarry without delay when the divorce has been granted in the cases provided for in Articles 246 and 247.

###### Article 285

The period referred to in the preceding article ends if a childbirth occurs after the decision authorizing or approving separate residence or, failing that, after the date on which the divorce judgment acquired the force of res judicata.

If the husband dies before the divorce judgment acquires the force of res judicata, the period runs from the day following the day on which the death is officially certified.

###### Article 286

The divorce judgment is enforceable against third parties, with regard to the property of the spouses, from the day on which the formalities of marginal notation prescribed by the civil status rules have been completed.

###### Article 287

The agreement or divorce judgment takes effect in the relations between the spouses, with regard to their property:

- when it is granted by mutual consent in accordance with Article 263, on the date of approval of the agreement settling all the consequences of the divorce, unless it provides otherwise;
- when it is granted for acceptance of the principle of the breakdown of the marriage, for irretrievable breakdown of the conjugal bond or for fault, on the date of the order of non-reconciliation.

One of the spouses may request that the effect of the judgment be brought forward to the date on which, through the fault of the other, their cohabitation and collaboration ceased.

###### Article 288

Any obligation contracted by one of the spouses at the expense of the community, any alienation of common property made by one of them within the limits of their powers, subsequent to the initial application, shall be declared null and void, if it is proven that there has been fraud against the rights of the other spouse.

###### Section II: Consequences of Divorce for the Spouses

###### § 1. General Provisions

###### Article 289

If the divorced spouses wish to enter into another union between themselves, a new celebration of marriage is necessary.

###### Article 290

Following the divorce, each of the spouses loses the use of their spouse's name.

One of the spouses may nevertheless retain the use of the other's name, either with the latter's consent, or with the authorization of the judge, if he or she establishes a particular interest for himself or herself or for the children.

###### Article 291

Divorce has no effect on matrimonial benefits that take effect during the marriage and on gifts of present property whatever their form.

Divorce entails automatic revocation of matrimonial benefits that only take effect upon dissolution of the matrimonial property regime or upon the death of one of the spouses and of testamentary dispositions, granted by one spouse to the other spouse by marriage contract or during the union, unless the spouse who granted them expressly wishes otherwise. This intention is recorded in the agreement signed by the spouses and approved by the judge, or by the judge at the time of granting the divorce; in these cases, the benefit or disposition maintained is irrevocable.

However, if the marriage contract so provides, the spouses may always take back the property they have contributed to the community.

###### Article 292

Divorce has no effect on the rights that either spouse holds from the law or from agreements entered into with third parties.

###### Article 293

The spouses may, during the divorce proceedings, enter into any agreements for the liquidation and division of their matrimonial property regime.

When the liquidation concerns property subject to land registration, the agreement must be made by notarial deed.

###### § 2. Consequences Specific to Divorces Other Than by Mutual Consent

###### Article 294

Without prejudice to the application of Article 297, damages may be awarded to a spouse in compensation for the consequences of particular gravity that he or she suffers as a result of the dissolution of the marriage:

1° either when he or she was the defendant in a divorce granted for irretrievable breakdown of the conjugal bond and he or she had not himself or herself filed any application for divorce;

2° or when the divorce is granted on the exclusive fault of his or her spouse.

This claim may only be made on the occasion of the divorce action.

###### Article 295

In the absence of a settlement by agreement between the spouses, the judge rules on their applications for maintenance in undivided ownership, preferential allocation and advance on share of community property or undivided property. The judge rules on applications for liquidation and division of property interests, under the conditions set out in Articles L.624-5 to L.624-11 of the Code of Civil Procedure, if the disagreements remaining between the parties are established by any means, in particular by producing:

- a joint declaration of acceptance of a judicial division, indicating the points of disagreement between the spouses;
- the draft prepared by the notary appointed on the basis of 10° of Article 273.

He may, even of his own motion, rule on the determination of the matrimonial property regime applicable to the spouses.

###### Article 296

The spouses may, during the proceedings, submit to the judge for approval agreements settling all or part of the consequences of the divorce.

The judge, after having verified that the interests of each of the spouses and the children are preserved, shall approve the agreements when granting the divorce.

###### § 3. Compensatory Allowances

###### Article 297

Divorce terminates the duty of support between spouses.

One of the spouses may be required to pay the other an allowance intended to compensate, as far as possible, for the disparity that the breakdown of the marriage creates in their respective living conditions. However, the judge may refuse to grant such an allowance if equity so requires, either in consideration of the criteria provided for in Article 298, or when the divorce is granted on the exclusive fault of the spouse who requests the benefit of this allowance, having regard to the particular circumstances of the breakdown.

###### Article 298

The compensatory payment is determined according to the needs of the spouse to whom it is paid and the resources of the other, taking into account the situation at the time of the divorce and the foreseeable evolution thereof in the future.

For this purpose, the judge takes into consideration, in particular:

- the duration of the marriage;
- the age and state of health of the spouses;
- their qualifications and professional situations;
- the consequences of professional choices made by one of the spouses during the common life for the education of the children and the time that will still need to be devoted thereto or to promote the career of his or her spouse to the detriment of his or her own;
- the estimated or foreseeable patrimony of the spouses, both in capital and in income, after the liquidation of the matrimonial regime;
- their existing and foreseeable rights;
- their respective situations with regard to retirement pensions, having estimated, as far as possible, the reduction in retirement rights that may have been caused, for the spouse who is the creditor of the compensatory payment, by the circumstances referred to in the sixth paragraph.

###### Article 299

In the context of the determination of a compensatory payment, by the judge or by the parties, or on the occasion of an application for revision, the parties provide the judge with a declaration certifying on their honour the accuracy of their resources, income, patrimony and living conditions.

###### Article 300

The compensatory payment has a fixed character. It may not be revised even in the event of an unforeseen change in the resources or needs of the parties, unless the absence of revision would have consequences of exceptional gravity for one of the spouses.

###### Article 301

Where the substance of the assets of the spouse who is the debtor of the compensatory payment permits, the latter takes the form of a capital, the amount of which is fixed by the judge.

###### Article 302

The judge decides on the methods according to which the allocation or assignment of assets in capital will be executed:

1° Payment of a sum of money;

2° Abandonment of assets in kind, movable or immovable, but for the usufruct only, the judgment operating forced assignment in favour of the creditor;

3° Deposit of income-producing securities with a third party responsible for paying the income to the spouse who is the creditor of the payment until the fixed term.

The divorce judgment may be made subject to the actual payment of the capital or to the constitution of the guarantees provided for in Article 306.

###### Article 303

If the spouse who is the debtor of the compensatory payment does not have immediate liquidity, he or she may be authorized, under the guarantees provided for in Article 306, to constitute the capital in three annuities. In the absence of capital or if it is not sufficient, the compensatory payment takes the form of an annuity.

###### Article 304

Where the compensatory payment takes the form of an annuity, that annuity is awarded for a period equal to or less than the life of the creditor spouse.

The annuity is indexed; the index is determined as in matters of alimony.

The amount of the annuity before indexation is fixed uniformly for its entire duration or may vary by successive periods according to the probable evolution of resources and needs.

###### Article 305

At the death of the debtor spouse, the burden of the annuity passes to his or her heirs.

###### Article 306

Independently of the legal or judicial mortgage, the judge may require the debtor spouse to constitute a personal or real security to guarantee the annuity.

###### Article 307

In the event of a joint application, the spouses fix the amount and methods of the compensatory payment in the agreement which they submit for homologation by the judge.

The judge, however, refuses to homologate the agreement if it fixes the rights and obligations of the spouses inequitably.

###### Article 308

The homologated agreement has the same enforcement power as a judicial decision.

It may only be modified by a new agreement between the spouses, also subject to homologation.

The spouses nevertheless have the option of providing in their agreement that each of them may, in the event of an unforeseen change in his or her resources and needs, request the judge to revise the compensatory payment.

###### Article 309

The transfers and abandonments provided for in this paragraph are considered as participating in the matrimonial regime. They are not assimilated to donations.

###### Article 310

The spouse at whose exclusive fault the divorce is pronounced is not entitled to any compensatory payment. However, he or she may obtain compensation on an exceptional basis if, taking into account the duration of the common life and the collaboration provided to the profession of the other spouse, it appears manifestly contrary to equity to refuse him or her any pecuniary compensation following the divorce.

###### § 4. Du devoir de secours après le divorce

###### Article 311

When divorce is pronounced for breakdown of common life, the spouse who took the initiative for the divorce remains entirely bound by the duty of support.

In the case of Article 247, the duty of support covers everything necessary for the medical treatment of the sick spouse.

###### Article 312

The fulfilment of the duty of support takes the form of alimony. The latter may always be revised according to the resources and needs of each of the spouses.

###### Article 313

Alimony ceases automatically to be due if the spouse who is the creditor thereof enters into a new marriage.

It is terminated if the creditor lives in a state of notorious concubinage.

###### Article 314

At the death of the debtor spouse, the burden of the pension passes to his or her heirs.

###### Article 315

Where the substance of the assets of the debtor spouse lends itself thereto, the alimony is replaced, in whole or in part, by the constitution of a capital, according to the rules of Articles 301 to 303, first paragraph, and 309.

If this capital becomes insufficient to cover the needs of the creditor spouse, the latter may request a supplement in the form of alimony.

###### § 5. Du logement

###### Article 316

If the premises serving as dwelling for the family belong as separate property or personally to one of the spouses, the judge may grant a lease thereon to the other spouse:

1° Where custody of one or more children has been entrusted to the latter;

2° Where the divorce has been pronounced at the request of the owner spouse, for breakdown of common life.

In the case provided for in 1° above, the judge fixes the duration of the lease and may renew it until the majority of the youngest of the children.

In the case provided for in 2°, the lease may not be granted for a period exceeding nine years, but may be extended by a new decision. It terminates, automatically, in the event of remarriage of the person to whom it was granted. It is terminated if the latter lives in a state of notorious concubinage.

In all cases, the judge may terminate the lease if new circumstances justify it.

###### Section III : Des conséquences du divorce pour les enfants

###### Article 317

Divorce leaves subsisting the rights and duties of the father and mother towards their children, subject to the rules which follow.

###### Article 318

According to the interest of the minor children, their custody is entrusted to one or the other of the spouses.

On an exceptional basis and if the interest of the children so requires, this custody may be entrusted:

1° either to another person chosen preferably from among their relatives;

2° or, if this proves impossible, to an educational establishment or to an association recognized in this field.

###### Article 319

Before ruling on custody of the children, provisional or final, and on visitation rights, the judge may assign any qualified person to conduct a social investigation. The purpose of this investigation is to gather information on the material and moral situation of the family, on the conditions in which the children live and are educated, and on the measures that should be taken in their interest. If one of the spouses contests the conclusions of the social investigation, they may request a counter-investigation. The social investigation may not be used in the debate on the cause of divorce.

###### Article 320

The spouse to whom custody of the children has not been entrusted retains the right to supervise their maintenance and education. They contribute to it in proportion to their resources.

A right of visitation and accommodation may only be refused for serious reasons.

They may be charged with administering, under judicial supervision, all or part of the children's patrimony, notwithstanding articles 480 and 518 paragraph 2, if the interest of proper administration of this patrimony so requires.

###### Article 321

The judge rules on the attribution of custody and on the modalities of exercising parental authority, at the request of one of the spouses, a family member or the public prosecutor.

###### Article 322

The judge takes into account:

1° Agreements made between the spouses;

2° Information that has been gathered in the investigation and counter-investigation provided for in article 319;

3° Sentiments expressed by minor children when their hearing appeared necessary and when it does not involve disadvantages for them.

###### Article 323

Decisions relating to the exercise of parental authority may be modified or supplemented at any time by the judge, at the request of a spouse, a family member or the public prosecutor.

###### Article 324

In case of divorce by joint application, the provisions of the agreement approved by the judge relating to the exercise of parental authority may be revised, for serious reasons, at the request of one of the spouses or the public prosecutor.

###### Article 325

The contribution to the maintenance and education of the children provided for in article 320 takes the form of alimony paid to the person who has custody of them.

The modalities and guarantees of this alimony are fixed by the judgment or, in case of divorce by joint application, by the agreement of the spouses approved by the judge.

###### Article 326

When the composition of the debtor's assets so permits, the alimony may be replaced, in whole or in part, according to the rules of articles 301 to 303, first paragraph, and 309, by the payment of a sum of money into the hands of an accredited organization charged with granting in return to the child an indexed annuity, the transfer of property in usufruct or the allocation of income-producing property.

###### Article 327

If the capital thus constituted becomes insufficient to cover the needs of the children, the person who has custody may request the award of a supplement in the form of alimony.

###### Article 328

The parent who primarily assumes the care of adult children who cannot themselves provide for their needs may request their spouse to pay them a contribution to their maintenance and education.

##### Chapitre IV: Legal Separation

###### Section I: Cases and Procedure for Legal Separation

###### Article 329

Legal separation may be pronounced at the request of one of the spouses in the same cases and under the same conditions as divorce.

###### Article 330

The spouse against whom a divorce petition is presented may file a counterclaim for legal separation. However, when the main divorce petition is based on the definitive breakdown of the marital bond, the counterclaim may only seek divorce. The spouse against whom a petition for legal separation is presented may file a counterclaim for divorce.

###### Article 331

When a divorce petition and a petition for legal separation are concurrently presented, the judge examines the divorce petition first. They pronounce it as soon as the conditions are met. Failing that, they rule on the petition for legal separation.

However, when these petitions are based on fault, the judge examines them simultaneously and, if they grant them, pronounces divorce on shared fault with regard to both spouses.

###### Article 332

The rules contained in article 250 as well as in Chapter II above are applicable to the procedure for legal separation.

###### Section II: Consequences of Legal Separation

###### Article 333

Legal separation does not dissolve the marriage but it ends the duty of cohabitation.

###### Article 334

Legal separation allows each spouse who was using the other's name to retain this use for the future. However, the judgment of legal separation, or a subsequent judgment, may prohibit a spouse from retaining the use of their spouse's name.

###### Article 335

In case of death of one of the spouses legally separated, the other spouse retains the rights that the law grants to the surviving spouse. When legal separation is pronounced by mutual consent, the spouses may include in their agreement a waiver of the succession rights conferred on them by articles 858 et seq. and 872 et seq. of this code.

###### Article 336

Legal separation always entails separation of property.

With regard to property, the date on which legal separation produces its effects is determined in accordance with the provisions of articles 286 to 288.

###### Article 337

Legal separation leaves the duty of support subsisting; the judgment pronouncing it or a subsequent judgment fixes the alimony that is due to the spouse in need.

This alimony is awarded without consideration of fault. The debtor spouse may nevertheless invoke, if applicable, the provisions of article 215, paragraph 2.

This alimony is subject to the rules of maintenance obligations; the provisions of article 315 are however applicable to it.

###### Article 338

Subject to the provisions of this section, the consequences of legal separation are governed by the same rules as the consequences of divorce set out in Chapter III above.

###### Section III: End of Legal Separation

###### Article 339

The voluntary resumption of life together ends legal separation.

To be enforceable against third parties, this must either be recorded by notarial act or be the subject of a declaration to the civil registrar. Mention of it is made in the margin of the marriage certificate.

The separation of property subsists unless the spouses adopt a new matrimonial regime following the rules of article 1642.

###### Article 340

At the request of one of the spouses, the judgment of legal separation is converted by operation of law into a divorce judgment when the legal separation has lasted three years.

###### Article 341

In all cases of legal separation, it may be converted into divorce by a joint application.

When legal separation has been pronounced on joint application, it may only be converted into divorce by a new joint application.

###### Article 342

As a result of the conversion, the cause of the legal separation becomes the cause of the divorce; the attribution of fault is not modified.

The judge fixes the consequences of the divorce. Benefits and pensions between spouses are determined according to the rules specific to divorce.

###### Article 343

The wife may contract a new marriage as soon as the conversion decision has become res judicata.

##### Chapter V: Conflict of Laws Relating to Divorce and Legal Separation

###### Article 344

Divorce and legal separation are governed by Djiboutian law:

- when both spouses are of Djiboutian nationality;
- when both spouses have their domicile on Djiboutian territory;
- when no foreign law recognizes jurisdiction, while the Djiboutian courts have jurisdiction over the divorce or legal separation.

#### Title VIII: Filiation

Chapter I: Provisions Common to Legitimate Filiation and Natural Filiation

###### Section I: Presumptions Relating to Filiation

###### Article 345

The law presumes that the child was conceived during the period extending from the three hundredth to the one hundred eightieth day, inclusively, before the date of birth.

Conception is presumed to have occurred at any moment during this period, according to what is required in the interest of the child.

Proof to the contrary is admissible to rebut these presumptions.

###### Article 346

Possession of status is established by a sufficient combination of facts that indicate the relationship of filiation and kinship between an individual and the family to which he is said to belong.

Possession of status must be continuous.

###### Article 347

The principal of these facts are:

- that the individual has always borne the name of those from whom he is said to be descended;
- that they have treated him as their child, and that he has treated them as his father and mother;
- that they have, in this capacity, provided for his education, his maintenance and his establishment;
- that he is recognized as such, in society and by the family;
- that the public authority considers him as such.

###### Article 348

The parents or the child may request from the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance or from the judge designated for this purpose that there be issued to them, under the conditions provided for in Articles 106 and 107 of this code, an act of notoriety providing evidence of possession of status until proof to the contrary; this without prejudice to all other means of proof to which they could resort to establish its existence in court, if it were to be contested.

###### Section II: Actions Relating to Filiation

###### Article 349

No action is received regarding the filiation of a child who was not born viable.

###### Article 350

The Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance has sole jurisdiction over actions relating to filiation under the civil code. The Personal Status Court of First Instance has jurisdiction over disputes relating to personal status matters of persons governed by the family code.

###### Article 351

In the case of an offense affecting the filiation of an individual, the criminal action may not be decided until after the judgment has become res judicata on the question of filiation.

###### Article 352

Whenever they are not confined by law within shorter terms, actions relating to filiation are prescribed by thirty years from the day when the individual would have been deprived of the status he claims, or began to enjoy the status that is contested.

###### Article 353

The action that belonged to an individual regarding his filiation may only be exercised by his heirs in cases where that individual died as a minor or within five years after his majority or emancipation. His heirs may also pursue the action that he had already initiated, unless there has been a withdrawal or lapse of proceedings.

###### Article 354

Actions relating to filiation may not be the subject of waiver.

###### Article 355

Judgments rendered in matters of filiation are enforceable against any person, even those who were not parties to the proceedings; but persons who were not parties to the proceedings have the right to file third-party opposition against said judgments.

Judges may order on their own motion that all interested parties whom they consider should be bound by the judgment be joined in the case.

###### Article 356

Similarly, when, in one of the actions opened by Articles 418 and 436 below, a dismissal or a defense is raised based on the fact that the mother had, during the legal period of conception, relations with a third party, the judge may order that the latter be called into the case.

###### Article 357

The courts settle conflicts of filiation for which the law has not established another principle, by determining by all means of proof the most plausible filiation.

In the absence of sufficient elements of conviction, they have regard to possession of status.

###### Article 358

In the case where they are led to dismiss the claim of the party who was, in fact, taking care of the education of the minor child, the courts may, nevertheless, taking into account the interest of the child, grant that party a right of visitation.

###### Section III: Conflict of Laws Relating to the Establishment of Filiation

###### Article 359

Filiation is governed by the personal law of the mother on the day of the child's birth; if the mother is not known, by the personal law of the child.

###### Article 360

However, if the legitimate child and his father and mother, the natural child and one of his father or mother have in Djibouti their habitual residence, common or separate, possession of status produces all the consequences that follow from it under Djiboutian law, this even in the case where the other elements of filiation could have depended on a foreign law.

###### Article 361

Marriage entails legitimation when, on the day the union was celebrated, this consequence is admitted, either by the law governing the effects of marriage, or by the personal law of one of the spouses, or by the personal law of the child.

Legitimation by judicial authority is governed, at the choice of the applicant, either by his personal law, or by the personal law of the child.

###### Article 362

Voluntary recognition of paternity or maternity is valid if it was made in conformity with either the personal law of its author or the personal law of the child.

###### Article 363

The action for the purpose of support is governed, at the choice of the child, either by the law of his habitual residence or by the law of the habitual residence of the debtor.

##### Chapter II: Legitimate Filiation

###### Section I: Presumption of Paternity

###### Article 364

The child conceived or born during the marriage has the husband as father.

Nevertheless, he may disavow the child in court, if he provides facts proper to demonstrate that he cannot be the father.

###### Article 365

In the case of a judgment or even an application, either for divorce or for legal separation, the presumption of paternity does not apply to a child born more than three hundred days after the order authorizing the spouses to reside separately, and less than one hundred eighty days since the final rejection of the application or since the reconciliation.

The presumption of paternity recovers, nevertheless, by operation of law, its force:

1° If the child, with regard to the spouses, has possession of status of legitimate child and if he does not have paternal filiation already established with regard to a third party.

2° If, upon the application brought by each of the spouses before the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance during the minority of the child, proof is provided that the husband is indeed the father of the child. This action is also open to the child during the ten years following his majority.

###### Article 366

The presumption of paternity is set aside when the child, registered without indication of the husband's name, has possession of status only with regard to the mother.

###### Article 367

When the presumption of paternity is set aside under the conditions provided for in the preceding articles, the child's filiation is established with respect to the mother as if there had been a disavowal admitted in court. Either spouse may request that the effects of the presumption of paternity be restored, by showing that, during the legal period of conception, a factual reunion took place between them, which makes the husband's paternity plausible.

###### Article 368

A child born before the one hundred and eightieth day of marriage is legitimate and deemed to have been so from conception.

The husband, however, may disavow the child according to the rules of Article 312.

He may even disavow the child on the sole proof of the date of delivery, unless he knew of the pregnancy before the marriage, or unless he behaved as the father after the birth.

###### Article 369

The presumption of paternity is not applicable to a child born more than three hundred days after the dissolution of the marriage, nor, in case of declared absence of the husband, to one who is born to a married woman more than one year after the absence or death of her husband or the date of divorce.

###### Article 370

The husband must bring the action for disavowal within six months of the birth, when he is present at the location.

If he was not at the location, within six months of his return.

And within six months following the discovery of the fraud, if the birth of the child had been concealed from him.

###### Article 371

If the husband died before bringing the action, but still being within the useful time limit to do so, his heirs will have standing to contest the legitimacy of the child.

Their action, nevertheless, shall cease to be admissible when six months have elapsed from the time when the child took possession of the alleged paternal property, or from the time when they were disturbed by him in their own possession.

###### Article 372

Any extrajudicial act containing disavowal on the part of the husband or contestation of legitimacy on the part of the heirs, shall be deemed null and void, if it is not followed by a legal action within six months.

###### Article 373

The action for disavowal is directed, in the presence of the mother, against a guardian ad hoc, appointed to the child by the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance or by the judge designated for this purpose.

###### Article 374

Even in the absence of disavowal, the mother may contest the husband's paternity, but only for purposes of legitimation, when she has, after dissolution of the marriage, remarried the true father of the child.

###### Article 375

On pain of inadmissibility, the action, directed against the husband or his heirs, is joined to a petition for legitimation made in the terms of Article 390 below.

It must be brought by the mother and her new spouse within six months of their marriage and before the child has reached the age of seven years.

###### Article 376

Both petitions are decided by one and the same judgment, which may grant the contestation of paternity only if legitimation is admitted.

###### Section II: Proof of legitimate filiation

###### Article 377

The filiation of legitimate children is proved by birth certificates recorded in the civil status registers.

###### Article 378

In the absence of such title, possession of the status of legitimate child is sufficient.

###### Article 379

There is possession of the status of legitimate child only insofar as it connects the child indivisibly to his father and mother.

###### Article 380

No one may claim a status contrary to that given to him by his birth certificate and the possession consistent with that title.

And reciprocally, no one may contest the status of one who has possession consistent with his birth certificate.

###### Article 381

However, if it is alleged that there has been a false representation of a child, or substitution, even involuntary, either before or after the drafting of the birth certificate, proof thereof shall be admissible and may be made by any means.

###### Article 382

In the absence of title and possession of status, or if the child was registered, either under false names, or without indication of the mother's name, proof of filiation may be made by witnesses.

Proof by witnesses may not, nevertheless, be admitted unless there exists, either a beginning of proof in writing, or presumptions or indications serious enough to determine its admission.

###### Article 383

A beginning of proof in writing results from family documents, registers and domestic papers, as well as from all other public or private writings emanating from a party involved in the dispute or who would have an interest therein if alive.

###### Article 384

Contrary proof may be made by all means suitable to establish that the claimant is not the child of the mother he claims to have, or even, maternity being proved, that he is not the child of the mother's husband.

If the husband was not made a party to the status claim proceedings, he may contest his paternity within six months from the day he became aware of the judgment having become res judicata granting the child's petition.

###### Article 385

Without waiting for a status claim to be brought by the child, the husband may, by all means, contest his paternity within six months from the day he became aware of the birth.

###### Article 386

After the husband's death, his heirs shall likewise have the right to contest his paternity either preventively if the husband was still within the useful time limit to do so, or in defense to an action claiming status.

###### Article 387

The spouses, separately or jointly, may, by providing the proof provided for in Article 382 above, claim a child as being theirs; but if the child already has another established filiation, they must first demonstrate its inaccuracy, assuming that one is in one of the cases where the law authorizes this demonstration.

###### Section III: Legitimation

###### Article 388

Legitimation is the act by which a lawfully married couple confers upon a natural child the status of legitimate child.

Legitimation may benefit all natural children, as soon as, either by voluntary recognition or by judgment, their filiation has been legally established.

Legitimation takes place, either by marriage of the parents, or by authority of justice.

###### § 1. Legitimation by marriage

###### Article 389

All children born out of wedlock are legitimated by operation of law by the subsequent marriage of their father and mother.

If their filiation was not already established, these children are the subject of a recognition at the time of the celebration of the marriage. In this case, the civil status officer who performs the celebration records the recognition and legitimation in a separate act.

###### Article 390

When the filiation of a natural child has been established with respect to his father and mother or one of them only after their marriage, legitimation may take place only by virtue of a judgment. This judgment must establish that the child has had, since the celebration of the marriage, possession of the status of common child.

###### Article 391

Every legitimation is mentioned in the margin of the birth certificate of the legitimated child.

This mention may be requested by any interested party. In the case of Article 389, the civil status officer provides for it himself, if he has had knowledge of the existence of the children.

###### Article 392

Legitimation may take place after the child's death, if he left descendants; it then benefits them.

###### Article 393

Legitimation confers upon the legitimated child the rights and duties of the legitimate child.

It takes effect on the date of the marriage.

###### 82 §

2. Legitimation by authority of justice

###### Article 394

If it appears that marriage is impossible between the two parents, the benefit of legitimation may still be conferred upon the child by judicial authority provided that the child has, with respect to the parent who requests it, the possession of status of natural child.

###### Article 395

The application for legitimation is filed by one of the two parents or by both jointly before the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance.

###### Article 396

If one of the child's parents was, at the time of conception, bound by a marriage that has not been dissolved, his or her application is admissible only with the consent of his or her spouse.

###### Article 397

The Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance verifies whether the conditions of the law are met and, after having received or solicited, as the case may be, the observations of the child himself or herself, of the other parent when he or she is not a party to the application, as well as of the applicant's spouse, it grants, if it deems it justified, the legitimation.

###### Article 398

Legitimation by judicial authority takes effect on the date of the decision that definitively grants it. If it has taken place at the request of only one of the parents, it has no effect with respect to the other; it does not entail modification of the child's name, except by contrary decision of the Civil Chamber.

###### Article 399

If legitimation by judicial authority has been granted with respect to both parents, the child takes the father's name; if the child is a minor, a decision on his or her custody is made by the Civil Chamber, as in matters of divorce.

###### Article 400

The provisions of Articles 391 to 393, paragraph 1, are applicable to legitimation by judicial authority.

##### Chapitre III: Of natural filiation

###### Section I: Of the effects of natural filiation and its modes of establishment in general

###### Article 401

Every natural child falls under the regime of the civil code whenever his or her parents have expressed their will to subject this child to this regime at the time of the declaration of his or her birth to the civil registrar.

The parent who, alone, makes the declaration is deemed to act in agreement with the other for this purpose. The one who has not made the declaration has one month, from the declaration made to the civil registrar to contest its meaning. In case of disagreement between the two parents, the regime of the family code shall then be applicable to the child.

If the parents of this child give birth to one or more other common children, these shall be subject to the choice made for the first common child.

###### Article 402

The natural child has in principle the same rights and the same duties as the legitimate child in his or her relations with his or her father and mother.

He or she enters into the family of his or her parent.

###### Article 403

The natural child acquires the name of whichever of his or her two parents with respect to whom his or her filiation is established first; the name of his or her father, if the filiation is established simultaneously with respect to both.

###### Article 404

Even in the case where his or her filiation would have been established only secondly with respect to the father, the natural child may take the latter's name by substitution, if, during his or her minority, his or her two parents make a joint declaration before the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance or the judge delegated for this purpose.

If the child is over fifteen years old, his or her personal consent is necessary.

###### Article 405

In all other cases, the change of name of the natural child must be requested from the Court of First Instance.

The action is available during the child's minority and in the two years that will follow, either his or her majority, or a modification made to his or her status.

###### Article 406

The substitution of name extends by operation of law to the minor children of the person concerned. It extends to adult children only with their consent.

###### Article 407

In the absence of established paternal filiation, the mother's husband may confer, by substitution, his own name upon the child by a declaration that he will make jointly with the mother, under the conditions provided for in Article 404 above.

The child may however request to resume the name he or she bore previously by a request that he or she will submit to the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance, within two years following his or her majority.

###### Article 408

The rules for attribution of name provided for in the preceding articles do not prejudice the effects of possession of status.

###### Article 409

In the case provided for in the third paragraph of Article 401 above, the natural child may be raised at the matrimonial home only with the consent of his or her parent's spouse.

###### Article 410

Natural filiation is legally established, either by voluntary recognition, or by judicial declaration, following an action to establish paternity or maternity.

Natural filiation may also be legally established by the necessary effect of a judgment, notably following an action for disavowal or contestation of legitimacy.

###### Article 411

Any recognition is null and void, any request for establishment is inadmissible, when the child has a legitimate filiation already established by possession of status.

###### Article 412

If there exists between the father and mother of the natural child one of the impediments to marriage provided for by Articles 173 and 174 by reason of kinship, the filiation being already established with respect to one, it is prohibited to establish the filiation with respect to the other.

###### Section II: Of the recognition of natural children

###### Article 413

The recognition of a natural child shall be made by authentic act, when it has not been so made in the birth certificate.

###### Article 414

The father's recognition, without the indication and acknowledgment of the mother, has effect only with respect to the father.

###### Article 415

The birth certificate bearing the indication of the mother is deemed recognition, when it is corroborated by possession of status.

###### Article 416

As long as it has not been contested in court, a recognition renders inadmissible the establishment of another natural filiation that would contradict it.

###### Article 417

The recognition may be contested by all persons who have an interest therein, even by its author. The action is also available to the public prosecutor, if evidence drawn from the acts themselves renders the declared filiation implausible.

When there exists a possession of status consistent with the recognition and which has lasted at least ten years since the latter, no contestation is any longer admissible, except from the other parent, from the child himself or herself or from those who claim to be the true parents.

###### Section III: Of actions to establish paternity and maternity

###### Article 418

In the absence of title and possession of status, the establishment of maternity is admissible. The mother may however, at the time of delivery, request that the secrecy of her admission and her identity be preserved. The child who brings the action is required to prove that he or she is the one of whom the alleged mother gave birth. He or she may prove it by establishing that he or she has, with respect to the latter, the possession of status of natural child. Failing that, proof of filiation may be made by witnesses, if there exist either serious presumptions or evidence, or a beginning of proof in writing, within the meaning of Article 383.

###### Article 419

Paternity outside marriage may be judicially declared in the presence of established facts that render the filiation plausible.

###### Article 420

The action belongs only to the child.

The parent, even if a minor, in respect of whom filiation is established has, during the minority of the child, sole standing to exercise the action for search of maternity or paternity.

If no filiation link is established or if this parent is deceased or unable to manifest their will, the action is brought by the guardian in accordance with the provisions of Article 542, paragraph 2.

###### Article 421

The action for search of paternity is exercised against the alleged parent or against their heirs. In the absence of heirs or if they have renounced the succession, it is directed against the State. The renouncing heirs are called to the proceedings to assert their rights therein.
