###### Article 422

The action must, under penalty of forfeiture, be exercised within two years following the birth. However, when the alleged father and the mother have lived during the legal period of conception in a state of concubinage, implying, in the absence of a community of life, stable and continuous relations, or when the alleged father has provided for or participated in the maintenance, education or establishment of the child in the capacity of father, the action may be exercised until the expiration of two years following the cessation, either of the concubinage or of the acts of participation in the maintenance and education of the child. If it has not been exercised during the minority of the child, the child may still exercise it during the two years following their majority.

###### Article 423

When it grants the action, the court may, at the request of the mother, order the father to reimburse her all or part of her maternity and maintenance expenses during the three months preceding and the three months following the birth, without prejudice to the damages to which she could claim under Article 1391.

###### Article 424

The court rules, if appropriate, on the attribution of the name and on the exercise of parental authority, in accordance with Articles 405 and 486.

###### Article 425

In rejecting the application, the judges may, nevertheless, grant subsidy to the child, if the relations between the mother and the defendant have been demonstrated under the conditions provided for in Articles 426 and following.

###### Section IV: Of the action for subsidy

###### Article 426

Any natural child whose paternal filiation is not legally established may claim subsidy from the person who had relations with their mother during the legal period of conception. The action is admissible even if the father or the mother was at the time of conception bound by the ties of marriage with another person, or if there existed between them one of the impediments to marriage governed by Articles 173 to 176 of this code.

###### Article 427

The action for subsidy may also be exercised by the child of a married woman, if their status as a legitimate child is not corroborated by possession of status.

###### Article 428

The subsidy is determined, in the form of a pension, according to the needs of the child, the resources of the debtor, and their family situation.

The pension may be due beyond the majority of the child, if they are still in need, unless this state is attributable to their fault.

###### Article 429

When there is occasion for the application of Article 356 above, the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance, in the absence of other decision elements, has the power to charge the defendants with an indemnity intended to ensure the maintenance and education of the child, if faults are established against them, or if commitments have been previously made by them.

The president determines the time limit within which the indemnity must be paid to the legal representative of the child; in case of default of payment within the indicated time limit, the creditor may seize this judge by simple petition with a view to accompanying the conviction with a penalty which shall be, here, immediately final.

The provisions governing subsidies are, for the remainder, applicable to this indemnity.

###### Article 430

The defendant may dismiss the application by providing proof that they could not be the father of the child.

###### Article 431

The burden of subsidies is transmitted to the succession of the debtor within the limits of Articles 216 to 219.

###### Article 432

Articles 420 to 423 above are applicable to the action for subsidy.

###### Article 433

The judgment granting subsidy creates between the debtor and the beneficiary, as well as, where applicable, between each of them and the parents or spouse of the other, the impediments to marriage governed by Articles 161 to 164 of this code.

###### Article 434

The res judicata on the action for subsidy raises no bar to a subsequent action for search of paternity.

The grant of subsidy shall cease to have effect if the paternal filiation of the child comes to be subsequently established with respect to someone other than the debtor.

#### Title IX: Of adoptive filiation

Chapter I: Of full adoption

###### Section I: Of the conditions required for full adoption

###### Article 435

Adoption, under the regime established by the civil code, may be requested after five years of marriage by two spouses not legally separated.

###### Article 436

If the adopter is married and not legally separated, the consent of their spouse is necessary unless this spouse is unable to manifest their will.

###### Article 437

The adopters must be fifteen years older than the children they propose to adopt. If the latter are the children of their spouse, the required age difference is only ten years. However, the court may, if there are just grounds, grant the adoption when the age difference is less than those provided for in the preceding paragraph.

###### Article 438

Adoption is permitted only in favor of children under fifteen years of age, received into the home of the adopter or adopters for at least six months.

However, if the child is over fifteen years old and was received before reaching that age by persons who did not meet the legal conditions for adopting or if they were the subject of a simple adoption before reaching that age, full adoption may be requested, if the conditions are met, throughout the minority of the child.

If they are over thirteen years old, the adoptee must personally consent to their full adoption.

###### Article 439

No one may be adopted by several persons except by two spouses.

However, a new adoption may be granted either after the death of the adopter, or of both adopters, or even after the death of one of the two adopters, if the request is submitted by the new spouse of the survivor of them.

###### Article 440

May be adopted:

1° Children for whom the father and mother or the family council have validly consented to the adoption;

2° Children who have been legally entrusted to an association duly registered for at least five years at the date on which consent is given, whose statutory purpose includes the defense or assistance of the child and which effectively works in this field. This association must also be recognized by the Ministry of Justice, and communicate a copy of the ministerial order of recognition to the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance or to the judge delegated for this purpose.

3° Children declared abandoned under the conditions provided for in Article 448.

###### Article 441

When the filiation of a child is established with respect to their father and mother, both must consent to the adoption.

If one of the two is dead or unable to manifest their will, or has lost their parental authority rights, the consent of the other suffices.

###### Article 442

When the filiation of a child is established only with respect to one of its parents, the latter gives consent to the adoption.

###### Article 443

When the father and mother of the child are deceased, unable to express their will or if they have lost their parental authority rights, consent is given by the family council, after consultation with the person who, in fact, takes care of the child.

The same applies when the filiation of the child is not established.

###### Article 444

Consent to adoption is given before the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance or the judge delegated for this purpose of the domicile or residence of the person consenting, or before a Djiboutian or foreign notary, or before Djiboutian diplomatic or consular agents. It may also be received by an association regularly registered for at least five years from the date on which consent is given, whose statutory purpose includes the defense or assistance of children and which effectively works in this area. This association must furthermore be recognized by the Ministry of Justice, and communicate a copy of the ministerial order of recognition to the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance or to the judge delegated for this purpose.

Consent to adoption may be withdrawn within three months. The withdrawal must be made by any means allowing assurance of its receipt by the person or service that had received the consent to adoption. The return of the child to its parents upon request, even verbal, also constitutes proof of withdrawal.

If upon expiration of the three-month period, the consent has not been withdrawn, the parents may still request the return of the child provided that the child has not been placed for adoption. If the person who has taken in the child refuses to return it, the parents may seize the court which assesses, taking into account the interest of the child, whether it is appropriate to order its return. The return renders the consent to adoption null and void.

###### Article 445

The father and mother or the family council may consent to the adoption of the child by leaving the choice of the adopter to an association as designated in article 444 or to an authorized adoption organization which would temporarily take in the child.

###### Article 446

Except in the case where there is a relationship of kinship or affinity up to and including the sixth degree between the adopter and the adopted person, consent to the adoption of children under two years of age is valid only if the child has been effectively handed over to an association as designated in article 444 or to an authorized adoption organization.

###### Article 447

The Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance may pronounce the adoption if it deems abusive the refusal of consent opposed by the legitimate and natural parents or by only one of them, when they have shown disinterest in the child at the risk of compromising its health or morality. The same applies in case of abusive refusal of consent by the family council.

###### Article 448

A child taken in by an individual, a private organization or an association as designated in article 444, whose parents have manifestly shown disinterest during the year preceding the filing of the application for declaration of abandonment, may be declared abandoned by the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance.

Parents who have not maintained with the child the relations necessary for maintaining emotional ties are considered to have manifestly shown disinterest in their child.

The simple withdrawal of consent to adoption, the request for news or the expressed but ineffective intention to take back the child, is not a sufficient mark of interest to automatically justify the rejection of an application for declaration of abandonment.

Abandonment is not declared if, during the period provided for in the first paragraph of this article, a family member has requested to assume responsibility for the child and if this request is deemed to be in the latter's interest.

When it declares the child abandoned, the court delegates by the same decision the parental authority rights over the child to an association as designated in article 444 or to the individual guardian of the child.

Third-party opposition is admissible only in case of deceit, fraud or error regarding the identity of the child.

###### Section II : On placement for full adoption and the judgment of full adoption

###### Article 449

Placement for adoption is achieved by the effective delivery to the future adopters of a child for whom valid and final consent to adoption has been given, or of a child declared abandoned by judicial decision.

When the filiation of the child is not established, there may be no placement for adoption during a period of three months from the taking in of the child.

Placement may not take place when the parents have requested the return of the child as long as no decision has been made on the merits of this request at the petition of the most diligent party.

###### Article 450

Placement for adoption precludes any return of the child to its family of origin. It prevents any declaration of filiation and any acknowledgment.

If the placement for adoption ceases or if the court has refused to pronounce the adoption, the effects of this placement are retroactively dissolved.

###### Article 451

The adoption is pronounced at the request of the adopter by the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance, which verifies whether the conditions of the law are met and whether the adoption is in the interest of the child.

In the case where the adopter has descendants, the court further verifies whether the adoption is not of a nature to compromise family life.

If the adopter dies after having lawfully taken in the child for adoption, the request may be presented in their name by the surviving spouse or one of the heirs of the adopter.

The judgment pronouncing the adoption is not reasoned.

###### Article 452

Third-party opposition against the adoption judgment is admissible only in case of deceit or fraud attributable to the adopters.

###### Article 453

Within fifteen days of the date on which it becomes final, the decision pronouncing full adoption is transcribed on the civil status registers of the place of birth of the adopted person, at the request of the public prosecutor.

The transcription states the day, hour and place of birth, the sex of the child as well as their given names, as they result from the adoption judgment, the given names, surnames, date and place of birth, profession and domicile of the adopter or adopters. It contains no indication relating to the actual filiation of the child.

The transcription serves as a birth certificate for the adopted person.

The original birth certificate and, where applicable, the birth certificate established pursuant to article 89 are, at the initiative of the public prosecutor, endorsed with the notation adoption and considered null and void.

###### Section III : On the effects of full adoption

###### Article 454

The adoption produces its effects from the day of filing the application for adoption.

###### Article 455

The adoption confers on the child a filiation that replaces their original filiation: the adopted person ceases to belong to their family by blood, subject to the prohibitions on marriage referred to in articles 161 to 164.

However, the adoption of the child of a spouse leaves intact their original filiation with respect to that spouse and their family. It produces, for the remainder, the effects of an adoption by two spouses.

###### Article 456

Adoption confers upon the child the name of the adopter and, in case of adoption by two spouses, the husband's name. Upon request of the adopter(s), the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance may modify the first names of the child.

If the adopter is a married woman, the Civil Chamber may, in the adoption judgment, deduce from the consent of the adopter's husband that the latter's name shall be conferred upon the adopted child; if the husband is deceased or unable to express his will, the court shall assess sovereignly after consulting the husband's heirs or his nearest successors.

###### Article 457

The adopted child has, in the adopter's family, the same rights and the same obligations as a legitimate child.

###### Article 458

Adoption is irrevocable.

##### Chapitre II : De l'adoption simple

###### Section I : Des conditions requises et du jugement

###### Article 459

Simple adoption is permitted regardless of the age of the adopted person.

If the adopted person is over fifteen years of age, he must personally consent to the adoption.

###### Article 460

The provisions of articles 435 to 437, 439 to 448, 451, 452, 454 and 456, last paragraph, are applicable to simple adoption.

###### Article 461

Within fifteen days from the date on which it becomes res judicata, the decision pronouncing simple adoption shall be noted or transcribed in the civil status registers at the request of the public prosecutor.

###### Section II : Des effets de l'adoption simple

###### Article 462

Simple adoption confers the adopter's name upon the adopted person by adding it to the latter's name. The court may however decide that the adopted person shall bear only the adopter's name.

###### Article 463

The adopted person remains in his family of origin and retains all his rights therein, notably his inheritance rights. The prohibitions on marriage provided for in articles 173 to 176 of this code apply between the adopted person and his family of origin.

###### Article 464

The adopter alone is vested with regard to the adopted person with all parental authority rights, including that of consenting to the marriage of the adopted person, unless he is the spouse of the father or mother of the adopted person; in this case, the adopter has parental authority concurrently with his spouse, but the latter retains its exercise.

Parental authority rights are exercised by the adopter(s) under the same conditions as with regard to a legitimate child.

The rules of legal administration and guardianship of a legitimate child apply to the adopted person.

###### Article 465

The kinship tie resulting from adoption extends to the legitimate children of the adopted person.

Marriage is prohibited:

1° Between the adopter, the adopted person and his descendants;

2° Between the adopted person and the spouse of the adopter; reciprocally between the adopter and the spouse of the adopted person; 3° Between the adoptive children of the same individual;

4° Between the adopted person and the children of the adopter.

Nevertheless, the prohibitions on marriage set forth in 3° and 4° above may be lifted by dispensation of the President of the Republic, if there are serious causes.

The prohibition on marriage set forth in 2° above may be lifted under the same conditions when the person who created the affinity is deceased.

###### Article 466

The adopted person owes support to the adopter if the latter is in need and, reciprocally, the adopter owes support to the adopted person.

The obligation to provide support continues to exist between the adopted person and his father and mother. However, the father and mother of the adopted person are only required to provide him with support if he cannot obtain it from the adopter.

###### Article 467

The adopted person and his legitimate descendants have in the adopter's family the same succession rights as a legitimate child without however acquiring the status of forced heir with regard to the adopter's ascendants.

###### Article 468

If the adopted person dies without descendants, the property given by the adopter or received in his succession shall return to the adopter or his descendants, if they still exist in kind at the time of the adopted person's death, subject to contributing to debts and without prejudice to rights acquired by third parties. Property that the adopted person had received gratuitously from his father and mother shall likewise return to the latter or to their descendants. The remainder of the adopted person's property shall be divided in half between the family of origin and the adopter's family, without prejudice to the rights of the spouse over the entire succession.

###### Article 469

Adoption retains all its effects, notwithstanding the subsequent establishment of a filiation link.

###### Article 470

If serious grounds are established, adoption may be revoked, at the request of the adopter or the adopted person.

The revocation request made by the adopter is only admissible if the adopted person is over fifteen years of age.

When the adopted person is a minor, the parents by blood or, failing them, a member of the family of origin up to and including the fourth degree, may also request revocation.

###### Article 471

The judgment revoking adoption must be reasoned.

The operative part of the judgment shall be noted in the margin of the birth certificate or of the transcription of the adoption judgment, under the conditions provided for in article 461.

###### Article 472

Revocation terminates all effects of adoption for the future.

#### Titre X : De l'autorité parentale

Chapitre Ier : De l'autorité parentale relativement à la personne de l'enfant

###### Article 473

The child, at any age, owes honor and respect to his father and mother.

###### Article 474

He remains under their authority until his majority or emancipation.

###### Article 475

Authority belongs to the father and mother to protect the child in his safety, health and morality.

They have with regard to him the right and duty of custody, supervision and education.

###### Article 476

The child may not, without permission of the father and mother, leave the family home and he may not be removed from it except in cases of necessity determined by law.

###### Article 477

The father and mother may not, except for serious reasons, obstruct the child's personal relations with his grandparents. In the absence of agreement between the parties, the modalities of these relations are determined by the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance.

In consideration of exceptional situations, the Civil Chamber may grant a right of correspondence or visitation to other persons, whether related or not.

###### Section I : De l'exercice de l'autorité parentale

###### Article 478

During marriage, the father and mother exercise their authority jointly.

###### Article 479

If the father and mother cannot agree on what the child's interest requires, the practice they may have previously followed in similar circumstances shall serve as their rule.

In the absence of such practice or in case of dispute as to its existence or its validity, the most diligent spouse may seize the president of the Court of First Instance or the judge he delegates for this purpose, who shall rule after having attempted to reconcile the parties.

###### Article 480

With regard to third parties in good faith, each spouse is deemed to act with the agreement of the other, when he alone performs a routine act of parental authority relating to the person of the child.

###### Article 481

Loses the exercise of parental authority or is temporarily deprived thereof the parent who is in one of the following cases:

1° If he is unable to manifest his will, by reason of his incapacity, his absence, his remoteness or any other cause;

2° If he has consented to a delegation of his rights according to the rules established in section III of this chapter;

3° If he has been convicted under one of the various counts of family abandonment, as long as he has not resumed assuming his obligations for a period of at least six months;

4° If a judgment of forfeiture or withdrawal has been pronounced against him, for those of his rights which have been withdrawn from him.

###### Article 482

If one of the parents dies or is in one of the cases enumerated by the preceding article, the exercise of parental authority is devolved entirely to the other.

###### Article 483

If the parents are divorced or legally separated, parental authority is exercised by the one to whom the court has entrusted custody of the child, subject to the right of visitation and supervision of the other. When custody has been entrusted to a third party, the other attributes of parental authority continue to be exercised by the parents. But the court, in designating a third party as provisional guardian, may decide that he must request the opening of a guardianship.

When ruling, the judge always does so taking into consideration the best interest of the child.

###### Article 484

Divorce or legal separation does not prevent the devolution provided for in article 482, even when the parent who remains able to exercise parental authority has been deprived of custody by the effect of the judgment pronounced against him.

Nevertheless, the Civil Chamber which had last ruled on custody may always be seized by the family or by the public prosecutor, in order to designate a third party as guardian of the child, with or without opening of a guardianship, as stated in the preceding article.

In exceptional circumstances, the Civil Chamber which rules on custody of the child after divorce or legal separation may decide, even during the lifetime of the spouses, that it will not pass to the survivor in case of death of the custodial spouse. It may, in that case, designate the person to whom custody will be provisionally devolved.

###### Article 485

If there remains neither father nor mother able to exercise parental authority, there shall be grounds for the opening of a guardianship.

###### Article 486

Concerning the natural child, parental authority is exercised by the parent who has voluntarily recognized him, if he has been recognized by only one of them.

If both have recognized him, parental authority is exercised entirely by the mother. The court may, nevertheless, at the request of either, or of the public prosecutor, decide that it will be exercised either by the father alone, or by the father and mother jointly, to whom articles 478 to 480 will then be applicable, as if the child were a legitimate child.

###### Section II: Educational Assistance

###### Article 487

If the health, safety or morality of an unemancipated minor are in danger, or if the conditions of his education are seriously compromised, educational assistance measures may be ordered by the court at the request of the parents jointly, or of one of them, of the guardian or tutor, of the minor himself or of the public prosecutor. The judge may seize the matter of his own motion on an exceptional basis. These educational assistance measures may be ordered at the same time for several children under the same parental authority.

###### Article 488

The president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance, or the judge he delegates for this purpose, has jurisdiction, subject to appeal, for all matters concerning educational assistance.

The president or the delegated judge must always endeavor to obtain the family's agreement to the measure contemplated.

###### Article 489

Whenever possible, the minor must be kept in his current environment. In this case, the judge designates either a qualified person or an association as designated in article 444, giving the designated person or association the mission of providing assistance and advice to the family, in order to overcome the material or moral difficulties it encounters. This person or association is responsible for monitoring the child's development and reporting on it to the judge periodically. The president of the Civil Chamber or the delegated judge may also make the child's continued presence in his environment subject to particular obligations, such as that of regularly attending an educational establishment, or of pursuing a professional activity.

###### Article 490

If it is necessary to remove the child from his current environment, the president of the Civil Chamber or the delegated judge may decide to entrust him:

1° To the parent who did not have custody;

2° To another family member or to a trustworthy third party;

3° To an association as designated in article 444.

However, when a petition for divorce has been filed or a divorce judgment rendered between the parents, these measures may only be taken if a new fact likely to cause danger to the minor has come to light after the decision ruling on custody of the child. They may not prevent the president of the Civil Chamber or the delegated judge from deciding, by application of article 302, to whom the child must be entrusted. The same rules apply to legal separation.

###### Article 491

In the cases specified in 1° and 2° of the preceding article, the president of the Civil Chamber or the delegated judge may instruct a qualified person, an association as designated in article 444, or an observation, education or re-education service in an open environment, to provide assistance and advice to the guardian as well as to the family and to monitor the child's development.

In all cases, the president of the Civil Chamber or the delegated judge may accompany the return of the child with the same modalities as under article 489, paragraph 2. He may also decide that he will be given periodic reports on the child's situation.

###### Article 492

On a provisional basis but subject to appeal, the president of the Civil Chamber or the delegated judge may, during the proceedings, take one of the measures provided for in articles 490 and 491.

In case of urgency, the public prosecutor of the place where the minor was found has the same power, subject to seizing within eight days the president of the Civil Chamber, who will maintain, modify or rescind the measure.

###### Article 493

Decisions made in matters of educational assistance may be, at any time, modified or rescinded by the judge who rendered them either of his own motion, or at the request of the parents jointly, or of one of them, of the guardian or tutor, of the minor himself or of the public prosecutor.

###### Article 494

The parents whose child has given rise to an educational assistance measure retain their parental authority over him and exercise all the attributes thereof which are not incompatible with the application of the measure. They may not emancipate the child without authorization from the children's judge, as long as the educational assistance measure is being applied.

If it has been necessary to place the child outside his parents' home, they retain a right of correspondence and a right of visitation. The judge sets the terms thereof and may, if the child's interest requires it, decide that the exercise of these rights, or of one of them, will be temporarily suspended.

###### Article 495

The costs of maintenance and education of the child who has been the subject of an educational assistance measure continue to be borne by their father and mother as well as by the ascendants from whom support may be claimed, except for the power of the judge to discharge them in whole or in part.

###### Section III : Delegation of Parental Authority

###### Article 496

No renunciation, no assignment relating to parental authority, may have effect, except by virtue of a judgment and in the cases determined below.

###### Article 497

The Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance may, when it is called upon to rule on the custody or education of a minor child, have regard to the agreements that the father and mother have been able to freely conclude between them on this subject, unless one of them justifies serious grounds that would authorize them to revoke their consent.

###### Article 498

The father and mother, together or separately, or the guardian authorized by the family council, may, when they have entrusted a minor child under sixteen years of age to a trustworthy individual or to an establishment approved for this purpose, or an association as designated in Article 444, renounce in whole or in part the exercise of their authority.

In this case, delegation, total or partial, of parental authority will result from the judgment that will be rendered by the Civil Chamber on the joint application of the delegators and the delegatee.

The same delegation may be decided, on the sole application of the delegatee, when the parents have shown no interest in the child for more than one year.

###### Article 499

The delegation of parental authority may also take place when the minor under sixteen years of age has been taken in without the intervention of the father and mother or the guardian. But it is necessary, in this case, that the individual, establishment or association, after having taken in the child, has made a declaration to the administrative authority of the place. This declaration is made within eight days. The administrative authority, within the following month, gives notice to the father and mother or to the guardian. The notification thus made to them opens a new period of three months at the expiration of which, failing by them to claim the child, they are presumed to renounce exercising their authority over him.

The individual, establishment or association that has taken in the child may then present an application to the Civil Chamber for the purpose of having parental authority delegated to them totally or partially.

###### Article 500

The delegation may, in all cases, end or be transferred by a new judgment, if new circumstances are justified.

In the case where the return of the child is granted to the father and mother, the Civil Chamber charges them, if they are not indigent, with the reimbursement of all or part of the maintenance costs. When the application for return has been rejected, it may not be renewed until after six months from the day the decision of rejection has become irrevocable.

###### Article 501

The right to consent to the adoption of the minor is never delegated.

###### Section IV : Forfeiture and Partial Withdrawal of Parental Authority

###### Article 502

May be deprived of parental authority by an express provision of the criminal judgment the father and mother who are convicted, either as perpetrators, co-perpetrators or accomplices of a crime or offense committed against the person of their child, or as co-perpetrators or accomplices of a crime or offense committed by their child.

This forfeiture is applicable to ascendants other than the father and mother for the share of parental authority that may fall to them over their descendants.

###### Article 503

May be deprived of parental authority, outside of any criminal conviction, the father and mother who, either through ill-treatment, or through harmful examples of habitual drunkenness, notorious misconduct or delinquency, or through lack of care or lack of direction, manifestly endanger the safety, health or morality of the child.

May likewise be deprived of it, when an educational assistance measure had been taken with regard to the child, the father and mother who, for more than two years, have voluntarily refrained from exercising the rights and fulfilling the duties that Article 494 left them.

The action for forfeiture is brought before the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance, either by the public prosecutor, or by a member of the family or the guardian of the child.

###### Article 504

The forfeiture pronounced by virtue of one of the two preceding articles extends by operation of law to all attributes, both patrimonial and personal, relating to parental authority; in the absence of other determination, it extends to all minor children already born at the time of the judgment.

It entails, for the child, exemption from the maintenance obligation, by derogation from Articles 212 to 214, unless otherwise provided in the judgment of forfeiture.

###### Article 505

The judgment may, instead of total forfeiture, limit itself to pronouncing a partial withdrawal of rights, limited to the attributes it specifies. It may also decide that the forfeiture or withdrawal will only have effect with regard to certain of the children already born.

###### Article 506

In pronouncing the forfeiture or withdrawal of the right of custody, the court seised must, if the other parent is deceased or if they have lost the exercise of parental authority, either designate a third party who will provisionally assume custody of the child with the responsibility of requesting the organization of guardianship, or entrust the child to an association as designated in Article 444.

The court seised may take the same measures when parental authority is devolved to one of the parents by the effect of the forfeiture pronounced against the other.

###### Article 507

The father and mother who have been subject to a forfeiture or withdrawal of rights for one of the causes provided for in Articles 502 and 503, may, by application, obtain from the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance, by justifying new circumstances, that the rights of which they had been deprived be restored to them, in whole or in part.

The application for restitution may be made only after six months from the day the judgment pronouncing the forfeiture or withdrawal has become irrevocable; in case of rejection, this application may be renewed only after a new period of one year. No application will be admissible when, before the filing of the application, the child has been placed with a view to adoption.

If restitution is granted, the public prosecutor will request, if necessary, educational assistance measures.

##### Chapitre II : Parental Authority Relating to the Child's Property

###### Article 508

The father and mother have, under the distinctions that follow, the administration and enjoyment of their child's property.

###### Article 509

Legal administration is exercised in accordance with the provisions of Articles 518 and following of this code.

###### Article 510

The right of enjoyment ceases:

1° As soon as the child has completed sixteen years of age, or even earlier when they contract marriage;

2° By the causes that terminate parental authority, or even more specifically by those that terminate legal administration;

3° By the causes that entail the extinction of any usufruct.

###### Article 511

The burdens of this enjoyment are:

1° Those to which usufructuaries are generally bound;

2° The food, maintenance and education of the child, according to their fortune;

3° The debts encumbering the estate inherited by the child insofar as they should have been paid from the income.

###### Article 512

This enjoyment will not take place for the benefit of the surviving spouse who has omitted to make an inventory, authentic or under private signature, of the property devolved to the minor.

###### Article 513

Legal enjoyment does not extend to property that the child may acquire through his or her work, nor to property given or bequeathed to him or her on the express condition that the father and mother shall not enjoy it.

#### Titre XI: On Minority, Guardianship and Emancipation

###### Article 514

In this title, whenever reference is made to the judge, it refers to the president of the Court of First Instance or the magistrate whom he or she has designated.

Chapitre Ier: On Minority

###### Article 515

A minor is an individual of either sex who has not yet reached the age of eighteen years.

###### Article 516

In any proceeding concerning him or her, the minor capable of discernment may, without prejudice to provisions requiring his or her intervention or consent, be heard by the judge or, when his or her interest so requires, by the person designated by the judge for that purpose.

This hearing is a right when the minor requests it. When the minor refuses to be heard, the judge assesses the merits of this refusal. He or she may be heard alone, with a lawyer or a person of his or her choice.

###### Article 517

The legal administrator represents the minor in all acts of civil life, except in cases where the law or custom authorizes minors to act themselves.

##### Chapitre II: On Legal Administration

###### Article 518

Legal administration belongs to the parents.

If parental authority is exercised jointly by both parents, each of them is a legal administrator. In other cases, legal administration belongs to the parent who exercises parental authority.

###### Article 519

When legal administration is exercised jointly by both parents, each of them is deemed, with respect to third parties, to have received from the other the power to perform alone acts of administration relating to the property of the minor.

The list of acts that are regarded as acts of administration is defined by presidential decree.

###### Article 520

When the interests of the sole legal administrator or, as the case may be, of both legal administrators are in conflict with those of the minor, the latter request the appointment of an ad hoc administrator by the judge. In the absence of diligence by the legal administrators, the judge may proceed with this appointment at the request of the public prosecutor, the minor himself or herself, or ex officio.

When the interests of one of the two legal administrators are in conflict with those of the minor, the judge may authorize the other legal administrator to represent the child for one or more specified acts.

###### Article 521

Property given or bequeathed to the minor on condition that it be administered by a third party is not subject to legal administration.

The third-party administrator has the powers conferred upon him or her by the gift, the will or, failing that, those of a legal administrator.

When the third-party administrator refuses this function or is legally unable to exercise it, the judge designates an ad hoc administrator to replace him or her.

###### Article 522

The legal administrator is required to exercise prudent, diligent and informed care in the management of the minor's property, solely in the interest of the minor.

###### Article 523

The legal administrator is liable for any damage resulting from any fault he or she commits in the management of the minor's property.

If legal administration is exercised jointly, both parents are jointly and severally liable. The action for liability is prescribed after five years from the majority of the person concerned or from his or her emancipation.

##### Chapitre III: On Guardianship

###### Section I: On Cases of Opening and Termination of Guardianship

###### Article 524

Guardianship opens when the father and mother are both deceased or are deprived of the exercise of parental authority.

It also opens with respect to a child whose filiation is not legally established.

###### Article 525

In case of legal administration, the judge may, at any time and for serious cause, either ex officio or at the request of relatives or in-laws or the public prosecutor, decide to open guardianship after having heard or summoned, except in cases of urgency, the legal administrator. The latter may not perform any act of disposition from the day he or she is informed of the request until the final judgment except in case of urgency. If guardianship is opened, the judge convenes the family council, which may either appoint the legal administrator as guardian or designate another guardian.

###### Article 526

If a child is recognized by one of his or her two parents after the opening of guardianship, the judge may, at the request of that parent, decide to substitute legal administration for guardianship.

###### Article 527

Without prejudice to the provisions of article 526, guardianship ends upon the emancipation of the minor or upon his or her majority. It also ends in case of a judgment of discharge having become res judicata or in case of death of the person concerned.

###### Section II: On the Organization and Operation of Guardianship

###### § 1. On Guardianship Duties

###### Article 528

Guardianship, protection owed to the child, is a public duty. It is a duty of families and the public community.

###### Article 529

The following may not exercise the various guardianship duties:

1° Unemancipated minors, unless they are the father or mother of the minor under guardianship 2° Adults who benefit from a legal protection measure provided for by this code; 3° Persons from whom parental authority has been withdrawn;

4° Persons who have been prohibited from exercising guardianship duties by court decision.

###### Article 530

Any guardianship duty may be withdrawn by reason of the incapacity, negligence, misconduct or fraud of the person to whom it has been entrusted. The same applies when a dispute or conflict of interest prevents the holder of the duty from exercising it in the interest of the minor.

Any person to whom a guardianship duty has been entrusted may be replaced in case of significant change in his or her situation or in that of the minor.

###### Article 531

The family council rules on impediments, withdrawals and replacements concerning the guardian.

The judge rules on those concerning the other members of the family council.

A guardianship duty may only be withdrawn, by the person who entrusted it, after its holder has been heard or summoned.

The judge may, if he or she considers that there is urgency, order provisional measures in the interest of the minor.

###### § 2. On the Family Council

###### Article 532

Even in the presence of a testamentary guardian and except in case of vacancy, guardianship is organized with a family council.

###### Article 533

The judge designates the members of the family council for the duration of the guardianship.

The family council is composed of at least four members, including the guardian. The judge is not included in this number.

The relatives and in-laws of the father and mother of the minor as well as any person, residing in Djibouti or abroad, who shows an interest in him or her may be members of the family council.

The members of the family council are chosen in consideration of the interest of the minor and according to their aptitude, the usual relations they maintained with the father or mother of the minor, the emotional ties they have with him or her as well as the availability they present.

The judge must avoid, as far as possible, leaving one of the two branches, paternal or maternal, without representation.

###### Article 534

The family council is presided over by the judge. Its deliberations are adopted by vote of its members.

However, the guardian does not vote.

In case of a tie vote, the judge's vote is decisive.

###### Article 535

The family council regulates the general conditions for the maintenance and education of the minor, having regard to the wishes that the father and mother may have expressed.

It assesses the allowances that may be granted to the guardian.

It makes decisions and gives the guardian the necessary authorizations for the management of the minor's property in accordance with the provisions of Title XIII of this code.

###### Article 536

The deliberations of the family council are null when they have been obtained by deceit or fraud or when substantial formalities have been omitted.

The action for nullity may be brought by the guardian, the other members of the family council and the Public Prosecutor within two years of the deliberation as well as by the minor who has reached majority or been emancipated within two years of his majority or his emancipation. The prescription does not run if there has been deceit or fraud as long as the fact that is at its origin has not been discovered.

Acts performed pursuant to an annulled deliberation are annulled upon simple request of one of the persons who may act pursuant to the preceding paragraph. The time limit runs, however, from the act and not from the deliberation.

###### § 3. Of the guardian

###### Article 537

The individual right to choose a guardian, whether or not related to the minor, belongs only to the last survivor of the father and mother if he or she has retained, on the day of his or her death, the exercise of parental authority. This designation may only be made in the form of a will or a special declaration before a notary.

It is binding on the family council unless the interest of the minor requires that it be set aside. In that case, the family council decides to refer the matter to the judge, who shall assess it.

The guardian designated by the father or mother is not required to accept the guardianship.

###### Article 538

If there is no testamentary guardian, or if the one who was designated in that capacity ceases his functions, or refuses the guardianship, the family council designates a guardian for the minor.

###### Article 539

The family council may, in consideration of the situation of the minor, the abilities of the interested parties and the composition of the estate to be administered, designate several guardians to exercise the protective measure jointly. Each guardian is deemed, with regard to third parties, to have received from the others the power to act alone for acts for which a guardian would not need any authorization.

The family council may decide that the exercise of guardianship will be divided between a guardian responsible for the person of the minor and a guardian responsible for the management of his property. Unless otherwise decided by the family council, these guardians are independent of each other, and are not responsible to each other. They nevertheless inform each other of the decisions they make

###### Article 540

The guardian is designated for the duration of the guardianship.

###### Article 541

Guardianship is a personal charge.

It is not transmitted to the heirs of the guardian.

###### Article 542

The guardian takes care of the person of the minor and represents him in all acts of civil life, except in cases where the law or custom authorizes the minor to act himself.

The guardian represents the minor in legal proceedings. However, he may not act, as plaintiff or defendant, to assert non-patrimonial rights except after authorization or upon injunction of the family council. The family council may also enjoin the guardian to withdraw from the proceedings or action, or to settle.

The guardian manages the property of the minor and accounts for his management in accordance with the provisions of Title

XIII.

###### § 4. Of the vacancy of guardianship

###### Article 543

The President of the Court of First Instance and the Public Prosecutor exercise general supervision over guardianships within their jurisdiction.

Guardians and other guardianship bodies are required to comply with their summons and to communicate to them any information they require.

The judge may issue injunctions against them and sentence to a civil fine of 50,000 to 200,000 FD those who have not complied.

###### § 5. Of liability

###### Article 544

All guardianship bodies are liable for damage resulting from any fault they commit in the exercise of their function.

When the fault at the origin of the damage was committed in the organization and operation of the guardianship by the judges or the court clerk, the action for liability is directed against the State, which has a right of recourse.

###### Article 545

The action for liability is prescribed after five years from the majority of the interested party, even if the management continued beyond, or from the end of the measure if it ceases before.

##### Chapter IV: Of emancipation

###### Article 546

The minor is emancipated by operation of law through marriage.

###### Article 547

The minor, even if not married, may be emancipated when he has reached the age of sixteen years. After hearing the minor, this emancipation shall be pronounced, if there are just grounds, by the judge, at the request of the father and mother or one of them.

When the request is made by only one of the parents, the judge decides, after hearing the other parent unless the latter is unable to express his will.

###### Article 548

The minor left without father or mother may be emancipated at the request of the family council, convened by the guardian or by the court at the request of a member of the family council or of the minor himself. Paragraphs 2 and 3 of Article 547 are then applicable.

###### Article 549

The account of the administration, if applicable, or of the guardianship is rendered to the emancipated minor in accordance with the provisions of Title XIII.

###### Article 550

The emancipated minor is capable, like an adult, of all acts of civil life.

He must nevertheless, to marry or give himself in adoption, observe the same rules as if he were not emancipated.

###### Article 551

The emancipated minor ceases to be under the authority of his father and mother.

They are not liable by operation of law, in their sole capacity as father or mother, for damage he may cause to others after his emancipation.

###### Article 552

The emancipated minor may not be a merchant.

#### Title XII: Of majority and adults protected by law

Chapter I: General provisions

###### Article 553

The age of majority is fixed at eighteen years completed; at that age, everyone is capable of exercising the rights of which he has enjoyment.

###### Section I: Of provisions independent of protective measures

###### Article 554

To make a valid act, one must be of sound mind. It is for those who seek nullity on this ground to prove the existence of a mental disorder at the time of the act.

###### Article 555

During his lifetime, the action for nullity belongs only to the interested party.

After his death, acts made by him, other than inter vivos donations and wills, may not be challenged by his heirs, for unsoundness of mind, except in the following cases:

1° If the act bears in itself proof of a mental disorder;

2° If it was made while the interested party was placed under judicial protection;

3° If an action was introduced before his death for the purpose of opening a curatorship or guardianship or for the purpose of family authorization.

The action for nullity is available within a period of five years, to the interested party from the cessation of his condition and, after his death, to the heirs, from the day of death.

###### Article 556

One who has caused damage to another while under the influence of a mental disorder is nonetheless obliged to make reparation.

###### Section II: Common Provisions for Protected Adults

###### Article 557

Adult persons shall receive protection of their person and property that their condition or situation renders necessary according to the procedures provided for in this title.

This protection is established and ensured in respect of individual freedoms, fundamental rights and the dignity of the person.

Its purpose is the interest of the protected person. It promotes, insofar as possible, the autonomy of the latter. It is a duty of families and of the public community.

###### Article 558

The President of the Court of First Instance and the Public Prosecutor exercise general supervision of protection measures within their jurisdiction. They may visit or have visited the protected persons and those who are the subject of an application for protection, whatever the measure pronounced or sought.

Persons in charge of the protection are required to comply with their summons and to communicate to them any information they require.

###### Article 559

The President of the Court of First Instance may issue injunctions against persons in charge of the protection and condemn to a civil fine of 10,000 FD to 100,000 FD those who have not complied therewith.

He may also remove them from their mission in case of a characterized failure in the exercise thereof, after having heard them or summoned them.

###### Article 560

Without prejudice to the application of the rules of management of affairs, the death of the protected person puts an end to the mission of the person in charge of the protection.

###### Article 561

Persons exercise judicial protection measures on a gratuitous basis.

However, the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the President of the Court of First Instance may authorize, according to the importance of the property managed or the difficulty of exercising the measure, the payment of an indemnity to the person in charge of the protection. He shall fix the amount thereof. This indemnity is borne by the protected person.

###### Article 562

All the organs of the judicial protection measure are liable for damage resulting from any fault they commit in the exercise of their function.

However, when the person who has been designated as organ of judicial protection exercises his mission on a gratuitous basis, he incurs liability, for acts accomplished with his assistance, only in case of fraud or gross negligence.

###### Article 563

When the fault at the origin of the damage was committed in the organization and operation of the protection measure by the judge or the clerk, the action for liability brought by the protected or formerly protected person or by his heirs is directed against the State, which has a right of recourse.

###### Article 564

The action for liability is prescribed after five years from the end of the protection measure even if the management continued beyond.

However, when the curatorship has ceased by the opening of a tutorship measure, the period runs only from the expiration of the latter.

##### Chapter II: Legal Protection Measures for Adults

###### Section I: General Provisions

###### Article 565

Any person unable to provide for his interests alone by reason of an impairment, medically established, either of his mental faculties, or of his bodily faculties of a nature to prevent the expression of his will, may benefit from a legal protection measure provided for in this chapter.

Unless otherwise provided, the measure is intended for the protection of both the person and the property interests of the latter. It may however be expressly limited to one of these two missions.

###### Article 566

The dwelling of the protected person and the furniture with which it is furnished, whether it is a principal or secondary residence, are kept at the disposal of the latter for as long as possible. The power to administer the property mentioned in the first paragraph permits only precarious enjoyment agreements which cease, notwithstanding any provisions or stipulations to the contrary, upon the return of the protected person to his dwelling.

If it becomes necessary or if it is in the interest of the protected person that the rights relating to his dwelling or his furniture be disposed of by alienation, termination or conclusion of a lease, the act is authorized by the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, by the President of the Court of First Instance, without prejudice to the formalities that the nature of the property may require. If the purpose of the act is the reception of the person concerned in an establishment, the prior opinion of a physician, not exercising a function or occupying a position in that establishment, is required. In all cases, souvenirs, objects of a personal nature, those essential to disabled persons or intended for the care of sick persons are kept at the disposal of the person concerned, where applicable by the care of the establishment in which the latter is accommodated.

###### Article 567

The person in charge of the protection measure may not proceed with the modification of accounts or savings books opened in the name of the protected person, nor with the opening of another account or savings book with a bank or any other organization that may legally receive funds from the public. The family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the President of the Court of First Instance may however authorize it if the interest of the protected person so requires.

A special account is opened in the name of the protected person with a bank of the place by the person in charge of the protection if the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the President of the Court of First Instance if he deems it necessary.

When the protected person is not the holder of any account or savings book, the person in charge of the protection measure opens one for him.

Banking operations of collection, payment and asset management carried out in the name and on behalf of the protected person are carried out exclusively by means of accounts opened in the name of the latter; the fruits, products and capital gains generated by the funds and securities belonging to the protected person revert exclusively to him.

If the protected person has been subject to a prohibition on issuing checks, the person in charge of the protection measure may nevertheless, with the authorization of the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, of the President of the Court of First Instance, operate under his signature the accounts of which the protected person is the holder and have access to all the usual means of payment.

###### Section II: Common Provisions for Judicial Measures

###### Article 568

The protection measure may be ordered by the judge only in case of necessity and when the interests of the person cannot be sufficiently provided for by the application, either of the rules of common law of representation, or of those relating to the respective rights and duties of spouses and the rules of matrimonial regimes, or by another less restrictive judicial protection measure. The measure is proportionate and individualized according to the degree of impairment of the personal faculties of the person concerned.

###### Article 569

The judicial protection measure may be opened for an emancipated minor as well as for an adult. For a non-emancipated minor, the application may be filed and judged in the last year of his minority. The judicial protection measure takes effect, however, only from the day of his majority.

###### Article 570

The application to open the measure may be presented to the judge by the person who should be protected or, as the case may be, by his or her spouse, or by a relative or relation, a person maintaining close and stable ties with the adult, or the person exercising a legal protection measure with regard to him or her.

It may also be presented by the public prosecutor either on his own initiative or at the request of a third party.

###### Article 571

The application must be accompanied, on pain of inadmissibility, by a detailed certificate drawn up by a doctor chosen from the list of judicial experts provided for in Article L.356-6 of the Code of Civil Procedure. This doctor may seek the opinion of the treating physician of the person who should be protected.

###### Article 572

The judge rules, after the person has been heard or summoned. The interested party may be accompanied by a lawyer or, subject to the agreement of the judge, by any other person of his or her choice.

The judge may however, by a specially reasoned decision and on the advice of a doctor registered on the list mentioned in Article 571, decide that there is no need to proceed with the hearing of the interested party if it is of a nature to harm his or her health or if he or she is unable to express his or her will.

###### Section III: On safeguard of justice

###### Article 573

The judge may place under safeguard of justice the person who, for one of the reasons provided for in Article 565, needs temporary legal protection or to be represented for the performance of certain specified acts.

This measure may also be pronounced by the judge, seized of curatorship or guardianship proceedings, for the duration of the proceedings.

###### Article 574

The person placed under safeguard of justice retains the exercise of his or her rights. However, he or she may not, on pain of nullity, perform an act for which a special agent has been designated pursuant to Article 576.

The acts that he or she has performed and the commitments that he or she has entered into during the duration of the measure may be annulled for simple injury or reduced in case of excess. The courts take into consideration in particular the utility or futility of the transaction, the importance or consistency of the assets of the protected person and the good or bad faith of those with whom he or she has contracted.

The action for nullity or reduction belongs only to the protected person and, after his or her death, to his or her heirs. It is extinguished by a period of five years from the day on which the holder of a right knew or should have known the facts enabling him or her to exercise it.

###### Article 575

The mandate by which the protected person has entrusted another person with the administration of his or her property continues to produce its effects during the safeguard of justice unless it is revoked or suspended by the president of the Court of First Instance; the agent being heard or summoned.

In the absence of a mandate, the rules of management of affairs are applicable.

Those who have the capacity to request the opening of a curatorship or guardianship are required to perform the conservatory acts essential to the preservation of the assets of the protected person as soon as they have knowledge both of their urgency and of the opening of the safeguard measure. The same provisions are applicable to the person or establishment that houses the person placed under safeguard.

###### Article 576

If there is reason to act outside the cases defined in Article 570, any interested party may give notice thereof to the judge. The judge may designate a special agent, for the purpose of performing one or more specified acts, even acts of disposition, made necessary by the management of the assets of the protected person.

The special agent is required to report on the execution of his or her mandate to the protected person and to the judge under the conditions provided for in Articles 639 to 644.

###### Article 577

The special agent may also be entrusted with a mission of protection of the person in compliance with Articles 595 to 600.

###### Article 578

On pain of lapsing, the safeguard of justice measure may not exceed one year, renewable once under the conditions set out in the fourth paragraph of Article 581.

The judge may, at any time, order its lifting if the need for temporary protection ceases. In the absence of lifting, the safeguard of justice ends upon expiration of the period or after the performance of the acts for which it was ordered. It also ends with the opening of a curatorship or guardianship measure from the day on which the new legal protection measure takes effect.

###### Section IV: On curatorship and guardianship

###### Article 579

The person who, without being unable to act himself or herself, needs, for one of the reasons provided for in Article 565, to be assisted or supervised in a continuous manner in the important acts of civil life may be placed under curatorship.

Curatorship is pronounced only if it is established that safeguard of justice cannot ensure sufficient protection.

The person who, for one of the reasons provided for in Article 565, must be represented in a continuous manner in the acts of civil life, may be placed under guardianship.

Guardianship is pronounced only if it is established that neither safeguard of justice nor curatorship can ensure sufficient protection.

###### Sub-section 1: On the duration of the measure

###### Article 580

The president of the Court of First Instance sets the duration of the measure without it being able to exceed five years.

The judge who pronounces a guardianship measure may, by a specially reasoned decision and on the confirming advice of a doctor registered on the list of judicial experts in accordance with Article L.356-6 of the Code of Civil Procedure finding that the impairment of the personal faculties of the interested party described in Article 565 does not manifestly appear likely to experience an improvement according to the established data of science, set a longer duration, not exceeding ten years.

###### Article 581

The judge may renew the measure for the same duration.

However, when the impairment of the personal faculties of the interested party described in Article 565 does not manifestly appear likely to experience an improvement according to the established data of science, the judge may, by a specially reasoned decision and on the confirming advice of a doctor registered on the list mentioned in Article 571, renew the measure for a longer duration that he or she determines, not exceeding twenty years.

The judge may, at any time, terminate the measure, modify it or substitute another measure provided for in this title, after having obtained the opinion of the person responsible for the protection measure. He or she rules on his or her own initiative or at the request of one of the persons mentioned in Article 570, in view of a medical certificate and under the conditions provided for in Article 572. He or she may not, however, strengthen the protection regime of the interested party unless he or she is seized of a request to that effect satisfying Articles 570 and 571.

###### Article 582

The measure ends, in the absence of renewal, upon expiration of the set period, in case of a judgment of lifting having become res judicata or in case of death of the interested party.

The judge may also terminate it when the protected person resides outside the national territory, if this remoteness prevents the monitoring and control of the measure.

###### Sub-section 2: On the publication of the measure

###### Article 583

Judgments concerning the opening, modification or lifting of curatorship or guardianship are enforceable against third parties only two months after the mention has been noted in the margin of the birth certificate of the protected person according to the procedures provided for by the Code of Civil Procedure. However, even in the absence of this mention, they are enforceable against third parties who have personal knowledge thereof.

###### Subsection 3: Protective Bodies

###### Article 584

Curatorships and guardianships are subject to the conditions provided for guardianships of minors by articles 529 to 531. However, the powers conferred by article 531 on the family council are exercised by the judge in the absence of constitution of that body.

Members of the medical and pharmacy professions, as well as medical auxiliaries, may not exercise a curatorship or guardianship with regard to their patients.

The fiduciary designated by the fiduciary contract may not exercise a curatorship or guardianship with regard to the settlor.

###### § 1. Of the Curator and the Guardian

###### Article 585

A curator or a guardian is designated for the protected person under the conditions provided in this paragraph and subject to the powers conferred on the family council if it has been constituted.

###### Article 586

The curator or guardian is designated by the judge.

The latter may, in consideration of the situation of the protected person, the aptitudes of the interested parties and the consistency of the estate to be administered, designate several curators or several guardians to jointly exercise the protective measure. Each curator or guardian is deemed, with regard to third parties, to have received from the others the power to act alone for acts for which a guardian would not need any authorization. The judge may divide the protective measure between a curator or a guardian responsible for the protection of the person and a curator or a guardian responsible for estate management.

Unless the judge has decided otherwise, the persons designated pursuant to the preceding paragraph are independent from each other, and are not responsible to each other. However, they inform each other of the decisions they make.

###### Article 587

The designation by a person of one or more persons responsible for exercising the functions of curator or guardian in the event that they are placed under curatorship or guardianship is binding on the judge, unless the designated person refuses the mission or is unable to perform it, or if the interest of the protected person requires excluding them. In case of difficulty, the judge decides.

The same applies when the parents or the last survivor of the father and mother, not subject to a curatorship or guardianship measure, who exercise parental authority over their minor child or assume the material and emotional care of their adult child designate one or more persons responsible for exercising the functions of curator or guardian from the day when they themselves die or can no longer continue to care for the interested party.

###### Article 588

In the absence of designation made pursuant to article 587, the judge appoints, as curator or guardian, the spouse of the protected person, unless common life has ceased between them or another cause prevents entrusting them with the measure.

In the absence of appointment made pursuant to the preceding paragraph and subject to the last reservation mentioned therein, the judge designates a relative, a relative by marriage or a person residing with the protected adult or maintaining close and stable ties with them.

The judge takes into consideration the feelings expressed by the latter, their usual relationships, the interest shown in them and any recommendations from their relatives and relatives by marriage as well as their entourage.

###### Article 589

When no family member or close person can assume the curatorship or guardianship, the judge designates a judicial representative for the protection of adults. This representative may not refuse to perform urgent acts required by the interest of the protected person, in particular the conservatory acts essential to the preservation of their estate.

###### Article 590

If the interest of the person accommodated or cared for in a health establishment justifies it, the judge may designate, as curator or guardian, a person or a service agent of the establishment registered on the list of judicial representatives for the protection of adults.

The mission entrusted to the representative extends to the protection of the person, unless otherwise decided by the judge.

###### Article 591

No one is required to retain the curatorship or guardianship of a person beyond five years, except for the spouse, the children of the interested party and judicial representatives for the protection of adults.

###### 112 §

2. Of the Curator ad hoc and the Guardian ad hoc

###### Article 592

The curator or guardian whose interests are, on the occasion of an act or a series of acts, in opposition to those of the protected person or who cannot provide them with assistance or act on their behalf due to the limitations of their mission, has appointed by the judge or by the family council if it has been constituted a curator or a guardian ad hoc, that is to say a curator or guardian for the act or series of acts referred to.

This appointment may also be made at the request of the Public Prosecutor, any interested party or ex officio.

###### § 3. Of the Family Council of Adults under Guardianship

###### Article 593

The judge may organize the guardianship with a family council if the necessities of the protection of the person or the consistency of their estate justify it and if the composition of their family and entourage allow it.

The judge designates the members of the family council in consideration of the feelings expressed by the protected person, their usual relationships, the interest shown in them and any recommendations from their relatives and relatives by marriage as well as their entourage.

The family council designates the guardian, and, where applicable, the guardian ad hoc in accordance with articles 584 to 591.

The rules prescribed for the family council of minors are applied, excluding those provided in article 532, the fourth paragraph of article 533 and the first paragraph of article 535. For the application of the third paragraph of article 536, the time limit runs, when the action is brought by the protected adult, from the day the protective measure ends.

###### Article 594

The judge may authorize the family council to meet and deliberate outside their presence, when the latter has designated a judicial representative for the protection of adults as guardian. The family council then designates a president and a secretary from among its members, excluding the guardian.

The president of the family council transmits to the judge in advance the agenda of each meeting. Decisions made by the family council only take effect in the absence of opposition filed by the judge, under the conditions set by the code of civil procedure.

The president exercises the missions devolved to the judge for the convocation, meeting and deliberation of the family council. However, the judge may, at any time, convene a meeting of the family council under their presidency.

###### Subsection 4: Effects of Curatorship and Guardianship with regard to the Protection of the Person

###### Article 595

The protected person receives from the person responsible for their protection, according to methods adapted to their condition and without prejudice to the information that third parties are required to provide them by virtue of the law, all information about their personal situation, about the acts that the person responsible for their protection wishes to perform, their usefulness, their degree of urgency, their effects and the consequences of a refusal on their part.

###### Article 596

Subject to special provisions provided by law, the performance of acts whose nature implies strictly personal consent can never give rise to assistance or representation of the protected person.

The following are deemed strictly personal: the declaration of birth of a child, recognition thereof, acts of parental authority relating to the person of a child, the declaration of choice or change of a child's name and consent given to one's own adoption or to that of one's child.

###### Article 597

Except in the cases provided for in Article 596, the protected person alone makes decisions relating to his or her person to the extent that his or her condition permits.

Where the condition of the protected person does not permit him or her to make an informed personal decision alone, the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the President of the Court of First Instance may provide that he or she shall benefit, for all acts relating to his or her person or those among them which it enumerates, from the assistance of the person responsible for his or her protection. In the event that such assistance would not suffice, the same person may, if necessary after the opening of a guardianship measure, authorize the guardian to represent the person concerned.

However, except in cases of urgency, the person responsible for the protection of the adult may not, without the authorization of the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, of the President of the Court of First Instance, make a decision having the effect of seriously affecting the bodily integrity of the protected person or the intimacy of his or her private life.

The person responsible for the protection of the adult may take with regard to the latter the protective measures strictly necessary to put an end to the danger that his or her own behavior would cause to the person concerned.

He or she shall inform the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the President of the Court of First Instance without delay.

###### Article 598

The protected person chooses the place of his or her residence.

He or she freely maintains personal relationships with any third party, whether related or not. He or she has the right to be visited and, where appropriate, accommodated by them.

In case of difficulty, the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the President of the Court of First Instance shall rule.

###### Article 599

The marriage of a person under curatorship is permitted only with the authorization of the curator or, failing that, that of the judge.
