The marriage of a person under guardianship is permitted only with the authorization of the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, of the President of the Court of First Instance, and after hearing of the future spouses by the judge.

The opinion of parents and those close to the person is, where appropriate, obtained by the judge.

###### Article 600

At the opening of the measure or, failing that, subsequently, the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the President of the Court of First Instance decides on the conditions under which the curator or guardian responsible for a mission of protection of the person accounts for the steps he or she takes in that capacity.

###### Sous-section 5 : De la régularité des actes

###### Article 601

The obligations arising from acts performed by the protected person less than two years before the publication of the judgment opening the protection measure may be reduced on mere proof that his or her inability to defend his or her interests, as a result of the impairment of his or her personal faculties, was notorious or known to the contracting party at the time when the acts were entered into.

These acts may, under the same conditions, be annulled if it is proven that the protected person suffered prejudice.

By way of derogation from Article 2387, the action must be brought within five years from the date of the judgment opening the measure.

###### Article 602

From the publication of the judgment of opening, the irregularity of acts performed by the protected person or by the person responsible for the protection is sanctioned under the following conditions: 1° If the protected person has performed alone an act which he or she could do without the assistance or representation of the person responsible for his or her protection, the act remains subject to the actions for nullity or reduction provided for in Article 574 as if it had been performed by a person placed under safeguard of justice, unless it was expressly authorized by the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, the President of the Court of First Instance.

2° If the protected person has performed alone an act for which he or she should have been assisted, the act may be annulled only if it is established that the protected person suffered prejudice;

3° If the protected person has performed alone an act for which he or she should have been represented, the act is null and void as of right without it being necessary to prove prejudice;

4° If the guardian or the curator has performed alone an act which should have been done by the protected person either alone or with his or her assistance or which could be performed only with the authorization of the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, of the President of the Court of First Instance, the act is null and void as of right without it being necessary to prove prejudice.

The curator or the guardian may, with the authorization of the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, of the President of the Court of First Instance, bring alone the action for nullity or reduction of the acts provided for in 1°, 2° and 3°.

In all cases, the action is extinguished by the period of five years from the day on which the holder of a right knew or should have known the facts allowing him or her to exercise it.

During this period and as long as the protection measure is open, the act provided for in 4° may be confirmed with the authorization of the judge or of the family council if it has been constituted.

###### Article 603

Articles 601 and 602 do not preclude the application of Articles 554 and 555.

###### Sous-section 6 : Des actes faits dans la curatelle

###### Article 604

The person under curatorship may not, without the assistance of the curator, perform any act which, in the case of guardianship, would have required authorization from the judge or from the family council.

When concluding a written act, the assistance of the curator is manifested by the affixing of his or her signature next to that of the protected person. If the latter does not know how to sign, the act bears his or her fingerprint.

On pain of nullity, any service of process made on the protected person shall also be made on the curator.

###### Article 605

Capital funds falling to the person under curatorship are paid directly into an account opened in his or her name alone and mentioning his or her protection regime, with an institution authorized to receive funds from the public.

The person under curatorship may not, without the assistance of the curator, use his or her capital. This assistance is also required to bring legal action or to defend in such action.

###### Article 606

The curator may not substitute himself or herself for the person under curatorship to act in his or her name.

However, the curator may, if he or she finds that the person under curatorship is seriously compromising his or her interests, refer the matter to the judge to be authorized to perform alone a specific act or cause the opening of guardianship. If the curator refuses his or her assistance for an act for which his or her cooperation is required, the person under curatorship may ask the judge for authorization to perform it alone.

###### Article 607

The person under curatorship may freely make a will subject to the provisions of Article 554. He or she may make a gift only with the assistance of the curator.

The curator is deemed to be in conflict of interest with the protected person when he or she is a beneficiary of the gift.

###### Article 608

At any time, the judge may, by way of derogation from Article 604, list certain acts that the person under curatorship has the capacity to perform alone or, conversely, add other acts to those for which the assistance of the curator is required.

###### Article 609

The judge may also, at any time, order reinforced curatorship. In that case, the curator alone receives the income of the person under curatorship in an account opened in the name of the latter. The curator personally ensures the settlement of expenses with third parties and deposits the surplus in an account left at the disposal of the person concerned or pays it into their hands.

Without prejudice to the provisions of Article 598, the judge may authorize the curator to conclude alone a residential lease or an accommodation agreement ensuring the housing of the protected person.

Reinforced curatorship is subject to the provisions of Articles 630 and 639 to 644.

###### Subsection 7: Of acts performed in guardianship

###### Article 610

Subject to cases where the law or custom authorizes the person under guardianship to act themselves, the guardian represents them in all acts of civil life.

However, the judge may, in the opening judgment or subsequently, list certain acts that the person under guardianship will have the capacity to perform alone or with the assistance of the guardian.

###### Article 611

The person under guardianship is represented in acts necessary for the management of their estate under the conditions and according to the modalities provided for in Title XIII.

###### Article 612

The person under guardianship is represented in court by the guardian.

The guardian may not act, as plaintiff or defendant, to assert the extra-patrimonial rights of the protected person except after authorization or upon injunction of the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, of the President of the Court of First Instance.

The judge or the family council may also enjoin the guardian to withdraw from the proceedings or action or to settle.

###### Article 613

The person under guardianship may, with the authorization of the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, of the President of the Court of First Instance, be assisted or if necessary represented by the guardian to make donations.

They may not make their will alone after the opening of the guardianship except with the authorization of the family council and, if the latter has not been constituted, of the President of the Court of First Instance, this on pain of nullity of the act. The guardian may neither assist nor represent them on that occasion. However, they may alone revoke the will made before or after the opening of the guardianship.

The will made prior to the opening of the guardianship remains valid unless it is established that, since that opening, the cause that had determined the testator to dispose has disappeared.

###### Section V: Of family authorization

###### Article 614

When a person is unable to express their will for one of the causes provided for in Article 565, the judge may authorize one or more persons chosen from among their ascendants or descendants, brothers and sisters or, unless the community of life has ceased between them, the spouse or cohabitant to represent them or to execute one or more acts in their name under the conditions and according to the modalities provided for in this section and those of Title XV of Book III of this code. The authorized person must fulfill the conditions for exercising guardianship duties. They exercise their mission free of charge.

###### Article 615

Family authorization may be ordered by the judge only in case of necessity and when the interests of the person cannot be sufficiently provided for by the application of either the rules of common law of representation, or those relating to the respective rights and duties of spouses and the rules of matrimonial regimes, or again by another less restrictive judicial protection measure.

###### Article 616

The application for the designation of an authorized person may be submitted to the judge by one of the persons mentioned in Article 614 or by the Public Prosecutor at the request of one of them. The application is filed, investigated and judged in accordance with the rules of the Code of Civil Procedure and in compliance with the provisions of Articles 569 and 571.

###### Article 617

The person in respect of whom authorization is requested is heard or summoned according to the modalities provided for in the first paragraph of Article 572. However, the judge may, by specially reasoned decision and on the advice of the physician mentioned in Article 571, decide that there is no need to proceed with their hearing if it is likely to harm their health or if the person is unable to express themselves. The judge ensures the adhesion or, failing that, the absence of legitimate opposition to the authorization measure and to the choice of the authorized person from the relatives mentioned in Article 614 who maintain close and stable ties with the person or who show interest in their regard and whose existence is known to them at the time of ruling.

###### Article 618

The judge rules on the choice of the authorized person and the extent of the authorization by ensuring that the proposed arrangement is in accordance with the patrimonial and, where appropriate, personal interests of the person concerned.

###### Article 619

The authorization may cover:

1° one or more of the acts that the guardian has the power to perform, alone or with authorization, on the property of the person concerned;

2° one or more acts relating to the person to be protected. In that case, the authorization is exercised in compliance with the provisions of Articles 595 to 598 of this code.

The authorized person may perform an act of gratuitous disposition only with the authorization of the judge.

If the interest of the person to be protected so requires, the judge may issue a general authorization covering all acts or one of the two categories of acts mentioned in points 1° and 2° of this article.

###### Article 620

The authorized person may, unless the judge decides otherwise, proceed without authorization to the acts mentioned in the first paragraph of Article 567.

###### Article 621

If the person in respect of whom authorization has been issued performs alone an act whose performance has been entrusted to the authorized person, it is null and void by operation of law without it being necessary to establish prejudice.

Obligations resulting from acts performed by a person in respect of whom a family authorization measure was pronounced less than two years before the judgment issuing the authorization may be reduced or annulled under the conditions provided for in Article 601.

The authorized person may, with the authorization of the judge, bring alone the action for nullity or reduction provided for in the paragraphs above.

If the authorized person performs alone, in that capacity, an act not falling within the scope of the authorization issued to them or which could only be performed with the authorization of the judge, the act is null and void by operation of law without it being necessary to establish prejudice.

In all cases, the action for nullity or reduction is exercised within five years from the day on which the holder of a right knew or should have known the facts enabling them to exercise it. During that period and as long as the authorization measure is in progress, the contested act may be confirmed with the authorization of the judge.

###### Article 622

The judge rules at the request of one of the persons mentioned in Article 614 or of the public prosecutor on difficulties that may arise in the implementation of the arrangement.

Seized for this purpose under the conditions provided for in the first paragraph of Article 616, the judge may, at any time, modify the extent of the authorization or terminate it, after having heard or summoned, on the one hand, the person in respect of whom the authorization was issued, under the conditions provided for in the first paragraph of Article 617 and, on the other hand, the authorized person.

###### Article 623

In addition to the death of the person in respect of whom the family authorization was issued, such family authorization terminates:

1° By the placement of the person concerned under safeguard of justice, under curatorship or under guardianship; 2° In the event of a judgment of discharge having become res judicata pronounced by the judge at the request of one of the persons mentioned in Article 614 or of the public prosecutor, when it appears that the conditions provided for in that article are no longer met or when the execution of the family authorization is likely to harm the interests of the protected person;

3° By operation of law in the absence of renewal at the expiration of the fixed period;

4° After the completion of the acts for which the authorization had been issued.

#### Title XIII: On the management of the patrimony of minors and adults under guardianship

Chapter I: On the modalities of management

###### Article 624

The guardian represents the protected person in acts necessary for the management of his or her patrimony. He is required to exercise prudent, diligent and informed care in such management, in the sole interest of the protected person.

The list of acts that are regarded, for the application of this title, as acts of administration relating to the current management of the patrimony and as acts of disposition that commit it in a lasting and substantial manner is fixed by decree.

###### Article 625

The capital due to the protected person is paid directly into an account opened in his or her name only and mentioning the guardianship measure, with a bank or any other institution that may legally receive funds from the public.

###### Article 626

Third parties may inform the judge of acts or omissions of the guardian that appear to them likely to prejudice the interests of the protected person. In this title, whenever mention is made of the judge, it refers to the president of the Court of First Instance or the magistrate he has designated. These third parties are not guarantors of the use of the capital. However, if in connection with such use they become aware of acts or omissions that manifestly compromise the interest of the protected person, they notify the judge.

Third-party opposition to authorizations of the family council or of the judge may be exercised only by the creditors of the protected person and in case of fraud on their rights.

###### Sole Section: On decisions of the family council or of the judge

###### Article 627

The guardian establishes the budget of the guardianship by determining, according to the importance of the property of the protected person and the operations involved in their management, the sums annually necessary for the maintenance of such person and for the reimbursement of the costs of administering his or her property. The guardian informs the family council or, failing that, the judge thereof. In case of difficulties, the budget is established by the family council or, failing that, by the judge.

The family council or, failing that, the judge may authorize the guardian to include in the management costs the remuneration of special administrators whose assistance he requests under his own responsibility. The family council or, failing that, the judge may authorize the guardian to enter into a contract for the management of the securities and financial instruments of the protected person. He chooses the contracting third party in consideration of his professional experience and solvency. The contract may, at any time and notwithstanding any stipulation to the contrary, be terminated in the name of the protected person.

###### Article 628

The family council or, failing that, the judge determines the sum from which begins, for the guardian, the obligation to invest liquid capital and surplus income.

The family council or, failing that, the judge prescribes all measures that it deems useful regarding the investment or reinvestment of funds either in advance or on the occasion of each operation. The investment or reinvestment is carried out by the guardian within the time limit set by the decision ordering it and in the manner it prescribes. After this time limit, the guardian may be declared debtor of the interest.

The family council or, failing that, the judge may order that certain funds be deposited in an unavailable account.

###### Article 629

The family council or, failing that, the judge rules on the authorizations that the guardian requests for acts that he cannot accomplish alone.

###### § 1. Acts that the guardian accomplishes without authorization

###### Article 630

Within three months of the opening of the guardianship, the guardian has an inventory of the property of the protected person carried out and transmits it to the judge. He ensures its updating during the measure.

He may obtain communication of all information and documents necessary for the establishment of the inventory from any public or private person, without professional secrecy or banking secrecy ever being invoked against him.

If the inventory has not been established or proves to be incomplete or inaccurate, the protected person and, after his or her death, his or her heirs may prove the value and initial composition of his or her property by any means.

###### Article 631

The guardian accomplishes alone conservatory acts and, subject to the provisions of the second paragraph of Article 608, the acts of administration necessary for the management of the patrimony of the protected person. He acts alone in court to assert the patrimonial rights of the protected person.

Leases granted by the guardian confer on the lessee, against the protected person who has become capable, no right of renewal and no right to remain in the premises at the expiration of the lease, even if there exist contrary legal provisions. These provisions are however not applicable to leases granted before the opening of the guardianship and renewed by the guardian.

###### § 2. Acts that the guardian accomplishes with authorization

###### Article 632

The guardian may not, without being authorized by the family council or, failing that, the judge, make acts of disposition in the name of the protected person.

The authorization that may be given to him by the family council or, failing that, the judge, determines the stipulations and, where applicable, the price or reserve price for which the act may be executed. Authorization is not required in case of forced sale by judicial decision or in case of amicable sale upon authorization of the judge.

###### Article 633

The guardian may not settle or submit to arbitration in the name of the protected person except after having had the clauses of the settlement or arbitration agreement and, where applicable, the arbitration clause approved by the family council or, failing that, by the judge.

###### Article 634

The partition with respect to a protected person may be made amicably upon authorization of the family council or, failing that, of the judge, who designates, if necessary, a notary to proceed therewith. It may be only

### partial.

The liquidation statement is subject to the approval of the family council or, failing that, of the judge.

The partition may also be made in court in accordance with Articles 981 and 998. Any other partition is considered as provisional.

###### Article 635

By way of derogation from Article 881, the guardian may only accept an inheritance devolving to the protected person subject to benefit of inventory. However, the family council or, failing that, the judge may, by resolution or decision, authorize the guardian to accept purely and simply if the assets manifestly exceed the liabilities.

The guardian may not renounce an inheritance devolving to the protected person without authorization from the family council or, failing that, the judge.

###### Article 636

In the case where the inheritance renounced on behalf of the protected person has not been accepted by another heir and as long as the State has not been sent into possession, the renunciation may be revoked, either by the guardian authorized for that purpose by a new resolution of the family council or, failing that, a new decision of the judge, or by the protected person having become capable. This revocation, like the renunciation, has retroactive effect to the day of the opening of the inheritance, without however calling into question the rights that may have been acquired by third parties over the property of the inheritance by prescription or by acts validly done with the curator to the vacant inheritance.

###### Article 637

On an exceptional basis and in the interest of the protected person, the guardian may, upon authorization of the family council or, failing that, the judge, purchase the property of the protected person or lease it.

For the conclusion of the act, the guardian is deemed to be in conflict of interest with the protected person.

###### § 3. Des actes que le tuteur ne peut accomplir

###### Article 638

The guardian may not, even with authorization:

1° Perform acts that entail a gratuitous alienation of the property or rights of the protected person except as provided with regard to donations, such as the remission of debt, the gratuitous renunciation of an acquired right, the advance renunciation of the action for reduction referred to in Articles 1085 and 1086, the release of mortgage or security without payment, or the gratuitous creation of an easement or security to guarantee the debt of a third party;

2° Acquire from a third party a right or claim that the latter holds against the protected person; 3° Carry on trade or a liberal profession in the name of the protected person;

4° Purchase the property of the protected person or lease it, subject to the provisions of Article 637;

5° Transfer into a fiduciary estate the property or rights of a protected adult.

##### Chapitre II : De l'établissement, de la vérification et de l'approbation des comptes

###### Article 639

The guardian establishes each year an account of his or her management to which are appended all useful supporting documents.

For this purpose, the guardian requests from the institutions with which one or more accounts are opened in the name of the protected person an annual statement thereof, without professional secrecy or banking secrecy ever being able to be invoked against him or her.

The guardian is required to ensure the confidentiality of the management account. However, a copy of the account and supporting documents is provided each year by the guardian to the protected person when he or she is at least sixteen years of age and, if the guardian deems it useful, to the other persons responsible for the protection of the person concerned.

In addition, the judge may, after having heard the protected person and obtained his or her consent, if he or she has reached the aforementioned age and if his or her condition permits, authorize the spouse, a relative, a relative by marriage of the protected person or one of his or her close relations, if they demonstrate a legitimate interest, to have the guardian communicate to them at their expense a copy of the account and supporting documents or part of these documents.

###### Article 640

The guardian submits each year the management account, accompanied by supporting documents, for verification, to the chief clerk of the Court of First Instance.

For the verification of the account, the chief clerk of the Court of First Instance may make use of the right of communication provided for in the second paragraph of Article 639. He or she may be assisted in his or her mission of account control under the conditions established by the code of civil procedure.

If he or she refuses to approve the account, the chief clerk of the Court of First Instance prepares a report of the difficulties encountered which he or she transmits to the judge. The latter rules on the conformity of the account. The judge may decide that the mission of verification and approval of accounts vested in the chief clerk of the Court of First Instance shall be exercised by a certified public accountant registered on the list of judicial experts.

When Article 594 is applied, the judge may decide that the family council shall verify and approve the accounts in lieu and place of the chief clerk of the Court of First Instance.

###### Article 641

The judge may, by way of derogation from Articles 639 and 640 and in consideration of the modest nature of the income and assets of the protected person, dispense the guardian from establishing the management account and from submitting it for approval to the chief clerk of the Court of First Instance director of judicial registry services.

###### Article 642

If the resources of the protected person permit and if the importance and composition of his or her assets justify it, the judge may decide, in consideration of the patrimonial interest at stake, that the mission of verification and approval of the management account shall be exercised, at the expense of the person concerned and according to the procedures he or she establishes, by a technician.

###### Article 643

When his or her mission ends for any reason whatsoever, the guardian establishes a management account of the operations that have occurred since the establishment of the last annual account and submits it for verification and approval as provided in Articles 640 and 642.

In addition, within three months following the end of his or her mission, the guardian or his or her heirs if he or she is deceased deliver a copy of the last five management accounts and of the account mentioned in the first paragraph of this article, as the case may be, to the person having become capable if he or she has not already received it, to the person newly responsible for the management measure or to the heirs of the protected person. The preceding paragraphs are not applicable in the case provided for in Article 641.

In all cases, the guardian delivers to the persons mentioned in the second paragraph of this article the documents necessary to continue the management or ensure the liquidation of the estate, as well as the initial inventory and the updates to which it has given rise.

##### Chapitre III : De la prescription

###### Article 644

The action for rendering of accounts, for revendication or for payment brought by the protected person or person having been protected or by his or her heirs in relation to acts of the guardianship is prescribed by five years from the end of the measure, even if the management continued beyond.

#### Titre XIV : Des mesures de protection des victimes de violences

###### Article 645

When violence exercised within the couple or by a former spouse, or a former cohabitant endangers the person who is the victim thereof, one or more children, the judge may issue on an urgent basis to the latter a protection order.

In this title, each time reference is made to the judge, it refers to the president of the Court of First Instance or the magistrate he or she has designated.

###### Article 646

The protection order is issued by the judge, petitioned by the person in danger, assisted if necessary, or, with the latter's consent, by the public prosecutor.

Upon receipt of the application for a protection order, the judge summons, by all appropriate means, for a hearing, the applicant party and the defendant party, assisted, where applicable, by a lawyer, as well as the public prosecutor. These hearings may take place separately. They must be held in chambers.

###### Article 647

A protection order is issued, as soon as possible, by the judge, if he considers, in light of the evidence produced before him and debated in adversarial proceedings, that there are serious reasons to consider as probable the commission of the alleged acts of violence and the danger to which the victim or one or more children are exposed. Upon its issuance, the judge has jurisdiction to:

1° Prohibit the defendant party from receiving or meeting certain persons as well as from entering into contact with them, in any manner whatsoever;

2° Prohibit the defendant party from possessing or carrying a weapon and, where applicable, order them to surrender to the police or gendarmerie service that he designates the weapons in their possession for deposit with the court registry;

3° Rule on the separate residence of the spouses by specifying which of the two will continue to reside in the matrimonial home and on the terms for covering the costs relating to this dwelling. Except in special circumstances, the enjoyment of this dwelling is granted to the spouse who is not the perpetrator of the violence, even if they have benefited from emergency accommodation;

4° Specify which of the cohabitants will continue to reside in the common dwelling and rule on the terms for covering the costs relating to this dwelling. Except in special circumstances, the enjoyment of this dwelling is granted to the cohabitant who is not the perpetrator of the violence, even if they have benefited from emergency accommodation;

5° Rule on the terms of exercise of parental authority and, where applicable, on the contribution to marital expenses and on the contribution to the maintenance and education of the children;

6° Authorize the applicant party to conceal their domicile or residence and to elect domicile with the lawyer who assists or represents them or with the Public Prosecutor for all civil proceedings in which they are also a party. If, for the purposes of executing a court decision, the bailiff responsible for this execution must have knowledge of the address of this person, it is communicated to them, without them being able to disclose it to their principal;

When the judge issues a protection order by reason of violence likely to endanger one or more children, he informs the Public Prosecutor without delay.

###### Article 648

The measures mentioned in Article 647 are ordered for a maximum period of six months from the notification of the order. They may be extended beyond this period if, during this time, a petition for divorce or legal separation has been filed or if the judge has been seised of a petition relating to the exercise of parental authority.

The judge may, at any time, at the request of the public prosecutor or either party, or after having ordered any useful investigative measure, and after having invited each of them to express themselves, remove or modify all or part of the measures set out in the protection order, decide on new ones, grant the defendant party a temporary dispensation from observing certain obligations that have been imposed on them, or withdraw the protection order.

###### Article 649

A protection order may also be issued urgently by the judge to the adult person threatened with forced marriage, under the conditions set out in Article 646.

The judge has jurisdiction to take the measures mentioned in 1°, 2° and 6° of Article 647.

## BOOK II. - ON PROPERTY, AND THE VARIOUS MODIFICATIONS OF OWNERSHIP

###### Article 650

The property of public entities is governed by the codes and laws concerning them and, in the absence of specific provisions, by the common law of property as established by this Book.

#### Title I: On patrimony and the property composing it

Subtitle I: Patrimony

###### Article 651

Patrimony is the universality of law comprising all the property of a person, both movable and immovable, present and future, the entirety of the assets answering for the entirety of the liabilities. Every natural or legal person holds a patrimony. Unless otherwise provided by law, a person may have only one patrimony.

###### Article 652

Property within the meaning of the preceding article consists of corporeal or incorporeal things that are the subject of appropriation by the holder of the patrimony in question, as well as the real and personal rights that are theirs.

###### Article 653

A real right is one that confers on its holder a direct power over property.

The holder of a real right may exercise their power over the thing in whosesoever hands it may be found. When it is accessory to a claim whose payment it guarantees, it confers, in addition to the right of pursuit, a right of preference over the property.

###### Article 654

A personal right is one held by the creditor of an obligation against their debtor.

Subtitle II. On the distinction of property

###### Article 655

All property is either movable or immovable.

###### Article 656

Subject to the laws that protect them, animals are subject to the legal regime of corporeal things.

###### Article 657

Except when the law provides otherwise:

- a consumable thing is a thing that is consumed when used. It cannot be used without being destroyed on first use or without leaving the patrimony of its owner;
- a non-fungible thing or specific thing consists of a determined and individualized thing; a fungible thing or generic thing is determined only by its kind and quantity;
- when a thing produces or yields fruits periodically, it is fruit-bearing. Fruits are what a property generates, periodically or not, spontaneously or through its development, without its substance being altered in any way. They may be natural, when they come spontaneously from the land or from animals; industrial, when they are obtained through cultivation or breeding; or civil, such as rents from leases, interest on sums due, and arrears of annuities. Civil fruits are also called income. Products affect the very substance of the property, which is diminished when it is exploited.

Chapter I: On immovables

###### Article 658

Corporeal property is immovable, either by its nature, or by its destination. Incorporeal property is immovable by the object to which it applies.

###### Article 659

Land, buildings and plants thereon are immovable by their nature, as well as all other things incorporated therein, as long as the connection with the ground is thus maintained. Pipes used for conducting water in a house or any other immovable by nature to which they are attached are immovable and form part of the land to which they are joined.

Co-ownership units are also immovable.

Houses known as plank houses are movable property, except when the State sells to its owner the land on which it is built. In that case, a land title may be established and the whole consisting of the land and the house then becomes immovable property subject to registration.

###### Article 660

Immovables by destination are a legal fiction by which the law treats movable property as immovable. A movable is immovable by destination when two cumulative conditions are met: 1° The two properties must be owned by the same person;

2° A relationship of destination must exist between the movable and the immovable to which it is attached. This relationship of destination results either from the assignment of the movable to the operation of an immovable by nature, or from the attachment of the movable property to the immovable property by nature in perpetuity.

###### Article 661

The assignment of movable property to the operation of immovable property by nature may result from the agricultural operation of land, such as animals attached to cultivation as long as they remain attached to the land by effect of an agreement; from the industrial operation of land, such as equipment in an industrial building serving the activity; from the commercial operation of land, such as movables serving the operation of an immovable property for hotel purposes; or from the civil operation of an immovable property, such as equipment elements that allow the use of an apartment rented by its owner.

###### Article 662

The attachment of a movable to immovable property by nature in perpetuity resides in the material attachment process implemented by the owner. This process externalizes the owner's will to attach the movable to the immovable.

Movables that have been fixed thereto by means of plaster, lime or cement, or any other method of attachment that would prevent the movables from being detached without being fractured or deteriorated, or without breaking or deteriorating the part of the land to which they are attached, are irrefutably presumed to be attached to the immovable property.

Movables that have been specially designed or adapted to be integrated into the immovable property by nature, or for which the owner has made a modification to the immovable property in order to receive them, such as a niche made expressly to receive a statue, even if it can be removed without fracture or deterioration, are presumed, unless proven otherwise, to be attached to the immovable property.

In other cases, the owner must establish that he had the intention to attach the movable in perpetuity to the immovable property by nature.

###### Article 663

The owner of an immovable property by destination may always terminate the destination relationship, by his sole will, subject to the rights of third parties.

###### Article 664

Are immovables by the object to which they apply:

1° Real property rights:

- a) ownership of immovable property;
- b) usufruct of the same property;
- c) rights of use and habitation;
- d) emphyteusis;
- e) right of superficies;
- f) easements and land services;
- g) antichresis;
- h) privileges and mortgages.

2° Actions that tend to claim an immovable property.

###### Article 665

The real rights enumerated in the preceding article are preserved and produce effect with regard to third parties only insofar as they have been made public in the forms, conditions and limits regulated in this code, without prejudice to the rights of the parties for the execution of their agreements.

By way of derogation from the rule of the preceding paragraph, creditors and legatees who request the separation of the estate of a deceased person retain, with regard to his heirs and representatives, in order to exercise their privilege over hereditary immovable properties, the benefit of the period of six months from the opening of the succession, notwithstanding any alienation by said heirs or representatives.

##### Chapitre II : Movable property

###### Article 666

Property is movable by its nature or by determination of law.

All corporeal things other than those referred to in Articles 659 and 660 are movable by their nature.

All rights other than those referred to in Article 664 are movable by determination of law.

###### Article 667

The word movable, used alone in the provisions of the law or in a legal act, without other addition or designation, does not include cash money, precious stones, active debts, books, medals, instruments of sciences, arts and crafts, body linen, weapons, grains, wines, hay and other commodities; it also does not include what is the object of commerce.

###### Article 668

The words household furnishings include only movables intended for the use and ornamentation of apartments, such as beds, seats, mirrors, clocks, tables, porcelain and other objects of this nature. The sale or gift of a furnished house includes only household furnishings. Similarly, the sale or gift of a house, with everything found therein, does not include cash money, nor active debts and other rights whose titles may be deposited in the house; all other movable effects are included therein.

###### Article 669

Subject to the rights of third parties, property that is currently immovable but that is destined, by effect of the will of the contracting parties, to soon become movable and in the perspective of realization of the agreement, is considered as movable property. Thus: crops sold standing, products to be extracted from quarries or mines, materials to come from the demolition of a building.

#### Titre II : Ownership, possession and holding

###### Article 670

Real rights not subject to publication, subject to the texts relating to legal acts, may be proven by any means.

In case of conflict, when no sufficiently probative title is produced, it is for the judge of the claim to identify the best and most characteristic presumptions of ownership, and he retains the most likely right after having analyzed all the circumstances to decide between the litigants. If he does not succeed in doing so, the possessor in place is attributed ownership. For immovable properties, the conflict between several persons invoking titles emanating from a common author is resolved according to the rules of land registration.

Chapitre Ier : Ownership

###### Article 671

Ownership is the exclusive right to enjoy and dispose of things and rights.

It confers upon its holder an absolute power, subject to the laws and regulations that govern it. This power may not be used for the purpose of harming others, except to constitute an abuse of right.

###### Article 672

No one may be compelled to cede his ownership, except for public utility purposes, and by means of just and prior compensation.

###### Article 673

Ownership of a thing, whether movable or immovable, extends to the fruits and products of the thing. The fruits produced by the thing, however, belong to the owner of the thing only subject to reimbursement of the costs of plowing, work and seeds done by third parties and whose value is estimated at the date of reimbursement.

Ownership of the thing also extends to everything that is united to it accessorily either naturally or artificially. This right is called the right of accession.

###### Article 674

Ownership is not lost by non-use.

The action for recovery, subject to contrary provision of law, is perpetual.

###### Article 675

By way of derogation from the preceding articles, when the owner victim of a minor encroachment on his land does not initiate an action for recovery within two years after having become aware of the encroachment, or within the limit of 10 years from the completion of the works, the author of the constructions and other works may request, if he is in good faith and if the circumstances permit, that the encroachment be attributed to him as a real right against payment of fair compensation. The owner victim of the encroachment may, within the time limits stated above, request at his choice, either the demolition of what was done in violation of his right, or the payment of fair compensation.

The encroachment is minor when it is less than 0.20 meters.

The compensation is fixed amicably by the owners concerned who establish an authentic act of their agreement and, failing that, determined by the judge who takes into account the value of the land occupied, the added value brought to the land of the author of the encroachment, and the harm he has caused to the owner of the land victim of the encroachment.

###### Article 676

Ownership of a treasure belongs to the person who finds it on their own land, by virtue of the right of accession; if the treasure is found on another person's land, it belongs half to the person who discovered it, by occupation, and the other half to the owner of the land, by accession.

A treasure is anything hidden or buried over which no one can prove ownership, and which is discovered by pure chance.

###### Article 677

The rights over items thrown into the sea, over objects that the sea washes up, of whatever nature they may be, over plants and vegetation growing on the seashore, are governed by special laws.

The same applies to lost things whose owner does not come forward.

###### Article 678

The public domain consists of all property of all kinds, immovable or movable, classified or delimited in the public domain, whether or not allocated to public use. The public domain of the State is determined by special law.

The public domain of the State comprises, on the one hand, natural sites determined by law, such as: the seashore, up to the limit of the highest tides, as well as a zone of 50 meters from this limit; islands and islets; springs as well as non-navigable and non-floatable watercourses within the limits determined by the height of the highest waters flowing at full bank before overflowing, as well as a passageway zone 25 meters wide from these limits on each bank; lakes, ponds and lagoons within the limits determined by the level of the highest waters before overflow, with a passageway zone 25 meters wide from these limits on each outer bank; underground water tables, whatever their source, nature and depth and, on the other hand, developments and works carried out for reasons of general interest or public utility, as well as the land supporting them, determined by law or having been the subject of a classification procedure, such as: irrigation or drainage canals, aqueducts, boreholes, dams and hillside reservoirs, cemented wells, as well as the dependencies of these works, when they are carried out for a purpose of public utility; railways, roads and communication routes of all kinds, ports and harbours, sea dikes, semaphores, lighting or beaconing works, as well as their dependencies; telegraph and telephone lines, radio stations and other telecommunications installations, as well as their dependencies; works declared of public utility for the use of hydraulic forces and the transport of electrical energy.

More generally, the public domain of the State comprises property of all kinds that Djiboutian laws declare not susceptible to private ownership.

Property that does not belong to private individuals is administered and can only be alienated in the forms and according to the rules specific to them.

###### Article 679

All immovable property that has no owner, and that of persons who die without heirs or whose estates are abandoned, belong to the State.

Movable property without an owner belongs to the first person who appropriates it, subject to special provisions.

###### Article 680

There are things that belong to no one and whose use is common to all. Police laws regulate the manner of enjoying them.

The right to hunt or fish is also regulated by special laws.

##### Chapitre II : Possession and detention

###### Section I : Possession

###### Article 681

Possession is the act of exercising, with the intention of being the holder, a right over a thing. It is immaterial whether the possessor is or is not the true holder of the right exercised. Possession only exists if it is public, unequivocal and peaceful. In case of violence, useful possession only begins on the day the violence ceased. It is protected, without regard to the merits of the right, against disturbance affecting or threatening it.

However, there is no possession of immovable property except in the presence of a title regularly published according to the laws governing immovable property.

Possession of incorporeal movables is governed by the special laws that govern them.

Payment made in good faith to the person who is in possession of the claim is valid, even if the possessor is subsequently evicted.

###### Article 682

Acts of pure faculty and those of simple tolerance cannot establish either possession or prescription.

###### Article 683

The possessor is in good faith when he possesses as the holder of the right he exercises would, by virtue of a title transferring ownership of which he is unaware of the defects.

Good faith is always presumed, and it is for the person who alleges bad faith to prove it. It is assessed on the day of entry into possession, unless otherwise provided.

He ceases to be in good faith from the moment these defects become known to him.

###### Article 684

One can possess by oneself or through another.

###### Article 685

Possession is proved by all means.

One is always presumed to possess for oneself, and as owner, unless it is proved that one began to possess for another.

When one has begun to possess for another, one is always presumed to possess under the same title, unless there is proof to the contrary.

###### Article 686

In the matter of movables, possession in good faith immediately confers title.

It is otherwise when the person who lost or from whom the thing was stolen intends to claim it: that person has three years, from the day of the loss or theft, to take action against the possessor. If the possessor purchased the claimed thing in a normal circuit of commercialization of goods and services, the claimant must pay the possessor the price the thing cost him; otherwise, he will obtain the property without having to reimburse the price to the possessor. The claimant who had to pay a price to the possessor, or the possessor who had to return the thing without obtaining reimbursement of its price, may take action for that amount against the person from whom the possessor held the thing, up to the finder or thief thereof.

When the possessor is in bad faith, the claimed right is only acquired after thirty years. When the period is reached, the right arises from the day the possession began.

In case of an action for recovery concerning the property he possesses, the possessor shall be defendant in the action brought. The plaintiff may reverse the presumptions favorable to the possessor, by all means.

###### Article 687

The current possessor of a movable who proves having possessed formerly is presumed to have possessed in the intermediate time, except proof to the contrary.

###### Article 688

One can always join to one's possession that of one's predecessor.

###### Article 689

The possessor in bad faith, in addition to the obligation to return the thing, owes to the owner who claims it, the interest, the fruits he has received in kind or their value estimated at the date of payment. The possessor in good faith only owes them from the day of the claim.

However, every possessor has the right to reimbursement of necessary and useful expenses for the conservation of the property within the limit of the added value provided.

###### Article 690

Articles 2401 et seq. are applicable during possession.

###### Section II: Holding

###### Article 691

When a person who holds property knows that the property is subject to a real right of which he is not the holder, he is a mere holder. Such is the case of the contractor to whom an object has been entrusted for repair, or of the usufructuary who holds the thing of the bare owner.

Holding is precarious and entails the obligation to return the thing to the holder of the real right that attaches to it under the conditions of the juridical act that gave rise to it.

###### Article 692

Article 685 paragraph three is applicable to the holder.

Possessory protection is granted to the holder against any person other than the one from whom he holds his rights.

###### Section III: The protection of possession and holding

###### Article 693

Possession is protected against disturbance that affects or threatens it.

Likewise, the holder is protected from disturbance that he suffers in the exercise of his right, caused by any person other than the one from whom he holds his rights.

##### Chapter III: The right of accession

###### Section I: The right of accession in relation to immovable things

###### Article 694

Ownership of the soil carries with it ownership of what is above and below.

Everything that is united with and incorporated into the thing belongs to the owner thereof.

###### Article 695

The owner may make above all plantations and constructions, within the limits imposed by laws, regulations and juridical acts, and below, all constructions and excavations that he deems appropriate, and draw from these excavations all the products they may provide, subject to modifications resulting from laws and regulations relating to mines, and laws and police regulations.

###### Article 696

All constructions, plantations and works on or within land are presumed to have been made by the owner at his expense and to belong to him, unless the contrary is proved.

The owner of the soil who has made constructions, plantations and works with materials that did not belong to him must pay their value estimated at the date of payment; he may also be ordered to pay damages, if appropriate. But the owner of the materials does not have the right to remove them.

###### Article 697

When plantations, constructions and works have been made by a possessor in good faith and with materials belonging to him, the owner of the land must compensate the latter for the lower of the two sums represented, at the date of payment, by the increase in value provided to the land or the cost of materials and labour, taking into account the state in which the said constructions, plantations and works are found. The possessor then benefits from a right of retention until full payment of the sum due.

When plantations, constructions and works have been made by a possessor in bad faith and with materials belonging to him, the owner of the land has the right either to retain ownership thereof under the conditions of the preceding paragraph, or to require the third party to remove them.

If the owner of the land requires the removal of the constructions, plantations and works, it is carried out at the expense of the third party, without any compensation for him; the third party may, in addition, be ordered to pay damages for any harm suffered by the owner of the land.

When plantations, constructions and works have been made by a holder, their fate is governed by the title that is at the origin of the possession. Failing that, only plantations, constructions and works made with the knowledge and awareness of the owner fall under the application of the first paragraph above.

###### Article 698

The movement of rivers or wadis that modifies riparian lands benefits riparian lands. The riparian owner on the opposite side cannot complain when he has, on his side, lost land as a result, except when a sudden force has carried away a considerable and recognizable part of riparian land, and remains identified at the place where it was carried; in this case, the owner of the removed part may claim his ownership, provided he acts within one year of the event.

###### Section II: The right of accession in relation to movable things

###### Article 699

The right of accession, when it concerns two movable things belonging to two different owners, is entirely subject to the principles of natural equity.

The following rules shall serve as an example to the judge in determining, according to particular circumstances.

###### Article 700

There are three kinds of movable incorporation.

Adjunction, which is the act of uniting one movable object to another movable object for the purpose of use, ornament or completion of the first. Such is the case of property used to personalize cars or motorcycles.

Specification, which is the act by a person of using material that does not belong to him and creating a new object from it. Such is the case of a person who takes pieces of wood and makes a table from them.

Mixture, which is the act of forming a thing by the union of several materials such that the resulting material can no longer be separated. Such is the case when two metals are mixed.

###### Article 701

In case of adjunction, the newly created property reverts in its entirety to the person whose thing was the most important in value and, failing that, in volume, regardless of whether the two things would be separable from one another. In return, the other person shall receive compensation.

It is otherwise if the thing united to the other is much more valuable than the principal thing and the operation was carried out without the knowledge of its owner, the latter may request that the united thing be separated to be returned to him, even when some damage to the thing to which it was joined might result.

###### Article 702

In case of specification, ownership of the new property reverts to the owner of the materials against remuneration for the work performed, except when the work clearly exceeds the value of the material used.

###### Article 703

In case of mixture, division of separable materials may be requested by the owner without whose knowledge the mixture was made. Failing that, ownership shall be common to the persons concerned, in proportion to the quantities. But when there is a manifest disproportion of the mixed quantities, the accessory shall again follow the principal.

###### Article 704

In all cases where property has been used without the knowledge of its owner, the latter has the choice of requesting the return of his material in the same nature, quantity, weight, measure and quality, or its value estimated at the date of return.

##### Chapter IV: Collective ownerships

###### Section I: Ordinary undivided ownership

###### Article 705

Undivided ownership is the situation in which several persons hold a real right of the same nature over the same property or the same mass of properties. None of these persons can then claim an exclusive right over the property.

This right may be ownership or another real right.

###### Article 706

Undivided ownership is governed by articles 933 et seq. (legal undivided ownership) and 2071 et seq. (conventional undivided ownership).

###### Section II: Co-ownership of built immovables divided into lots

###### Article 707

Co-ownership of built immovables divided into lots is a combination of private ownership, on the one hand, and co-ownership, on the other hand. Ownership of the immovable is divided into lots each comprising a private part, such as an apartment, and a share of the common parts of the immovable. Co-ownership of built immovables divided into lots is governed by the texts that govern it.

#### Titre III

Of usufruct, use and habitation, special real rights, emphyteusis and superficies rights

Chapitre Ier: Of usufruct

###### Section I: General provisions

###### Article 708

Usufruct is the real right to use and enjoy things owned by another, as the owner himself, but with the obligation to preserve their substance.

###### Article 709

Usufruct is established by law, or by the will of man.

###### Article 710

The will of the parties expressed in the constitutive act determines the starting point of the usufruct right. Usufruct is temporary and terminates in accordance with the provisions of Section IV below, which govern its duration.

###### Article 711

Usufruct may be established over any kind of property or collection of property, movable or immovable, corporeal or incorporeal.

###### Section II: Of the mutual obligations of the bare owner and the usufructuary

###### Article 712

An inventory of the property subject to usufruct and their condition is drawn up, at the latest at the time the usufructuary takes possession. The latter may only take possession after having had the inventory drawn up, in the presence of the owner, or having duly summoned him.

In case of disagreement between them, the inventory is carried out by an independent professional chosen by mutual agreement and, failing that, appointed by the president of the civil chamber of the court of first instance, ruling by order on the merits.

The usufructuary takes the things in the state in which they are.

###### Article 713

The owner may not, by his act, nor in any manner whatsoever, harm the rights of the usufructuary.

###### Article 714

Unless otherwise agreed, the owner is liable for all major works and repairs, namely works relating to the structure and general solidity of the building such as the repair of load-bearing walls, dikes, retaining walls and fences in their entirety, or also, the restoration of beams or roofing, also in their entirety.

All other repairs are maintenance repairs.

###### Article 715

Maintenance and conservation works, like other periodic expenses, are the responsibility of the usufructuary.

If major repairs are the responsibility of the owner, it is otherwise when they have been caused by the lack of maintenance repairs, since the commencement of the usufruct. In this case, the usufructuary is liable for them. He is also liable for expenses made necessary by his abuse of enjoyment. In case of legal proceedings, the usufructuary is liable only for the costs of proceedings concerning the enjoyment, and other condemnations to which these proceedings might give rise.

###### Article 716

The usufructuary may not, upon termination of the usufruct, claim any compensation for improvements he may have made, even though the value of the thing may have been increased thereby. In this case, he may however, or his heirs, remove the improvements he has made to the property, but with the obligation to restore the premises to their original state.

###### Article 717

When the obligations provided for in the preceding articles are not respected, the other party may seize the judge so that he orders the one who is bound to carry out the necessary works and, failing that, to authorize him to have them carried out, at the expense of the one who has the responsibility.

He may also request from the judge authorization to constitute a security over the property, in order to guarantee, as the case may be, the financing of the works by the other, or the reimbursement of the sums expended.

###### Article 718

In case of usufruct with a simply determinable duration, the contract may provide that upon its termination, the owner may request from the usufructuary, a contribution to the expenses he has covered for major works. This contribution is calculated according to the value of the usufruct in relation to what its actual duration has been.

###### Article 719

Neither the owner, nor the usufructuary, is obliged to rebuild what has fallen from age, or what has been destroyed by fortuitous event.

###### Article 720

With regard to charges that may be imposed on the property during the duration of the usufruct, the usufructuary and the owner contribute to them as follows:

The owner is obliged to pay them, and the usufructuary must account to him for the interest; If they are advanced by the usufructuary, he has the recovery of the capital at the end of the usufruct.

###### Section III: Of the rights and obligations of the usufructuary

###### § 1. The rights of the usufructuary

###### Article 721

The usufructuary has the right to use and enjoy the property of which he has the usufruct.

The right of enjoyment covers all kinds of fruits that the property concerned may produce.

###### Article 722

The usufructuary exercises his right, either by himself, or by granting the use and enjoyment to others. He may transfer his right, for consideration or gratuitously, or encumber it with real securities. In this case, the right thus constituted terminates, at the latest, on the date provided for the transferred usufruct. The usufructuary may not constitute any other real right over the property than use and habitation.

The constitution or renewal of leases subject to commercial or rural lease statutes, as well as those constituting a real right, may only be carried out with the agreement of the owner. Other leases may be concluded by the usufructuary alone, but if they subsist upon termination of the usufruct, the owner is bound only for the current period and, unless his written agreement, for a maximum duration of six years for immovable leases and three years for movable leases.

###### Article 723

The usufructuary uses and enjoys all the rights which the owner may use and enjoy, and he uses and enjoys them as the owner himself.

###### Article 724

He also uses and enjoys, in the same manner as the owner, the products of the exploitation of the property subject to usufruct; such is the case with mines and quarries that are in operation at the commencement of the usufruct. Nevertheless, if it is an exploitation that cannot be made without a concession, the usufructuary may only use and enjoy it after having obtained permission from the President of the Republic.

He has no right to mines and quarries not yet opened, nor to treasure that might be discovered during the duration of the usufruct.

###### Article 725

Unless otherwise agreed, natural and industrial fruits, hanging by branches or by roots at the time the usufruct is opened, belong to the usufructuary.

Those that are ripe at the time the usufruct ends belong to the owner, without compensation on either side for plowing and seeds.

###### Article 726

Unless otherwise agreed, the revenues provided by the property, such as rents, interest and dividends whose distribution has been voted, are acquired day by day.

###### § 2. The obligations of the usufructuary

###### Article 727

The usufructuary uses and enjoys the property subject to usufruct in a manner consistent with the destination of the property. If, during the duration of the usufruct, a third party commits any usurpation on the land, or otherwise infringes the rights of the owner, the usufructuary is obliged to report it to him; failing which, he is liable for all damage that may result to the owner, as he would be for damage committed by himself.

Upon termination of the usufruct, he returns the property to its owner, subject to the provisions specific to special usufructs.

###### Article 728

If the usufruct is established only on an animal that dies without fault of the usufructuary, the usufructuary is not required to provide another one, nor to pay its estimated value.

If the herd on which a usufruct has been established perishes entirely by accident or by disease and without fault of the usufructuary, the usufructuary is only required towards the owner to account for the hides, or their estimated value at the date of restitution. However, if the herd does not perish entirely, the usufructuary is required to replace, up to the amount of the increase, the animals that have perished.

###### Article 729

The usufructuary must provide sufficient security for compliance with the obligations mentioned in the preceding article, unless exempted by law, the constitutive act of the usufruct, or by the owner. However, the following are exempted: the father and mother having the legal usufruct of the property of their children, as well as the seller or donor with reservation of usufruct.

###### Article 730

If the usufructuary does not find security, the immovable property is leased or placed under sequestration;

The sums included in the usufruct are invested;

The commodities are sold and the price resulting therefrom is similarly invested;

The interest on these sums and prices belongs, in this case, to the usufructuary.

###### Article 731

In the absence of security from the usufructuary, the owner may require that the movable property that deteriorates through use be sold, so that the price may be invested like that of the commodities.

###### Article 732

Delay in providing security does not deprive the usufructuary of the fruits to which he may be entitled; they are due to him from the moment the usufruct was opened.

###### Article 733

The universal or general usufructuary and the owner are liable for the estate debts in proportion to their respective value of the usufruct and the bare ownership. They contribute thereto in the same proportions, unless otherwise agreed.

###### Article 734

The particular usufructuary is not liable for the debts that burden the property.

###### Article 735

If the usufructuary fails to comply with his obligations, either by committing waste on the property or by allowing it to deteriorate for lack of maintenance, the owner may seize the court to pronounce the forfeiture of the right of usufruct.

The creditors of the usufructuary may intervene in the proceedings for the preservation of their rights; they may propose to substitute themselves for him in the performance of his obligations and by providing all guarantees.

The judges may, according to the seriousness of the circumstances, either pronounce the absolute extinction of the usufruct, or order the owner's return to enjoyment of the object that is encumbered thereby, only subject to the obligation to pay annually to the usufructuary, or to his successors in interest, a determined sum, until the time when the usufruct should have ceased.

###### Section IV : The Duration of Usufruct

###### Article 736

The usufruct is established for the life of its holder.

It may also be established for a determined or determinable duration. In this case, whether the duration of the usufruct is determined or determinable, it cannot exceed thirty years.

###### Article 737

The life usufruct is extinguished by the death of the usufructuary, natural person, or the dissolution of the legal entity when such person holds the right. When the usufruct is established in favor of a legal entity, it can never exceed thirty years.

The usufruct established for a determined or determinable duration is extinguished by the expiration of the time for which it was granted. When the usufruct has been granted until a third party has reached a fixed age, it lasts until that time, even if the third party dies before the fixed age.

Any usufruct is extinguished by the union in the same person of the two capacities of usufructuary and owner.

###### Article 738

In case of assignment of the right of usufruct, the right is extinguished:

- by the death or dissolution of the first holder and not by that of the assignee;
- by the non-use of the right for thirty years;
- by the total loss of the thing on which the usufruct is established, except by agreement of the usufructuary and the owner to transfer it to the thing representing that which has perished.

###### Section V : Special Usufructs

###### § 1. Quasi-usufruct

###### Article 739

If the usufruct includes consumable things, such as money, grain, the usufructuary has the right to use them, but subject to restoring to the owner, at the end of the usufruct, either things of the same quantity and quality, or their estimated value at the date of restitution.

###### Article 740

If the usufruct includes things which, without being consumed immediately, deteriorate gradually through use, such as linen, furnishings, the usufructuary has the right to use them for the purpose for which they are intended, and is only required to return them at the end of the usufruct in the state in which they are found, not deteriorated by his fault.

###### Article 741

If the constitutive act of the usufruct so provides, the usufructuary may dispose of any non-consumable movable property. The constitutive act then specifies the conditions under which restitution will occur. The usufructuary may reinvest the funds resulting from the alienation. The constitutive act may even require this of the usufructuary. The court may also, at the request of the owner, be seized for this purpose for the preservation of his rights. The reinvestment made may be proved by any means.

At the end of the usufruct, in the absence of contractual provision, the usufructuary restores to the owner either things of the same quantity and quality, or their estimated value at the date of restitution. If there has been reinvestment, he restores the property resulting therefrom or their estimated value at the same date. When the reinvestment has been made freely and spontaneously by the usufructuary, the latter restores the greater of the sums representing the current value of the property acquired in reinvestment or that of the property on which the quasi-usufruct had been initially established.

###### § 2. Usufruct of Claims

###### Article 742

The usufruct of a claim for a sum of money entitles the usufructuary to interest, as fruits. In case of repayment of the capital during his usufruct, the usufructuary exercises, unless otherwise agreed, his right over this capital in accordance with Article 739.

The usufruct of a life annuity gives the usufructuary, during the duration of his usufruct, the right to receive the arrears thereof, without being required to make any restitution.

###### § 3. Usufruct of Corporate Rights

###### Article 743

Dividends distributed as income belong to the usufructuary.

Unless otherwise agreed, the usufructuary exercises his right over other sums in accordance with Article 744, during the duration of his usufruct.

###### § 4. Usufruct of Property Forming a Whole

###### Article 744

Unless otherwise agreed, when the usufruct relates to property forming a whole, the usufructuary may dispose of each of its elements, but he shall do so by replacing them and in accordance with the purpose of that whole.

If compliance with the purpose of the whole jeopardizes his right, the usufructuary may request the court to adapt and modify that purpose.

##### Chapitre II : On Use and Habitation

###### Article 745

The right of use, like the right of use and habitation, is that which confers on its beneficiary, within the limits of his needs and those of his family, present and future, the personal use of a property and the collection of fruits.

These rights are established and lost in the same manner as usufruct.

They can be neither assigned nor leased.

###### Article 746

One cannot enjoy them, as in the case of usufruct, without previously providing security and without making statements and inventories.

###### Article 747

The user, and the person who has a right of habitation, must exercise their right reasonably and with respect for the normal purpose of the property.

###### Article 748

When the user uses the entirety of the land or receives all of its fruits, they are responsible for maintenance expenses and, more generally, periodic expenses that Article 715 places on the usufructuary.

If they take only a portion of the fruits or occupy only a portion of the property, they contribute in proportion to what they enjoy.

##### Chapitre III : Des droits réels spéciaux

###### Section I : Les droits réels conférés par des baux

###### Article 749

Certain contracts, such as emphyteutic leases or construction leases, confer on the lessee a real property right.

Such rights are transferable and susceptible to real property securities. They confer on their holder, during the duration of the contract, ownership of constructions, plantations, or installations, the realization of which they authorize.

These contracts are governed by the laws that establish them.

###### Section II : Le droit réel de jouissance spéciale

###### Article 750

The owner may grant, subject to rules of public order, one or more real rights conferring the benefit of special enjoyment of one or more of their properties.

###### Article 751

The real right of special enjoyment is established and extinguished in the same manner as usufruct.

It cannot be established in perpetuity, but may be granted for the lifetime of the person who benefits from it.

###### Article 752

The real right of special enjoyment, subject to the constitutive act, gives its holder all the rights that benefit the usufructuary and imposes, likewise, all the obligations.

It is always exercised with respect for the normal purpose of the property concerned.

###### Article 753

Subject to contractual provisions, the real right of special enjoyment is extinguished:

- by the expiration of the time for which it was granted;
- by non-use of the right for a duration established by the constitutive act and, failing that, for a reasonable period set by the judge;
- by the merger in the same person of the two capacities of holder of the real right of special enjoyment and owner;
- by the total loss of the thing on which the real right of special enjoyment relates.

##### Chapitre IV : De l'emphytéose

###### Article 754

The emphyteutic lease of immovable property confers on the lessee a real right susceptible to mortgage; this right may be transferred and seized in the forms prescribed for real property seizure.

This lease must be granted for more than eighteen years and cannot exceed ninety-nine years; it cannot be extended by tacit renewal.

###### Article 755

The emphyteutic lease can only be validly granted by those who have the right to alienate, and under the same conditions, as well as in the same forms.

Immovable property belonging to minors or to adults under guardianship may be given in emphyteutic lease by virtue of a deliberation of the family council.

When spouses are subject to the dotal regime, the husband may give in emphyteutic lease the dotal immovable property with the consent of the wife and judicial authorization.

Concerning premises for residential use, lease contracts concluded by the emphyteuta with tenants continue automatically with the owner of the immovable property until the term of each of the lease contracts as signed with the tenants.

###### Article 756

Proof of the emphyteusis contract is established in accordance with the rules of this code regarding leases.

###### Article 757

In the absence of contrary agreements, it is governed by the following provisions.

###### Article 758

The lessee cannot request a reduction of the rent due to partial loss of the land, nor due to sterility or deprivation of any harvest following fortuitous events.

###### Article 759

In the absence of payment for two consecutive years, the lessor is authorized, after a summons that remains without effect, to have the resolution of the emphyteusis pronounced in court.

Resolution may also be requested by the lessor in case of non-performance of the conditions of the contract or if the lessee has committed serious deterioration on the land.

Nevertheless, the courts may grant a delay depending on the circumstances.

###### Article 760

The lessee cannot free themselves from the rent, nor evade the performance of the conditions of the emphyteutic lease by abandoning the land.

###### Article 761

The lessee cannot make any change to the land that would diminish its value.
