These conservatory acts may be of a material nature, such as an act of occasional maintenance, or legal, such as formal notice to a debtor in default. They may be directed both against another co-owner and against a third party to the co-ownership.

The co-owner may use for this purpose the funds of the co-ownership held by them and is deemed to have free disposal thereof with regard to third parties.

In the absence of funds of the co-ownership, they may compel their co-owners to make with them the necessary expenses.

When undivided property is encumbered with a usufruct, these powers are enforceable against the usufructuary to the extent that the latter is liable for repairs.

###### Article 941

Co-owners may grant a mandate to one or more of them or to a third party to perform a specific act, which constitutes a special mandate, or even to handle all the affairs of the undivided property, which is a general mandate. A general mandate only permits acts of administration.

If one of the co-owners or a third party takes the initiative to manage the undivided property with the knowledge of the others and without opposition on their part, such person shall be deemed to have received a tacit mandate. This mandate only permits acts of administration; it covers neither acts of disposition nor the conclusion or renewal of leases. A co-owner who manages one or more undivided properties is liable for his or her management. He or she is entitled to remuneration for his or her activity under conditions fixed by agreement or, failing that, by court decision. If a co-owner or a third party performs an act useful to the undivided property without the conditions provided for in the preceding paragraphs being met, he or she is obliged to continue his or her management in accordance with the rules governing management of affairs.

###### Article 942

When the situation does not allow for granting a mandate, a co-owner may apply for judicial authorization:

1° Where another co-owner is unable to express his or her will: the applicant co-owner may have himself or herself authorized by the court to represent such co-owner, either generally or for certain specific acts. The court shall then determine the conditions and scope of the representation;

2° In case of refusal by one of the co-owners to give consent to an act deemed necessary by the applicant, where such refusal jeopardizes the common interest. However, it is not within the power of the judge to authorize the sale in full ownership requested by a bare owner when the usufructuary opposes it;

3° For all urgent measures required by the common interest.

In cases 2° and 3°, authorization is sought before the President of the Court of First Instance, who is seized and rules in summary proceedings. The President may, in particular, authorize a co-owner to collect from debtors of the undivided property or from depositaries of undivided funds a provision intended to meet urgent needs, prescribing, if necessary, the conditions of use. This authorization does not entail assumption of status for the surviving spouse or for the heir. He or she may also either appoint a co-owner as administrator, requiring him or her if necessary to provide security, or appoint a sequestrator, or prohibit the removal of movable property except to specify those of which he or she assigns personal use to one or the other of the beneficiaries, subject to their providing security if he or she deems it necessary.

###### Article 943

Where an undivided immovable property for residential use or for mixed residential and professional use is vacant or has not been effectively occupied for more than two calendar years, a co-owner may be authorized by the court to carry out improvement, rehabilitation and restoration works on the immovable property and to perform acts of administration and formalities of publication, for the sole purpose of leasing it as a principal residence.

###### Article 944

For this purpose, a co-owner may seize the President of the Court of First Instance to have himself or herself appointed as mandatory. The President shall fix the duration of his or her mission as well as his or her remuneration. At the request of the designated co-owner, the President may extend this mission for a period which he or she determines.

The appointment decision is registered and published in a journal authorized to receive legal publications.

###### Article 945

Within the limits of the powers conferred upon him or her, the designated co-owner represents all the co-owners for the acts provided for in Article 943. He or she exercises his or her powers even if there is a minor or a protected adult among the other co-owners.

The acts which he or she performs within the scope of his or her mission have no effect on the hereditary option of the co-owner designated as mandatory.

###### Article 946

At the request of any interested person or the public prosecutor, the President may remove the mandatory from his or her mission in case of a characterized failure in the exercise thereof. The President shall then appoint another mandatory, for a period which he or she defines.

###### Article 947

Each heir may require the mandatory to consult, at any time, the documents relating to the performance of his or her mission.

Each year and at the end of his or her mission, the mandatory submits to the judge and to each heir upon request a report on the performance of his or her mission.

The mission ceases automatically by the effect of an undivided property agreement that would be signed between the heirs or by the signing of the partition deed. It also ceases when the judge finds the complete performance of the mission entrusted to the estate mandatory.

###### § 3. Des droits et obligations des indivisaires

###### Article 948

Each co-owner has the same right of use and enjoyment over the undivided property as the others. The co-owners settle the division of this right among themselves. It is possible for them to grant to a co-owner an exclusive right of use or enjoyment over the thing, in exchange for compensation.

In the absence of agreement on the use of the undivided property, the president of the court shall settle the matter on a provisional basis. He or she is seized and rules by summary order.

###### Article 949

Each person is entitled to the benefits of the undivided property and bears the losses in proportion to his or her rights in the undivided property. No claim relating to fruits and revenues shall, however, be admissible more than five years after the date on which they were received or could have been.

Any person who receives revenues or incurs expenses on behalf of the undivided property must keep a record thereof which is available to the co-owners.

The fruits and revenues benefit the entire undivided property; they may however, by express agreement, be attributed to one of the co-owners.

Any co-owner may request his or her annual share in the benefits. In case of disagreement, the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance shall rule taking into account the extent of each person's rights in the undivided property.

###### Article 950

By operation of law undivided, by the effect of real subrogation, are the claims and indemnities which replace undivided property, as well as property acquired, with the consent of all the co-owners, in employment or re-employment of undivided property.

###### Article 951

Where a co-owner has improved at his or her own expense the condition of an undivided property, it must be taken into account according to equity, having regard to the amount by which the value of the property is increased at the time of partition or alienation. He or she must likewise be given credit for necessary expenses which he or she has incurred from his or her personal funds for the preservation of said property, even though they have not improved them.

Conversely, the co-owner is liable for degradations and deteriorations which have diminished the value of the undivided property by his or her act or fault.

###### § 4. On the right of pursuit of creditors

###### Article 952

The creditors of the undivided estate, being those who could have taken action against the undivided property before there was co-ownership and those whose claim arose from the management of the undivided estate or from acts of preservation of which they were the authors, shall be paid from the assets of the undivided estate before any partition and, if the undivided estate should not be sufficient to satisfy their rights, they may take action against each of the co-owners. The latter are jointly and severally liable for the balance. The creditors of the undivided estate may also pursue the seizure and sale of the undivided property.

The personal creditors of a co-owner may not seize either the undivided property or their debtor's share. On the other hand, they may seek partition in the name of their debtor or intervene in the partition that the latter has sought. The co-owners have, however, the power to halt the course of the action for partition by discharging the obligation owed by the debtor. Those who exercise this option shall reimburse themselves by drawing on the undivided property.

###### § 5. On applications for partition

###### Article 953

No one may be compelled to remain in co-ownership and partition may always be sought, except where there is a judgment or agreement to the contrary.

Co-owners who hold title to ownership, bare ownership or usufruct may agree to remain in co-ownership for a limited time: such agreement may not be binding beyond five years; but it may be renewed. Conventional co-ownership is subject to the rules of articles 2071 and following.

###### Article 954

Where several co-ownerships exist exclusively between the same persons, whether relating to the same property or to different property, a single partition may take place.

###### Article 955

Partition may be requested even when one of the co-heirs has separately enjoyed all or part of the undivided property, if there has been no act of partition, or sufficient possession to acquire title by prescription where it is admitted.

###### Article 956

If a minor, an adult under guardianship or curatorship, or a presumed absentee, is called to a partition, the latter may be done amicably.

In such case, the judge authorises the partition, even partial, and appoints, if necessary, a notary to proceed thereto, in the presence as the case may be of the representative or curator of the person referred to in the preceding paragraph or, if that person is himself interested in the partition, of his substitute appointed in accordance with article 143. The liquidation statement is subject to the approval of the judge.

The partition may also be done judicially in accordance with the provisions of articles 981 and following. Failing compliance with these conditions, the amicable partition is considered provisional.

###### Article 957

A spouse may not, without the consent of the other, proceed to the partition of property devolving to the latter which falls into the community. Any partition to which he proceeds alone, with respect to such property, is valid only as a provisional partition.

###### Article 958

The co-owner in usufruct may request the partition in kind of the undivided usufruct; if such partition in kind among the different usufructuaries is not possible, the usufruct may be sold. Where the sale of the usufruct alone cannot be envisaged under satisfactory conditions for the usufructuaries, the sale may relate to the full ownership provided that it appears to be the only measure capable of preserving the interests of all holders of rights in the undivided property.

###### Article 959

The same option belongs to the co-owner in bare ownership with respect to the undivided bare ownership. But in the case of sale of the full ownership, where the property is encumbered with a usufruct, such sale may not operate against the will of the usufructuary.

###### Article 960

Where a person is in co-ownership both in respect of the usufruct and of the bare ownership, he has the options provided for in the two preceding articles. The contrary will of a usufructuary, if he requests the sale of the property in full ownership, may not be set up against him.

###### Article 961

Where all parties agree on the partition, it is amicable; if one of the co-heirs refuses to consent to the partition, or if disputes arise either as to the manner of proceeding thereto, or as to the manner of completing it, the partition is judicial.

###### § 6. On preferential allocations

###### Article 962

Subject to a decision or agreement to maintain co-ownership, preferential allocation may be granted to the spouse or to any heir called to succeed by operation of law, whether he is a co-owner in full ownership or in bare ownership, under the conditions provided for by the following provisions. These provisions also benefit the heir having a universal or general title vocation to the succession by virtue of a will or a contractual institution.

###### Article 963

The surviving spouse or any co-owner heir may request preferential allocation by way of partition, subject to payment of equality money if appropriate, of any enterprise, or part of an agricultural, commercial, industrial, craft or professional enterprise or undivided share of such an enterprise, even formed in part from property of which he was already owner or co-owner before the death, in the operation of which he participates or has effectively participated. In the case of the heir, the condition of participation may be or have been fulfilled by his spouse or his descendants.

If appropriate, the application for preferential allocation may relate to company shares, without prejudice to the application of statutory provisions or clauses in the articles of association on the continuation of a company with the surviving spouse or one or more heirs.

###### Article 964

The surviving spouse or any co-owner heir may also request preferential allocation:

1° Of the ownership or right to the lease of the premises which effectively serves as his dwelling, if he had his residence there at the time of death, and of the furniture furnishing it, as well as of the deceased's vehicle provided that this vehicle is necessary for him for the needs of everyday life. This preferential allocation is automatic for the surviving spouse;

2° Of the ownership or right to the lease of the premises for professional use effectively serving for the exercise of his profession and of the movable objects for professional use furnishing such premises;

3° Of the ownership of any agricultural holding whose size in area makes it a family holding. Preferential allocation is automatic for the surviving spouse;

4° Of all the movable elements necessary for the operation of a rural property cultivated by the deceased in a professional capacity, where the lease continues for the benefit of the applicant, or where a new lease is granted to the latter.

The rights resulting from preferential allocation do not prejudice the life rights of habitation and use, or enjoyment, which the spouse may exercise by operation of law or by contract.

###### Article 965

If maintenance in indivision has not been ordered and in the absence of preferential allocation in ownership, provided for in the preceding articles, the surviving spouse or any co-owner heir may request the preferential allocation of all or part of the immovable property and rights with agricultural purpose forming part of the succession with a view to constituting, with one or more co-heirs and, if applicable, one or more third parties, an agricultural land grouping.

This allocation is of right if the surviving spouse or one or more of the co-heirs fulfilling the personal conditions provided for in articles 963 and 964, require that all or part of the property of the grouping be leased to them.

In case of multiple requests, the property of the grouping may, if its composition permits, be the subject of several leases benefiting different co-heirs; otherwise, and in the absence of an amicable agreement, the court designates the lessee taking into account the aptitude of the different applicants to manage the property concerned and to maintain themselves therein. If the clauses and conditions of this lease or these leases have not been the subject of an agreement, they are fixed by the court.

The immovable property and rights that the applicants do not contemplate contributing to the agricultural land grouping, as well as the other property of the succession, are allocated by priority, within the limits of their respective succession rights, to the co-owners who have not consented to the formation of the grouping. If these co-owners are not filled in their rights by the allocation thus made, a balancing payment must be paid to them. Except by amicable agreement between the co-partitioners, the balancing payment possibly due is payable within the year following the partition. It may be the subject of a dation in payment in the form of shares of the agricultural land grouping, unless the interested parties, within the month following the proposal made to them, have made known their opposition to this method of settlement.

The partition is only complete after the signature of the constitutive instrument of the agricultural land grouping and, if applicable, of the long-term lease or leases.

###### Article 966

If an agricultural operation constituting an economic unit and not operated in corporate form is not maintained in indivision and has not been the subject of a preferential allocation under the conditions provided for in the preceding articles, the surviving spouse or any co-owner heir who wishes to continue the operation in which he participates or has effectively participated may require, notwithstanding any request for sale by auction, that the partition be concluded on the condition that his co-partitioners grant him a long-term lease on the lands of the operation that fall to them. In the case of the heir, the condition of participation may be or have been fulfilled by his spouse or his descendants. Except by amicable agreement between the parties, the one who requests to benefit from these provisions receives by priority in his share the farm and dwelling buildings.

The foregoing provisions are applicable to a part of the agricultural operation that may constitute an economic unit. This economic unit may be formed, in part, of property of which the surviving spouse or the heir was already owner or co-owner before the death.

Account is taken, if applicable, of the depreciation due to the existence of the lease in the valuation of the lands included in the different lots.

If, by reason of the manifest inaptitude of the applicant or applicants to manage all or part of the operation, the interests of the co-heirs risk being compromised, the court may decide that there is no need to apply the first three paragraphs of this article.

###### Article 967

In the absence of an amicable agreement, the request for preferential allocation is brought before the court, which rules, except contrary provision, according to the interests at stake.

The preferential allocation may be requested jointly by several successors in order to preserve together the undivided property.

In case of multiple requests that are opposed concerning an operation or an enterprise, the court designates the allottee or the joint allottees according to the interests at stake and the aptitude of the different applicants to manage this operation or this enterprise and to maintain themselves therein and in particular the duration of their personal participation in the activity of the operation or the enterprise.

###### Article 968

The property subject to the allocation is valued at its value on the day of partition.

Except by amicable agreement between the co-partitioners, the balancing payment possibly due is payable in cash. However, when the allottee is the surviving spouse, he may require from his co-partitioners for the payment of a fraction of the balancing payment, equal at most to one-half, terms not exceeding ten years. Except contrary agreement, the sums remaining due bear interest at the legal rate.

In case of sale of the entirety of the allocated property, the fraction of balancing payment remaining due becomes immediately payable; in case of partial sales, the proceeds of these sales are paid to the co-partitioners and charged against the fraction of balancing payment still due.

###### Article 969

The beneficiary of the preferential allocation only becomes exclusive owner of the allocated property on the day of the final partition.

Until that date, he may only renounce the allocation when the value of the property, as determined on the day of this allocation, has increased by more than one-quarter on the day of the partition independently of his personal act.

###### § 7. On the constitution of shares and lots and the partition

A. Common provisions

###### Article 970

The partitionable mass includes the property existing at the opening of the succession, or those which have been subrogated thereto, and which the deceased has not disposed of by reason of death, as well as the fruits relating thereto. It is increased by the values subject to collation or reduction, as well as the debts of the co-partitioners towards the deceased or towards the indivision.

###### Article 971

The partition of undivided property is carried out per capita. However, it is done per stirpes when there is occasion for representation. Once the partition per stirpes is carried out, within each stirps, the partition is done, if applicable, per capita among the heirs of each stirps.

When a person dies, his heirs come to the succession of the one from whom he would have inherited if he had not died before him. The heirs come by representation of their author. Thus, the grandchildren succeed to their grandparents by representation of their father or mother who predeceased. These heirs by representation constitute "a stirps".

###### Article 972

When the debtor of a balancing payment has obtained payment terms, and when, as a result of economic circumstances, the value of the property placed in his lot has increased or decreased by more than one-quarter since the partition, the sums remaining due increase or decrease in the same proportion.

The parties may however agree that the amount of the balancing payment will not vary.

###### Article 973

Any person, even related to the deceased, who is not his successor, and to whom a co-heir would have transferred his right to the succession, may be excluded from the partition, either by all his co-heirs, or by one alone, by reimbursing him the price of the transfer.

This faculty granted to the co-heirs or to one of them to exclude from the partition any person not a successor to whom a co-heir would have transferred his right to the succession, also belongs to the undivided co-owner of an immovable, to the superficiary for the acquisition of the land, and to the owner of the land, for the acquisition of the superficies; any withdrawal indiscriminately must be exercised within a period of three months from the day when the sale was made public.

###### Article 974

In the formation and composition of lots with a view to partition, one must avoid fragmenting lands and dividing economic units and other groups of property whose division would result in depreciation.

B. Amicable partition

###### Article 975

Amicable partition may be total or partial. It is partial when it allows the co-ownership to continue with respect to certain property or certain persons.

###### Article 976

If all co-owners are present and capable, the partition may take place in the form and according to the methods chosen by the parties.

When the co-ownership relates to property subject to land registration, the deed of partition is executed by notarial deed.

###### Article 977

If a co-owner is presumed absent or, due to remoteness, is unable to express his will, an amicable partition may take place under the conditions provided for in article 146.

Likewise, if a co-owner is subject to a protective regime, an amicable partition may take place in compliance with the provisions of the titles On Minority, Guardianship and Emancipation and On Majority and Adults Protected by Law.

###### Article 978

If a co-owner is in default, without nevertheless being in one of the cases provided for in the preceding article, he may, at the initiative of a co-partitioner, be served notice, by extrajudicial act, to arrange representation at the amicable partition.

If such co-owner fails to appoint a representative within three months of the notice, a co-partitioner may request the president of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance to appoint any qualified person who shall represent the defaulting party until the complete completion of the partition. Such person may consent to the partition only with the authorization of the judge.

###### Article 979

The co-owners compose the lots at their convenience, and agree on the distribution of the lots among themselves. In the absence thereof, the lots once constituted shall be drawn by lot.

Each lot must, as far as possible, be composed, either in whole or in part, of movables or immovables, rights or claims of equivalent value, subject to compliance with the proportion of each person's rights in the co-ownership. In case of inequality of the lots constituted, such inequality is compensated, either by annuity or in money.

The equality of all in the partition, understood as the rights that each holds proportionally in the co-ownership, is a rule of public policy.

###### Article 980

The co-owners freely proceed with the valuations of the value of the undivided rights and property. The property is valued at its value on the date of divided enjoyment, taking into account, where applicable, the charges encumbering it. The determination of the day corresponding to the divided enjoyment of the property by the co-owners is the subject of a special clause in the deed of partition.

The date selected must be as close as possible to the partition. However, the judge may set the divided enjoyment at an earlier date if the choice of such date appears more favorable to the achievement of equality.

C. Judicial partition

###### Article 981

The partition is made in court when one of the co-owners refuses to consent to the amicable partition or if disputes arise regarding the manner of proceeding with or completing it or when the amicable partition has not been authorized or approved in one of the cases provided for in articles 977 and 978.

In such cases, the affixing of seals on the effects of the succession is carried out as soon as possible, either at the request of the heirs, or at the initiative of the public prosecutor at the Court of First Instance, or ex officio by the judge of the court within whose jurisdiction the succession is opened.

###### Article 982

Creditors may also request the affixing of seals, by virtue of an enforceable title or permission from the judge.

###### Article 983

When the seal has been affixed, all creditors may file opposition to it, even if they have neither an enforceable title nor permission from the judge. The formalities for the removal of seals and the preparation of the inventory are governed by the code of civil procedure.

###### Article 984

The action for partition and disputes that arise, either in connection with the maintenance of co-ownership or during partition operations, are subject to the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance of the place of opening of the succession which has exclusive jurisdiction to hear them. Any other judge must raise his lack of jurisdiction ex officio.

It is before this court that sales by auction are conducted and that applications relating to the warranty of lots between co-partitioners and those for nullity of the partition or for supplementary share must be brought.

###### Article 985

If it considers that the settlement of the partition is simple, the court orders the partition; if it appears complex to it, it appoints, on the one hand, a notary to carry out the partition operations and, on the other hand and from within its ranks, a judge to supervise such operations.

The notary certifies the property rights of each, establishes the accounts of the co-ownership, forms the mass to be partitioned and constitutes the lots.

If the appointed notary encounters the inertia of a co-owner, he serves notice on him, by extrajudicial act, to arrange representation. If the co-owner fails to appoint a representative within three months of the notice, the notary requests, without formality, the judge who appointed him to appoint any qualified person who shall represent the defaulting party until the complete completion of the operations.

###### Article 986

A co-owner may request that certain property be allocated to him preferentially. In case of opposition from another co-owner, the difficulty is decided by the judge in charge of supervising the operations. Such judge, for property that cannot be easily partitioned or allocated, orders the sale by auction of said property, under the conditions he determines.

###### Article 987

When the lots are constituted, each co-partitioner is allowed to submit his claims against their formation.

When the claims are resolved or decided by the judge, the notary proposes to the co-partitioners to agree on the allocation of the lots. In the absence thereof, a drawing by lot is conducted.

###### Article 988

At any time, the co-partitioners may abandon the judicial route to pursue the partition amicably if the conditions provided for a partition of this nature are met.

###### § 8. Judicial maintenance in co-ownership

###### Article 989

At the request of a co-owner, the court may stay the partition for up to two years if its immediate completion risks impairing the value of the undivided property or if one of the co-owners can take over the agricultural, commercial, industrial, craft or professional enterprise belonging to the succession only upon expiration of such period. Such stay may apply to all of the undivided property or to only some of it.

Where appropriate, the request for stay of partition may relate to corporate rights.

###### Article 990

In the absence of amicable agreement, the judge may order the maintenance in co-ownership of any agricultural, commercial, industrial, craft or professional enterprise, the operation of which was ensured by the deceased or by his spouse, as well as residential or professional premises actually used by the deceased or his spouse, and movable objects furnishing the residential premises or serving the exercise of the profession.

Where appropriate, the request for maintenance in co-ownership may relate to corporate rights.

###### Article 991

In all these cases, when there are one or more minor descendants, the application may be presented by the surviving spouse, by any heir or by the legal representative of the minor heirs; if there are no minor descendants, the action belongs to the surviving spouse alone.

Two conditions are then added: the surviving spouse must have had the status of co-owner of the property concerned, whether this status predated the death or is linked to it, and, in the case of residential premises, this surviving spouse must have resided in the premises at the time of death.

###### Article 992

The court rules according to the interests involved and the means of subsistence that the family can derive from the undivided property.

It may order the maintenance of the undivided ownership for up to five years, renewable as the case may be until the death of the surviving spouse and until the majority of the youngest of the descendants.

###### Article 993

When only one co-owner requests partition, the court may, at the request of one or more of the co-owners who wish instead to remain in undivided ownership, according to the interests involved and without prejudice to the application of articles 962 and following of this code, allocate after appraisal his share to the one who requested the partition, either in kind if this share is easily detachable from the rest of the undivided property, or in value.

If there is not a sufficient sum in the undivided estate, the balance is paid by those co-owners who have concurred in the application, without prejudice to the possibility for the other co-owners to participate, if they express their wish to do so. Each person's share in the undivided estate is increased in proportion to his payment.

###### Section II: Of reports, imputation and reduction of liberalities made to heirs

###### Article 994

Every heir, even having accepted the succession subject to an inventory, coming to a succession, must report to his co-heirs everything he has received from the deceased, by inter vivos donations, directly or indirectly; he cannot retain the gifts made to him by the deceased, unless they were expressly made to him outside the succession share.

Legacies made to an heir are deemed to be made outside the succession share, unless the testator has expressed a contrary intention, in which case the legatee may only claim his legacy by taking less.

###### Article 995

Gifts made outside the succession share cannot be retained nor legacies claimed by the heir coming to partition except up to the amount of the disposable portion: the excess is subject to reduction.

###### Article 996

The heir who renounces the succession may nevertheless retain the inter vivos gift or claim the legacy made to him up to the amount of the disposable portion, unless the disposer has expressly required the report in case of renunciation.

In this case, the report is made in value. When the reported value exceeds the rights he should have had in the partition had he participated, the renouncing heir compensates the accepting heirs for this excess.

###### Article 997

The donee who was not a presumptive heir at the time of the donation, but who is found to be an heir on the day of the opening of the succession, does not owe the report, unless the donor has expressly required it.

###### Article 998

Gifts and legacies made to the son or daughter of the one who is found to be an heir at the time of the opening of the succession are always deemed to be made with dispensation from report.

The father or mother coming to the succession of the donor is not required to report them.

###### Article 999

Similarly, the son or daughter coming in his own right to the succession of the donor is not required to report the gift made to his father or mother, even when he has accepted the succession; but if this child comes only by representation, he must report what had been given to his father or mother, even in the case where he has repudiated his succession.

###### Article 1000

Gifts and legacies made to the spouse of a spouse who is an heir are deemed to be made with dispensation from report. If gifts and legacies are made jointly to two spouses, of whom only one is an heir, the latter reports half; if the gifts are made to the spouse who is an heir, he reports them in full.

###### Article 1001

Report is only made to the succession of the donor.

###### Article 1002

Report is owed for what has been used for the establishment of one of the co-heirs or for the payment of his debts.

It is also owed in case of donation of fruits or revenues, unless the liberality was made expressly outside the succession share.

###### Article 1003

The costs of food, maintenance, education, apprenticeship, ordinary equipment costs, wedding costs and customary gifts, need not be reported, unless the disposer has expressed a contrary intention. The character of a customary gift is assessed at the date when it is granted and taking into account the fortune of the disposer.

###### Article 1004

It is the same for the profits that the heir has been able to derive from agreements made with the deceased, if these agreements presented no indirect advantage, when they were made.

###### Article 1005

Similarly, no report is owed for associations made without fraud between the deceased and one of his heirs, when the conditions have been settled by an authentic act.

###### Article 1006

Property that has perished by fortuitous event and without the fault of the donee is not subject to report. However, if this property has been reconstituted by means of compensation received due to its loss, the donee must report it in the proportion in which the compensation was used for its reconstitution.

If the compensation has not been used for this purpose, it is itself subject to report.

###### Article 1007

The fruits of things subject to report are only owed from the day of the opening of the succession.

Interest is only owed from the day when the amount of the report is determined.

###### Article 1008

Report is only owed by the co-heir to his co-heir; it is not owed to legatees or to creditors of the succession.

###### Article 1009

Report is made by taking less, thus the donee keeps the property received but takes, in return, less than the others in the mass to be shared in order to restore equality in figures, except in the case of the second paragraph of article 996.

It cannot be required in kind except by contrary stipulation in the deed of donation.

In the case of such a stipulation, the alienations and constitutions of real rights granted by the donee will be extinguished by the effect of the report unless the donor has consented to them.

###### Article 1010

The heir also has the option to report in kind the donated property that still belongs to him provided that this property is free of any charge or occupation with which it had not already been encumbered at the time of the donation.

###### Article 1011

Report is owed for the value of the donated property at the time of partition, according to its state at the time of the donation.

If the property has been alienated before partition, account is taken of the value it had at the time of alienation. If new property has been subrogated to the alienated property, account is taken of the value of this new property at the time of partition, according to its state at the time of acquisition. However, if the depreciation of the new property was, by reason of its nature, inevitable on the day of its acquisition, no account is taken of the subrogation.

All this unless otherwise stipulated in the deed of donation.

If it results from such a stipulation that the value subject to report is less than the determined value of the property, this difference forms an indirect advantage acquired by the donee outside the succession share.

###### Article 1012

The bringing back into hotchpot of a sum of money is equal to its amount. However, if it has been used to acquire property, the bringing back is owed of the value of such property, under the conditions provided in the preceding article.

###### Article 1013

When the bringing back is made in kind and the state of the gifted objects has been improved by the act of the donee, account must be taken of it, having regard to the increase in their value at the time of partition or alienation.

Account must likewise be taken of the necessary expenses the donee has made for the preservation of the property, even though they have not improved it.

###### Article 1014

The co-heir who makes the bringing back in kind may retain possession of the gifted property until the effective reimbursement of the sums owed to him for expenses or improvements.

###### Article 1015

The donee, for his part, must, in case of bringing back in kind, account for degradations and deteriorations that have diminished the value of the gifted property through his act or fault.

###### Section III: Payment of Debts

###### § 1. Debts of Co-partitioners

###### Article 1016

When the partible mass includes a claim against one of the co-partitioners, whether due or not, the latter is allotted it in the partition up to the extent of his rights in the mass.

To the corresponding extent, the debt is extinguished by confusion. If its amount exceeds the debtor's rights in this mass, he owes payment of the balance under the conditions and time limits that affected the obligation.

###### Article 1017

Except when it relates to undivided property, the claim is not due before the closing of partition operations. However, the debtor heir may decide at any time to discharge it voluntarily.

###### Article 1018

Amounts subject to bringing back bear interest at the legal rate, unless otherwise stipulated.

This interest runs from the opening of the succession when the heir was debtor thereof to the deceased and from the day when the debt becomes due, when it arose during the indivision.

###### Article 1019

When the co-partitioner himself has a claim to assert, he is allotted his debt only if, balance having been made, the account shows a balance in favor of the undivided mass.

###### § 2. Other Debts

###### Article 1020

The co-heirs contribute among themselves to the payment of debts and charges of the succession, each in proportion to what he takes therein.

###### Article 1021

The universal legatee contributes with the heirs, in proportion to his emolument; but the particular legatee is not liable for debts and charges, except however the hypothecary action on the immovable bequeathed.

###### Article 1022

When immovables of a succession are charged with annuities by special hypothec, each of the co-heirs may require that the annuities be reimbursed and the immovables made free before proceeding to the formation of lots.

If the co-heirs partition the succession in the state in which it is found, the charged immovable must be valued at the same rate as the other immovables; deduction is made of the annuity capital from the total price; the heir in whose lot this immovable falls remains alone charged with the service of the annuity and he must guarantee his co-heirs thereof.

###### Article 1023

The heirs are liable for the debts and charges of the succession, personally for their successoral share, and hypothecarily for the whole; subject to their recourse either against their co-heirs or against the universal legatees, by reason of the share for which they must contribute thereto.

###### Article 1024

The particular legatee who has discharged the debt with which the bequeathed immovable was charged remains subrogated to the rights of the creditor against the heirs and universal successors.

###### Article 1025

The co-heir or universal successor who, by effect of the hypothec, has paid beyond his share of the common debt, has recourse against the other co-heirs or universal successors only for the share that each of them must personally bear, even in the case where the co-heir who paid the debt has been subrogated to the rights of the creditors; without prejudice however to the rights of a co-heir who, by effect of the benefit of inventory, has retained the faculty to claim payment of his personal claim, like any other creditor.

###### Article 1026

In case of insolvency of one of the co-heirs or universal successors, his share in the hypothecary debt is apportioned among all the others, pro rata.

###### Article 1027

Executory titles against the deceased are likewise executory against the heir personally, eight days after service of these titles has been made to him.

###### Article 1028

The creditors of the deceased and legatees of sums of money may request to be preferred on the successoral assets over any personal creditor of the heir.

Reciprocally, the personal creditors of the heir may request to be preferred over any creditor of the deceased on the property of the heir not received by title of succession.

The right of preference gives rise to the privilege on immovables provided for in article 2354, and it is subject to registration.

###### Article 1029

This right of preference may be exercised by any act by which a creditor manifests to the competing creditor his intention to be preferred on a determined property.

The right of preference may not be exercised when the requesting creditor has renounced it.

###### Article 1030

The right of preference is prescribed, with respect to movables, by the lapse of three years.

With regard to immovables, the action may be exercised as long as they exist in the hands of the heir.

###### Article 1031

The creditors of a co-partitioner, to prevent the partition from being made in fraud of their rights, may oppose that it be proceeded with outside their presence: they have the right to intervene therein at their expense; but they may not attack a consummated partition, unless however it has been proceeded with without them and in prejudice of an opposition they had formed.

###### Section IV: Effects of Partition and Guarantee of Lots

###### Article 1032

Each co-divider is deemed to have succeeded alone and immediately to all the effects included in his lot, or devolved to him by licitation, and never to have had ownership of the other effects of the succession. The same applies to property that has come to him by any other act having the effect of terminating the indivision. No distinction is made according to whether the act terminates the indivision in whole or in part, with regard to certain property or certain co-dividers only.

However, acts validly performed either by virtue of a mandate from the co-dividers or by virtue of judicial authorization retain their effects whatever may be, at the time of partition, the attribution of the property that was the object thereof.

###### Article 1033

The co-dividers remain respectively guarantors, toward one another, of disturbances and evictions only that proceed from a cause prior to the partition. They are equally guarantors of the insolvency of the debtor of a debt placed in the lot of a co-partitioner, revealed before the partition.

The guarantee does not take place if the kind of eviction suffered has been excepted by a particular and express clause of the partition act; it ceases if it is by his fault that the co-divider suffers the eviction.

###### Article 1034

Each of the co-dividers is personally obligated, in proportion to his emolument, to indemnify the evicted co-divider for the loss he has suffered. This loss is evaluated on the day of eviction. If one of the co-dividers is found to be insolvent, the portion for which he is liable must be equally apportioned between the guaranteed party and all the solvent co-dividers.

###### Article 1035

The warranty action is prescribed by two years from the eviction or the discovery of the disturbance.

###### Section V: Actions for nullity of partition or for additional share

###### § 1. Actions for nullity of partition

###### Article 1036

The partition may be annulled on the grounds of violence or fraud.

It may also be annulled on the grounds of error, if such error related to the existence or the extent of the rights of the copartitioners or to the ownership of the property included in the partitionable estate.

The action for nullity is prescribed by five years from the discovery of the defect or the cessation of the violence.

However, if it appears that the consequences of the violence, fraud or error can be remedied otherwise than by the annulment of the partition, the court may, at the request of one of the parties, order a supplementary or rectifying partition.

###### Article 1037

The partition may also be annulled if one of the co-indivisors has been omitted.

The omitted co-indivisor may however request to receive his share, either in kind or in value, without annulment of the partition.

To determine this share, the property and rights which were the subject of the partition already carried out are revalued in the same manner as if it were a new partition.

###### Article 1038

The copartitioner who has alienated his lot in whole or in part is no longer entitled to bring the action for nullity for error, fraud or violence, if the alienation he has made is subsequent to the discovery of the error or fraud or to the cessation of the violence.

###### § 2. Action for additional share

###### Article 1039

When one of the copartitioners establishes, to his detriment, a lesion of more than one quarter, the additional share is provided to him, at the choice of the defendant, either in cash or in kind.

To judge whether there has been lesion, the objects are valued according to their value at the time of the partition, which corresponds to the date of divided enjoyment.

The action for additional share is prescribed by two years from the partition.

###### Article 1040

The action for additional share is allowed against any act whose purpose is to terminate the indivision, regardless of the qualification that the parties may have given to such act.

But after the partition, or the act which takes its place, the action for additional share is no longer allowed against the settlement made on the difficulties presented by such partition or such act.

###### Article 1041

The action is not allowed against a sale of succession rights made without fraud to an indivisor by his co-indivisors or by one of them, when the assignment includes an uncertainty defined in the act and expressly accepted by the assignee.

###### Article 1042

The mere omission of an object of the succession gives rise to a supplementary partition relating to such property.

#### Title II: Gifts inter vivos and wills

Chapter I: General provisions

###### Article 1043

A liberality is an act by which a person disposes gratuitously of all or part of his property or his rights for the benefit of another person.

A liberality may only take the form of these two categories of acts which are the gift inter vivos and the will.

###### Article 1044

The gift inter vivos is an act by which a person, the donor, transfers gratuitously to another person, the donee, who accepts it, the ownership of property.

The donor may, without being deprived of his liberal intent, impose on the donee the obligation to perform a specific service; the act is then called a gift with charges.

###### Article 1045

The will is an act by which the testator disposes, for the time when he will no longer exist, of all or part of his property, in full ownership or in the form of any other real right. If it is not full ownership, the right transmitted is only for the time provided in the act and in the absence of such provision, with regard to the legatee, the object of the legacy reverting, upon its extinction, to the succession of the testator.

The will may be revoked by the testator, but the revocation is only valid insofar as it has been made by authentic act or by an act entirely written and signed by the hand of the testator.

The legacy may, after the death of the testator and at the latest two months after the notification of the will to the legatee, be refused, totally or in part, by the latter or by his agent. The silence of the legatee during this period constitutes acceptance; if the legatee dies within this period, his heirs exercise the rights of their predecessor from the notification of the will made to them. The decision of the legatee is final, unless the heirs consent to his modifying it.

###### Article 1046

Any provision by which a person is charged with preserving and returning to a third party only produces effect in the case where it is authorized by law.

###### Article 1047

The father and mother may impose on the child whom they gratify the charge of preserving and handing over the property received to his own children.

A person without posterity may encumber a liberality granted to his brothers or sisters with a charge requiring them to transmit the property received to their children and thus ensure the maintenance of the property in the family.

However, clauses of inalienability affecting a given or bequeathed property are only valid if they are temporary and justified by a serious and legitimate interest. Even in this case, the donee or legatee may be judicially authorized to dispose of the property if the interest which had justified the clause has disappeared or if it happens that a more important interest requires it.

The provisions of this article do not prejudice liberalities granted to legal persons or even to natural persons charged with constituting legal persons.

Any clause by which the disposer deprives of the liberality the one who would challenge the validity of a clause of inalienability or request authorization to alienate is deemed unwritten.

###### Article 1048

Any gratified person may request that the conditions and charges encumbering the donations or legacies he has received be revised in court, when, as a result of a change in circumstances, the execution thereof has become for him either extremely difficult or seriously harmful.

The application for revision is made by principal action; it may also be made by way of counterclaim, in response to the action for execution or revocation that the heirs of the disposer have brought. It is made against the heirs and, at the same time, against the public prosecutor if there is doubt about the existence or identity of some of them; if there is no known heir, it is made against the public prosecutor. The latter must, in all cases, have communication of the matter.

The application is only admissible ten years after the death of the disposer or, in case of successive applications, ten years after the judgment which ordered the previous revision. The gratified person must justify the diligence he has undertaken, in the interval, to execute his obligations.

###### Article 1049

The judge seized of the application for revision may, according to the circumstances and even ex officio, either reduce in quantity or periodicity the services encumbering the liberality, or modify its object by drawing inspiration from the intention of the disposer, or even group them with similar services resulting from other liberalities. He may authorize the alienation of all or part of the property which is the subject of the liberality by ordering that the price will be used for purposes in relation to the will of the disposer.

He prescribes the measures appropriate to maintain, as far as possible, the designation that the disposer had intended to give to his liberality.

###### Article 1050

Third-party opposition to the judgment granting the application for review is admissible only in case of fraud attributable to the donee or legatee.

The retraction or reformation of the judgment challenged opens no right to any action against the third-party purchaser in good faith.

###### Article 1051

If, subsequent to the review, the performance of the conditions or charges, as originally provided, becomes possible again, it may be requested by the heirs.

###### Article 1052

The clause by which the maker of a liberality designates a beneficiary of second rank for the case where the beneficiary designated in the first place would have predeceased or, in case of survival, would refuse the liberality, is authorized.

The same applies to the inter vivos or testamentary disposition by which the usufruct will be given to one and the bare ownership to the other.

###### Article 1053

In every inter vivos or testamentary disposition, impossible conditions, those which are contrary to law or morals, shall be deemed unwritten.

If the thing bequeathed perishes before the death of the disposer, or if it is claimed after having been recognized as being the property of a third party, nothing is due to the donee or the legatee. If only a part of the thing bequeathed perishes or is claimed after having been recognized as being the property of a third party, the donee or the legatee receives the remainder.

##### Chapitre II : On the capacity to dispose or to receive by inter vivos donation or by will

###### Article 1054

Every person may dispose and receive, either by inter vivos donation or by will, except for persons whom the law declares incapable thereof. The maker of such liberality must be of sound mind. If the donation or will was given while the consent was vitiated by error, fraud or duress, the act is null.

The donation as well as the will made in favor of a foreigner is valid subject to the legal provisions in force.

###### Article 1055

The will made by a minor is valid, on condition of being approved by the judge.

###### Article 1056

To be capable of receiving inter vivos, it suffices to be conceived at the time of the donation.

To be capable of receiving by will, it suffices to be conceived at the time of the death of the testator. Nevertheless, the donation or will shall have effect only insofar as the child is born viable. When the testator dies before the delivery of the child already conceived at the date of the will and in whose favor the will was made, from the death of the testator until the delivery, the fruits shall be subject to conservatory measures.

###### Article 1057

The minor may not, even by will, dispose in favor of his guardian.

The minor, having become of age or emancipated, may not dispose, either by inter vivos donation or by will, in favor of the person who has been his guardian, if the final account of the guardianship has not been previously rendered and settled.

Excepted, in the two cases above, are the ascendants of minors, who are or who have been their guardians.

###### Article 1058

The members of medical professions and pharmacy, as well as medical auxiliaries who have provided care to a person during the illness from which he dies, may not benefit from the inter vivos or testamentary dispositions that he would have made in their favor during the course of that illness.

The judicial mandataries for the protection of adults and the legal persons on behalf of whom they exercise their functions may not similarly benefit from the inter vivos or testamentary dispositions that the persons whose protection they ensure would have made in their favor regardless of the date of the liberality.

Excepted are:

1° Remunerative dispositions made on a particular basis, having regard to the means of the disposer and the services rendered;

2° Universal dispositions, in the case of relationship up to the fourth degree inclusively, provided however that the deceased does not have heirs in direct line; unless the person for whose benefit the disposition was made is himself among those heirs.

The same rules shall be observed with regard to the minister of religion.

###### Article 1059

The inter vivos or testamentary dispositions, for the benefit of health establishments, medical-social establishments, or establishments of public utility, shall have effect only insofar as they have been authorized by decree.

However, inter vivos or testamentary dispositions for the benefit of foundations, places dedicated to worship and legally constituted associations and associations, are freely accepted by them. If it concerns religious establishments, the liberality is valid even if the disposer and the person who receives the property are not of the same faith.

###### Article 1060

Every disposition for the benefit of a person, natural or legal, subject to an incapacity to receive gratuitously, whether it is disguised in the form of an onerous contract, or whether it is made in the name of interposed persons is sanctioned by absolute nullity.

Shall be deemed interposed persons, until proof to the contrary, the father and mother, the children and descendants, as well as the spouse of the incapable person.

##### Chapitre III : On the hereditary reserve, the disposable portion, and reduction

###### Section I : On the hereditary reserve and the disposable portion

###### Article 1061

The hereditary reserve is the share of property and succession rights whose devolution free of charges the law ensures to certain heirs called forced heirs, if they are called to the succession and if they accept it. The beneficiaries of the reserve are:

- the descendants of the deceased, that is to say: children, grandchildren, great-grandchildren;
- in the absence of a descendant, the ascendants of the deceased, that is to say: father and mother, grandparents, great-grandparents;
- the surviving spouse, in the absence of descendants and ascendants.

The disposable portion is the share of property and succession rights which is not reserved by law and which the deceased was able to dispose of freely by liberalities.

###### Article 1062

The liberalities, whether by inter vivos acts or by will, may not exceed one-half of the property of the disposer, if he leaves at his death only one child; one-third, if he leaves two children; one-quarter, if he leaves three or a greater number;

The child who renounces the succession is included in the number of children left by the deceased only if he is represented or if he is bound to the return of a liberality in application of the provisions of article 900.

###### Article 1063

Included in article 1062, under the name of children, are descendants in whatever degree, even though they must be counted only for the child whose place they take in the succession of the disposer.

###### Article 1064

The liberalities, by inter vivos acts or by will, may not exceed three-quarters of the property if, in the absence of a descendant, the deceased leaves a surviving spouse, not divorced.

###### Article 1065

In the absence of a surviving spouse and heirs, the liberalities by inter vivos or testamentary acts may exhaust the totality of the property.

###### Article 1066

If the liberality consists of a usufruct or a life annuity whose value exceeds the disposable portion, the heirs for whose benefit the law makes a reserve, shall have the option, either to execute this disposition, or to make the abandonment of the ownership of the disposable portion.

###### Section II: On the reduction of excessive liberalities

###### Article 1067

The value in full ownership of property alienated, whether subject to a life annuity, for lost capital, or with reservation of usufruct to one of the successors in the direct line, is imputed on the disposable portion. Such acts are irrefutably reclassified as liberalities outside the successoral share. Any excess is brought back to the mass and therefore gives rise to reduction of the excessive liberality. This imputation and this reduction may only be requested by those other successors in the direct line who did not consent to these alienations.

###### Article 1068

The disposable portion may be given in whole or in part either by act inter vivos or by will, to the children or other successors of the donor, without being subject to contribution by the donee or the legatee coming to the succession, provided that with respect to donations the disposition was expressly made outside the successoral share.

The declaration that the donation is outside the successoral share may be made either by the act that will contain the disposition, or subsequently, in the form of inter vivos or testamentary dispositions.

###### Article 1069

Liberalities made as advancement of successoral share to a reserve heir who accepts the succession are imputed on his reserve share and, subsidiarily, on the disposable portion, if it has not been otherwise agreed in the act that provides for them. The excess is subject to reduction.

###### Article 1070

Liberalities made as advancement of successoral share to a reserve heir who renounces the succession are treated as a liberality made outside the successoral share.

However, when he is bound to contribution pursuant to the provisions of Article 900, the heir who renounces is treated as an accepting heir for the fictitious reunion of all the property of the deceased, the imputation and, where applicable, the reduction of the liberality that was granted to him. This principle is derogated from for:

- premiums of a life insurance policy taken out for the benefit of a specified third party, unless they prove to be manifestly excessive having regard to the means of the insured or the transaction was purely an investment;
- expenses for food, maintenance, education, apprenticeship, ordinary equipment expenses, wedding expenses and customary presents, which need not be contributed unless the disposer willed otherwise, in accordance with Article 1003;
- fruits and revenues accrued between the day of the donation and the death, in accordance with Article 1081.

###### Article 1071

The liberality made outside the successoral share is imputed on the disposable portion. The excess is subject to reduction.

###### Article 1072

The liberality made to a successor, or to successors jointly, that exceeds the disposable portion, may be retained in its entirety by the beneficiaries, whatever the excess, subject to compensating the co-heirs in money.

When the reducible portion does not exceed the reserve share of the interested party, he may always claim the totality of the objects bequeathed and therefore, execute the reduction in kind when the property donated or bequeathed still belongs to him and it is free of any charge with which it had not already been encumbered on the date of the liberality, as well as of any occupation of which it had not already been the object on that same date. This faculty is extinguished if he does not express his choice for this method of reduction within a period of three months from the date on which a reserve heir served notice on him to take a position.

###### Article 1073

When the value of inter vivos donations exceeds or equals the disposable portion, all testamentary dispositions shall lapse.

###### Article 1074

The reduction indemnity is calculated, in all cases, according to the value of the objects at the time of partition or alienation by the beneficiary and according to their state on the day the liberality took effect. If there has been subrogation, the calculation of the reduction indemnity takes into account the value of the new property at the time of partition, according to their state at the time of acquisition. However, if the depreciation of the new property was, by reason of their nature, inevitable on the day of their acquisition, the subrogation is not taken into account.

The reduction indemnity is payable at the time of partition, subject to agreement between the co-heirs. However, when the liberality has as its object one of the properties that may be the object of a preferential allocation, delays may be granted by the court, taking into account the interests involved, if they have not been granted by the disposer. The granting of these delays may not, in any case, have the effect of deferring payment of the indemnity beyond ten years from the opening of the succession. The provisions of Article 972 are then applicable to the payment of sums due.

In the absence of any agreement or stipulation to the contrary, these sums bear interest at the legal rate in civil matters. The advantages resulting from the delays and methods of payment granted do not constitute a liberality.

In the event of sale of the totality of the property donated or bequeathed, the sums remaining due become immediately payable; in the event of partial sales, the proceeds of these sales are paid to the co-heirs and imputed on the sums still due.

###### Article 1075

Liberalities, direct or indirect, that exceed the disposable portion, are reducible to that portion upon the opening of the succession.

###### Article 1076

Reduction of inter vivos dispositions may only be requested by those for whose benefit the law makes the reserve, by their heirs or assigns.

Donees, legatees, and creditors of the deceased may not request this reduction, nor profit from it.

The limitation period for the action for reduction is set at five years from the opening of the succession, or two years from the day on which the heirs became aware of the infringement on their reserve, without ever being able to exceed ten years from the death.

###### Article 1077

Reduction is determined by forming a mass of all property existing at the death of the donor or testator.

There are fictitiously reunited to it, after having deducted the debts, those of which he disposed by inter vivos donation according to their state at the time of the donation and their value at the opening of the succession. If the property has been alienated, account is taken of its value at the time of the alienation and, if there has been subrogation, of the value of the new property on the day of the opening of the succession according to their state at the time of acquisition; however, if the depreciation of the new property was, by reason of their nature, inevitable on the day of their acquisition, the subrogation is not taken into account.

There is calculated on all this property, having regard to the quality of the heirs he leaves, what is the portion of which the deceased was able to dispose.

###### Article 1078

Reduction of inter vivos donations presupposes that the value of all property included in the testamentary dispositions has been previously determined. Once the reunion of property has been accomplished, reduction is effected by beginning with the last donation, and so on going back from the last to the oldest.

###### Article 1079

When the testamentary dispositions exceed either the disposable portion, or the portion of that portion that would remain after having deducted the value of inter vivos donations, the reduction shall be made pro rata, without any distinction between universal legacies and particular legacies.

###### Article 1080

Nevertheless, in all cases where the testator has expressly declared that he intends that such legacy be satisfied in preference to the others, this preference shall take place; and the legacy which is the object thereof shall be reduced only to the extent that the value of the others would not fulfill the legal reserve.

###### Article 1081

When the reduction is carried out in kind, the donee restores the fruits of that which exceeds the available portion, from the day of the death of the donor if the demand for reduction has been made within the year; otherwise from the day of the demand.

###### Article 1082

The real rights created by the donee shall be extinguished by the effect of the reduction. These rights shall nevertheless retain their effects when the donor has consented thereto in the very act of creation or in a subsequent act. The donee shall then be liable for the resulting depreciation.

###### Article 1083

The action for reduction or revendication may be exercised by the heirs against third party holders of immovable property forming part of the donations and alienated by the donees, in the same manner and in the same order as against the donees themselves, and after prior discussion of their property. This action must be exercised according to the order of the dates of the alienations, beginning with the most recent. When the donor has consented to the alienation with the agreement of all forced heirs born and living at the time thereof, the action may no longer be exercised against the third party holders.

###### Article 1084

After prior discussion of the property of the debtor of the reduction indemnity and in case of insolvency of the latter, the forced heirs may exercise the action for reduction or revendication against third party holders of immovable property forming part of the liberalities and alienated by the donee. The action is exercised in the same manner as against the donees themselves and according to the order of the dates of the alienations, beginning with the most recent. It may be exercised against third party holders of movable property when article 2276 (number to be added when file No. 15 is numbered) cannot be invoked. When, on the day of the donation or subsequently, the donor and all presumptive forced heirs have consented to the alienation of the donated property, no forced heir, even born after the consent of all interested heirs has been obtained, may exercise the action against third party holders. With regard to bequeathed property, this action may no longer be exercised when the forced heirs have consented to the alienation.

###### Article 1085

Any presumptive forced heir may renounce, totally or partially, for example to target only the reduction of a liberality relating to a determined property, to exercise an action for reduction in an unopened succession, for the benefit of one or more determined persons. The renunciation binds the renouncer only from the day it has been accepted by the person from whom he has a vocation to inherit; but it cannot create obligations on the part of the person from whom one has a vocation to inherit or be conditioned upon an act emanating from the latter.

###### Article 1086

The act of renunciation is, on pain of nullity, established by specific authentic act received by two notaries and precisely mentions its future legal consequences for the renouncer. The renunciation may be made in the same act by several forced heirs, but they then sign separately before the notaries who receive the act.

The capacity required of the renouncer is that required to consent to a donation inter vivos. However, the emancipated minor may not renounce in advance the action for reduction.

The renunciation, whatever its modalities, does not constitute a liberality.

It is opposable to the representatives of the renouncer.

###### Article 1087

The renunciation produces no effect if the hereditary reserve of the renouncer has not been infringed. If the infringement of the hereditary reserve has been exercised only partially, the renunciation produces effects only up to the amount of the infringement of the reserve of the renouncer resulting from the liberality granted. If the infringement of the reserve relates to a fraction greater than that provided for in the renunciation, the excess is subject to reduction.

The renunciation relating to the reduction of a liberality relating to a determined property lapses if the liberality infringing the reserve does not relate to that property. The same applies if the liberality has not been made for the benefit of the determined person or persons.

###### Article 1088

The renouncer has the possibility to revoke his renunciation, but only in the following cases: 1° When the person from whom he has a vocation to inherit does not fulfill his maintenance obligations towards him; 2° When on the day of the opening of the succession, he is in a state of need which would disappear if he had not renounced his forced heirship rights;

3° When the beneficiary of the renunciation has been guilty of a crime or an offence against his person.

###### Article1089

In case of dispute, the renouncer seizes the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance, within one year from the day of the opening of the succession when the revocation is based on point 2° of the preceding article, and within one year from the fact imputed by the renouncer or from the day when the fact could be known by his heirs, if it is based on point 2° or 3° of the preceding article. The revocation in application of 2° of the preceding article is pronounced only up to the needs of the one who had renounced.

##### Chapitre IV: Of donations inter vivos

###### Section I: Of the conditions and effects of donations inter vivos

###### Article 1090

To be valid, any donation must be made by authentic act.

In case of defect of form, a donation inter vivos cannot be the object of confirmation: it must be remade in legal form.

After the death of the donor, the confirmation or voluntary execution of a donation by the heirs or successors in title of the donor entails their renunciation to oppose defects of form or any other cause of nullity.

###### Article 1091

The donation inter vivos shall not bind the donor, and shall produce no effect, except from the day it has been accepted in express terms.

The acceptance may be made during the lifetime of the donor by a subsequent and authentic act, of which a minute shall remain; but then the donation shall have effect, with regard to the donor, only from the day when the act which establishes this acceptance has been notified to him.

###### Article 1092

If the donee is of age, the acceptance must be made by him or, in his name, by a representative endowed with the express power to accept the donation made, or with a general power to accept donations which have been or could be made.

This power of attorney must be made before a notary; and a certified copy must be annexed to the minute of the donation or to the minute of the acceptance which would be made by separate act.

###### Article 1093

The donation made to an unemancipated minor or to a major under guardianship must be accepted by his guardian, in accordance with article 600, under the title Of minority, guardianship and emancipation. Nevertheless, the father and mother of the unemancipated minor, or the other ascendants, even during the lifetime of the father and mother, although they are not guardians of the minor, may accept for him.

###### Article 1094

The deaf-mute who knows how to write may accept himself or by a representative.

If he does not know how to write, the acceptance must be made by a curator appointed for this purpose, according to the rules established under the title Of minority, guardianship and emancipation.

###### Article 1095

Donations made for the benefit of the institutions referred to in Article 1059 shall be accepted by the administrators of these institutions, after having been duly authorized.

A donation made by a terminally ill patient is deemed to be a legacy.

###### Article 1096

A donation duly accepted shall be perfected by the mere consent of the parties; and the ownership of the donated objects shall be transferred to the donee, without the need for any other delivery.

If delivery of the donated thing has not taken place, the donee has the right to demand it.

###### Article 1097

When there is a donation of property capable of being mortgaged, the publication of the instruments containing the donation and acceptance, as well as the notification of acceptance that would have taken place by separate instrument, must be made at the mortgage registry office of the place where the property is located.

When the donation is made to minors, to adults under guardianship, or to public institutions, publication is made at the request of the tutors, curators or administrators.

###### Article 1098

The lack of publication may be raised by all persons having an interest, except however those who are charged with having the publication made, or their successors, and the donor.

###### Article 1099

Minors and adults under guardianship cannot request that the effects of the lack of acceptance or publication of donations not apply against them, even if the said tutors are found to be insolvent. Minors and adults under guardianship may however obtain compensation; against their tutors, at least if the abstention of the latter has caused them prejudice.

###### Article 1100

A donation inter vivos may only include the present property of the donor; if it includes future property, it is null in that respect.

###### Article 1101

Any donation inter vivos, made under conditions whose execution depends on the sole will of the donor, is null.
