The same applies to a donation made under the condition of discharging debts or charges other than those which existed at the time of the donation.

###### Article 1102

When the donor has reserved the liberty to dispose of a property included in the donation or of a fixed sum on the donated property, if he dies without having disposed of it, the said property or the said sum belongs to the heirs of the donor, notwithstanding any clause to the contrary.

###### Article 1103

The three preceding articles do not apply to donations mentioned in chapters VIII and IX of this title.

###### Article 1104

Any instrument of donation of movable property shall be valid only for the property of which an estimated statement, signed by the donor and the donee, or by those who accept for him, has been annexed to the original of the donation.

###### Article 1105

It is permitted to the donor to make a reservation for his benefit or to dispose, for the benefit of another, of the enjoyment or usufruct of the movable or immovable property donated.

###### Article 1106

When the donation of movable property is made with reservation of usufruct, the donee shall be required, at the expiration of the usufruct, to take the donated property that is found in kind, in the state in which it shall be; and he shall have action against the donor or his heirs, by reason of non-existing objects, up to the amount of the value that was given to them in the estimated statement.

###### Article 1107

The donor may stipulate the right of return of the donated objects either for the case of the predeceasing of the donee alone, or for the case of the predeceasing of the donee and his descendants.

This right may be stipulated only for the benefit of the donor alone.

###### Article 1108

The effect of the right of return is to resolve all alienations of the donated property, and to cause this property to return to the donor, free of all charges and mortgages, except however the mortgage of the spouses, if the other property of the donee spouse is not sufficient, and in the case only where the donation will have been made to him by the same marriage contract from which these charges and mortgages result.

###### Article 1109

The donor guarantees eviction only if he has intentionally concealed the cause of the eviction or if the donation was made with charges. In the first case, an equitable indemnity shall be awarded to the donee for the prejudice he has suffered; in the second case, the donor is liable only up to the value of the charges executed by the donee, all subject to contrary agreement.

In case of eviction, the donee is subrogated to the rights and actions of the donor.

###### Article 1110

The donor does not guarantee the defect of the donated thing.

However, if the donor has intentionally concealed the defect or if he has guaranteed its non-existence, he shall owe the donee reparation for the damage caused thereby. He shall also be liable for damages if the donation is made with charges, provided that the amount of damages does not exceed, in that case, the value of the charges executed by the donee.

###### Section II: Exceptions to the rule of irrevocability of donations inter vivos

###### Article 1111

A donation inter vivos may be revoked only for reason of non-performance of the conditions under which it was made, for reason of ingratitude, and for reason of supervening children.

###### Article 1112

In the case of revocation for reason of non-performance of conditions, the property shall return to the hands of the donor, free of all charges and mortgages from the donee; and the donor shall have, against third party holders of the donated immovables, all the rights that he would have against the donee himself.

###### Article 1113

A donation inter vivos may be revoked for reason of ingratitude only in the following cases:

1° If the donee has made an attempt on the life of the donor;

2° If he has become guilty towards him of cruelty, offenses or serious injuries;

3° If he refuses him sustenance.

###### Article 1114

Revocation for reason of non-performance of conditions, or for reason of ingratitude, shall never take place by operation of law.

###### Article 1115

The demand for revocation for reason of ingratitude must be brought within one year, from the day of the offense imputed by the donor to the donee or from the day that the offense could have been known by the donor. This revocation cannot be requested by the donor against the heirs of the donee, nor by the heirs of the donor against the donee, unless, in the latter case, the action was instituted by the donor, or he died within one year of the offense.

###### Article 1116

Revocation for reason of ingratitude does not prejudice either the alienations made by the donee, or the mortgages and other real charges that he may have imposed on the object of the donation, provided that all is prior to the publication, at the mortgage registry office of the location of the property, of the demand for revocation.

In the case of revocation, the donee is condemned to restore the value of the alienated objects, having regard to the time of the demand, and the fruits, from the day of this demand.

###### Article 1117

Donations in favor of marriage are not revocable for reason of ingratitude.

###### Article 1118

All donations inter vivos made by persons who had no children or descendants currently living at the time of the donation, of whatever value these donations may be, and under whatever title they were made, and even though they were mutual or remunerative, even those that would have been made in favor of marriage by persons other than the spouses to each other, may be revoked, if the instrument of donation so provides, by the supervening of a child born of the donor, even after his death, or adopted by him in the forms and conditions provided for in chapter I of title IX of book I.

###### Article 1119

This revocation may take place even though the child of the donor was conceived at the time of the donation.

###### Article 1120

The donation may similarly be revoked even if the donee has entered into possession of the donated property, and has been left there by the donor since the birth of the child. However, the donee is not required to restore the fruits he has received, of whatever nature they may be, except from the day on which the birth of the child or his adoption in full form was notified to him by writ or other act in due form, even if the claim to recover the donated property was made after this notification.

###### Article 1121

The property included in the revoked donation returns to the patrimony of the donor, free of all charges and mortgages from the donee, without being able to remain affected, even subsidiarily, by the mortgage of the spouses; this shall take place even if the donation was made in favor of the marriage of the donee and inserted in the contract, and the donor obligated himself as surety, by the donation, for the execution of the marriage contract.

###### Article 1122

The death of the donor's child is without effect on the revocation of donations provided for in Article 1118. The donor may renounce exercising the revocation for birth of a child, at any time, that is to say before or after the birth of the child.

###### Article 1123

The action for revocation is prescribed after five years from the birth or adoption of the last child.

It may only be exercised by the donor.

##### Chapitre V : Des dispositions testamentaires

###### Section I : Règles générales

###### Article 1124

Any person may dispose by will, either under the title of institution of heir, or under the title of legacy, or under any other denomination appropriate to manifest his will.

###### Article 1125

A will cannot be made in the same act by two or more persons, whether for the benefit of a third party or as a reciprocal or mutual disposition.

###### Article 1126

To be valid, the will must be made by an authentic act or by an act entirely written and signed by the hand of the testator.

###### Article 1127

The will by authentic act is received either by two notaries, or by one notary assisted by two witnesses who cannot be either the legatees, in whatever capacity, nor their relatives or relatives by marriage up to and including the fourth degree, nor the clerks of the notaries by whom the acts will be received. In both circumstances, the will is dictated by the testator and, as the case may be, one of the two notaries or the notary, writes it himself or has it written by hand or mechanically.

It is then obligatorily read to the testator.

When the testator cannot express himself in French or Arabic, the dictation and reading may be accomplished by an interpreter whom the testator chooses from the list of judicial experts provided for in Article L.356-6 of the Code of Civil Procedure. The interpreter ensures the exact translation of the statements made. The notary is not required to use an interpreter when he himself as well as, as the case may be, the other notary or the witnesses understand the language in which the testator expresses himself.

When the testator can write in French or Arabic but cannot speak, the notary writes the will himself or has it written by hand or mechanically from the notes written before him by the testator, then reads it to the latter. When the testator cannot hear, he takes knowledge of the will by reading it himself, after reading made by the notary. When the testator can neither speak or hear, nor read or write, the dictation or reading are accomplished, when possible, through a sign language interpreter and according to the same procedures. The act expressly mentions compliance with the above-mentioned requirements.

###### Article 1128

This will by authentic act must be signed by the testator in the presence, as the case may be, of the witnesses and the notary or the two notaries; if the testator declares that he does not know or cannot sign, the act bears his fingerprint.

It is also signed, as the case may be, by the witnesses and by the notary or the two notaries.

###### Article 1129

The mystic will is the will whose content remains hidden until the death of the person. When the testator wants to make a mystic will, the paper containing the dispositions or the paper serving as envelope, if there is one, is delivered closed, sealed and stamped, either to a notary before two witnesses, or to two notaries, or closed, sealed and stamped in their presence. The testator then declares that the content of this paper is his will, signed by him, and written by him or by another, affirming, in the latter case, that he personally verified the wording. He indicates, in all cases, the mode of writing he has employed (by hand or mechanical).

As the case may be, the notary or the notaries, write or have written by hand or mechanically on this paper or on the sheet that will serve as envelope intended to contain it, the date and indication of the place where the mystic will is executed, the description of the fold and the impression of the seal, and mention of all the above formalities; this act is signed both by the testator and by the notary and the witnesses, or by the two notaries. If the testator, either by an impediment occurring since the signature of the will, or because he does not know how to sign, has not been able to sign this act, mention is made of it as well as the reason he will have given.

All of these operations must be carried out in one continuous period and without interruption.

###### Article 1130

Those who do not know or cannot read cannot make dispositions in the form of a mystic will.

On the other hand, the testator who cannot speak but who knows how to write, may make a mystic will, with the express condition that the will be signed by him and written by him or by another, that he present it to the notary and the witnesses, or to the two notaries, and that at the top of the act of superscription he write, in their presence, that the paper he presents is his will, this before signing the act. As the case may be, the notary or the notaries, write on this act that the testator has written and signed these words in his presence and that of the witnesses, or in their presence. The provisions of Article 1129, except those contrary to this article, are applicable.

In all cases provided for in this article or in the preceding articles, the mystic will in which the legal formalities have not been observed, and which will be null as such, shall nevertheless be valid as a holographic will if all the conditions required for its validity as a holographic will are met, even if it has been qualified as a mystic will.

###### Article 1131

The witnesses called to be present at wills must be Djiboutian and of age, know how to sign and have the enjoyment of their civil rights. They may be of either sex, but the husband and wife may not be witnesses in the same act.

###### Article 1132

The testaments of military personnel, state sailors and persons employed with the armies may be received in the cases and conditions provided for in article 125 in one of the following forms: 1° by a senior officer or military physician of a corresponding rank, in the presence of two witnesses;

2° by two intendance officials or commissariat officers or by one of these officials or officers in the presence of two witnesses;

3° in case of an isolated detachment and if there does not exist in this detachment a senior officer or military physician of a corresponding rank, intendance official or commissariat officer, by the officer commanding this detachment assisted by two witnesses;

4° if the testator is sick or wounded and stays in a military hospital or medical formation, by the chief physician, whatever his rank, assisted by the administrative officer in charge. In the absence of this administrative officer, the presence of two witnesses is necessary.

The testament of the officer commanding an isolated detachment may be received by the officer who comes after him in the order of service.

The faculty to make a testament in the conditions provided for in this article extends to prisoners with the enemy. In all cases, a duplicate original of the testaments thus established is made. If this formality of the duplicate cannot be fulfilled due to the state of health of the testator, a copy of the testament is drawn up to serve in place of the second original; this copy is signed by the witnesses and by the instrumenting officers. Mention is made therein of the causes which prevented the drawing up of the second original. As soon as communication is possible, and within the shortest time, the two originals or the original and the copy of the testament are sent, separately and by different couriers, under sealed and closed envelope, to the Minister of Defense, to be deposited with the notary indicated by the testator or, in the absence of indication, with the president of the chamber of notaries.

The testament made in the form established above is null by operation of law six months after the testator has arrived in a place where he has the freedom to use the ordinary forms, unless, before the expiration of this period, he has been again placed in one of the special situations provided for in article 125. The testament is then valid during the duration of this special situation and for a new period of six months after its expiration.

All the formalities provided for must be observed on pain of nullity.

###### Article 1133

During a maritime voyage, both en route and during a stop in a port, when there is impossibility to communicate with the land or when there does not exist in the port, if one is abroad, a Djiboutian diplomatic or consular agent vested with the functions of notary, the testaments of persons present on board shall be received, in the presence of two witnesses:

1° on state vessels, by the administrative officer or, in his absence, by the commander or the person fulfilling his functions. The testament of the administrative officer is received by the commander or by the person fulfilling his functions, and, if there is no administrative officer, the testament of the commander is received by the person who comes after him in the order of service;

2° on other vessels, by the captain, master or skipper, assisted by the second of the ship, or, in their absence, by those who replace them. The testament of the captain, master or skipper, or that of the second, is received by the persons who come after them in the order of service.

The act indicates which of the circumstances provided for above in which it is received.

In all cases, a duplicate original of the testaments thus established is made. If this formality of the duplicate cannot be fulfilled due to the state of health of the testator, a copy of the testament is drawn up to serve in place of the second original; this copy is signed by the witnesses and by the instrumenting officers. Mention is made therein of the causes which prevented the drawing up of the second original. At the first stop in a foreign port where a Djiboutian diplomatic or consular agent is found, delivery is made, under sealed and closed envelope, of one of the originals or of the copy of the testament into the hands of this official, who sends it to the Minister of Defense, to be deposited with the notary indicated by the testator or, in the absence of indication, with the president of the chamber of notaries. And, upon the arrival of the vessel in a port of Djibouti, the two originals of the testament or the original and its copy, or the original which remains, in case of transmission or delivery made during the course of the voyage, shall be deposited, under sealed and closed envelope, for state vessels, at the armaments office, and for other vessels at the maritime registration office. Each of these documents shall be sent, separately and by different couriers, to the Minister of Defense, who shall transmit them as stated in the preceding paragraph.

The testament made during a maritime voyage, in the form prescribed by article 1132, shall be valid only insofar as the testator dies on board or within six months after he has disembarked in a place where he could redo it in the ordinary forms. However, if the testator undertakes a new maritime voyage before the expiration of this period, the testament is valid during the duration of this voyage and for a new period of six months after the testator has again disembarked.

All the formalities provided for must be observed on pain of nullity.

###### Article 1134

The provisions inserted in a testament made, during a maritime voyage, for the benefit of the officers of the vessel other than those who would be relatives or allied to the testator, are null and void.

###### Article 1135

The testator, in the cases of articles 1132 and 1133, is informed, in the presence of the witnesses, that his testament shall be null by operation of law six months after he has arrived in a place where he will have the freedom to use the ordinary forms, unless, before the expiration of this period, he is again placed in a situation which falls under the said articles.

###### Article 1136

On pain of nullity, testaments must be signed by the testator, by those who will have received them and by the witnesses.

If the testator declares that he cannot or does not know how to sign, mention shall be made of his declaration, as well as of the cause which prevents him from signing.

In the case where the presence of two witnesses is required, the testament shall be signed by at least one of them, and mention shall be made of the cause for which the other will not have signed.

###### Article 1137

A Djiboutian who is in a foreign country may make his testamentary dispositions by private instrument or by authentic act, with the forms customary in the place where this act will be executed. Such testaments made in a foreign country may be executed on property located in Djibouti only after having been registered at the office of the domicile of the testator, if he has retained one, otherwise at the office of his last known domicile in Djibouti. In the case where the testament would contain dispositions of immovable property which are located there, it must be, in addition, registered at the office of the location of this immovable property, without a double fee being required.

###### Section II: Of the institutions of heirs and legacies in general

###### Article 1138

Testamentary dispositions are either universal, or by universal title, or by particular title. Each of these dispositions shall produce its effect according to the rules hereinafter established for universal legacies, for legacies by universal title, and for particular legacies.

###### Article 1139

Unless the disposer wills otherwise, when the succession has been accepted by at least one heir designated by law, the legatee may limit his emolument to part of the property disposed of in his favour. This limitation does not constitute a liberality made by the legatee to the other successors. Unless the disposer wills otherwise, any person gratified with a legacy may decide to receive only part of the property provided, provided that the succession has been accepted by at least one heir designated by law. This decision of the legatee is not considered a liberality from the legatee to the other successors.

###### Sous-section 1 : Du legs universel

###### Article 1140

The universal legacy is the testamentary disposition by which the testator gives to one or more persons the universality of the property that he will leave at his death.

###### Article 1141

When at the death of the testator there are heirs to whom a portion of his property is reserved by law, these heirs are seised by operation of law, by his death, of all the property of the succession; and the universal legatee is required to request from them the delivery of the property included in the will.

Nevertheless, in the same cases, the universal legatee shall have the enjoyment of the property included in the will, from the day of death, if the request for delivery was made within the year from that time; otherwise, this enjoyment shall begin only from the day of the request made in court, or from the day that the delivery was voluntarily consented to.

###### Article 1142

When at the death of the testator there are no heirs to whom a portion of his property is reserved by law, the universal legatee shall be seised by operation of law by the death of the testator. If the will was executed by authentic act, he is not required to request delivery by a sending into possession; in the contrary case, the legatee is required to have himself sent into possession, by an order of the president, placed at the bottom of a petition, to which is attached the act of deposit.

###### Article 1143

Every will under private signature is, before being put into execution, deposited in the hands of a notary. The will is opened if it is sealed. The notary immediately draws up a report of the opening and of the state of the will, specifying the circumstances of the deposit. The will as well as the report are preserved among the minutes of the depositary.

Within the month following the date of the report, the notary sends a copy of the report and a reproduced copy of the will to the clerk of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance of the place of opening of the succession, who acknowledges receipt of these documents and preserves them among his minutes.

###### Article 1144

The universal legatee, who is in concurrence with an heir to whom the law reserves a portion of the property, is liable for the debts and charges of the succession of the testator, personally for his share and portion and by mortgage for the whole; and he is required to discharge all legacies, except in case of reduction, as explained in articles 1079 and 1080.

###### Sous-section 2 : Du legs à titre universel

###### Article 1145

The legacy by universal title is that by which the testator bequeaths a share of the property which the law permits him to dispose of, for example, a half, a third, or all his immovable property, or all his movable property, or a fixed portion of all his immovable property or of all his movable property.

Any other legacy constitutes only a disposition by particular title.

###### Article 1146

Legatees by universal title must request delivery from the heirs to whom a portion of the property is reserved by law; in their absence, from the universal legatees and, in the absence of the latter, from the heirs called in the order established in the title On Successions.

The delivery of legacies may be effected amicably; it may be recorded by act under private signature: a written, dated and signed document. However, an authentic act must be drawn up when immovable property is concerned. Whether it is an act under private signature or an authentic act, the delivery of legacies specifies the property that is concerned.

###### Article 1147

The legatee by universal title is liable, like the universal legatee, for the debts and charges of the succession of the testator, personally for his share and portion, and by mortgage for the whole.

When the testator has disposed of only a portion of the disposable portion, and he has done so by universal title, this legatee is required to discharge the particular legacies by contribution with the natural heirs.

###### Sous-section 3 : Des legs particuliers

###### Article 1148

Every pure and simple legacy gives to the legatee, from the day of the death of the testator, a right to the thing bequeathed, a right transmissible to his heirs or assigns.

Nevertheless the particular legatee cannot take possession of the thing bequeathed, nor claim the fruits or interest thereof, except from the day of his request for delivery, made according to the order established in the title On Successions, or from the day on which this delivery was voluntarily consented to him.

###### Article 1149

The interest or fruits of the thing bequeathed run in favour of the legatee, from the day of death, and without his having made his request in court:

1° When the testator has expressly declared his will, in this respect, in the will;

2° When a life annuity or a pension has been bequeathed as maintenance.

###### Article 1150

The costs of the request for delivery are chargeable to the succession, without however any reduction of the legal reserve resulting therefrom.

Registration fees are payable by the legatee.

All subject to contrary stipulation in the will.

Each legacy may be registered separately, without this registration being able to benefit anyone other than the legatee or his assigns.

###### Article 1151

The heirs of the testator, or other debtors of a legacy, are personally liable to discharge the legacy, each in proportion to the share and portion in which they will benefit from the succession.

They are liable, by mortgage for the whole, to deliver the thing bequeathed with the necessary accessories and in the state in which it will be found on the day of the death of the donor, up to the value of the immovable property of the succession of which they are holders. However, if he who has bequeathed the ownership of an immovable property has subsequently increased it by acquisitions, these acquisitions, even if they are contiguous, shall not be deemed, without a new disposition, to form part of the legacy. On the other hand, the embellishments, or new constructions made on the bequeathed land are necessarily included in the legacy.

###### Article 1152

If, before the will or since, the thing bequeathed has been subject to a real right by the testator, the legatee receives the bequeathed property in the state in which it is at the death of the disposer and he who must deliver the legacy is not required to discharge this property before delivering it.

###### Article 1153

When the testator has bequeathed the thing of another, the legacy is null, even if the testator did not know that it did not belong to him.

###### Article 1154

When the legacy relates to an undetermined thing, the heir is not obliged to give it of the best quality, and he cannot offer it of the worst.

###### Article 1155

The legacy made to the creditor is not deemed in compensation of his debt, nor the legacy made to the servant in compensation of his wages.

###### Article 1156

The legatee by particular title is not liable for the debts of the succession, except for the reduction of the legacy as stated above, and except for the mortgage action of the creditors.

###### Section III: Mandataries and testamentary executors

###### Article 1157

The heirs may, by common agreement, entrust the administration of the succession to one of them or to a third party. The mandate is governed by the provisions of articles 2175 and following.

When at least one heir has accepted the succession up to the amount of the net assets, the mandatary may not, even with the agreement of all the heirs, be designated except by the judge.

The judge may also be seized by any interested party or by the public prosecutor so that he designates a qualified person as successoral mandatary, for the purpose of provisionally administering the succession by reason of the inertia, default or fault of one or more heirs in this administration, their disagreement, an opposition of interests between them or the complexity of the successoral situation.

###### Article 1158

In the preceding cases, the mandate or the judge, as the case may be, fixes the duration of his mission of the appointed mandatary, the limit of his powers and his remuneration.

The appointment of a testamentary mandatary is subject to publication at the mortgage registry.

###### Article 1159

At the request of any interested party or the public prosecutor, the judge may divest the successoral mandatary, and designate another, when the first has failed in his mission.

The mission ceases by operation of law by the effect of an agreement of undivided ownership between the heirs or by the signature of the deed of partition. It also ceases when the judge notes the complete execution of the mission entrusted to the successoral mandatary.

###### Article 1160

As soon as the succession has been accepted by at least one heir, either purely and simply, or subject to inventory, the judge who designated the successoral mandatary may authorize him to perform all acts of administration of the succession.

He may also authorize him, at any time, to carry out acts of disposition necessary for the proper administration of the succession and determine the prices and stipulations thereof.

###### Article 1161

The testator may appoint one or more testamentary executors, enjoying full civil capacity, to ensure or proceed with the execution of his wishes.

The testamentary executor who has accepted his mission is required to fulfill it in the same capacity as a gratuitous mandatary. He assumes responsibility for it. He ensures that the testament is executed; and, in case of dispute over its validity or execution, he must be made a party or intervene as the case may be to support the validity or require the execution of the disputed provisions.

The testamentary executor exercises his mission gratuitously, except for a liberality made on a particular basis having regard to the means of the disposer and the services rendered.

###### Article 1162

The testator may authorize the testamentary executor to seize all or only part of the movable property of the succession, and to sell it if necessary to discharge the particular legacies within the limit of the disposable portion; this seizure may not last beyond one year and one day from the opening of the testament.

The heir may cause the seizure to cease by offering to deliver to the testamentary executors a sufficient sum for the payment of the movable legacies or by proving this payment.

###### Article 1163

In the absence of an accepting reserve heir, the testator may authorize, for a period of two years from the opening of the testament, the testamentary executor to dispose of all or part of the immovables of the succession, receive and invest capital, pay debts and charges and proceed with the attribution or partition of the remaining property between the heirs and the legatees.

On pain of unenforceability, the sale of an immovable of the succession may only occur after information of the heirs by the testamentary executor.

###### Article 1164

The authorizations provided for in the two preceding articles may, by decision of the judge, be extended by one year at most.

###### Article 1165

If there are several testamentary executors who have accepted their mission, only one may act in the absence of the others, unless the testator has provided otherwise or has divided their functions. In case of joint acceptance, they are jointly and severally liable for the account of the property entrusted to them.

###### Article 1166

The testamentary executor takes any conservatory measure useful for the proper execution of the testament. He may make, in the presence of the presumptive heir, or he duly called, the inventory of the property of the succession.

He provokes the sale of the movable property in the absence of sufficient liquidity to discharge the legacies and urgent debts of the succession.

###### Article 1167

In case of dispute over the validity or execution of the testament, the testamentary executor must be made a party or intervene as the case may be, to support the validity or require the execution of the disputed provisions.

###### Article 1168

The mission of the testamentary executor ends:

- upon completion of his mission;
- by decision of the judge, who relieves him of his mission for serious reasons;
- by his death, his powers not being transmissible to his heirs.

The testamentary executor renders account within six months following the end of his mission; in case of death, this obligation is imposed on his heirs.

###### Article 1169

The expenses incurred by the testamentary executor in the exercise of his mission are charged to the succession. He is reimbursed before the delivery of the legacies.

###### Section IV: Revocation of testaments and their lapse

###### Article 1170

Testaments may be revoked, in whole or in part, only by a subsequent testament or by an act before a notary declaring the change of will.

###### Article 1171

In the absence of express revocation, the testator is deemed to have tacitly revoked his testament: 1° By a subsequent testament whose provisions prove incompatible with the previous ones. In this case, the new provisions replace the old ones;

2° By the voluntary alienation of the thing bequeathed when the legacy is on a particular basis and has as its object a certain body, even if the alienation should subsequently be called into question, subject to the contrary will expressed by the testator in the act of alienation;

3° By the destruction or voluntary alteration of the testament. In case of erasure or tearing of only part of the paper containing the testamentary provisions, there is no revocation of the provisions mentioned on the preserved part, at least if these fulfill the conditions of form provided by law.

###### Article 1172

The revocation made in a subsequent testament has its full effect, even if this new act should remain without execution due to the incapacity of the instituted heir or the legatee, or by their refusal to receive the succession or the legacy.

The revocation of a testament does not restore the previously established testament in the absence of a will clearly manifested in this sense by the deceased.

###### Article 1173

Any testamentary provision lapses if the person in whose favor it is made does not survive the testator.

The same applies when the testamentary provision was made under a condition, and the instituted heir or legatee dies before the fulfillment of this condition, except in the case of a suspensive condition whose right was immediately acquired by the instituted heir, or the legatee and who, in this case, transmits this right to his heirs.

###### Article 1174

The testamentary disposition lapses:

1° If the bequeathed thing has totally perished during the testator's lifetime;

2° If the bequeathed thing has perished since the testator's death, without the act or fault of the heir, even though the heir has been put in delay to deliver it, when it would equally have perished in the hands of the legatee; 3° When the instituted heir or the legatee renounces it or is found incapable of receiving it.

###### Article 1175

In the absence of provision in the testamentary dispositions, the revocation, lapse or nullity of a legacy benefits the debtors of the revoked, lapsed or null legacy or legacies, that is to say, as the case may be, the heir, the universal legatee or the legatee of a universal portion. Thus, the ineffectiveness of a universal legacy benefits the heirs; in the absence of a forced heir, the ineffectiveness of a particular legacy benefits the universal legatee. By exception, the property included in the legacy deprived of effect may be transmitted to other legatees. There is thus accretion when the legacy has been made to several jointly. Two types of legacies are deemed joint within the meaning of this article, namely:

- the legacy made by one and the same disposition of the will and without assignment of shares to each of the co-legatees;
- the legacy, to several persons, of a thing that can be divided without deterioration.

###### Article 1176

After the testator's death, the legacies he had established may be judicially revoked if the legatee:

1° Has not performed the charges incumbent upon him;

2° Has attempted on the testator's life;

3° Has made himself guilty towards the testator of cruelty, offences or serious injuries;

4° Has uttered a serious insult against the testator's memory.

The action for revocation belongs to all those who have an interest in it: the testator's heirs, the universal legatees, and by oblique action the testator's creditors, heirs or legatees. The testamentary executor is also entitled to request revocation for non-performance of charges. On the other hand, the beneficiary of the legacy, as well as the beneficiary of the charge may only bring an action for performance.

In case 4°, the action must be brought within one year from the day of the offence.

##### Chapitre VI : Des libéralités graduelles et résiduelles

###### Section I : Des libéralités graduelles

###### Article 1177

A liberality may be burdened with a charge involving the obligation for the donee or legatee to preserve the property or rights that are the object thereof and to transmit them, upon his death, to a second gratified person, designated in the instrument.

###### Article 1178

The liberality thus granted may only produce its effect on property or rights identifiable at the date of the transmission and subsisting in kind at the death of the burdened person.

When it relates to securities, the liberality also produces its effect, in case of alienation, on the securities that have been subrogated thereto.

When it concerns immovable property, the charge burdening the liberality is subject to publicity.

###### Article 1179

The rights of the second gratified person open at the death of the burdened person.

However, the burdened person may abandon, for the benefit of the second gratified person, the enjoyment of the property or right object of the liberality.

This anticipated abandonment cannot prejudice the creditors of the burdened person prior to the abandonment, nor third parties having acquired, from the latter, a right on the property or right abandoned.

###### Article 1180

The second gratified person is deemed to hold his rights from the author of the liberality. The same applies to his heirs when they receive the liberality under the conditions provided for in Article 1066.

###### Article 1181

It is for the disposer to prescribe guarantees and securities for the proper performance of the charge.

###### Article 1182

The second gratified person cannot be subjected to the obligation to preserve and transmit.

If the charge has been stipulated beyond the first degree, it remains valid but for the first degree only.

###### Article 1183

If the burdened person is a forced heir of the disposer, the charge may only be imposed on the disposable portion.

The donee may however accept, in the deed of donation or subsequently in an instrument established by specific authentic act received by two notaries, that the charge burdens all or part of his reserved portion. The instrument is signed in the presence of the notaries alone and precisely mentions its future legal consequences for the donee, on pain of nullity.

The legatee may, within a period of one year from the day he became aware of the will, request that his share of the reserved portion be, in whole or in part, released from the charge. Failing this, he must assume its performance. The charge bearing on the reserved share of the burdened person, with his consent, benefits by operation of law, in this measure, all his children born and to be born.

###### Article 1184

The author of a gradual donation may revoke it with regard to the second gratified person as long as the latter has not notified, in the forms required for donation, his acceptance to the donor.

By derogation from Article 1091, the gradual donation may be accepted by the second gratified person after the donor's death.

###### Article 1185

When the second gratified person dies before the burdened person or renounces the benefit of the gradual liberality, the property or rights that were the object thereof form part of the estate of the burdened person, unless the instrument expressly provides that his heirs may receive it or designates another second gratified person.

###### Section II : Des libéralités résiduelles

###### Article 1186

It may be provided in a liberality that a person will be called to receive what will remain of the gift or legacy made to a first gratified person at the latter's death.

###### Article 1187

The residual liberality does not oblige the first gratified person to preserve the property received. It obliges him to transmit the remaining property.

When the property, objects of the residual liberality, have been alienated by the first gratified person, the rights of the second beneficiary do not transfer to the proceeds of these alienations nor to the new property acquired.

###### Article 1188

The first gratified person cannot dispose by will of the property given or bequeathed on a residual basis.

The residual liberality may prohibit the first gratified person from disposing of the property by inter vivos donation. However, when he is a forced heir, the first gratified person retains the possibility of disposing inter vivos or mortis causa of the property that has been given in advancement of successoral share.

###### Article 1189

The first gratified person is not required to account for his management to the disposer or his heirs.

###### Article 1190

The provisions set forth in Articles 1178, 1180, 1181, 1184 and 1185 are applicable to residual liberalities.

##### Chapitre VII : Des donations-partages et des testaments-partages

###### Section I : Dispositions générales

###### Article 1191

Any person may make, among his presumptive heirs, the distribution and partition of his property. This instrument may be made in the form of a donation-partition or a will-partition. It is subject to the formalities, conditions and rules prescribed for inter vivos donations in the first case and wills in the second, subject to the application of the provisions that follow.

###### Article 1192

Any person may also make the distribution and partition of his property and rights among descendants of different degrees, whether or not they are his presumptive heirs. The agreement of the forced heirs is then necessary.

###### Article 1193

The action for supplement of share for cause of lesion cannot be exercised against donation-partitions and will-partitions.

###### Article 1194

The provisions of Article 972, first paragraph, are applicable to balancing payments charged to donees, notwithstanding any provision to the contrary.

###### Article 1195

If all the property that the disposer leaves on the day of their death has not been included in the partition, those of their property that have not been included therein are allocated or partitioned in accordance with the law.

###### Section II: Gifts with partition

###### § 1. Gifts with partition made to presumptive heirs

###### Article 1196

A gift with partition may only have present property as its object.

The gift and the partition may be made by separate acts provided that the ascendant participates in both acts.

###### Article 1197

In case of a gift with partition made jointly by two spouses, the non-common child may be allotted from their parent in that parent's separate property or in common property, without the spouse being able, however, to be a co-donor of the common property.

###### Article 1198

Property received as an advance partition by a presumptive forced heir is chargeable to their reserved portion, unless it was expressly given in excess of their share.

###### Article 1199

The forced heir who did not participate in the gift with partition, or who received a lot less than their reserved portion, may exercise the action for reduction, if there do not exist at the opening of the succession property not included in the partition and sufficient to constitute or complete their reserved portion, taking into account the gifts from which they may have benefited.

###### Article 1200

Gifts with partition follow the rules of gifts inter vivos for everything concerning the charging, the calculation of the reserved portion and the reduction.

The action for reduction may only be brought after the death of the disposer who made the partition. In case of a gift with partition made jointly by both spouses, the action for reduction may only be brought after the death of the survivor of the disposers, except for the non-common child who may act from the death of their parent. The action is barred after five years from that death.

The child not yet conceived at the time of the gift with partition has a similar action to constitute or complete their hereditary share.

###### Article 1201

Notwithstanding the rules applicable to gifts inter vivos, the property given shall, unless otherwise agreed, be valued on the day of the gift with partition for the charging and calculation of the reserved portion, provided that all forced heirs living or represented at the death of the ascendant have received a lot in the advance partition and have expressly accepted it, and that no reservation of usufruct over a sum of money has been provided.

###### Article 1202

The lot of certain beneficiaries may be formed, in whole or in part, from gifts, either returnable or in excess of their share, already received by them from the disposer, having regard where applicable to the investments and reinvestments that they may have made in the interim.

The valuation date applicable to the advance partition shall also be applicable to previous gifts that have been thus incorporated into it. Any provision to the contrary is deemed unwritten.

###### Article 1203

The parties may also agree that a previous gift made in excess of their share shall be incorporated into the partition and charged to the reserved portion of the donee as an advancement of succession share.

###### Article 1204

The agreements referred to in the two preceding articles may take place even in the absence of new gifts from the disposer. They are not regarded as gifts between presumptive heirs, but as a partition made by the disposer.

###### § 2. Gifts with partition made to descendants of different degrees

###### Article 1205

When the ascendant proceeds with a gift with partition, their children may consent to their own descendants being allotted therein in their place and stead, in whole or in part.

Descendants of a subsequent degree may, in the advance partition, be allotted separately or jointly among themselves.

###### Article 1206

This gift constitutes a gift with partition even though the donor ascendant has only one child, whether the partition is made between the child and their descendants or between their descendants only. It requires the consent, in the instrument, of the child who renounces all or part of their rights, as well as of their descendants who benefit from it. The gift is void when the consent of the renouncer has been vitiated by error, fraud or duress.

###### Article 1207

When descendants of different degrees participate in the same gift with partition, the partition is made by root.

Allocations may be made to descendants of different degrees in certain roots and not in others.

###### Article 1208

Gifts with partition made to descendants of different degrees may include the agreements provided for in Articles 1202 to 1204.

###### Article 1209

In the succession of the donor ascendant, property received by children or their descendants as advance partition is charged to the reserved portion due to their root and subsidiarily to the disposable quotient.

All gifts made to members of the same root are charged together, regardless of the degree of relationship with the deceased.

When all the children of the donor ascendant have given their consent to the advance partition and no reservation of usufruct over a sum of money has been provided, the property with which the beneficiaries have been allotted is valued according to the rule provided in Article 1201.

If the descendants of a root have not received a lot in the gift with partition or have received only a lot less than their reserved portion, they are satisfied in their rights according to the rules provided by Articles 1199 and 1200.

###### Article 1210

In the succession of the child who consented to their own descendants being allotted in their place and stead, the property received by them from the ascendant is treated as if they held it from their direct parent. This property is subject to the rules applicable to gifts inter vivos for the notional reunion, the charging, the return and, where applicable, the reduction.

However, when all descendants have received and accepted a lot in the advance partition and no usufruct over a sum of money has been provided, the property with which the beneficiaries have been allotted is treated as if they had received it from their parent by gift with partition.

###### Article 1211

The rules laid down in Article 1210 do not apply when the child who consented to their own descendants being allotted in their place and stead subsequently proceeds themselves, with the latter, to a gift with partition into which the property previously received under the conditions provided in Article 1205 is incorporated.

This new gift with partition may include the agreements provided for in Articles 1202 and 1203.

###### Section III: Testamentary partitions

###### Article 1212

A testamentary partition produces the effects of a partition. Its beneficiaries may not renounce relying on the will to claim a new partition of the succession.

###### Article 1213

The beneficiary who has not received a lot equal to their reserved portion may exercise the action for reduction in accordance with Article 1200.

##### Chapter VIII: Gifts made by marriage contract to the spouses, and to children to be born of the

marriage

###### Article 1214

Any gift inter vivos of present property, although made by marriage contract to the spouses, or to one of them, shall be subject to the general rules prescribed for gifts made for that purpose.

It may not take place for the benefit of children to be born, except in the cases set out in Chapter VI of this Title.

###### Article 1215

Fathers and mothers, other ascendants, collateral relatives of the spouses, and even strangers, may, by marriage contract, dispose of all or part of the property they will leave on the day of their death, both for the benefit of said spouses and for the benefit of the children to be born of their marriage, in the event that the donor survives the donee spouse.

Such a donation, although made for the benefit only of the spouses or one of them, shall always, in said case of survival of the donor, be presumed made for the benefit of the children and descendants to be born of the marriage.

###### Article 1216

The donation in the form provided in the preceding article shall be irrevocable only in the sense that the donor may no longer dispose, by gratuitous title, of the objects included in the donation, except for modest sums, by way of reward or otherwise.

###### Article 1217

The donation by marriage contract may be made cumulatively of present and future property, in whole or in part, on condition that a statement of the donor's debts and charges existing on the day of the donation be appended to the deed; in which case, the donee shall be free, upon the death of the donor, to limit himself to the present property, renouncing the surplus of the donor's property.

###### Article 1218

If the statement mentioned in the preceding article has not been appended to the deed containing the donation of present and future property, the donee shall be obliged to accept or repudiate this donation for the whole. In case of acceptance, he may only claim the property that will be existing on the day of the donor's death, and he shall be subject to the payment of all debts and charges of the succession.

###### Article 1219

The donation by marriage contract in favor of the spouses and the children to be born of their marriage may also be made, on condition of paying indiscriminately all the debts and charges of the donor's succession, or under other conditions the execution of which would depend on his will, by whatever person the donation is made: the donee shall be bound to fulfill these conditions, unless he prefers to renounce the donation; and if the donor, by marriage contract, has reserved the liberty to dispose of an item included in the donation of his present property or of a fixed sum to be taken from this same property, the item or the sum, if he dies without having disposed of it, shall be deemed included in the donation and shall belong to the donee or his heirs.

###### Article 1220

Donations made by marriage contract may not be attacked or declared null on the pretext of lack of acceptance.

###### Article 1221

Any donation made in favor of the marriage shall lapse if the marriage does not follow.

###### Article 1222

Donations made to one of the spouses, in the terms of Articles 1215, 1217 and 1219 above, shall lapse if the donor survives the donee spouse and his posterity.

###### Article 1223

All donations made to the spouses by their marriage contract shall, upon the opening of the donor's succession, be reducible to the portion which the law permitted him to dispose of.

##### Chapitre IX: Provisions between spouses, either by marriage contract or during the marriage

###### Article 1224

The spouses may, by marriage contract, make reciprocally, or one of the two to the other, such donation as they see fit, subject to the modifications hereinafter expressed.

###### Article 1225

Any inter vivos donation of present property, made between spouses by marriage contract, shall not be deemed made under the condition of survival of the donee, if this condition is not formally expressed; and it shall be subject to all the rules and forms prescribed above for such donations.

###### Article 1226

The donation of future property, or of present and future property, made between spouses by marriage contract, whether simple or reciprocal, shall be subject to the rules established by the preceding chapter, with regard to similar donations that will be made to them by a third party, except that it shall not be transmissible to the children born of the marriage, in case of death of the donee spouse before the donor spouse.

###### Article 1227

The spouse, either by marriage contract or during the marriage, may, in the event that he would not leave any child or descendant, dispose in favor of the other spouse in ownership, of all that he could dispose of in favor of a stranger.

###### Article 1228

In the event that the spouse would leave children or descendants, whether or not born of the marriage, he may dispose in favor of the other spouse, either of the ownership of what he could dispose of in favor of a stranger, or of one quarter of his property in ownership and three other quarters in usufruct, or of the totality of his property in usufruct only.

Unless otherwise stipulated by the disposer, the surviving spouse may limit his emolument, that is to say accept only certain of the property disposed of in his favor. This limitation may not be considered as a liberality made to the other successors.

###### Article 1229

The children or descendants may, notwithstanding any contrary stipulation of the disposer, require, with regard to the property subject to the usufruct, that an inventory be made of the movables as well as a statement of the immovables, that the sums be invested and that the bearer securities be, at the choice of the usufructuary, converted into registered securities or deposited with an approved depositary.

###### Article 1230

The minor may not, by marriage contract, give to the other spouse, whether by simple donation or by reciprocal donation, except with the consent and assistance of those whose consent is required for the validity of his marriage; and, with this consent, he may give all that the law permits the adult spouse to give to the other spouse.

###### Article 1231

The donation of future property made between spouses during the marriage is always revocable.

The donation of present property taking effect during the marriage made between spouses is revocable only under the conditions provided for by Articles 1111 to 1116.

Donations made between spouses of present property or of future property are not revoked by the supervening of children.

###### Article 1232

If a spouse has made to his spouse, within the limits of Article 1228, a liberality in ownership, each of the children who are not born of the two spouses shall have, as far as he is concerned, unless contrary and unequivocal will of the disposer, the faculty to substitute for the execution of this liberality the abandonment of the usufruct of the share of succession that he would have received in the absence of a surviving spouse. Those who have exercised this faculty may require that the provisions of Article 1229 be applied.

###### Article 1233

The spouses may not give each other indirectly beyond what is permitted to them by the above provisions.

Any donation, either disguised or made to interposed persons, shall be null.

Shall be deemed made to interposed persons, donations from one of the spouses to the children or to one of the children of the other spouse born of another marriage, and those made by the donor to the relatives of whom the other spouse will be presumptive heir on the day of the donation, even if the latter has not survived his donee relative.

###### Article 1234

When a spouse acquires a property with money that has been given to him by the other for this purpose, the donation is only of the sums handed over and not of the property to which they are employed.

In this case, the rights of the donor or his heirs have as their object only a sum of money according to the current value of the property. If the property has been alienated, the value it had on the day of alienation is considered, and if a new property has been subrogated to the alienated property, the value of this new property.

#### Title III: Obligations

###### Article 1235

Obligations arise from juridical acts, juridical facts, or from the sole authority of the law. They may arise from the promise to perform a natural obligation or from the voluntary performance of such an obligation. The promise to perform a natural obligation constitutes a contract; the completed performance of a natural obligation cannot give rise to restitution once the performance has been voluntarily discharged.

###### Article 1236

Juridical acts are manifestations of will intended to produce legal effects. They may be a contract or a unilateral juridical act.

Juridical acts are governed, insofar as reasonable, as to their validity and effects, by the rules governing contracts.

###### Article 1237

Juridical facts are acts or events to which the law attaches legal effects. Obligations arising from a juridical fact are governed, as the case may be, by the sub-title relating to civil liability or the sub-title relating to quasi-contracts.

Sub-title I: The Contract

Chapter I: Preliminary Provisions

###### Article 1238

A contract is an agreement of wills between two or more persons intended to create, modify, transfer or extinguish obligations.

###### Article 1239

Everyone is free to contract or not to contract, to choose their contracting party and to determine the content and form of the contract, within the limits set by law.

Freedom of contract does not allow derogation from rules relating to public policy and good morals.

###### Article 1240

Legally formed contracts have the force of law for those who made them.

Contracts are in principle consensual.

By way of exception, the validity of solemn contracts is subject to compliance with forms determined by law, failing which the contract is null and void, except for possible regularization.

Furthermore, the law makes the formation of certain contracts subject to the delivery of a thing.

On the other hand, forms required for purposes of proof or enforceability have no effect on the validity of contracts.

###### Article 1241

When a writing is required for the validity of a contract, whether in the form of a private signature or by authentic act, it may be established and preserved in electronic form, provided that the person from whom it emanates can be duly identified and that it is established and preserved under conditions such as to guarantee not only its integrity but also the link between the electronic signature and the act to which it is attached.

The reliability of an electronic signature process is presumed until proven otherwise when that process implements a secure electronic signature, established by means of a secure electronic signature creation device and the verification of that signature is based on the use of a qualified electronic certificate.

When a written mention in the hand of the person who binds himself is required, the latter may affix it in electronic form if the conditions of such affixing are such as to guarantee that it can only be done by himself.

###### Article 1242

Exception is made to the provisions of the preceding article for:

1° Private signature acts relating to family law and succession;

2° Private signature acts relating to personal or real security interests, of a civil or commercial nature.

###### Article 1243

The requirement to send in multiple copies is deemed satisfied by electronic means if the writing can be printed by the recipient.

###### Article 1244

The requirement for a detachable form is satisfied by an electronic process that allows access to the form and its return by the same means.

###### Article 1245

Contracts must be negotiated, formed and performed in good faith.

This provision is a matter of public policy.

###### Article 1246

Contracts, whether they have a specific designation or not, are subject to general rules, which are the subject of this title.

The specific rules for certain contracts are established in the provisions specific to each of them; the general rules apply subject to these specific rules.

###### Article 1247

A contract is synallagmatic or bilateral when the contracting parties mutually bind themselves to each other, modify, transfer or extinguish obligations.

It is unilateral when one or more persons are bound to one or more others, without there being a reciprocal commitment from the latter.

###### Article 1248

A contract is commutative when each of the parties undertakes to provide the other with an advantage that is regarded as the equivalent of that which it receives.

It is aleatory when the equivalent consists in the chance of gain or loss for each of the parties, according to an uncertain event.

###### Article 1249

A contract is for valuable consideration when each of the parties receives from the other an advantage in return for that which it provides.

It is gratuitous or benevolent when one of the parties provides the other with an advantage without expecting or receiving anything in return.

###### Article 1250

A contract is consensual when it is formed by the mere exchange of consents without the expression of will having to take a particular form.

A contract is solemn when it requires for its validity, in addition to the agreement of wills, compliance with forms determined by law.

A contract is real when its formation is subject to the delivery of a thing.

###### Article 1251

A freely negotiated contract is one whose stipulations are freely negotiated between the parties. A contract of adhesion is one whose general conditions, removed from negotiation, are determined in advance by one of the parties who proposes them to the other.

###### Article 1252

A framework contract is an agreement by which the parties agree on the general characteristics of their future contractual relations. It subsequently incorporates implementation contracts, which specify the terms of performance.

###### Article 1253

A contract for immediate performance is one whose obligations can be performed in a single performance.

A contract for successive performance is one whose obligations of at least one party are performed in several performances staggered over time.

##### Chapter II: Formation of the Contract

###### Section I: Contractual Negotiation

###### Article 1254

The initiation, conduct and termination of pre-contractual negotiations are free. They must imperatively satisfy the requirements of good faith.

It is always possible to break off pre-contractual negotiations, except in case of abrupt termination or termination without legitimate reason.

In case of fault committed in the negotiations, the reparation of the damage is of an extra-contractual nature. In case of an agreement in principle, by which the parties undertake to continue a negotiation, to lead to the conclusion of a contract whose conditions remain to be defined, a contractual obligation to negotiate in complete good faith arises. Consequently, the termination of the negotiation must be justified. Failing this, damages may be awarded on the basis of contractual liability.

In all cases, the reparation granted cannot have the purpose of compensating for the loss of the expected benefits of the contract not concluded.

###### Article 1255

The party who knows information of decisive importance for the consent of the other must inform them of it when the latter legitimately does not know this information or trusts their co-contractor. Information of decisive importance is information that has a direct and necessary connection with the content of the contract or the quality of the parties; however, the duty to inform does not extend to the estimation of the value of the performance.

The parties may neither limit nor exclude this duty.

It is incumbent upon the person who claims that information was owed to them to prove that the other party owed it to them, with the burden on that other party to prove that they provided it.

In addition to the liability of the person who was bound by it, failure to comply with this duty to inform may result in the annulment of the contract under the conditions provided for in Articles 1283 and following.

###### Article 1256

Anyone who uses or discloses without authorization confidential information obtained during negotiations incurs liability under the conditions of common law.

###### Section II: The Meeting of Consents

###### § 1. The Offer and Acceptance

###### Article 1257

The contract is formed by the meeting of an offer and an acceptance by which the parties manifest their will to be bound.

A declaration of will, made expressly and without formality, is sufficient to be bound. The will to be bound may also be expressed tacitly or implicitly, when it results from unequivocal conduct of its author.

###### Article 1258

A proposal to conclude a contract, addressed to one or more specific persons or to an unspecified person, constitutes an offer if it is sufficiently precise and if it indicates the will of its author to be bound in case of acceptance.

A proposal is sufficiently precise when it contains the essential elements of the contemplated contract. Otherwise, there is only an invitation to enter into negotiations.

###### Article 1259

An offer takes effect as soon as it reaches its addressee. It is considered as having reached its addressee when it has been made verbally or when it has been delivered by any other means to the addressee themselves, to their principal place of business, or to their postal address. An offer may be freely revoked, provided that the revocation reaches the addressee before the latter has sent their acceptance. However, an offer cannot be revoked if it specifies that it is irrevocable or if it sets a specific time limit for its acceptance. Revocation of the offer in violation of this prohibition prevents the conclusion of the contract. It engages the extracontractual liability of its author under the conditions of common law without obliging them to compensate for the loss of the expected benefits of the contract.

An offer, even if irrevocable, terminates when its rejection reaches the author of the offer.

###### Article 1260

The offer lapses upon expiration of the time limit set by its author or, in the absence thereof, after a reasonable period.

It also lapses in case of incapacity or death of its author.

###### Article 1261

A declaration or any other conduct of the addressee indicating that they intend to be bound by the terms of the offer made, constitutes an acceptance.

The silence or inaction of the person claimed to be bound cannot alone, in the absence of any other circumstance, constitute proof against them of the alleged obligation. It is otherwise when the law, customs, business relations or particular circumstances give the value of acceptance to silence maintained.

###### Article 1262

When the author of the offer has set a time limit for acceptance in a letter, this time limit begins to run, unless otherwise indicated in the letter, from the day of the dispatch of the offer, the postal service stamp being proof thereof. The time limit for acceptance that the author of the offer sets by telephone, telex, fax, email or any other means of instantaneous communication begins to run at the moment when the offer reaches the addressee.

###### Article 1263

The law or the contract may provide, on the one hand, for a period of reflection for the benefit of the addressee of the offer, which is the period before the expiration of which the latter cannot manifest their acceptance, or on the other hand, for a period of retraction, which is the period before the expiration of which its beneficiary may retract their consent.

###### Article 1264

Acceptance takes effect at the moment when the agreement issued by the acceptor reaches the author of the offer. Acceptance does not take effect if this indication does not reach the author of the offer within the time limit they have stipulated or, in the absence of stipulation, within a reasonable time, taking into account the circumstances surrounding the contemplated transaction and the means of communication used by the author of the offer.

An acceptance is considered as having reached its addressee when it has been made verbally or when it has been delivered by any other means to the addressee themselves, to their principal place of business, or to their postal address.

A verbal offer must be accepted immediately, unless the circumstances imply otherwise.

###### Article 1265

A response that purports to be the acceptance of an offer, but which contains additional or different elements that do not substantially alter the terms of the offer, constitutes an acceptance. A response that purports to be the acceptance of an offer, but which contains additions, limitations or other substantial modifications to the terms of the offer, must be considered as a rejection of the offer and constitutes a counter-offer.

###### Article 1266

Acceptance may be freely retracted, provided that the retraction reaches the author of the offer before the moment when the acceptance would have taken effect.

###### Article 1267

General conditions invoked by a party have effect with regard to the other only if they have been brought to the knowledge of the latter and if the latter has accepted them.

In case of discrepancy between general conditions invoked by each of the parties, the incompatible clauses have no effect.

In case of discrepancy between general conditions and particular conditions, the latter prevail over the former.

###### Article 1268

The contract is concluded at the moment when the acceptance of an offer takes effect in accordance with these provisions, thus making the meeting of wills complete.

###### Article 1269

The contract is concluded at the place where the acceptance reached.

###### Article 1270

When it is concluded electronically, the contract is valid only if the addressee of the offer has had the possibility to verify the details of their order and its total price and to correct any errors before confirming it to express their final acceptance.

The author of the offer must acknowledge receipt without unjustified delay, electronically, of the order that has been addressed to them.

The order, the confirmation of acceptance of the offer and the acknowledgment of receipt are considered as received when the parties to whom they are addressed can have access to them.

###### § 2. Representation

###### Article 1271

Representation is the power recognized to a person, the representative, to act in the name and on behalf of another, the represented. The representative does not become a party to the contract.

This power is of legal, judicial or conventional origin. Conventional representation has its source in the contract of mandate.

This power is either special and for one matter or certain matters only, or general and for all matters of the represented. A mandate conceived in general terms embraces only acts of administration.

###### Article 1272

The legal, judicial or conventional representative is only authorized to act within the limits of the powers conferred upon them.

###### Article 1273

Representation is perfect when the representative acts within the limits of their powers and declares to act in the name and on behalf of the represented party. In this case, only the latter is bound by the commitment made and the contract entered into by the representative produces its effects directly, immediately and retroactively on the person of the represented party.

Representation is imperfect when the representative does not reveal to the third party the name of their principal. In this case, they alone are bound with regard to the contracting party.

###### Article 1274

The represented party is not bound by what has been done without power or beyond the power they gave to the representative. The same applies when the representative misuses their powers to the detriment of the represented party. The person who was unaware of the absence, excess or misuse of power, or could not have been unaware of it, may bring an action for relative nullity of the contract, without prejudice to damages that may, where appropriate, be claimed from the representative.

By exception, the represented party is bound by the concluded act when the contracting third party legitimately could have believed in the reality of the representative's powers, particularly due to the behavior or statements of the represented party.

These provisions do not exclude the application of rules specific to the management of affairs.

The represented party may ratify the act concluded without power or beyond the power given, or confirm the act performed through misuse of power. In these cases, the contract entered into by the representative produces its effects directly, immediately and retroactively on the person of the represented party.

###### Article 1275

The establishment of legal or judicial representation divests during its duration the represented party of the powers transferred to the representative.

Conventional representation leaves the represented party with the exercise of their rights.

###### Article 1276

The powers of the representative cease if they become incapable or are struck by incapacity during the execution of the mandate. These powers also end with the death of the representative.

###### Article 1277

A representative cannot act on behalf of both parties to the contract nor contract on their own account with the represented party.

The act performed is null and void, with relative nullity, solely due to the breach of the rule provided in the preceding paragraph, unless the law authorizes it or the represented party has authorized or ratified it.

###### Section III: The pact of preference and the unilateral promise to contract

###### Article 1278

The pact of preference is the promise made by one person to another, who accepts it, to offer them as a priority the conclusion of a contract of a determined nature, in the event that the promisor decides one day to conclude such a contract.

###### Article 1279

When a contract is concluded with a third party in violation of a pact of preference, the beneficiary of the pact may obtain compensation for the harm they suffer. If the third party knew of the existence of the pact and the beneficiary's intention to avail themselves of it, the latter may, in addition, ask the judge to annul the contract entered into with the third party and for their substitution for the third party in the concluded contract; they must bring this action within six months of becoming aware of the violation of the pact of preference.

The third party may request in writing from the beneficiary of the pact to confirm within a period of two months, the existence of a pact of preference and whether they intend to avail themselves of it. The writing mentions that in the absence of a response within this period, the beneficiary of the pact may no longer request their substitution for the contract concluded with the third party.

###### Article 1280

The unilateral promise to contract is the act by which one person, the promisor, commits to another, the beneficiary, who accepts it, to grant them, for a certain period, the right to opt for the conclusion of a contract whose essential elements are already determined, and for the formation of which only the consent of the beneficiary is lacking.

The definitive contract is formed as soon as the option is exercised. The revocation of the promise during the time left to the beneficiary to opt does not prevent the formation of the promised contract.
