However, for communities dissolved by divorce, legal separation or separation of property, preferential allocation is never a right, and it may always be decided that the totality of any equalizing payment due shall be payable in cash.

###### Article 1705

The spouse who has misappropriated or concealed any assets of the community is deprived of their portion in said assets. Likewise, the one who has knowingly concealed the existence of a common debt must assume it definitively.

###### Article 1706

After the partition is completed, if one of the two spouses is a personal creditor of the other, as when the price of their property has been used to pay a personal debt of their spouse, or for any other cause, they exercise their claim on the share that has fallen to them in the community or on their personal property.

###### Article 1707

Personal claims that the spouses have to exercise against each other do not give rise to withdrawal and bear interest only from the day of summons.

Unless otherwise agreed by the parties, these personal claims that the spouses have to exercise against each other are valued according to the rules of Article 1697, in the cases provided for therein; interest then runs from the day of liquidation.

###### Article 1708

Gifts that one of the spouses may have made to the other are executed only on the donor's share in the community and on their personal property.

###### § 3. Of the obligation and contribution to liabilities after dissolution

###### Article 1709

Each of the spouses may be sued for the totality of existing debts, on the day of dissolution, that had entered the community on their account.

###### Article 1710

Each of the spouses may be sued only for half of the debts that had entered the community on their spouse's account.

After partition and except in case of concealment, the spouse who is not personally bound is liable only up to the amount of their emolument, that is to say up to the amount of the active share of the community they receive, provided there has been an inventory, and subject to accounting for both the contents of that inventory and what has fallen to them by partition as well as the common liabilities already paid.

###### Article 1711

The inventory provided for in Article 1710 must take place in the forms regulated by the code of civil procedure, adversarially with the other spouse or with them duly summoned. It must be closed within nine months from the day the community was dissolved, except for extension granted by the summary proceedings judge. It must be affirmed sincere and true before the public officer who received it.

###### Article 1712

Each of the spouses contributes half to the community debts for which no recompense was due, as well as to the costs of sealing, inventory, sale of movables, liquidation, sale by auction and partition. When the debt was ultimately incumbent on only one of the spouses and the other spouse nevertheless contributed, the latter is entitled to corresponding recompense.

###### Article 1713

The spouse who may avail themselves of the benefit of Article 1710, second paragraph, does not contribute more than the active share of the community they receive, to debts that had entered the community on the other spouse's account, unless they are debts for which they would have owed recompense.

###### Article 1714

The spouse who has paid beyond the portion for which they were liable by application of the preceding articles has, against the other, recourse for the excess.

###### Article 1715

They do not have, for this excess, a right of recovery against the creditor, unless the receipt states that they intend to pay only within the limit of their obligation.

###### Article 1716

The one of the two spouses who, by the effect of the mortgage exercised on the immovable that fell to them in partition, is sued for the totality of a community debt, has by right recourse against the other for half of that debt.

###### Article 1717

The provisions of the preceding articles do not prevent that, without prejudice to the rights of third parties, a clause of the partition obligates one or the other of the spouses to pay a portion of debts other than that fixed above, or even to discharge the liabilities entirely.

###### Article 1718

The heirs of the spouses exercise, in case of dissolution of the community, the same rights as the spouse they represent and are subject to the same obligations.

###### Section II: Of the conventional community

###### Article 1719

The spouses may, in their marriage contract, modify the legal community by any kind of agreement not contrary to Articles 1633, 1635 and 1636.

They may, in particular, agree:

1° That the community shall include movables and acquisitions;

2° That the rules concerning administration shall be derogated from;

3° That one of the spouses shall have the right to withdraw certain property subject to compensation;

4° That one of the spouses shall have received sums or property outside their inheritance share;

5° That the spouses shall have unequal shares;

6° That there shall be between them universal community.

The rules of the legal community remain applicable in all points that have not been the subject of the parties' agreement.

###### Subsection 1: Community of movables and acquisitions

###### Article 1720

When the spouses agree that there shall be a community of movables and acquisitions between them, the common assets comprise, in addition to the property that would form part thereof under the legal community regime, the movable property of which the spouses had ownership or possession on the day of marriage or which has since devolved to them by succession or liberality, unless the donor or testator has stipulated otherwise. Nevertheless, those of these movable properties that would have formed separate property by their nature under Article 1651, under the legal regime, if they had been acquired during the community, remain separate. If one of the spouses had acquired immovable property after the marriage contract, containing a stipulation of community of movables and acquisitions, and before the celebration of the marriage, the immovable property acquired in that interval shall enter into the community, unless the acquisition was made in execution of some clause of the marriage contract, in which case it shall be governed according to the agreement.

###### Article 1721

Under this regime, the common liabilities include, in addition to the debts that would form part thereof under the legal regime, a fraction of those with which the spouses were already burdened when they married, or with which successions and liberalities that devolve to them during the marriage are charged.

The fraction of liabilities that the community must bear is proportional to the fraction of assets that it receives according to the rules of Article 1720, either in the spouse's patrimony on the day of marriage, or in the entirety of the property that is the subject of the succession or liberality.

For the establishment of this proportion, the composition and value of the assets are proved in accordance with Article 1649.

###### Article 1722

The debts for which the community is liable in consideration of the property it receives are its definitive charge.

###### Article 1723

The distribution of liabilities prior to the marriage or encumbering successions and liberalities cannot prejudice the creditors. They retain, in all cases, the right to seize the property that previously formed their security. They may even pursue their payment against the entirety of the community when the movable property of their debtor has been merged into the common patrimony and can no longer be identified according to the rules of Article 1649.

###### Subsection 2:Joint administration clause

###### Article 1724

The spouses may agree that they will jointly administer the community.

In that case, acts of administration and disposition of common property are made under the joint signature of both spouses. This dual signature entails by operation of law joint and several liability for the obligations undertaken. Conservatory acts may be done separately by each spouse.

###### Subsection 3: Withdrawal clause against compensation

###### Article 1725

The spouses may stipulate that the survivor of them or one of them if he or she survives, or even one of them in all cases of dissolution of the community, shall have the option of withdrawing certain common property, subject to accounting for it to the community according to the value it will have on the day of partition, unless otherwise agreed.

###### Article 1726

The marriage contract may fix bases of valuation and terms of payment of the potential balancing payment. Taking into account these clauses and in the absence of agreement between the parties, the value of the property shall be fixed by the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance.

###### Article 1727

The option of withdrawal lapses if the beneficiary spouse has not exercised it by notification made to the other spouse or to his or her heirs within one month from the day on which they have formally demanded that he or she take a position. This formal demand cannot itself take place before the expiration of the time limits provided in Article 906 for making an inventory and deliberating.

###### Article 1728

The withdrawal is a partition operation: the property withdrawn is charged against the share of the beneficiary spouse; if their value exceeds that share, a balancing payment is due. The spouses may agree that the compensation owed by the person making the withdrawal shall be charged subsidiarily against his or her rights in the succession of the predeceased spouse.

###### Subsection 4: Attribution to the spouse of sums or property outside the inheritance share

###### Article 1729

It may be agreed, in the marriage contract, that the survivor of the spouses, or one of them if he or she survives, shall be authorized to withdraw from the community, before any partition, either a certain sum, or certain property in kind, or a certain quantity of a specified kind of property.

###### Article 1730

This attribution outside the inheritance share is not regarded as a donation, either as to substance or as to form, but as a marriage contract and between associates.

###### Article 1731

When the community is dissolved during the lifetime of the spouses, there is no place for delivery of the sums and property whose attribution is provided outside the inheritance share; but the spouse in whose favor it has been stipulated retains his or her rights in case of survival, subject to Article 291.

He or she may require security from his or her spouse as guarantee of his or her rights.

###### Article 1732

The creditors of the community always have the right to have the property included outside the inheritance share sold, without prejudice to the spouse's recourse against the remainder of the community.

###### Subsection 5: Stipulation of unequal shares

###### Article 1733

The spouses may derogate from the equal partition established by law.

###### Article 1734

When it has been stipulated that the spouse or his or her heirs shall have only a certain share in the community, such as one-third or one-quarter, the spouse thus reduced or his or her heirs bear the debts of the community only in proportion to the share they take in the assets.

The agreement is void if it obliges the spouse thus reduced or his or her heirs to bear a greater share, or if it exempts them from bearing a share in the debts equal to that which they take in the assets.

###### Article 1735

The attribution of the entire community may only be agreed for the case of survival, either in favor of a designated spouse, or in favor of whoever will survive. The spouse who thus retains the totality of the community is obliged to pay all its debts.

It may also be agreed, for the case of survival, that one of the spouses shall have, in addition to his or her half, the usufruct of the share of the predeceased. In that case, he or she will contribute to the debts, as to the usufruct, according to the rules of Articles 714 and following of this code.

The provisions of Article 1731 are applicable to these clauses when the community is dissolved during the lifetime of both spouses.

###### Article 1736

The stipulation of unequal shares and the clause of full attribution are not deemed to constitute donations, either as to substance or as to form, but simply marriage contracts and between associates. Unless otherwise stipulated, they do not prevent the heirs of the predeceased spouse from recovering the contributions and capital that fell into the community from their predecessor.

###### Subsection 6: Universal community

###### Article 1737

The spouses may establish by their marriage contract a universal community of their property, both movable and immovable, present and future. However, unless otherwise stipulated, the property that Article 1651 declares separate by its nature does not fall into this community.

The universal community definitively bears all the debts of the spouses, present and future.

###### Section III: Common provisions to the first two sections of chapter II

###### Article 1738

The benefits that either spouse may derive from the clauses of a conventional community property regime, as well as those that may result from the pooling of movable property or debts, are not regarded as constituting donations.

Nevertheless, in the event that there are children who are not issue of both spouses, any agreement which would have the effect of giving to one of the spouses beyond the portion regulated by Article 1228, under the title Of Inter Vivos Donations and Wills, shall be without effect for the entire excess; but the simple benefits resulting from common work and from savings made on the respective incomes, though unequal, of the two spouses, are not considered as a benefit made to the prejudice of children from another marriage.

##### Chapter III: The separate property regime

###### Article 1739

When the spouses have stipulated in their marriage contract that they would be separate as to property, each of them retains the administration, enjoyment and free disposal of their personal property. Each of them remains solely liable for debts arising in their person before or during the marriage, except in the case of Article 228.

###### Article 1740

The spouses contribute to the charges of the marriage according to the agreements contained in their contract; and, if none exist in this regard, in the proportion determined in Article 222.

###### Article 1741

Both with regard to their spouse and to third parties, a spouse may prove by all means that they have exclusive ownership of property.

The presumptions of ownership stated in the marriage contract have effect with regard to third parties as well as in the relations between spouses, unless otherwise agreed. Proof to the contrary shall be as of right, and it shall be made by all means proper to establish that the property does not belong to the spouse whom the presumption designates, or even, if it belongs to them, that they acquired it through a liberality from the other spouse.

Property over which neither spouse can justify exclusive ownership is deemed to belong to them jointly, to each for one half.

###### Article 1742

If, during the marriage, one of the spouses entrusts to the other the administration of their personal property, the rules of mandate are applicable. The mandatary spouse is, however, exempt from accounting for the fruits, when the power of attorney does not expressly require it.

###### Article 1743

When one of the spouses takes over the management of the property of the other, with the knowledge of the latter, and nevertheless without opposition on their part, they are deemed to have received a tacit mandate, covering acts of administration and management, but not acts of disposal.

This spouse is liable for their management toward the other as a mandatary. They are, however, accountable only for existing fruits; for those which they would have neglected to collect or fraudulently consumed, they may be pursued only within the limit of the last five years.

If it is in defiance of a recorded opposition that one of the spouses has interfered in the management of the property of the other, they are liable for all the consequences of their interference, and accountable without limitation for all the fruits which they have collected, neglected to collect or consumed.

###### Article 1744

A spouse is not guarantor of the failure to invest or reinvest the property of the other, unless they have interfered in the operations of alienation or collection, or unless it is proven that the monies were received by them, or have been turned to their profit.

###### Article 1745

After the dissolution of the marriage by the death of one of the spouses, the partition of undivided property between spouses separate as to property, for everything concerning its forms, the maintenance of the undivided ownership and preferential attribution, the sale by licitation of property, the effects of partition, the warranty and the equalization payments, is subject to all the rules which are established under the title Of Successions for partitions between co-heirs.

The same rules apply after divorce or legal separation. However, preferential attribution is never as of right. It may always be decided that the totality of any equalization payment due shall be payable in cash.

###### Article 1746

The rules of Article 1707 are applicable to claims that one of the spouses may have to exercise against the other.

##### Chapter IV: The participation in acquests regime

###### Article 1747

When the spouses have declared that they are marrying under the participation in acquests regime, each of them retains the administration, enjoyment and free disposal of their personal property, without distinguishing between those which belonged to them on the day of the marriage or came to them since by succession or liberality and those which they acquired during the marriage for valuable consideration. During the duration of the marriage, this regime functions as if the spouses were married under the separate property regime. Upon dissolution of the regime, each of the spouses has the right to participate for one half in value in the net acquests recorded in the patrimony of the other, and measured by the double estimation of the original patrimony and the final patrimony.

The right to participate in acquests is inalienable as long as the matrimonial regime is not dissolved. If the dissolution occurs by the death of a spouse, their heirs have, over the net acquests made by the other, the same rights as their predecessor.

###### Article 1748

The original patrimony comprises the property which belonged to the spouse on the day of the marriage and that which they acquired since by succession or liberality, as well as all property which, in the legal community property regime, forms separate property by nature without giving rise to compensation. No account is taken of the fruits of this property, nor of that property which would have had the character of fruits or which the spouse disposed of by inter vivos donation during the marriage.

The composition of the original patrimony is proven by a descriptive statement, even under private signature, established in the presence of the other spouse and signed by them. In the absence of a descriptive statement or if it is incomplete, proof of the composition of the original patrimony may only be provided by the means of Article 1649.

###### Article 1749

The original property is valued according to its condition on the day of the marriage or of the acquisition, and according to its value on the day when the matrimonial regime is liquidated. If it has been alienated, its value on the day of the alienation is retained. If new property has been subrogated to the alienated property, the value of this new property is taken into consideration.

From the original assets are deducted the debts with which it was encumbered, revalued, if appropriate, according to the rules of Article 1697. If the liabilities exceed the assets, this excess is notionally added to the final patrimony.

###### Article 1750

All property which belongs to the spouse on the day when the matrimonial regime is dissolved forms part of the final patrimony, including, where applicable, that which they would have disposed of by reason of death and without excluding the sums of which they may be creditor toward their spouse. If there is divorce, legal separation or early liquidation of acquests, the matrimonial regime is deemed dissolved on the day of the application. The composition of the final patrimony is proven by a descriptive statement, even under private signature, which the spouse or their heirs must establish in the presence of the other spouse or their heirs or they being duly summoned. This statement must be drawn up within nine months of the dissolution of the matrimonial regime, except extension by the President of the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance ruling in summary proceedings. Proof that the final patrimony would have comprised other property may be provided by all means, even by testimony and presumptions.

Each of the spouses may, as to the property of the other, request the affixing of seals and the inventory according to the rules provided in the code of civil procedure.

###### Article 1751

To existing property are notionally added property that does not appear in the original estate and which the spouse has disposed of by inter vivos gift without the consent of his or her spouse, as well as property that he or she would have alienated fraudulently. Alienation in exchange for a life annuity or without return is presumed to be made in fraud of the rights of the spouse, if the latter has not consented to it.

###### Article 1752

Existing property is valued according to its condition at the time of dissolution of the matrimonial regime and according to its value on the day of liquidation thereof. Property that has been alienated by inter vivos gifts, or in fraud of the rights of the spouse, is valued according to its condition on the day of alienation and the value it would have had, if it had been preserved, on the day of liquidation.

From the assets thus reconstituted, all debts that have not yet been paid are deducted, including sums that might be owed to the spouse. The value, on the day of alienation, of improvements that had been made during the marriage to original property given by a spouse without the consent of his or her spouse before the dissolution of the matrimonial regime must be added to the final estate.

###### Article 1753

If the final estate of a spouse is less than his or her original estate, the deficit is borne entirely by that spouse. If it is greater, the increase represents the net acquests and gives rise to participation.

If there are net acquests on both sides, they must first be offset. Only the surplus is divided: the spouse whose gain has been the lesser is a creditor of his or her spouse for half of this surplus. To the participation claim are added, to subject them to the same settlement, the sums of which the spouse may otherwise be a creditor towards his or her spouse, for values provided during the marriage and other indemnities, deduction made, if applicable, of what he or she may be a debtor towards him or her.

###### Article 1754

The participation claim gives rise to payment in money. If the debtor spouse encounters serious difficulties in discharging it entirely upon closure of the liquidation, the judges may grant him or her delays that shall not exceed five years, on condition of providing security and paying interest. The amount of this interest is determined by mutual agreement and, failing that, the legal interest shall apply. The participation claim may however give rise to settlement in kind, either with the consent of both spouses, or by virtue of a decision of the judge, if the debtor spouse justifies serious difficulties that prevent him or her from discharging it in money.

The settlement in kind provided for in the preceding paragraph is considered as a partition operation when the property allocated was not included in the original estate or when the spouse receiving the allocation succeeds to the other.

The liquidation may not be enforced against the creditors of the spouses: they retain the right to seize the property allocated to the spouse of their debtor.

###### Article 1755

The creditor spouse pursues recovery of his or her participation claim first on existing property and, subsidiarily, beginning with the most recent alienations, on the property mentioned in article 1751 that had been alienated by inter vivos gift or in fraud of the rights of the spouse.

###### Article 1756

Upon dissolution of the matrimonial regime, if the parties do not agree to proceed with liquidation by agreement, one of them may request the Civil Chamber of the Court of First Instance to proceed with it.

Applicable to this request, insofar as appropriate, are the rules prescribed for achieving judicial partition of successions and communities.

The parties are required to communicate to each other, and to communicate to the experts appointed by the judge, all information and documents useful for the liquidation. The action for liquidation is time-barred after three years from the dissolution of the matrimonial regime. Actions brought against third parties pursuant to article 920, paragraph 4, are time-barred after two years from the closure of the liquidation.

###### Article 1757

If the application of the valuation rules provided for by articles 1749 and 1752 were to lead to a result manifestly contrary to equity, which the judge should specifically state the reasons for, the court could derogate from them at the request of one of the spouses.

###### Article 1758

If the disorder of the affairs of a spouse, his or her mismanagement or his or her misconduct, give reason to fear that the continuation of the matrimonial regime may compromise the interests of the other spouse, the latter may request early liquidation of his or her participation claim.

The rules of separation of property are applicable to this request. When the request is granted, the spouses are placed under the regime of articles 1739 to 1744.

###### Article 1759

By stipulating participation in acquests, the spouses may adopt all clauses not contrary to articles 1633, 1635 and 1636. They may in particular agree to a clause of unequal partition, or stipulate that the survivor of them or one of them if he or she survives, shall be entitled to all of the net acquests made by the other. It may also be agreed between the spouses that the one of them who, upon liquidation of the regime, shall have towards the other a participation claim, may require the dation in payment of certain property of his or her spouse, if he or she establishes that he or she has an essential interest in having them allocated to him or her.

#### Title VII: Of Sale

Chapter I. Of the nature and form of sale

###### Article 1760

Sale is a contract by which one party undertakes to deliver a thing, and the other to pay for it. It may be made by authentic act, under private signature, or verbally.

###### Article 1761

The sale is complete between the parties, and ownership is acquired by right to the buyer with regard to the seller, as soon as the parties have agreed on the thing and on its price, even if the thing has not yet been delivered nor the price paid.

###### Article 1762

The sale may be made purely and simply, or subject to a condition, which may be suspensive or resolutory.

It may also have as its object two or more alternative things.

In all these cases, its effect is governed by the general principles provided for by this code and which govern the contract.

###### Article 1763

When goods are not sold in bulk, but by weight, by count or by measure, the sale is not complete: the things sold remain at the risk of the seller until they are weighed, counted or measured; but, in case of non-performance of his obligation by the seller, the buyer may request delivery of the thing or damages, if appropriate.

On the other hand, if the goods have been sold in bulk, the sale is complete, regardless of the fact that the goods have not yet been weighed, counted or measured.

###### Article 1764

In case of sale on trial, as for wine, oil, and other things that one is in the habit of tasting before purchasing them, there is no sale until the buyer has tasted and approved them. Such a sale is always presumed to be made subject to a suspensive condition.

###### Article 1765

The promise of sale is equivalent to a sale, as soon as there is mutual consent of both parties on the thing and on the price.

When a unilateral promise to sell land already subdivided or to be subdivided is signed, the lifting of the option necessarily results from payment of part of the price by the beneficiary of the promise, whatever name the parties give to this payment, provided that he has taken possession of the immovable that is the subject of the act.

The date of the agreement, even if regularized subsequently, shall be that of payment of the first installment.

###### Article 1766

Any unilateral undertaking entered into for the acquisition of property or a real property right for which a payment is required or received from the person who undertakes, whatever its cause and form, is null and void.

###### Article 1767

If it is not recorded by authentic act or by a private signed instrument registered within ten days from the date of its acceptance by the beneficiary, any unilateral promise of sale relating to an immovable, a real property right, a business goodwill, a right to a lease covering all or part of an immovable, or to shares of companies whose shares or interests confer on their holders the right to enjoyment of immovables or fractions of immovables and to those of companies whose sole purpose in fact is either the construction or acquisition of immovables or groups of immovables with a view to their division into fractions intended to be allocated to the members in ownership or enjoyment, or the management of such immovables or groups of immovables so divided, or the leasing on behalf of one or more members of the company of all or part of the immovables or fractions of immovables belonging to each of these members, is null and void.

The same applies to any transfer relating to said promises which has not been the subject of an authentic act or a private signed instrument registered within ten days of its date.

###### Article 1768

If the promise to sell has been made with a deposit each of the contracting parties has the possibility to withdraw from the contract:

The one who gave them, by forfeiting the sum represented by the deposit paid, And the one who received the deposit, by returning double the sum received.

Unless otherwise stipulated, for any contract of sale or provision of services concluded between a professional and a consumer, the sums paid in advance are deposits.

###### Article 1769

The sale price must be determined and designated by the parties.

###### Article 1770

The parties to the contract may however designate a third party to estimate the sale price; if the third party does not wish to or cannot make the estimate, there is no sale.

If the expert has not been designated due to the silence or behaviour of one of the parties to the contract, its non-performance is resolved in damages.

The price fixed by the expert can only be challenged in case of gross error on their part in its determination.

###### Article 1771

Unless otherwise stipulated, the costs of deeds and other accessories to the sale are borne by the buyer.

##### Chapitre II. Who may buy or sell

###### Article 1772

All those whom the law does not prohibit may buy or sell.

###### Article 1773

The contract of sale may only take place between spouses in the following three cases:

1° That where one of the two spouses transfers property to the other, judicially separated from them, in payment of their rights;

2° That where the transfer that the husband makes to his wife, even not separated, has a legitimate cause, such as the reinvestment of her alienated immovables, or of monies belonging to her, if such immovables or monies do not fall into community property;

3° That where the wife transfers property to her husband in payment of a sum she would have promised him as dowry, and when there is exclusion of community property; subject, in these three cases, to the rights of the heirs of the contracting parties, if there is an indirect advantage.

###### Article 1774

May not become purchasers, under penalty of nullity, either by themselves or through intermediaries:

- guardians, of the property of those of whom they have guardianship;
- agents, of the property they are charged with selling;
- administrators, of those of municipalities or public institutions entrusted to their care;
- public officers, of national property the sales of which are made through their ministry.
- fiduciaries, of the property or rights composing the fiduciary estate.

###### Article 1775

It is prohibited for persons vested with judicial functions, such as judges, their alternates, magistrates of the public prosecutor's office, clerks, bailiffs, notaries, lawyers or any other person authorized to represent others in court, to acquire rights or actions liable to be contested before the jurisdiction within whose jurisdiction they exercise their functions.

##### Chapitre III. Of things which may be sold

###### Article 1776

Unless otherwise provided by law, everything that is in commerce may be sold.

###### Article 1777

Is null and void:

1° The sale of another's property. Such a sale may give rise to damages when the buyer was unaware that the thing belonged to another;

2° The succession of a living person, even with their consent;

3° The sale of a thing which did not exist or no longer existed at the time of the sale. The purchaser may then, at their option, abandon the sale or request the preserved part of the thing with reduction of the price in a proportion analogous to that of the loss incurred.

##### Chapitre IV. Of the sale of immovables to be built

###### Article 1778

The sale of immovables to be built is that by which the seller undertakes to erect an immovable within a time period determined by the contract.

It may be concluded on a term basis or in the future state of completion.

###### Article 1779

The sale on a term basis is the contract by which the seller undertakes to deliver the immovable upon its completion, the buyer undertakes to take delivery of it and to pay the price on the date of delivery. The transfer of ownership operates by operation of law by the recording by authentic act of the completion of the immovable; it produces its effects retroactively to the day of the sale.

###### Article 1780

The sale in the future state of completion is the contract by which the seller immediately transfers to the purchaser their rights to the land as well as the ownership of existing constructions. The works to come become the property of the purchaser as and when they are executed; the purchaser is required to pay the price as the works progress.

The seller retains the powers of project owner until the reception of the works.

###### Article 1781

The transfer by the purchaser of the rights they hold from a sale of immovable to be built substitutes by operation of law the transferee in the obligations of the purchaser towards the seller.

If the sale has been accompanied by a mandate, it continues between the seller and the transferee. These provisions apply to any transfer inter vivos, voluntary or forced, or by reason of death.

##### Chapitre V. Of the obligations of the seller

###### Section I: General provisions

###### Article 1782

The seller is required to clearly explain what they undertake.

Any obscure or ambiguous clause is interpreted against the seller.

In contracts proposed by professionals to consumers, the clauses must be presented and drafted in a clear and comprehensible manner. In case of doubt, they are interpreted in the sense most favourable to the consumer.

###### Article 1783

The seller has two main obligations: that of delivering and that of guaranteeing the thing they sell.

###### Section II: Of delivery

###### Article 1784

Delivery consists in making available to the buyer the thing sold so that they may use it, enjoy it and dispose of it materially.

Delivery must take place at the location where, at the time of the sale, the thing which was the subject thereof was located, if it has not been otherwise agreed.

###### Article 1785

The obligation to deliver immovables is fulfilled on the part of the seller when they have handed over the keys, if it is a building, or when they have handed over the title deeds.

###### Article 1786

Delivery of movable property is effected:

- by handing over the thing to the purchaser;
- by handing over the keys to the buildings that contain them;
- or by mere consent of the parties, if the transfer cannot be made at the time of sale, or if the purchaser already had them in his possession under another title.

###### Article 1787

Delivery of incorporeal rights is effected by handing over the titles, signature of transfer orders, or by the use that the purchaser makes of them with the consent of the seller.

###### Article 1788

Unless otherwise stipulated, the costs of delivery are borne by the seller, and those of removal by the purchaser.

###### Article 1789

If the seller fails to make delivery within the time agreed between the parties, the purchaser may, at his choice, demand the rescission of the sale or his taking of possession, if the delay is solely due to the seller's act.

The burden of proof that he placed the thing sold at the disposal of the purchaser within the agreed time falls on the seller.

###### Article 1790

In all cases where the purchaser suffers damage due to the failure to deliver at the agreed term, the seller is ordered to pay him compensatory damages.

###### Article 1791

The seller is not bound to deliver the thing if the purchaser does not pay the price, and the seller has not granted him a period for payment.

He will also not be obliged to deliver, even if he had granted a period for payment, if, since the sale, the purchaser has gone bankrupt, such that the seller finds himself in imminent danger of losing the price; unless the purchaser gives him security to pay at the term.

###### Article 1792

The thing must be delivered in the state in which it is at the time of sale. From that day, unless otherwise agreed, all fruits belong to the purchaser.

###### Article 1793

The obligation to deliver the thing includes its accessories and everything that has been intended for its perpetual use.

###### Article 1794

The seller is bound to deliver the area as it is stated in the contract, subject to the modifications hereinafter expressed.

###### Article 1795

If the sale of an immovable has been made with indication of the area, at so much per unit of measurement, the seller is obliged to deliver to the purchaser, if he demands it, the quantity indicated in the contract; if this is not possible for him or if the purchaser does not demand it, the seller is obliged to suffer a proportionate reduction of the price.

If, on the contrary, the area is greater than that expressed in the contract, the purchaser has the choice of providing the supplement of the price, or of withdrawing from the contract, if the excess is one-twentieth above the declared area.

###### Article 1796

In all other cases of immovable sale, which have therefore not been made at so much per unit of measurement, the deficiency of area can give rise, in favor of the purchaser, only to a reduction of the price when the difference in less reaches one-twentieth, and, in favor of the seller only to an increase of the price when the difference in more reaches one-twentieth, all subject to stipulation to the contrary.

###### Article 1797

In the case where, pursuant to Article 1796, there is ground for an increase of price for excess of measurement, the purchaser has the choice either of withdrawing from the contract or of providing the supplement of the price, and this, with interest if he has kept the immovable.

###### Article 1798

In all cases where the purchaser has the right to withdraw from the contract, the seller is bound to restore to him, in addition to the price, if he has received it, the costs of this contract.

###### Article 1799

The action for supplement of price on the part of the seller of the immovable, and that for reduction of price or for rescission of the contract on the part of the purchaser of this property, must be brought within one year, from the day of the contract, on pain of forfeiture.

###### Article 1800

If two properties have been sold by the same contract, and for one and the same price, with designation of the measurement of each, and there is found to be less area in one and more in the other, compensation is made up to due concurrence; and the action, either for supplement, or for reduction of the price, takes place only according to the rules established above.

###### Article 1801

The question of knowing on which, the seller or the purchaser, must fall the loss or the deterioration of the thing sold before delivery, is decided according to the rules prescribed in the title On obligations.

###### Section III: Of the seller's warranty

###### Article 1802

The warranty that the seller owes to the purchaser of any right of property, corporeal or incorporeal, has two objects:

- the first is the peaceful possession of the thing sold;
- the second, the hidden defects of this thing or the redhibitory defects.

###### § 1. Of the warranty in case of eviction

###### Article 1803

Even if the sale contains no stipulation on the warranty, the seller is obliged by law to warrant the purchaser against the eviction that he suffers in all or part of the object sold, or from charges claimed on this object, and not declared at the time of sale.

###### Article 1804

The parties may, by special agreements, add to this obligation by law, or diminish its effect.

The parties may even agree that the seller will be subject to no warranty; in this case, the seller nevertheless remains bound by the warranty that results from a fact that is personal to him. Any agreement to the contrary is void.

###### Article 1805

Even if a clause of non-warranty has been stipulated, the seller, in case of eviction, is nevertheless bound to the restitution of the price, unless the purchaser knew at the time of sale the danger of the eviction or that he purchased at his own perils and risks.

###### Article 1806

When the warranty has been promised, or when nothing has been stipulated on this subject, if the purchaser is evicted, he has the right to demand from the seller the reparation of all the damage caused by the non-performance of the contract, namely:

1° The restitution of the price;

2° The restitution of the fruits, when he is obliged to return them to the owner who evicts him; 3° The costs incurred on the claim for warranty of the purchaser, and those incurred by the original claimant; 4° Lastly, damages, as well as the costs and fair costs of the contract.

###### Article 1807

When at the time of eviction, the thing sold is found to be diminished in value, or considerably deteriorated, either by the negligence of the purchaser, or by accidents of force majeure, the seller is nonetheless bound to restore the totality of the price.

But if the purchaser has drawn profit from the degradations made by him, for example, by selling the materials that he removed from the thing or decorative elements, the seller has the right to retain from the price a sum equal to this profit.

Conversely, the seller is bound to reimburse or to have reimbursed to the purchaser, by the one who evicts him, all the useful repairs and improvements that he has made to the property.

###### Article 1808

On the other hand, if the thing sold is found to have increased in price at the time of eviction, even independently of the act of the purchaser, the seller is bound to pay him the amount of this increase in value in relation to the price of the sale.

###### Article 1809

If the seller has sold in bad faith the property of another, he is obliged to reimburse to the purchaser all expenses, even voluptuary or of pleasure, that the latter has made to the property.

###### Article 1810

If the buyer is evicted from only part of the thing but it is so essential that the buyer would not have purchased without it, he may have the sale rescinded.

In this case of partial eviction, when the sale is not rescinded, the value of the part from which the buyer is evicted is reimbursed to him according to the valuation at the time of eviction, and not in proportion to the total price of the sale, regardless of whether the thing sold has increased or decreased in value.

###### Article 1811

If the land that has been sold is found to be encumbered, without any declaration having been made, with non-apparent easements, and they are of such importance that there is reason to presume that the buyer would not have purchased if he had been informed of them, he may demand, at his choice, rescission of the contract or compensation.

Other questions to which damages resulting for the buyer from non-performance of the sale may give rise must be decided according to the general rules established in the title On Obligations.

###### Article 1812

The warranty for eviction ceases when the buyer has allowed himself to be condemned by a final judgment, or from which appeal is no longer admissible, without calling his seller, if the latter proves that there existed sufficient means to have the claim rejected.

###### § 2. Of the warranty for defects in the thing sold

###### Article 1813

The seller is bound by the warranty by reason of hidden defects in the thing sold which render it unfit for the use for which it is intended, or which diminish such use to such an extent that the buyer would not have acquired it, or would have given only a lower price, if he had known of them.

###### Article 1814

The seller is not liable for apparent defects and of which the buyer could have satisfied himself.

###### Article 1815

The seller of an immovable to be constructed cannot be discharged, either before the reception of the works, or before the expiration of a period of one month after taking possession by the acquirer, of construction defects or defects of conformity then apparent.

There is no ground for rescission of the contract or reduction of the price if the seller undertakes to repair the defect.

###### Article 1816

The seller is liable for hidden defects, even if he had not known of them, unless, in that case, he has stipulated that he will not be bound to any warranty.

###### Article 1817

In the cases of articles 1813 and 1816, the buyer has the choice of returning the thing and having the price restituted to him, or of keeping the thing and having part of the price returned to him, as it shall be fixed by the judge who may, where appropriate, appoint an expert.

###### Article 1818

If the seller knew of the defects in the thing, he is liable, in addition to the restitution of the price he received for it, for all damages to the buyer.

If the seller was unaware of the defects in the thing, he is liable only for the restitution of the price, and for reimbursing to the acquirer the costs occasioned by the sale.

###### Article 1819

The seller of an immovable to be constructed is liable, from the reception of the works, for the obligations for which architects, contractors and other persons bound to the owner by a contract for the hire of work are themselves liable pursuant to articles 1950 et seq. of this code. These warranties benefit successive owners of the immovable.

There will be no ground for rescission of the sale or reduction of the price if the seller undertakes to repair the damage defined in articles 1953, 1954 and 1955 of this code and to assume the warranty provided for in article 1956.

###### Article 1820

If the thing which had defects has perished as a result of its poor quality, the loss falls on the seller, who shall be liable to the buyer for the restitution of the price and for the other compensation explained in articles 1818 and 1819.

But the loss occurring by force majeure shall be for the account of the buyer.

###### Article 1821

The action resulting from redhibitory defects must be brought by the acquirer, within a brief period, according to the nature of the redhibitory defects, and the usage of the place where the sale was made.

In the case provided for by article 1815, the action must be brought, on pain of forfeiture, within the year following the date on which the seller may be discharged of apparent defects.

###### Article 1822

It does not take place in sales made by judicial authority.

##### Chapitre VI. Of the obligations of the buyer

###### Article 1823

The principal obligation of the buyer is to pay the price on the day and at the place settled by the sale.

###### Article 1824

If nothing has been settled in this regard at the time of the sale, the buyer must pay at the place and at the time when delivery must be made.

###### Article 1825

The buyer owes interest on the sale price until payment of the principal, in the following three cases:

- if it was so agreed at the time of sale;
- if the thing sold and delivered produces fruits or other revenues;
- if the buyer has been summoned to pay. In this last case, interest runs only from the summons.

###### Article 1826

If the buyer is disturbed or has just cause to fear being disturbed by an action, either in mortgage or in revendication, he may suspend payment of the price until the seller has caused the disturbance to cease, unless the latter prefers to give security, or unless it has been stipulated that, notwithstanding the disturbance, the buyer shall pay.

###### Article 1827

If the buyer does not pay the price, the seller may demand rescission of the sale.

###### Article 1828

The rescission of the sale of immovables is pronounced immediately, if the seller is in danger of losing the thing and the price.

If this danger does not exist, the judge may grant to the acquirer a longer or shorter period according to the circumstances.

After this period has passed without the acquirer having paid, the rescission of the sale shall be pronounced.

###### Article 1829

If it was stipulated at the time of sale of immovables that, for want of payment of the price within the agreed term, the sale would be rescinded by operation of law, the acquirer may nevertheless pay after the expiration of the period, as long as he has not been put on notice by a summons; but, after this summons, the judge cannot grant him this period.

###### Article 1830

In the matter of sale of commodities and movable effects, the rescission of the sale shall take place by operation of law and without summons, for the benefit of the seller, after the expiration of the term agreed for the retirement.

##### Chapitre VII. Of the nullity and rescission of the sale

###### Article 1831

Independently of the causes of nullity or rescission already explained in this title, and of those which are common to all contracts, the contract of sale may be rescinded by the exercise of the right of redemption and by the baseness of the price.

###### Section I : Of the right of redemption

###### Article 1832

The right of redemption is a pact by which the seller reserves the right to take back the thing sold, upon restitution of the principal price and the reimbursement set out in article 1843.

###### Article 1833

The right of redemption cannot be stipulated for a term exceeding five years.

The fixed term is strict and cannot be extended by the judge.

If it has been stipulated for a longer term, it is reduced to this term of five years.

###### Article 1834

For want of the seller having exercised his action of redemption within the prescribed term, the acquirer remains irrevocable owner.

The period runs against all persons, even against the minor, except, if applicable, recourse against the person to whom this omission is imputable.

###### Article 1835

The seller with a pact of redemption may exercise his action against a second acquirer, even if the right of redemption had not been declared in the second contract.

###### Article 1836

The purchaser with a redemption clause exercises all the rights of his vendor; he may acquire by prescription both against the true owner and against those who would claim rights or mortgages on the thing sold.

###### Article 1837

He may raise the benefit of discussion against the creditors of his vendor.

###### Article 1838

If the purchaser with a redemption clause of a part of an undivided property has become the successful bidder for the whole upon a sale by licitation brought against him, he may compel the vendor to redeem the whole when the latter wishes to exercise the clause.

###### Article 1839

If several persons have sold jointly, and by a single contract, a property common among them, each may exercise the action for redemption only for the share he had in it.

The same applies if the person who alone sold a property has left several heirs. But each of these coheirs may exercise the right of redemption only for the share he takes in the succession.

###### Article 1840

However, in the case of the preceding article, the purchaser may require that all the co-vendors or all the coheirs be made parties, in order to reach an agreement among themselves for the redemption of the thing sold in its entirety; and, if they do not reach an agreement, the purchaser may retain the thing in its entirety, except that the person who has exercised the action for redemption who has not obtained the agreement of the others may exercise the action for the whole and pay the entire price and costs of the sale.

###### Article 1841

If the sale of a property belonging to several persons was not made jointly and as a whole, and each has therefore sold only the share he had in it, these persons may separately exercise the action for redemption on the portion that belonged to them.

The purchaser, in this case, may not force the person who exercises the action for his share to redeem the whole.

###### Article 1842

If the purchaser has left several heirs, the action for redemption may be exercised against each of them only for his share, in the case where it is still undivided, and in that where the thing sold has been divided among them.

But if there has been a partition of the succession and the thing sold has fallen to the lot of one of the heirs, the action for redemption may be brought against him for the whole.

The parties may stipulate that in case of death of the purchaser leaving several heirs, the redemption shall be effected, against these heirs, only for the whole. Likewise, several persons acquiring jointly with a redemption clause may stipulate that the vendor shall not exercise partial redemption.

###### Article 1843

The vendor who exercises the redemption clause must reimburse not only the principal price, but also the fees and lawful costs of the sale, the necessary repairs, and those which have increased the value of the property, up to the amount of that increase. He may not enter into possession of the property until he has satisfied all these obligations.

When the redemption clause has been duly published at the mortgage office, all charges and mortgages with which the purchaser may have encumbered it subsequent to the sale are unenforceable against the vendor who redeems his property. He is however bound to perform the leases made without fraud by the purchaser.

###### Section II : De l'annulation de la vente pour cause de lésion

###### Article 1844

If the vendor has been injured by more than seven-twelfths in the price of immovable property, he has the right to demand the nullity of the sale, even in the case where he had expressly renounced in the contract the right to demand this annulment and had declared he was giving the added value.

The remedy of lesion does not apply in favor of the purchaser.

###### Article 1845

To determine whether there is lesion of more than seven-twelfths, the immovable property must be valued according to its condition and value at the time of the sale.

In case of a unilateral promise to sell, the lesion is assessed on the day of completion, that is to say at the time the option is exercised.

###### Article 1846

The action is no longer admissible after the expiration of two years, from the day of the sale. This period runs against spouses and against absentees, adults under guardianship and minors deriving title from an adult who has sold.

This period also runs and is not suspended during the duration of the time stipulated for the redemption clause.

###### Article 1847

In case of disagreement between the parties on the existence of the lesion, the judge may order an expert assessment only if the plaintiff presents facts sufficiently serious for the lesion to appear possible if not probable. In this case, the judge appoints, ex officio or upon joint and unanimous choice of the parties on each of the experts, a panel of three experts. They must draw up a joint report, in which they shall express a single opinion on the existence or not of the lesion and this, by majority vote. If nevertheless different opinions remain, the report shall contain the reasons therefor, without it being permitted to make known which opinion each expert held.

###### Article 1848

In the case where the action for nullity is allowed, the purchaser has the choice:

1° to return the thing by withdrawing the price he paid for it;

2° to keep the property by paying the supplement of the fair price, less one-tenth of the total price.

The third-party possessor has the same right, except for his warranty against his vendor.

###### Article 1849

If the purchaser prefers to keep the thing by providing the supplement prescribed by the preceding article, he owes interest on the supplement, from the day of the action for nullity.

If he prefers to return it and receive the price, he returns the fruits from the day of the action.

Interest on the price he paid is also counted to him from the day of the same action, or from the day of payment, if he has not received any fruits.

###### Article 1850

Sales which must be made by judicial authority may not be the subject of an action for nullity for lesion.

###### Article 1851

The rules explained in the preceding section for cases where several persons have sold jointly or separately, and for the case where the vendor or the purchaser has left several heirs, are likewise observed for the exercise of the action for nullity.

##### Chapitre VIII. De la licitation

###### Article 1852

Licitation consists in the sale by auction, in a voluntary manner, of movable or immovable property held in indivision, by the holders of real rights over that thing.

The sale is followed by a distribution of its proceeds by allocation to each co-owner of a portion corresponding to his undivided rights.

###### Article 1853

Each of the co-owners has the right to request that third parties be admitted to participate in the bidding. They are necessarily called when one of the co-owners is a minor.

###### Article 1854

The method and formalities to be observed for licitation are explained in the Title on Successions and in the Code of Civil Procedure.

##### Chapitre IX. Du transport des créances et autres droits incorporels

###### Article 1855

In the transfer of a right or an action against a third party, delivery is effected between the assignor and the assignee by the handing over of the title.

###### Article 1856

The assignee is seized with respect to third parties only by the service of the transfer made on the debtor. Nevertheless, the assignee may also be seized by the acceptance of the transfer made by the debtor in an authentic act.

###### Article 1857

If, before the assignor or the assignee had served the transfer on the debtor, the latter had paid the assignor, he shall be validly discharged.

###### Article 1858

A person who sells an incorporeal right must warrant its existence at the time of the transfer, even though it is made without warranty.

###### Article 1859

One who sells a succession without specifying the items in detail is only required to guarantee their quality as heir.

If they had already benefited from the fruits of a thing present in this succession, or received the amount of a claim that was in it, or sold property that was nevertheless part of the succession, they are required to reimburse them to the purchaser, unless otherwise stipulated at the time of sale.

The purchaser must in turn reimburse the seller of the succession for what the latter paid for the debts and charges thereof, and any claim that the latter could have on the succession, unless otherwise stipulated.

###### Article 1860

The assignment of litigious rights effects the transfer of the right from the assignor to the assignee by substituting the latter for the former in the pending proceedings.

Nevertheless, the person against whom a litigious right has been assigned may, either by extrajudicial act or by way of principal submissions filed in the pending proceedings, be released from it by the assignee, by reimbursing them the actual price of the assignment together with the costs and legal expenses, and with interest from the day on which the assignee paid the price of the assignment made to them.

###### Article 1861

A thing is deemed litigious as soon as there is a lawsuit and dispute on the substance of the right.

###### Article 1862

The assigned debtor may not benefit from the faculty of litigious redemption:

1° In the case where the assignment was made to a co-heir or co-owner of the assigned right; 2° When it was made to a creditor in payment of what is owed to them;

3° When it was made to the possessor of the inheritance subject to the litigious right.

###### Article 1863

Articles 1855 to 1858 do not apply to assignments governed by articles 1507 to 1512 of this code.

#### Titre VIII: De l'échange

###### Article 1864

Exchange is a contract by which the parties respectively give each other one thing for another.

###### Article 1865

Exchange is effected by consent alone, in the same manner as sale.

###### Article 1866

If one of the co-exchangers has already received the thing given to them in exchange, and subsequently proves that the other contracting party is not the owner of that thing, they cannot be forced to deliver what they promised in counter-exchange, but only to return what they received.

###### Article 1867

The co-exchanger who is evicted from the thing they received in exchange has the choice of claiming damages or compelling the other party to return their thing to them.

###### Article 1868

Rescission for lesion does not apply to the contract of exchange.

###### Article 1869

All other rules prescribed for the contract of sale apply to exchange.

#### Titre IX: Du contrat de louage

Chapitre Ier. Dispositions générales

###### Article 1870

There are two kinds of contracts of lease:

- that of things,
- and that of work and industry.

###### Article 1871

The lease of things is a contract by which one of the parties undertakes to allow the other to enjoy a thing for a certain time, and for a certain price that the latter undertakes to pay.

The contract of lease confers on the lessee only a movable and personal right.

The rules applicable to the contract of lease do not apply to the emphyteutic lease, which is subject to its own rules.

###### Article 1872

The lease of work and industry is a contract by which one of the parties undertakes to do something for the other, for a price agreed between them.

Estimates, contracts or fixed prices, for the undertaking of work for a determined price, are also a lease, when the material is supplied by the person for whom the work is done.

###### Article 1873

Leases of national property, property of municipalities and public institutions are subject to special regulations.

##### Chapitre II. Du louage des choses

###### Article 1874

All movable and immovable property that is in commerce may be the subject of a contract of lease.

###### Section I : Dispositions communes aux baux

###### Article 1875

The contract of lease may be made in writing or verbally.

If the lease made without writing has not yet received any execution, and one of the parties denies it, proof may not be received by witnesses, even if the stated price is modest. The possible payment of a sum of money, without further specification, does not constitute the commencement of execution of the verbal lease. The oath may only be referred to the person who denies the lease.

###### Article 1876

When there is a dispute over the price of a verbal lease whose execution has begun and there is no receipt, the lessee has the choice between two modes of proof to establish the price of the lease: oath or expert assessment. If they opt for oath, the owner shall be believed on their word; if they opt for expert assessment, the costs thereof shall remain at the lessee's expense if the valuation should exceed the price they declared. The judge may neither apply the provisions of the preceding paragraph of their own motion nor, when seized of the question, fix the rent based on elements other than those provided for by the text.

###### Article 1877

The lessee has the right to sublet, and even to assign their lease to a third party, if this faculty has not been prohibited to them, in whole or in part, by the contract.

When the clause prohibiting subletting or assignment of the lease is pure and simple, it is absolutely binding and the lessee must respect it, even if they would demonstrate that the lessor has no interest in requiring its application and that they themselves have an important interest in subletting or assigning their lease.

###### Article 1878

Article 722, paragraph 4, is applicable to leases of property of minors.

###### Article 1879

The lessor is obliged, by the nature of the contract, and without any need for any special stipulation: 1° To deliver to the lessee the thing leased;

2° To maintain this thing in a state fit for the use for which it was leased;

3° To ensure for the lessee the peaceful enjoyment of the thing leased during the entire duration of the lease; 4° To ensure, if there are any, the permanence and quality of plantings.

###### Article 1880

The lessor is required to deliver the thing in good state of repairs of all kinds.

They must make thereto, during the duration of the lease, all repairs that may become necessary, other than those relating to maintenance. The owner thus has the burden of major repairs due to age or defective workmanship; they must also guarantee their lessee against all defects or faults of the thing leased that prevent its use, even if the lessor was not aware of them at the time of the lease. If any loss for the lessee should result from these defects or faults, the lessor would be required to compensate them.

###### Article 1881

The tenant may not request reimbursement from their owner for major repairs that they would have carried out without the latter's prior agreement.

###### Article 1882

It is otherwise if, during the lease, the thing leased needs urgent repairs that cannot be deferred, when the lessor cannot be reached or is slow to react: the tenant may then have the work carried out without requesting prior authorization from their owner; they may subsequently obtain reimbursement.

Conversely, if such repairs are undertaken by the lessor during the lease, the lessee must endure them, whatever inconvenience they cause them, and even if they must be deprived, while they are being done, of a part of the thing leased.

But, if these repairs last more than thirty days, the price of the lease shall be reduced in proportion to the time and the part of the thing leased of which they will have been deprived. And, if the repairs are of such a nature that they render uninhabitable what is necessary for the accommodation of the lessee and their family, the latter may have the lease terminated.

###### Article 1883

The lessor may not, during the term of the lease, change the form of the leased property.

###### Article 1884

The lessee is bound by two principal obligations:

1° To use the leased property as a normally diligent person, and according to the purpose given to it by the lease, or according to that presumed from the circumstances, in the absence of agreement; 2° To pay the rent, price of the lease, at the agreed terms.

###### Article 1885

If the lessee uses the leased property contrary to the obligations imposed upon him, or according to a use from which damage could result to the lessor, the latter may, depending on the circumstances, have the lease terminated.

###### Article 1886

If an inventory of fixtures has been made between the lessor and the lessee, the latter must return the property as he received it, according to that inventory.

If no inventory of fixtures has been made, the lessee is presumed to have received them in good state of tenancy repairs, and must return them as such, unless proven otherwise.

In both cases, the lessee is not responsible for what has perished or been damaged during the lease, when the harmful event occurred without his fault, for example, due to deterioration, a break-in causing the damage, fortuitous event or fault of the lessor.

###### Article 1887

The lessee must ensure that the premises he occupies are maintained in their condition. He must therefore bear the cost of minor repairs and tenancy repairs, that is to say the current maintenance of the dwelling and its equipment elements.

The lessee must bear the cost of major repairs when the damage is due to poor maintenance on his part, excluding deterioration, defective workmanship, construction defect, fortuitous event or force majeure. He is not further liable for damage related to normal use of the equipment and premises.

###### Article 1888

The lessee is however liable for damage and losses that occur by the act of persons of his household or his subtenants.

###### Article 1889

The lessee is also liable for fire, unless he proves that the fire occurred by fortuitous event or force majeure, by construction defect, or that the fire was communicated from a neighboring house. If there are several tenants, they are jointly and severally liable for the fire, in proportion to the rental value of the part of the building they occupy, unless they prove either that the fire started in the dwelling of one of them, in which case only that one is liable, or that certain ones manage to prove that the fire could not have started in their premises, in which case those are not liable.

###### Article 1890

If the lease was made without written document, the lease ends by notice given by one party to the other, observing a reasonable period.

If it was made in writing, it ceases by operation of law at the expiration of the fixed term, without it being necessary to give notice.

###### Article 1891

If, at the expiration of written leases, the lessee remains in the premises and is left in possession by the lessor, a new lease is created whose effect is governed by article 1890 first paragraph relating to leases made without written document.

In this case, the security given for the lease does not extend to the obligations resulting from the extension.

###### Article 1892

The lessor is not required to guarantee the lessee against disturbance that third parties bring by acts of trespass to his enjoyment, without claiming any right over the leased property; except for the lessee to pursue them in his personal name.

The perpetrators of an act of trespass cannot justify it on the pretext of a right they would have over the property. The judge shall order restoration and cessation of the disturbance, and invite the interested parties to act according to legal procedures.

If, on the contrary, the tenant has been disturbed in his enjoyment as a result of an action concerning the ownership of the property, he is entitled to a proportionate reduction in the rent, provided that the disturbance and impediment have been reported to the owner.

###### Article 1893

If the lessee is himself summoned to court by a third party who intends to see him ordered to relinquish all or part of this property, or to suffer the exercise of some easement, this lessee must call the lessor as warrantor, and must be dismissed from the proceedings, if he so requires, by naming the lessor for whom he possesses.

###### Article 1894

If, during the term of the lease, the leased property is destroyed or lost in its entirety by fortuitous event, the lease is terminated by operation of law; if it is only partially destroyed, the lessee may, depending on the circumstances, request either a reduction in price, or the termination of the lease itself. In either case, there is no entitlement to any compensation.

###### Article 1895

The contract of lease is terminated by the respective failure of the lessor and the lessee to fulfill their commitments.

###### Article 1896

The contract of lease is not terminated by the death of the lessor nor by that of the lessee.

###### Article 1897

If the lessor sells the leased property, the acquirer cannot evict the lessee who has an authentic lease or whose date is certain, unless he has reserved this right in the lease contract.

###### Article 1898

If it has been agreed, at the time of the lease, that in case of sale the acquirer may evict the lessee, and no stipulation has been made regarding damages, the lessor is required to compensate the lessee: 1° In case of lease of a house, apartment or shop, a sum equal to the rent price, for the time which, according to local custom, is granted between the notice and the departure.

2° If it concerns rural property, a sum equal to one-third of the lease price for all the time remaining to run.

The amount of compensation is, in case of dispute, fixed by the judge who may, if necessary, appoint an expert.

As long as the compensation has not been paid, the lessee may remain in the premises.

###### Article 1899

If the lease is not made by authentic deed, or does not have a certain date, the acquirer is not liable for any damages.

###### Article 1900

The acquirer with right of redemption cannot use the right to evict the lessee, until, by the expiration of the period fixed for redemption, he becomes definitive owner, unless agreed by his seller.

###### Article 1901

The acquirer who wishes to use the right reserved by the lease, to evict the lessee in case of sale is required to give notice to the lessee, for a period as provided in the lease contract for notices in case of termination and, failing that, for a reasonable period.

###### Section II : Particular Rules

###### Article 1902

The lease with option to purchase is a lease contract providing that at its term, the tenant may acquire the property at a price fixed in advance.

When the contract concerns an individual, the transaction is a lease with promise of sale or lease-purchase; when it concerns professionals, it is a lease-financing contract governed by the provisions of law No. 183/AN/17/7th L on lease-financing, of May 29, 2017.

###### § 1. Relationships between lessors and tenants of residential premises or for professional use without

industrial or commercial character

###### Article1903

These provisions are applicable to relations between lessors and tenants or occupants of premises belonging to the following categories:

1° Premises for residential use, with the exception of hotels and boarding houses;

2° Premises for professional use without commercial and industrial character;

3° Premises leased by a legal person of public law to install services or agents;

4° Premises leased by legal persons engaged in non-profit activities, in particular by registered associations and professional unions;

5° Premises leased by commercial or industrial enterprises for the exclusive residential use of their staff.

These provisions do not apply either to relations between legal persons of public law and their agents or to relations between commercial or industrial enterprises and their staff, with respect to premises allocated to housing for these agents or this staff, when housing constitutes a benefit in kind accessory to remuneration under the regulatory status of civil servants, or under the provisions of the labor code for private sector employees.

A. Rent

###### Article1904

The amount of rent for leases covered by this section, as well as the conditions for its revision, are freely fixed by agreement of the parties upon conclusion of the initial lease between the lessor and the tenant.

###### Article1905

When the lease does not provide for special conditions for the revision of rent, the latter, unless otherwise stipulated in the lease contract, may be revised at the request of one of the parties when a change in the inflation rate has occurred since the conclusion of the lease or since the last revision of rent, likely to cause this rate to vary by more than ten percent.

The requested revision may not exceed the justified variation in the inflation rate during the period considered.

The request for revision must specify the new rent requested or offered and provide all details on the elements taken into consideration to justify the amount of the revision.

###### Article1906

The request for revision of rent made pursuant to Article 1905 may not, in any event, be made until at least two years after the date of entry into enjoyment by the tenant, or after the starting point of the renewed lease, or after the last revision.

###### Article 1907

In addition to the elements mentioned in Article 1905 that may justify a revision, a request for revision may be made by the owner who has made improvements to the substance, comfort or amenity of the leased premises, with the express agreement of the tenant. This agreement must also cover the increase in rental value that will result from these improvements. The new rent thus revised may take effect upon completion of these improvements.

However, if the owner wishes to make improvements to the premises dictated by hygiene concerns, the prior agreement of the tenant is not necessary. The increase in rental value that will result from these improvements will justify a revision of rent in proportion to the expenses incurred. On the other hand, improvements made by the tenant cannot be taken into account for a revision of rent.

###### Article1908

In the absence of agreement between the parties on the revision requested pursuant to Articles 1905 and 1907 (second paragraph), disputes are brought before the President of the Court of First Instance or before the judge who replaces him, who rule on the request.

###### Article1909
