The lease contract may provide for the payment by the tenant, upon entry into the premises, of a deposit as guarantee for possible damages and payment of rent due. The amount of the deposit, which cannot exceed two months' rent, shall be returned to the lessee upon expiration of the lease, except in case of renewal.

###### Article 1910

In case of sublease, the amount of the sublease price may not exceed the amount of rent owed by the principal tenant to the owner, unless the premises have been furnished or have received improvements by the principal tenant, in which case the rent increase must be in proportion to the expenses incurred.

The subtenant is liable to the owner only up to the amount of the sublease price that he may owe at the time of seizure, and without being able to oppose payments made in advance.

Payments made by the subtenant, either by virtue of a stipulation in his lease or as a consequence of the use of the premises, are not deemed to have been made in advance.

In the case of partial sublease, the rent must be at most equal to a fraction of the principal rent proportionate to the size of the subleased premises, subject, as in the previous paragraph, to the furniture provided and improvements made by the principal tenant that will justify increases in proportion to the expenses incurred.

###### Article1911

If the lease, or sublease, concerns premises furnished by the owner, or by the principal tenant, the rent may be increased by a rental price for the furniture in proportion to the price of the latter, without this additional price being able to exceed the amount of rent for the unfurnished premises.

###### Article1912

In the case where the tenant or occupant is authorized, either amicably or by court order, to carry out maintenance or repair work normally the responsibility of the owner, he may offset the expenses incurred against future rent. In case of departure from the premises before the debt expires, he may pursue the owner for reimbursement of the balance owed.

###### Article1913

Notwithstanding any contrary stipulation, the clause inserted in the lease providing for termination by operation of law for failure to pay rent on the agreed due dates, takes effect only one month after the date of the summons or payment order that remained unsuccessful.

The formal notice or order must, on pain of nullity, mention this period.

The president of the court, petitioned by the lessee within the aforementioned one-month period, may by order grant him additional time for payment of rent within a limit of three months.

###### Article 1914

In case of termination of the lease due to the fault of the tenant, the latter is required to pay the agreed rent for the time necessary for reletting by the owner without this period being able to exceed two months, without prejudice to damages that may have resulted from his fault.

B. Maintenance in the premises

###### Article 1915

The right to the lease of premises, without professional or commercial character, that effectively serves as housing for two spouses, regardless of their matrimonial regime and notwithstanding any contrary agreement and even if the lease was concluded before the marriage.

In case of divorce or legal separation, this right may be attributed, in consideration of the social and family interests at stake, by the court hearing the application for divorce or legal separation, to one of the spouses, subject to rights to compensation or indemnity in favor of the other spouse. In case of death of one of the spouses, the surviving spouse co-holder of the lease has an exclusive right to it unless he expressly renounces it.

###### Article1916

1° Occupants in good faith of premises, unfurnished or furnished, defined in Article 1903, if they have lived there for at least one year, benefit by right and without the completion of any formality from maintenance in the leased premises, under the clauses and conditions of the original contract not contrary to the provisions of this resolution, the lease continuing by tacit renewal beyond the term fixed by the contract, except for notice given by one or the other party with three months' notice, by extrajudicial act or by bailiff's service;

2° Notice given by the tenant need not be justified;

3° Notice given by the owner must specify, on pain of nullity, the reason for which it is given and apply Articles 1917, 1918 and 1920, subject to the provisions of Articles 1919 and 4° Are deemed to be in good faith tenants, subtenants, assignees of leases, during the term and after the expiration of their contract, as well as occupants who, living in the premises by virtue of or following a written or verbal lease, a regular sublease of a regular assignment of a prior lease, fulfill their obligations;

5° However, to be enforceable against the owner, the subletting of a premises or the assignment of a lease must have had his express or tacit consent. For this purpose, and except for special provisions in this regard in the lease contract, the proposed sublease or assignment of lease must be served on the owner by extrajudicial act two months before the entry into the premises of the subtenant or assignee. Within one month following service, the owner must make known whether he intends to participate in the act. After this period, he is deemed to have given his tacit agreement;

6° The benefit of maintenance in the premises for the premises referred to in Article 1903 belongs, in case of abandonment of domicile or death of the occupant, to his relatives or in-laws in the first degree who habitually lived with him for more than six months;

7° In case of divorce or legal separation proceedings, the court seized awards to one of the spouses the possible right to maintenance in the premises in consideration of the social or family interests at stake. If the spouse who is the beneficiary is not the one in whose name the receipts were issued, notification of the decision must be made to the lessor within three months of its pronouncement by extrajudicial means;

8° However, maintenance in the premises may not benefit the persons referred to in the two preceding paragraphs for premises for exclusively professional use, unless one of these persons continues to practice there the profession for which these premises were assigned;

9° Maintenance in the premises is granted to legal entities occupying premises for professional use as well as to legal entities exercising a non-profit activity, including declared associations and professional unions if these persons meet the conditions provided for in paragraphs 1 and 4 of this article. However, the right to maintenance in the premises thus recognized to legal entities is not enforceable against the owner who wants to occupy the premises himself or have it occupied by his spouse, his ascendants or descendants, or by those of his spouse.

###### Article1917

Persons, whether legal or natural, do not have the right to maintenance in the premises:

1° Who have been or will be subject to a final judicial decision having pronounced their expulsion by application of common law, or who will be subject to a similar decision for one of the causes and under the conditions admitted by this resolution;

2° Who have several dwellings, except for those constituting their principal establishment, unless they justify that their functions or profession require them to do so;

3° Who have not actually occupied the leased premises themselves or have not had them occupied by relatives or in-laws in the first degree who habitually lived with them;

4° Who occupy premises subject to an administrative injunction for reasons of hygiene or public utility requiring their evacuation;

5° Who cease or have ceased the functions of which the title of occupation was accessory;

6° Who have at their disposal or can recover, by exercising their right of recovery, another premises meeting their needs and those of their relatives or in-laws in the first degree in their care;

7° Installed in the premises by the principal tenant or any other beneficiary of maintenance in the premises, without the consent of the lessor given under the conditions specified in point 5° of Article 1916; 8° Who occupy premises located in buildings acquired or expropriated following a public declaration, subject to the administration ensuring the rehousing of expelled tenants or occupants.

C. Of the right of recovery

###### Article1918

The right of recovery may be exercised by the owner who has obtained authorization to reconstruct or raise the building, or to make modifications to it requiring its evacuation. The exercise of this right of recovery is however subject to the following conditions.

The owner:

1° Must give the occupants, by extrajudicial act, three months' notice which shall indicate precisely the reason or reasons justifying the exercise of the right of recovery and shall bear reference to the administrative decision authorizing the works, all on pain of nullity;

2° Shall be required to commence the works within a maximum period of three months from the evacuation of the premises by the last occupant;

3° Must, to the extent of his means, proceed with the rehousing of the evicted occupants if he possesses other premises;

4° May not rent out, occupy or have occupied the premises before completion of the works;

5° Must, upon completion of the works, grant to the evicted occupant a priority right over any applicants.

###### Article1919

The owner who has not satisfied the obligations prescribed by the provisions of paragraphs 2, 3, 4 and 5 of Article 1918 above shall be liable to the evicted occupants for payment, for unjustified deprivation of enjoyment, of compensation which may not be less than the amount of the annual rent.

###### Article1920

The right of recovery also belongs to the owner who wishes to take back the building to occupy it himself or have it occupied by his spouse or by his relatives or in-laws in the first degree.

The owner who wishes to benefit from the above provisions must, by extrajudicial act, give three months' notice to the occupant whose premises he proposes to take back.

The owner must, within a maximum period of two months from the evacuation of the premises, occupy them himself or have them occupied by the beneficiary of the right of recovery for a minimum period of one year.

The owner who has not occupied or had occupied the premises under the conditions defined in the preceding paragraphs of this article shall be liable for payment to the evicted occupant of compensation which may not be less than the amount of the annual rent.

###### Article1921

The owner may not exercise the right of recovery provided for in Article 1920:

1° If he is the owner of another vacant premises corresponding to his needs and those of the beneficiaries of the right of recovery;

2° If he is the owner of another premises corresponding to his needs and those of the beneficiaries of the right of recovery, of which he can regain possession from occupants who do not benefit from the right to maintenance in the premises.

D. Miscellaneous provisions

###### Article1922

Any demand by the landlord or his agents, any agreement, tending to impose on the tenant, in an indirect form (handing over of money, taking over furniture, provision of service, etc.) a rental price higher than that which has been stipulated in the lease contract or than that which will result from the application of the provisions of point B. of this section, shall be null and void.

###### Article1923

A presidential decree may, in all or part of the territory of the Republic, subject to prior authorization the conversion of premises for residential use into premises for any other use. Offenders shall be punished by a civil fine which may not be less than 100,000 FD nor greater than three times the annual rent provided for prior to the offense. In all cases, the court shall order the reallocation and restoration of the premises at the expense of the offender within the time limit it shall set. In the event of failure to comply within the time limits set, the fine provided for may be doubled.

###### Article1924

Any landlord of premises for residential use rented unfurnished, convicted of having refused to rent a vacant premises to a prospective tenant, on the grounds of the existence or number of children for whom the latter is responsible, shall be punished by a civil fine equal to at least one quarter and at most three times the rent payable at the time of the refusal.

The perpetrator of the offense shall, in addition, be required to grant to the evicted family, for a minimum period of two years, a lease on the refused property, unless the premises have already been rented, in which case the said perpetrator of the offense shall be condemned, towards the injured party, to all damages and interest.

###### Article 1925

The maintenance repairs or minor upkeep for which the tenant is responsible, unless there is a clause to the contrary, are those designated as such by the usage of the premises and, failing that, by the general provisions of the first section of this chapter.

###### Article 1926

The lease of furniture provided to furnish the rented premises is deemed to be made for the ordinary duration of leases, according to the usage of the premises.

###### Article 1927

The lease of a furnished apartment is deemed to be taken out for the year, when it has been made at so much per year; For the month, when it has been made at so much per month;

For the day, when it has been made at so much per day.

If nothing establishes that the lease is made at so much per year, per month or per day, the lease is deemed to be made according to the usage of the premises.

###### Article 1928

If the tenant of a house or an apartment continues his enjoyment after the expiration of the written lease, without opposition from the landlord, there is tacit renewal of the original contract.

###### § 2. Le bail emphytéotique et le bail à construction

A. Du bail emphytéotique

###### Article 1929

The emphyteutic lease of immovable property is a contract by which the lessor confers on the lessee, called emphyteuta, a real property right called emphyteusis.

The lease is granted for a term which is between eighteen and ninety-nine years. It may not be extended by tacit renewal; in the event of express renewal, the total duration of the lease may not exceed 99 years.

The right thus conferred is capable of being mortgaged, transferable and seizable in the forms prescribed for immovable seizure.

###### Article 1930

The emphyteutic lease may only be validly granted by those who have the right to alienate, and under the same conditions, as in the same forms. It is enforceable against third parties from the publication at the registry of mortgages.

Immovable property belonging to minors or to adults under guardianship may be given on emphyteutic lease by virtue of a resolution of the family council.

Concerning premises for residential use, the lease contracts concluded by the emphyteuta with the tenants continue automatically with the owner of the property until the end of each of the lease contracts signed with the tenants and under the same conditions.

In the absence of contrary agreements, the emphyteutic lease is governed by the following provisions.

###### Article 1931

The lessee is liable for a periodic rent, called redevance, in the form of a sum of money or in a portion of fruits and products.

The lessee may not request the reduction of this redevance on grounds of partial loss of the property. In the event of failure to pay for six consecutive months, the lessor is authorized, after a summons that has remained without effect, to have the termination of the emphyteusis pronounced in court.

###### Article 1932

The lessee may not make any change to the property which decreases its value. Conversely, if he makes improvements or constructions which increase the value of the property, he may not destroy them, nor claim in this regard any compensation from the lessor.

The termination may also be requested by the lessor in the event of non-performance of the conditions of the contract or if the lessee has committed serious deterioration to the property.

Nevertheless, the courts may grant a time limit according to the circumstances.

###### Article 1933

The lessee is liable for all contributions and charges weighing on the property.

He is liable for the maintenance and repairs of all kinds on the constructions which exist at the time of the lease and those which will have been erected in execution of the agreement, but he is not obliged to rebuild the buildings, if he proves that they were destroyed by fortuitous event, by force majeure or that they perished by the defect of construction prior to the lease.

He is liable for fire, in accordance with Article 1394, paragraphs 2 and 3, of the Civil Code.

###### Article 1934

The lessee may acquire for the benefit of the property active easements, and encumber them, by deed, with passive easements, for a time which shall not exceed the duration of the lease, subject to notifying the owner. If the lessee has concluded agreements with third parties, they end with the termination of the emphyteusis, without the possibility for the lessee's contracting parties to claim extension, nor compensation.

###### Article 1935

The lessee benefits from the right of accession during the duration of the emphyteusis.

B. Du bail à construction

###### Article 1936

The building lease is the lease contract by which the lessee undertakes, as the principal obligation, to erect constructions on the lessor's land and to keep them in good state of repair throughout the duration of the lease.

The building lease is subject, subject to the provisions hereafter, to the rules provided for the emphyteutic lease.

When the lease provides for a possibility of purchase of the land by the lessee and the lessee exercises the option, the lease ends on the date of the sale.

###### Article 1937

The parties agree on their respective property rights over existing constructions and over constructions erected. In the absence of such an agreement, the lessor becomes the owner at the end of the lease and benefits from the improvements.

###### Article 1938

The building lease confers on the lessee a real property right.

This right may be mortgaged, as well as the constructions erected on the leased land; it may be seized in the forms prescribed for immovable seizure.

The lessee may assign all or part of his rights or contribute them to a company. The assignees or the company are bound by the same obligations as the assignor who remains guarantor thereof until the completion of all the constructions that the lessee has undertaken to erect in application of Article 1936. The lessee may grant the passive easements essential to the realization of the constructions provided for in the lease.

The provisions of the two preceding paragraphs are of public policy.

###### Article 1939

The lessee is liable for all charges, taxes and duties relating to both the constructions and the land. Unless otherwise stipulated in the lease, he may demolish, with a view to rebuilding them, the existing buildings.

###### Article 1940

The price of the lease may consist, in whole or in part, in the delivery to the lessor, at agreed dates and under agreed conditions, of immovable property or fractions of immovable property or titles giving entitlement to the ownership or enjoyment of such immovable property.

If a periodic rent payable in cash is stipulated, this rent is affected by a coefficient revisable by three-year periods counted from the completion of the works. However, the first revision takes place at the latest upon the expiration of the first six years of the lease.

The variation of the coefficient is proportional to that of the gross income of the immovable property. The income taken as the basis for the variation of the coefficient is that of the first calendar year following that of the completion of the works.

Disputes relating to the application of the provisions of the two preceding paragraphs are brought before the President of the Court of First Instance.

In the event of loss of the buildings, the rent is maintained at the rate it had reached on the date of this loss until the possible reconstruction of the destroyed buildings.

###### Article 1941

Passive easements, other than those mentioned in the fourth paragraph of Article 1938, privileges, mortgages or other charges arising from the lessee and, in particular, leases and occupancy titles of any kind relating to the constructions, are extinguished at the expiration of the lease except for residential lease contracts.

However, when the lease provides for a possibility of purchase of the land by the lessee and the lessee exercises the option in accordance with the fourth paragraph of Article 1936, the privileges and mortgages of the lessee registered before the exercise of the option are not extinguished at the expiration of the lease but retain their effects, until their date of extinction, on the immovable property that has become the property of the grantor. They extend by operation of law to the land and may secure loans granted for the acquisition of said land. Moreover, if the lease ends by judicial or amicable termination, the privileges and mortgages mentioned in the first paragraph and registered, as the case may be, before the publication of the legal claim seeking to obtain this termination or before the publication of the act or agreement recording it, are extinguished only on the date originally agreed for the expiration of the lease.

###### Article 1942

If during the term of the lease the constructions are destroyed by fortuitous event or force majeure, the termination may, at the request of either party, be ordered by judicial decision, which also rules on the compensation that may be due.

##### Chapter III. Of the hire of work and industry

###### Article 1943

There are three main types of hire of work and industry:

1° The hire of service;

2° That of carriers, both by land and by water, who undertake the transport of persons or goods;

3° That of architects, contractors of works and technicians pursuant to studies, estimates or contracts.

###### Section I: Of the hire of service

###### Article 1944

One can engage one's services only for a time, or for a determined undertaking.

In the case of a contract concluded for an indefinite duration, the hire of service may always cease by the will of one of the contracting parties.

Nevertheless, this right of unilateral termination may give rise to damages when, by the conditions under which it occurs, the termination has caused prejudice to the other party. For the determination of the compensation to be awarded, if applicable, account is taken of customs, the nature of the services engaged, the time elapsed, the deductions made and the payments made with a view to a retirement pension, and, in general, all the circumstances that may justify the existence and determine the extent of the prejudice caused.

The parties may not waive in advance the potential right to claim damages under the above provisions.

Disputes to which the application of the preceding paragraphs may give rise, when they are brought before the civil courts and before the courts of appeal, shall be investigated and judged urgently.

###### Section II: Of the hire of carriers by land and by water

###### Article 1945

Carriers by land and by water are subject, for the safekeeping and preservation of things entrusted to them, to the same obligations as innkeepers, which are dealt with in the title Of Deposit and Sequestration.

With regard to their liability, carriers are subject to the regime provided for in Articles L.2223-1 and following of the Commercial Code (Section 3 Of the liability of the carrier of the Commercial Code).

###### Article 1946

They are liable not only for what they have already received in their vessel or vehicle, but also for what has been delivered to them at the port or in the warehouse, to be placed in their vessel or vehicle.

###### Article 1947

They are liable for the loss and damage to things entrusted to them, unless they prove that they were lost and damaged by fortuitous event or force majeure.

###### Article 1948

Operators of public vehicles by land and by water, and those of public haulage, must keep a register of the money, effects and packages they take charge of.

###### Article 1949

Operators and directors of public vehicles and haulage, masters of barges and ships, are furthermore subject to particular regulations.

###### Section III: Of estimates and contracts

###### Article 1950

When one entrusts someone with making a work, one may agree that he will provide only his work or his industry, or that he will also provide the material.

###### Article 1951

When the contractor provides the material and the thing perishes, in whatever manner, before being delivered, the loss is borne by the contractor, unless the master of the work was in default in receiving the thing.

###### Article 1952

When the contractor provides only his work or his industry and the thing perishes, the risks of the thing are borne by its owner, except in case of fault of the contractor who, in that case, is liable for the loss.

The contractor who undertakes to manufacture an object with the material provided by the master of the work is not entitled to remuneration if the object perishes, even in the absence of fault on his part, before he has delivered it.

###### Article 1953

If the building perishes in whole or in part due to a defect in construction, even due to a defect in the ground, the architects, contractors and other persons bound to the master of the work by a contract for hire of work are liable for it for ten years.

###### Article 1954

Is deemed constructor of the work:

1° Any architect, contractor, technician or other person bound to the master of the work by a contract for hire of work;

2° Any person who sells, after completion, a work that he has constructed or had constructed; 3° Any person who, although acting in the capacity of agent of the owner of the work, performs a mission comparable to that of a hirer of work.

###### Article 1955

The presumption of liability established by Article 1953 also extends to damage that affects the solidity of equipment elements of a work, but only when these form an inseparable part of the works of roads, foundation, framework, enclosure or roofing. An equipment element is considered as forming an inseparable part of one of the works of roads, foundation, framework, enclosure or roofing when its removal, dismantling or replacement cannot be carried out without deterioration or removal of material from this work.

###### Article 1956

The other equipment elements of the work are subject to a proper functioning warranty of a minimum duration of two years from its acceptance.

###### Article 1957

The manufacturer of a work, part of a work or equipment element designed and produced to satisfy, in service condition, specific and predetermined requirements, is jointly and severally liable for the obligations imposed by articles 1953, 1955 and 1956 on the contractor who has implemented, without modification and in accordance with the rules established by the manufacturer, the work, part of work or equipment element in question.

Are assimilated to manufacturers for the application of this article:

- the person who has imported a work, part of a work or equipment element manufactured abroad
- the person who has presented it as their work by placing on it their name, trademark or any other distinctive sign.

###### Article 1958

Any natural or legal person whose liability may be engaged pursuant to articles 1953 to 1957 of this code is discharged from the responsibilities and warranties weighing on them, in application of articles 1953 to 1955, after ten years from the acceptance of the works or, in application of article 1956, upon expiration of the period referred to in that article.

###### Article 1959

Actions in liability directed against a subcontractor by reason of damage affecting a work or equipment elements of a work mentioned in articles 1953 and 1955 are prescribed after ten years from the acceptance of the works and, for damage affecting those equipment elements of the work mentioned in article 1956, after two years from that same acceptance.

###### Article 1960

Outside of the actions governed by articles 1956, 1958 and 1959, actions in liability directed against the builders designated in articles 1953 and 1954 and their subcontractors are prescribed after ten years from the acceptance of the works.

###### Article 1961

Any clause of a contract which has as its object, either to exclude or limit the liability provided for in articles 1953, 1954 and 1955, or to exclude the warranties provided for in articles 1956 and 1962 or to limit their scope, or to set aside or limit the joint and several liability provided for in article 1957, is deemed unwritten.

###### Article 1962

Acceptance is the act by which the project owner declares accepting the work with or without reservations. It occurs at the request of the most diligent party, either amicably or, failing that, judicially. It is, in any event, pronounced adversarially.

The warranty of perfect completion, to which the contractor is bound for a period of one year from acceptance, extends to the repair of all defects reported by the project owner, either by means of reservations mentioned in the acceptance report, or by written notification for those revealed after acceptance.

The time periods necessary for the execution of repair works are fixed by mutual agreement by the project owner and the contractor concerned.

In the absence of such agreement or in case of non-execution within the fixed period, the works may, after unsuccessful formal notice, be executed at the expense and risk of the defaulting contractor. The execution of works required under the warranty of perfect completion is established by mutual agreement, or, failing that, judicially.

The warranty does not extend to works necessary to remedy the effects of normal wear or use.

###### Article 1963

Are not considered as equipment elements of a work within the meaning of articles 1953, 1955, 1956 and 1957 the equipment elements, including their accessories, whose exclusive function is to permit the exercise of a professional activity in the work.

###### Article 1964

When an architect or contractor has undertaken the construction at a fixed price of a building, according to a plan settled and agreed upon with the owner of the land, they may not demand any increase in price, neither under the pretext of an increase in labor or materials, nor under that of changes or increases made to this plan, if these changes or increases have not been authorized in writing, and the price agreed upon with the owner.

###### Article 1965

The project owner may terminate, by their sole will, the fixed-price contract, even though the work has already begun, by compensating the contractor for all their expenses, all their work, and all that they could have earned from this undertaking.

###### Article 1966

The contract for work is dissolved by the death of the architect or contractor.

The death of the project owner only results in the termination of the contract if their person was a determining element in the conclusion of the contract.

The dissolution of the contract by death does not, however, allow the project owner to retain without compensation the unfinished work, in the state in which it is: the project owner is bound to pay in proportion to the price stated in the agreement, to the estate of the architect or contractor, the value of works done and that of materials prepared, but only when these works or materials can be useful to them. In the case of paragraph 2, the same effect applies to the heirs of the project owner.

###### Article 1967

The contractor is liable for the acts of the persons they employ.

###### Article 1968

The employees and subcontractors who have been employed in the construction of a building or other works made by contract, have action against the person for whom the works have been made, only up to the amount of which they find them indebted to the contractor, at the time when their action is brought.

#### Title X: Of Partnership

Chapter I. General Provisions

###### Article 1969

Partnership is instituted by two or more persons who agree by contract to commit to a common enterprise property or their industry with a view to sharing the profit or to benefit from the economy which may result therefrom.

Partnership may also be instituted, in cases provided by law, by the act of will of a single person.

The partners undertake to contribute to losses.

Even if they use only community property for contributions to a partnership or for the acquisition of partnership shares, two spouses alone or with other persons may be partners in the same partnership and participate together or not in partnership management.

###### Article 1970

Every partnership must have a lawful object, and be contracted for the common interest of the partners.

###### Article 1971

The provisions of this chapter are applicable to all partnerships unless otherwise provided by law by reason of their form or their object.

###### Article 1972

The articles of association must be established in writing. They determine, in addition to the contributions of each partner, the form, object, name, registered office, share capital, duration of the partnership and the terms of its operation.

###### Article 1973

The articles of association may not be modified, in the absence of a contrary clause, except by unanimous agreement of the partners. In no case may the commitments of a partner be increased without the consent of that partner.

###### Article 1974

Every partnership whose registered office is situated on the territory of the Republic of Djibouti is subject to the provisions of Djiboutian law.

Third parties may rely on the statutory registered office, but it is not enforceable against them by the partnership if the actual registered office is situated in another place.

###### Article 1975

The duration of the partnership may not exceed ninety-nine years.

###### Article 1976

If the articles of association do not contain all the particulars required by law or if a formality prescribed thereby has been omitted or irregularly performed, any interested party has standing to apply to the court for an order, subject to a periodic penalty payment, for the regularisation of the incorporation. The public prosecutor may act for the same purposes.

The same rules apply in the event of amendment of the articles of association.

The action for regularisation provided for in the first paragraph is time-barred after three years from the registration of the company or the publication of the instrument amending the articles of association.

###### Article 1977

The founders, as well as the first members of the management, executive or administrative bodies, are jointly and severally liable for damage caused either by the absence of a compulsory particular in the articles of association or by the omission or irregular performance of a formality prescribed for the incorporation of the company.

In the event of amendment of the articles of association, the provisions of the preceding paragraph apply to the members of the management, executive or administrative bodies then in office.

The action is time-barred after three years from the day of performance of the formality omitted or irregularly performed. The disappearance of the omission or irregularity does not preclude the exercise of the action for damages seeking compensation for the damage caused thereby. This action is time-barred after three years from the day on which the nullity was cured.

###### Article 1978

Companies other than the partnerships referred to in Chapter III enjoy legal personality from the time of their registration.

Until registration, the relations between the partners are governed by the company contract and by the general principles of law applicable to contracts and obligations.

###### Article 1979

Persons who have acted in the name of a company in formation before registration are bound by the obligations arising from acts thus performed, with joint and several liability if the company is commercial, without joint and several liability in other cases.

The company duly registered may take over the commitments entered into, which are then deemed to have been contracted by it from the outset.

###### Article1980

The contribution of property or a right subject to publicity for its enforceability against third parties may be published even before registration and subject to the condition that registration take place.

From the registration of the company, the effects of the formality relate back to the date of performance of the said formality.

###### Article 1981

The rights of each partner in the share capital are proportional to his contributions at the time of incorporation of the company or during the life thereof.

Contributions in industry do not contribute to the formation of the share capital but give rise to the allotment of shares conferring a right to share in the profits and the net assets, subject to contributing to losses.

###### Article 1982

Each partner is a debtor to the company for everything he has promised to contribute to it in kind, in cash or in industry.

Contributions in kind are made by the transfer of the corresponding rights and by the effective placing of the property at the disposal of the company.

Where the contribution is in ownership, the contributor is guarantor towards the company as a vendor towards his purchaser.

Where it is in use, the contributor is guarantor towards the company as a lessor towards his lessee. However, where the contribution in use relates to fungible things or to any other property normally due to be replaced during the life of the company, the contract transfers to the company the ownership of the property contributed, subject to the obligation to return a like quantity, quality and value; in this case, the contributor is guarantor under the conditions provided for in the preceding paragraph.

The partner who was required to contribute a sum to the company and who has not done so becomes by operation of law and without demand a debtor in respect of the interest on that sum from the day on which it was to be paid, without prejudice to further damages, if any. Furthermore, where calls for capital have not been made in order to achieve the full release of the capital, any interested party may apply to the president of the court of first instance sitting in summary proceedings either to order, subject to a periodic penalty payment, the administrators, managers and directors to make such calls for capital, or to appoint an agent responsible for carrying out this formality.

The partner who has undertaken to contribute his industry to the company owes it an account of all gains he has realised through the activity that is the subject of his contribution.

###### Article 1983

I. In cases where the law refers to this article to determine the conditions of price of a transfer of the social rights of a partner, or the repurchase thereof by the company, the value of these rights is determined, in the event of dispute, by an expert appointed either by the parties or, in the absence of agreement between them, by order of the president of the court of first instance sitting in summary proceedings and without possibility of appeal.

II. In cases where the articles of association provide for the transfer of the social rights of a partner or the repurchase of these rights by the company without their value being either determined or determinable, such value is determined, in the event of dispute, by an expert appointed in accordance with the conditions of the first paragraph.

III. In the cases provided for in points I. and II., the expert thus appointed is required to apply, where they exist, the rules and methods for determining the value provided for by the articles of association of the company or by any agreement binding the parties.

###### Article 1984

In addition to the action for compensation for damage suffered personally, one or more partners may bring the corporate action for liability against the managers. The claimants have standing to seek compensation for the damage suffered by the company; in the event of an order for damages, the damages are awarded to the company.

Any clause in the articles of association having the effect of making the exercise of the corporate action subject to prior opinion or authorisation of the general meeting or which involves advance waiver of the exercise of this action is deemed to be unwritten.

No decision of the general meeting of partners may have the effect of extinguishing an action for liability against the managers for fault committed in the performance of their mandate.

###### Article 1985

Every partner has the right to participate in collective decisions.

The co-owners of an undivided share are represented by a single agent, chosen from among the co-owners or outside them. In the event of disagreement, the agent is appointed by the court at the application of the most diligent.

If a share is encumbered with a usufruct, the right to vote belongs to the bare owner, except for decisions concerning the allocation of profits, where it is reserved for the usufructuary.

The articles of association may derogate from the provisions of the two preceding paragraphs.

###### Article 1986

The share of each partner in the profits and his contribution to losses are determined in proportion to his share in the share capital, and the share of the partner who has contributed only his industry is equal to that of the partner who has contributed the least, all subject to any clause to the contrary.

However, the stipulation attributing to a partner all of the profit derived from the company or exempting him from all of the losses, as well as that excluding a partner entirely from the profit or placing upon him all of the losses, are deemed to be unwritten.

###### Article 1987

A mortgage or any other security interest in rem over the assets of the company may be granted by virtue of powers resulting from resolutions or delegations established under private signature even though the creation of the mortgage or the security must be by authentic instrument.

###### Article 1988

The regular transformation of a company into a company of another form does not result in the creation of a new legal person. The same applies to the extension or any other statutory modification.

###### Article 1989

A company, even in liquidation, may be absorbed by another company or participate in the formation of a new company, by way of merger. It may also transfer its assets by way of division to existing companies or to new companies.

These operations may take place between companies of different forms.

They are decided by each of the interested companies, under the conditions required for the modification of its articles of association.

If the operation involves the creation of new companies, each of them is formed according to the rules specific to the form of company adopted.

###### Article 1990

The union of all shares in a single hand does not result in the dissolution by operation of law of the company. Any interested party may request this dissolution if the situation has not been regularized within one year. The court may grant the company a maximum period of six months to regularize the situation. It may not order dissolution if, on the day it rules on the merits, such regularization has taken place.

The ownership of the usufruct of all shares by the same person has no consequence on the existence of the company.

In case of dissolution, it results in the universal transfer of the company's assets to the sole member, without liquidation being necessary.

Creditors may oppose the dissolution within thirty days from its publication. A judicial decision rejects the opposition or orders either the repayment of the debts or the provision of guarantees if the company offers them and if they are deemed sufficient. The transfer of assets is effected and the legal person disappears only at the end of the opposition period or, as the case may be, when the opposition has been rejected at first instance or when the repayment of debts has been made or guarantees provided.

The provisions of the two preceding paragraphs are not applicable to companies whose sole member is a natural person.

###### Article 1991

The extension of the company is decided unanimously by the members or, if the articles of association so provide, by the majority required for their modification.

At least one year before the expiry date of the company, the members must be consulted to decide whether the company should be extended.

In default thereof, any member may apply to the president of the court of first instance, ruling on petition, for the appointment of a judicial representative responsible for initiating the consultation provided for above.

###### Article 1992

The company comes to an end:

1° By expiration of the time for which it was formed, except for extension made in accordance with Article 1991;

2° By the achievement or extinction of its object;

3° By annulment of the company contract;

4° By early dissolution decided by the members;

5° By early dissolution ordered by the court of first instance at the request of a member for just cause, particularly in case of failure by a member to perform his obligations, or of disagreement among members paralyzing the functioning of the company;

6° By early dissolution ordered by the court of first instance in the case provided for in Article 1990;

7° By the effect of a judgment ordering the closure of judicial liquidation for insufficiency of assets; 8° For any other cause provided for in the articles of association.

###### Article 1993

The dissolution of the company results in its liquidation, except in the cases provided for in Article 1989 and the third paragraph of Article 1990. It has effect with respect to third parties only after its publication.

The liquidator is appointed in accordance with the provisions of the articles of association. In the absence thereof, he is appointed by the members or, if the members have been unable to make this appointment, by judicial decision. The liquidator may be removed under the same conditions. The appointment and removal are enforceable against third parties only from their publication. Neither the company nor third parties may, to avoid their commitments, rely on an irregularity in the appointment or removal of the liquidator, provided that it has been properly published.

The legal personality of the company continues for the purposes of liquidation until the publication of its closure.

If the closure of the liquidation has not occurred within three years from the dissolution, the public prosecutor or any interested party may seize the court of first instance, which shall have the liquidation carried out or, if it has been commenced, its completion.

###### Article 1994

After payment of debts and reimbursement of share capital, the distribution of assets is carried out among the members in the same proportions as their participation in profits, unless otherwise provided by clause or agreement.

The rules concerning the division of estates, including preferential allocation, apply to distributions among members.

However, the members may validly decide, either in the articles of association or by a separate decision or act, that certain property shall be allocated to certain members. In default thereof, any contributed property found in kind in the divided mass is allocated, upon request, and subject to balancing payment if applicable, to the member who had made the contribution. This option is exercised before any other right to preferential allocation.

All the members, or only some of them, may also remain in undivided ownership for all or part of the company property. Their relations are then governed, at the closure of the liquidation, with respect to such property, by the provisions relating to undivided ownership.

###### Article 1995

The nullity of the company may result only from violation of the provisions of Articles 1969 and 1970, or from one of the causes of nullity of contracts in general.

Any statutory clause contrary to a mandatory provision of this title whose violation is not sanctioned by the nullity of the company, is deemed unwritten.

The nullity of acts or resolutions of the company's organs may result only from violation of a mandatory provision of this title or from one of the causes of nullity of contracts in general.

###### Article 1996

The action for nullity is extinguished when the cause of the nullity has ceased to exist on the day the court rules on the merits at first instance, except if this nullity is based on the illegality of the corporate object.

###### Article 1997

In case of nullity of a company or of acts or resolutions subsequent to its formation, based on a defect of consent or the incapacity of a member, and when regularization may occur, any person having an interest therein may give notice to the person who may effect it, either to regularize or to bring an action for nullity within six months under penalty of foreclosure. This notice is served on the company.

The company or a member may submit to the court seized within the period provided in the preceding paragraph, any measure likely to eliminate the interest of the claimant, particularly through the purchase of his membership rights. In this case, the court may either pronounce the nullity or make the proposed measures mandatory if they have been previously adopted by the company under the conditions provided for statutory amendments. The vote of the member whose rights are sought to be purchased has no influence on the decision of the company.

In case of dispute, the value of the membership rights to be reimbursed to the member is determined in accordance with the provisions of Article 1983.

###### Article 1998

The court, seized with an application for nullity, may, even of its own motion, set a time limit to allow for the curing of nullities. It may not pronounce the nullity less than two months after the date of the writ initiating proceedings.

If, to cure a nullity, a meeting must be convened, or a consultation of the members must be carried out, and if proof is provided of a proper convening of that meeting or of the sending to the members of the text of draft decisions accompanied by the documents that must be communicated to them, the president of the court of first instance seized by way of summary proceedings, grants the time necessary for the members to make a decision.

###### Article 1999

Actions for nullity of the company or of acts and deliberations subsequent to its formation are barred by limitation after three years from the day on which the nullity was incurred.

###### Article 2000

When the nullity of the company is pronounced, it terminates, without retroactive effect, the performance of the company contract.

With regard to the legal person that may have come into being, the nullity of the company produces the effects of a dissolution pronounced by the court.

###### Article 2001

Neither the company nor the members may invoke a nullity against third parties in good faith. However, the nullity resulting from incapacity or from one of the defects of consent is enforceable even against third parties in good faith by the incapable person and their legal representatives, or by the member whose consent was obtained through error, fraud or duress.

###### Article 2002

The action for liability based on the annulment of the company or of acts and deliberations subsequent to the formation is barred by limitation after three years from the day on which the annulment decision became final.

The disappearance of the cause of nullity does not prevent the exercise of the action for damages seeking compensation for the prejudice caused by the defect with which the company, the act or the deliberation was tainted. This action is barred by limitation after three years from the day on which the nullity was cured.

##### Chapitre II. De la société civile

###### Section I : Dispositions générales

###### Article 2003

The provisions of this chapter apply to all civil companies, unless they are derogated from by the special legal status to which some of them are subject.

All companies to which the law does not attribute another character by reason of their form, their nature, or their object have a civil character.

###### Article 2004

The capital is divided into equal shares.

The provisions of Chapter I of Title II of Book III of the Commercial Code relating to the variable capital of companies are applicable to civil companies.

###### Section II : De la gérance

###### Article 2005

The company is managed by one or more persons, whether members or not, appointed either by the articles of association, or by a separate instrument, or by a decision of the members.

The articles of association set the rules for appointing the manager or managers and the method of organizing the management. Unless otherwise provided in the articles of association, the manager is appointed by a decision of the members representing more than half of the company shares.

Where the articles of association are silent, and if the members have not decided otherwise at the time of appointment, the managers are deemed to be appointed for the duration of the company.

If, for any reason whatsoever, the company finds itself without a manager, any member may apply to the president of the court of first instance ruling on application for the appointment of a representative responsible for bringing the members together to appoint one or more managers.

###### Article 2006

Apart from the cases referred to in Article 1992, the company is terminated by early dissolution that may be pronounced by the court of first instance at the request of any interested party, when it has been without a manager for more than one year.

###### Article 2007

The appointment and termination of office of managers must be published.

Neither the company nor third parties may, to escape their commitments, rely on an irregularity in the appointment of managers or in the termination of their office, when these decisions have been duly published.

###### Article 2008

If a legal person exercises the management, its directors are subject to the same conditions and obligations and incur the same civil and criminal liabilities as if they were managers in their own name, without prejudice to the joint and several liability of the legal person they direct.

###### Article 2009

In relations between members, the manager may perform all management acts required by the interest of the company.

If there are several managers, they exercise these powers separately, except for the right of each to oppose an operation before it is concluded.

All of the above, in the absence of provisions in the articles of association on the method of administration.

###### Article 2010

In relations with third parties, the manager binds the company by acts falling within the company's object. In case of plurality of managers, they hold separately the powers provided for in the preceding paragraph. Opposition made by one manager to the acts of another manager has no effect with regard to third parties, unless it is established that they had knowledge of it.

Provisions in the articles of association limiting the powers of managers are unenforceable against third parties, unless it is established that they had knowledge of them.

###### Article 2011

Each manager is individually liable to the company and to third parties, whether for infringements of laws and regulations, or for violation of the articles of association, or for faults committed in their management. If several managers have participated in the same acts, their liability is joint and several with regard to third parties and members. However, in their relations with each other, the court determines each person's contributory share in the reparation of the damage.

###### Article 2012

Unless otherwise provided in the articles of association, the manager may be removed by a decision of the members representing more than half of the company shares. If the removal is decided without just cause, it may give rise to damages.

The manager may also be removed by the courts for legitimate cause, at the request of any member. Unless otherwise provided, the removal of a manager, whether a member or not, does not entail the dissolution of the company. If the removed manager is a member, he may, unless otherwise agreed in the articles of association, or unless the other members decide on the early dissolution of the company, withdraw from it and may claim reimbursement of the value of his company rights determined, in the absence of an amicable agreement, by expert opinion, in accordance with Article 1983.

###### Section III : Des décisions collectives

###### Article 2013

Decisions that exceed the powers granted to managers are made in accordance with the provisions of the articles of association or, in the absence of such provisions, by unanimous consent of the members.

###### Article 2014

Decisions are made by the members meeting in an assembly. The articles of association may also provide that they result from a written or electronic consultation.

###### Article 2015

Decisions may also result from the consent of all members expressed in an instrument.

###### Section IV : De l'information des associés

###### Article 2016

Members have the right to obtain, at least once a year, access to the company's books and documents, and to ask written questions about the company's management to which answers must be provided in writing within one month.

###### Article 2017

The managers must, at least once a year, account for their management to the partners. This accounting must include a comprehensive written report on the activity of the company during the past year or financial period, indicating the profits realized or foreseeable and the losses incurred or anticipated.

###### Section V : Obligations of partners towards third parties

###### Article 2018

With regard to third parties, the partners are indefinitely liable for corporate debts in proportion to their share in the capital at the date of maturity or on the day of cessation of payments.

The partner who has only contributed their labor is liable as the one whose share in the capital is the smallest.

###### Article 2019

Creditors may not pursue payment of corporate debts against a partner until after having previously and unsuccessfully pursued the legal entity.

###### Article 2020

All actions against non-liquidating partners or their heirs and successors are time-barred after three years from the publication of the dissolution of the company.

###### Article 2021

If there is insolvency, personal bankruptcy, liquidation of assets or judicial settlement affecting one of the partners, unless the other partners unanimously decide to dissolve the company early or unless such dissolution is provided for in the articles of association, the interested party's share rights shall be reimbursed under the conditions set out in Article 1983, and they shall then lose their status as a partner.

###### Section VI : Transfers of shares

###### Article 2022

Shares may only be transferred with the approval of all partners.

The articles of association may, however, provide that this approval shall be obtained either by a majority that they determine or granted by the managers. They may also waive the approval requirement for transfers made to partners or to the spouse of one of them. Unless the articles of association provide otherwise, transfers made to ascendants or descendants of the transferor are not subject to approval.

The proposed transfer is notified, with a request for approval, to the company and to each of the partners. It is only notified to the company when the articles of association provide that approval may be granted by the managers. When two spouses are simultaneously members of a company, transfers made by one to the other must, to be valid, result from a notarial deed or a deed under private signature having acquired certain date otherwise than by the death of the transferor.

###### Article 2023

When several partners express their intention to acquire, they are, unless otherwise provided by clause or agreement, deemed purchasers in proportion to the number of shares they previously held. If no partner comes forward as a purchaser, the company may have the shares acquired by a third party designated unanimously by the other partners or according to the procedures provided for in the articles of association. In case of deadlock, Article 2024, paragraph 1 applies. The company may also proceed to repurchase the shares with a view to their cancellation.

The name of the proposed purchaser(s), whether partners or third parties, or the offer of repurchase by the company, as well as the price offered, are notified to the transferor. In case of dispute over the price, it is fixed in accordance with the provisions of Article 1983, all without prejudice to the right of the transferor to retain their shares.

###### Article 2024

If no purchase offer is made to the transferor within six months from the last of the notifications provided for in the third paragraph of Article 2022, approval of the transfer is deemed granted, unless the other partners decide, within the same period, on the early dissolution of the company. In the latter case, the transferor may render this decision null and void by making known that they are renouncing the transfer within one month from said decision.

###### Article 2025

The provisions of the two preceding articles may only be derogated from to modify the six-month period provided for in the first paragraph of Article 2024, and without the period provided for in the articles of association being able to exceed one year or be less than one month.

###### Article 2026

The transfer of shares must be recorded in writing. It is made enforceable against the company by service of the transfer made or, if the articles of association so stipulate, by transfer in the company's registers. It is only enforceable against third parties after completion of these formalities and after publication.

###### Article 2027

Shares may be subject to a pledge recorded either by notarial deed or by deed under private signatures served on the company or accepted by it in a notarial deed, and giving rise to publication the date of which determines the rank of pledged creditors. Those whose securities are published on the same day rank equally.

The privilege of the pledgee creditor subsists over the pledged share rights by the mere fact of publication of the pledge.

###### Article 2028

Any partner may obtain from the other partners their consent to a pledge project under the same conditions as their approval for a transfer of shares.

The consent given to the pledge project entails approval of the transferee in case of forced realization of the shares on condition that this realization is notified one month before the sale to the partners and to the company.

Each partner may substitute themselves for the purchaser within five clear days from the sale. If several partners exercise this option, they are, unless otherwise provided by clause or agreement, deemed purchasers in proportion to the number of shares they previously held. If no partner exercises this option, the company may repurchase the shares itself, with a view to their cancellation.

###### Article 2029

Forced realization that does not proceed from a pledge to which the other partners have given their consent must likewise be notified one month before the sale to the partners and to the company. The partners may, within this period, decide on the dissolution of the company or the acquisition of the shares under the conditions provided for in Articles 2023 and 2024.

If the sale has taken place, the partners or the company may exercise the right of substitution recognized to them by Article 2028. The non-exercise of this option entails approval of the purchaser.

###### Section VII : Withdrawal or death of a partner

###### Article 2030

Without prejudice to the rights of third parties, a partner may withdraw totally or partially from the company, under the conditions provided for in the articles of association or, failing that, after authorization given by a unanimous decision of the other partners. This withdrawal may also be authorized for just cause by a court decision.

Unless certain assets of the company of equivalent value are allocated to them, the partner who withdraws is entitled to reimbursement of the value of their share rights, fixed, failing amicable agreement, by expert determination, in accordance with Article 1983.

###### Article 2031

The company is not dissolved by the death of a partner, but continues with their heirs or legatees, unless the articles of association provide that they must be approved by the partners.

It may, however, be agreed that this death will result in the dissolution of the company or that the company will continue with the surviving partners only.

It may also be agreed that the company will continue either with the surviving spouse, or with one or more of the heirs, or with any other person designated by the articles of association or, if they so authorize, by testamentary provision.

Unless the articles of association provide otherwise, when the succession devolves to a legal entity, the latter may only become a partner with the approval of the other partners, given according to the statutory conditions or, failing that, by unanimous agreement of the partners.

###### Article 2032

Heirs or legatees who do not become partners are only entitled to the value of the company shares of their predecessor. This value must be paid to them by the new holders of the shares or by the company itself if it has repurchased them for cancellation.

The value of these company rights is determined as of the date of death by expert assessment, except by amicable agreement, under the conditions provided for in Article 1983.

##### Chapter III: Undisclosed Partnership

###### Article 2033

The partners may agree that the company will not be registered. The company is then called an "undisclosed partnership". Such a company is not a legal person and is not subject to publicity requirements. Its existence may be proved by any means.

The partners freely agree on the object, operation and conditions of the undisclosed partnership, subject to the public policy rules of the general law of companies.

###### Article 2034

Unless a different organization has been provided for, relations between partners are governed, as appropriate, either by the provisions applicable to civil companies, if the company has a civil nature, or, if it has a commercial nature, by those applicable to general partnerships.

###### Article 2035

With regard to third parties, each partner remains owner of the property that he makes available to the company. Property acquired through the use or reinvestment of undivided funds during the duration of the company and property that was undivided before being made available to the company are deemed undivided among the partners.

The same applies to property that the partners have agreed to place in undivided ownership.

It may further be agreed that one of the partners is, with regard to third parties, owner of all or part of the property that he acquires for the purpose of carrying out the company's object.

###### Article 2036

Each partner contracts in his own name and is alone bound with regard to third parties.

However, if the participants act in the capacity of partners with the knowledge and awareness of third parties, each of them is liable to the latter for obligations arising from acts performed in that capacity by one of the others, jointly and severally if the company is commercial, without joint and several liability in other cases.

The same applies to a partner who, by his interference, has led the contracting party to believe that he intended to bind himself towards him, or whose engagement is proven to have been for his benefit.

In all cases, with regard to property deemed undivided pursuant to Article 2035 (paragraphs 2 and 3), the provisions of Chapter VI of Title I of Book III of this Code (Articles 933 and following) apply in relations with third parties, or, if the formalities provided for in Article 2037 have been completed, those of Title XI of this Book (Article 2071 and following), all partners being then, unless otherwise agreed, deemed managers of the undivided property.

###### Article 2037

When the undisclosed partnership is of indefinite duration, its dissolution may result at any time from a notification sent by one of them to all the partners provided that this notification is made in good faith and not at an inopportune time.

Unless otherwise agreed, no partner may request the partition of undivided property pursuant to the rules applicable to undivided ownership under Article 2035 as long as the company has not been dissolved.

###### Article 2038

The provisions of this chapter are applicable to de facto companies.

##### Chapter IV: Professional Civil Company

###### Section I: General Provisions

###### Article 2039

Professional civil companies may be formed between natural persons exercising the same liberal profession subject to a legislative or regulatory status or whose title is protected, and in particular between public and ministerial officers, which enjoy legal personality and are subject to the provisions of this Chapter III.

These professional civil companies have as their object the joint exercise of the profession of their members, notwithstanding any legislative or regulatory provision reserving the exercise of this profession to natural persons.

Registration of the company may only take place after approval by the competent authority or its registration on the list or roll of the professional order.

The conditions for applying this Chapter III to each profession are determined by the laws and regulations applicable to each of the professions considered.

###### Article 2040

A decree may authorize, under the conditions it determines, natural persons exercising a liberal profession referred to in the preceding article to form companies governed by this Chapter III with natural persons exercising other liberal professions for the purpose of jointly exercising their respective professions.

Members of the professions referred to in Article 2039 may only enter into a professional civil company grouping persons belonging to liberal professions not referred to in Article 2039 on condition of having been authorized to do so by the body exercising disciplinary jurisdiction over them. In the event of refusal of authorization, an appeal may be made to the Civil Chamber of the Court of Appeal.

Companies referred to in this article may only perform the acts of a given profession through one of their members qualified to exercise that profession.

###### Article 2041

Only persons who, prior to the formation of the company, regularly exercised the profession as well as those who, meeting all the conditions required by the laws and regulations in force, are entitled to exercise it, may be partners, subject to the provisions of Article 2062.

###### Article 2042

Except where otherwise provided by the regulations specific to each profession, any partner may only be a member of one professional civil company and may not exercise the same profession individually.

###### Article 2043

Natural persons holding a public or ministerial office and exercising the same profession may also form professional civil companies among themselves for the joint exercise of their profession, without these companies themselves being appointed holders of an office. The application of the preceding paragraph is subject to the provisions of Article 2039, paragraph 3. The provisions of Article 2040 are applicable to companies formed pursuant to this article.

###### Section II: Formation of the Company

###### Article 2044

Professional civil companies are freely formed under the conditions provided for by the regulations specific to each profession, which shall determine the approval or registration procedure and the role of professional bodies.

With regard to public and ministerial offices, the company must be approved or granted title to the office under the conditions to be provided for by decree.

###### Article 2045

The articles of association of the company must be drawn up in writing. The regulations specific to each profession determine the information that must mandatorily appear in the articles of association.

###### Article 2046

The company name of the company must be immediately preceded or followed by the mention: "professional civil company" or the initials: "SCP", themselves followed by an indication of the profession exercised.

The name of one or more partners may be included in the company name.

###### Article 2047

The share capital is divided into equal shares which may not be represented by negotiable securities.

The regulations specific to each profession may limit the number of partners.

###### Article 2048

The company shares must be subscribed in full by the partners. Those representing contributions in kind must be fully paid up upon incorporation of the company.

The allocation of company shares is mentioned in the articles of association. It takes into account cash contributions and, according to the valuation made, contributions in kind and in particular contributions of intangible rights.

The articles of association may, with the unanimous consent of the partners, set the principles and methods applicable to determining the value of company shares.

Unless otherwise provided by the regulations specific to each profession, the value of company shares takes into consideration a value representative of the civil clientele. However, with the unanimous consent of the partners, the articles of association may exclude this value representative of the civil clientele from the valuation of company shares.

###### Section III : Operation of the Company

###### Article 2049

All partners are managers unless otherwise stipulated in the articles of association, which may designate one or more managers from among the partners or provide for their designation by a subsequent act.

The conditions for appointment and removal of managers, their powers and the duration of their term are determined by the articles of association. The powers of managers may in no case have the effect of creating subordination of the partners to the company for the performance of their professional acts.

###### Article 2050

Managers are liable, individually or jointly and severally as the case may be, to the company or to third parties, either for violations of laws and regulations, or for breach of the articles of association, or for faults committed in their management. If several managers have cooperated in the same acts, the court determines the contributory share of each in the apportionment of damages.

###### Article 2051

Decisions that exceed the powers of the managers are made by the partners.

Each partner has, unless otherwise provided by the decree specific to each profession or, failing that, the articles of association, a single vote, regardless of the number of company shares held. The regulations specific to each profession and, failing that, the articles of association determine the method of consulting the partners, the quorum and majority rules required for the validity of their decisions and the conditions under which they are informed of the state of company affairs.

###### Article 2052

Remuneration of any kind, paid in consideration of the professional activity of the partners, constitutes revenue of the company and is received by it.

The regulations specific to each profession and, failing that, the articles of association may determine methods of profit distribution that would not be proportional to capital contributions. In the absence of a regulatory provision or statutory clause, each partner is entitled to the same share of profits.

###### Article 2053

The partners are indefinitely liable for company debts to third parties. This provision does not prevent two spouses from being partners in the same professional civil company.

The company's creditors may not pursue payment of company debts against a partner unless they have first unsuccessfully served formal notice on the company and on condition that they join it as a party.

The articles of association may stipulate that, in relations between partners, each of them is liable for company debts in the proportion they determine.

###### Article 2054

Each partner is liable on his entire assets for the professional acts he performs. The company is jointly and severally liable with him for the harmful consequences of these acts. The company or the partners must take out professional liability insurance, under the conditions provided by the regulations specific to each profession.

###### Article 2055

The regulations specific to each profession determine the responsibilities and powers of each partner and of the company for the practice of the profession, and provide, where appropriate, for the adaptation of the rules of professional ethics and discipline applicable to them.

###### Article 2056

A partner may withdraw from the company, either by transferring his company shares or by the company reimbursing him the value of his shares.

Upon the withdrawal of a partner, the professional civil company is subject to registration amendments and the transferee of company shares to the approval procedure, as provided by the regulations specific to each profession.

With regard to public and ministerial offices, the regulations specific to each profession determine the conditions under which the transferee of company shares must be approved by the appointing authority and the withdrawal of the partner who is reimbursed the value of his shares must be approved.

###### Article 2057

Company shares may be transmitted or transferred to third parties with the consent of partners representing at least three-quarters of the votes. However, the articles of association may impose the requirement of a higher majority or unanimity of the partners.

The transmission or proposed transfer is notified to the company and to each of the partners. If the company has not made its decision known within two months from the last of the notifications provided for in this paragraph, consent is implicitly given.
