If the company has refused to give its consent, the partners are required, within six months from such refusal, to acquire or have acquired the company shares at a price representing their value determined in accordance with the third and fourth paragraphs of Article 2048 or, where the articles of association do not provide for the method of determining the price, a price fixed under the conditions provided for in Article 1983 of the Civil Code.

###### Article 2058

Unless otherwise provided in the articles of association, company shares are freely transferable between partners. If the articles of association contain a clause limiting freedom of transfer, the provisions of Article 2057, paragraphs 2 and 3, apply in the absence of statutory stipulations.

###### Article 2059

When a partner so requests, the company is required either to have his shares acquired by other partners or third parties, or to acquire them itself, under the conditions determined by the regulations specific to each profession. In the latter case, the company is required to reduce its capital by the amount of the nominal value of these shares.

###### Article 2060

The transfer of company shares must be recorded in writing. It is made enforceable against the company in the forms provided for in Article 1994.

The transfer of company shares is only enforceable against third parties after completion of these formalities and, furthermore, after publication inserted in the Official Journal or in a legal notices journal.

###### Article 2061

Unless otherwise provided by the regulations specific to each profession, the articles of association freely determine the duration of the company.

###### Article 2062

Unless otherwise provided by the special regulations for each profession or, failing that, by the articles of association, the professional civil company is not dissolved by the death, incapacity or withdrawal from the company of a partner for any other reason. Nor is it dissolved when one of the partners is subject to a permanent prohibition from practicing his profession.

In the event of death, the beneficiaries of the deceased partner do not acquire the status of partner. However, they have the option to transfer the company shares of the deceased partner, within the time limits and conditions provided for in Articles 2057 and 2060; furthermore, if one or more of them meet the conditions required by Article 2041, they may request the consent of the company under the conditions provided for in Article 2057. If consent is given, the company shares of the deceased partner may be the subject of a preferential allocation to the approved beneficiary, subject to payment of a balancing sum if applicable. In the event of refusal, the above-mentioned time limit is extended by the time elapsed between the request for consent and its refusal. If no transfer or consent has occurred upon expiration of the time limit, the company or the partners reimburse the value of the company shares to the beneficiaries under the conditions provided for in Article 2059.

The partner subject to a permanent prohibition from practicing the profession loses, on the day of such prohibition, the status of partner. The provisions of the preceding paragraph apply, with the exception of those concerning the beneficiaries of the person concerned.

During the time limit provided for in paragraph 2 above, the partner, his heirs or beneficiaries, as the case may be, may not exercise any right in the company. However, and unless they are deprived thereof, they retain entitlement to the distribution of profits, under the conditions provided for by the articles of association.

###### Article 2063

The special regulations for each profession determine the effects of a temporary prohibition from practicing the profession with which a partner or the company may be subject.

###### Article 2064

The dissolution or extension of the company is decided by the partners voting by a majority that will be determined by the special regulations for the profession.

When the company formed between partners practicing different professions no longer includes, at least, one partner practicing each of the professions concerned, the partners may, within a period of one year, regularize the situation or decide to modify the corporate purpose. Failing this, the company is dissolved.

###### Article 2065

The professional civil company may not, unless otherwise provided by the special regulations for the profession, be transformed into a company of another form.

A company of another form may be transformed into a professional civil company without such transformation resulting in the creation of a new legal entity.

###### Article 2066

The nullity of the professional civil company may only be pronounced for lack of a constitutive instrument or in the cases provided for by the provisions governing the nullities of contracts.

Neither the company nor the partners may invoke the nullity against third parties.

###### Article 2067

The designation "professional civil company" may only be used by companies subject to the provisions of this Chapter III.

The unlawful use of this designation or any expression liable to cause confusion therewith is punishable by one year's imprisonment and a fine of 1,000,000 FD, or by one of these two penalties only.

The court may, in addition, order the publication of the judgment, at the expense of the convicted person, and its posting.

###### Article 2068

Articles 1969 to 2037 are applicable to professional civil companies, in their provisions that are not contrary to those of this chapter.

###### Article 2069

The partners of professional civil companies formed and operating in accordance with the provisions of this chapter are personally subject to individual income tax for the share of company profits attributed to them.

###### Section IV: Civil companies for sharing resources

###### Article 2070

Notwithstanding any contrary legislative or regulatory provisions, natural or legal persons practicing liberal professions and in particular public and ministerial officers, may form civil companies among themselves with the exclusive purpose of facilitating for each of their members the exercise of his activity.

For this purpose, the partners pool the resources useful for the exercise of their professions, without the company itself being able to exercise them.

#### Title XI: Conventional regime of undivided ownership

Chapter I: Conventions relating to the exercise of undivided rights in the absence of a usufructuary

###### Article 2071

The co-owners in undivided ownership, if they all consent thereto, may agree to remain in undivided ownership.

On pain of nullity, the agreement must be established in writing containing the designation of the undivided property and the indication of the shares belonging to each co-owner. If the undivided property includes debts, the agreement is enforceable against the debtors concerned only from the service thereof upon them, or its acceptance by the debtor in an authentic instrument; if it includes immovable property, the formalities of land registration must be completed.

###### Article 2072

The agreement may be concluded for a fixed term, less than or equal to five years. It is renewable by an express decision of the parties. Partition may not be provoked before the agreed term unless there are just grounds therefor.

It may also be decided that this fixed-term agreement will be renewed by tacit renewal, for a fixed or indefinite term. In the absence of such an agreement, the undivided ownership will be governed by Articles 933 and following upon expiration of the fixed-term agreement.

The agreement may also be concluded for an indefinite term. Partition may, in this case, be provoked at any time, provided that it is not in bad faith or at an inopportune time.

###### Article 2073

The agreement tending to maintain undivided ownership requires the capacity or power to dispose of the undivided property.

It may, however, be concluded on behalf of a minor, by his legal representative alone; but, in this case, the minor having reached majority may terminate it, whatever its duration, within the year following his majority.

###### Article 2074

The co-owners may appoint one or more managers, chosen or not from among them.

The terms and conditions for appointing and removing the manager may be determined by a unanimous decision of the co-owners.

In the absence of such an agreement, the manager chosen from among the co-owners may only be removed from his functions by a unanimous decision of the other co-owners.

The manager, who is not a co-owner, may be removed under the conditions agreed upon between his principals or, failing that, by a decision taken by a majority of the co-owners in number and in shares. In all cases, removal may be pronounced by the court at the request of a co-owner when the manager, through his mismanagement, endangers the interests of the undivided ownership.

If the removed manager is a co-owner, the agreement shall be deemed concluded for an indefinite term from the time of his removal.

###### Article 2075

The manager represents the co-owners within the limits of his powers, either for acts of civil life or in court, both as plaintiff and as defendant. He is required to indicate, for purely informative purposes, the names of all the co-owners in the first procedural act.

The manager administers the undivided property and exercises, for this purpose, the powers attributed to each spouse over community property. He may not, however, dispose of tangible movable property except for the needs of normal operation of the undivided property, or if the items are difficult to preserve or subject to deterioration. Any clause extending the manager's powers is deemed unwritten.

###### Article 2076

The manager exercises the powers granted to him by the preceding article even when there is an incapacitated person among the co-owners.

###### Article 2077

Decisions that exceed the manager's powers are made unanimously, except that the manager, if he is himself a co-owner, may use the procedures provided for in Article 942.

If there are incapacitated minors or adults among the co-owners, the decisions referred to in the preceding paragraph give rise to the application of the protective rules provided for in their favor. It may be agreed among the co-owners that in the absence of incapacitated persons, certain categories of decisions will be made otherwise than unanimously. However, no undivided immovable property may be alienated without the agreement of all co-owners, except pursuant to Article 942 or the rules of management of another's affairs.

###### Article 2078

The indivision agreement may regulate the method of administration in case of a plurality of managers. In the absence of special stipulations, they hold separately the powers provided for in Article 2075, except the right of each to oppose any operation before it is concluded.

###### Article 2079

The manager is entitled, unless otherwise agreed, to remuneration for his work. The conditions are fixed by the co-owners, excluding the interested party, or, failing that, by the president of the Court of First Instance ruling provisionally.

The manager is liable, as a mandatary, for faults he commits in his management.

###### Article 2080

Each co-owner may require the communication of all documents relating to the management. The manager must, once a year, account for his management to the co-owners. On this occasion, he shall indicate in writing the profits realized and the losses incurred or foreseeable.

Each co-owner is required to participate in the expenses of preservation of the undivided property. In the absence of a particular agreement, the texts governing legal indivision are applicable to the exercise of the right of use and enjoyment, as well as to the distribution of profits and losses.

###### Article 2081

Similarly, in case of alienation of all or part of the rights of a co-owner in the undivided property, or in one or more of these properties, the co-owners benefit from the rights of preemption and substitution provided for by this legal regime. However, as soon as an undivided share is devolved to a person outside the indivision, for whatever reason, the agreement is deemed concluded for an indefinite period.

###### Article 2082

The co-owners may agree that upon the death of one of them, each of the survivors may acquire the share of the deceased, or that the surviving spouse, or any other designated heir, may have it attributed to him on condition of accounting for it to the estate according to its value at the time of acquisition or attribution.

If several co-owners or several heirs simultaneously exercise their right of acquisition or attribution, they are deemed, unless otherwise agreed, to acquire together the share of the deceased in proportion to their respective rights in the indivision or the estate.

The provisions of this article may not prejudice the application of provisions relating to preferential attributions.

###### Article 2083

The right of acquisition or attribution lapses if its beneficiary has not exercised it by notification made to the surviving co-owners and to the heirs of the predeceased within one month from the day he was given notice to decide. This notice cannot itself take place before the expiration of the period provided for in the title On Successions for making inventory and deliberating.

When no right of acquisition or attribution has been provided for, or when it has lapsed, the share of the deceased devolves to his heirs or legatees. In such a case, the indivision agreement shall be deemed concluded for an indefinite period from the opening of the succession.

###### Article 2084

Article 952 is applicable to creditors of the indivision, as well as to personal creditors of the co-owners.

However, the latter may provoke partition only in cases where their debtor could himself provoke it. In other cases, they may pursue the seizure and sale of their debtor's share in the indivision by following the forms provided for by the Code of Civil Procedure. The provisions of Article 2081 are then applicable.

##### Chapter II: Agreements Relating to the Exercise of Undivided Rights in the Presence of a Usufructuary

###### Article 2085

When the undivided property is encumbered with a usufruct, agreements, subject in principle to the provisions of the preceding chapter, may be concluded either among the bare owners, or among the usufructuaries, or between them.

There may likewise be an agreement between those who are in indivision for enjoyment and the person who is bare owner of all the property, as well as between the universal usufructuary and the bare owners.

###### Article 2086

When the usufructuaries have not been party to the agreement, third parties who have dealt with the manager of the indivision cannot rely, to the prejudice of the usufruct rights, on the powers that would have been conferred upon him by the bare owners.

###### Article 2087

When the agreement entered into between usufructuaries and bare owners provides that decisions will be made by a majority in number and in shares, the voting right attached to the shares is divided in half between the usufruct and the bare ownership, unless the parties have agreed otherwise.

Any expenditure exceeding the obligations of the usufructuary, as they are defined by the provisions of Section III of Chapter One (Articles 721 et seq.), binds him only with his consent given in the agreement itself or by a subsequent act.

The alienation of full ownership of the undivided property cannot be made without the agreement of the usufructuary, except in the case where it is provoked by creditors entitled to pursue the sale.

#### Title XII: Loan

###### Article 2088

There are two kinds of loan:

That of things which may be used without destroying them;

And that of things which are consumed by the use made of them.

The first type is called loan for use.

The second is called loan for consumption.

Chapter I. Loan for Use

###### Section I: Nature of the Loan for Use

###### Article 2089

The loan for use is a contract by which one party delivers a thing to the other to use it, on condition that the borrower return it after having used it. The lender remains owner of the thing lent.

###### Article 2090

In the absence of contrary provision by the parties, the loan for use is gratuitous.

###### Article 2091

Anything that is in commerce and which is not consumed by use may be the object of such a loan.

###### Article 2092

The obligations that are formed by the loan for use pass to the heirs of the one who lends, and to the heirs of the one who borrows.

But if the loan was made only in consideration of the person of the borrower, the heirs must immediately return the loaned thing.

###### Section II: Obligations of the borrower

###### Article 2093

The borrower is required to watch over, as a normally diligent person, the safekeeping and preservation of the loaned thing. He may only use it for the use determined by its nature or by the agreement; all of this on pain of nullity of the agreement, without prejudice to damages, if applicable.

###### Article 2094

If, to use the thing, the borrower has made some expense, he cannot obtain reimbursement from the lender.

It is otherwise if, during the duration of the loan, the borrower was obliged, for the preservation of the thing, to make some extraordinary expense, necessary and so urgent that he could not warn the lender, the latter is then required to reimburse him.

###### Article 2095

He is not liable for fortuitous events or force majeure when the destruction of the thing, occurring during its normal use, results from such a fact or from the proper functioning of the loaned thing. The borrower is however liable for the loss of the loaned thing occurring by fortuitous event or force majeure:

1° If he makes use of the thing for a different purpose or for a longer time than he should;

2° If the loaned thing perishes by fortuitous event that the borrower could have countered by using a thing that belonged to him, or if, being forced to only be able to preserve one of the two things, he preferred to save his own;

3° If the borrower had estimated the value of the thing upon lending it, unless otherwise agreed; 4° If by express or tacit agreement the borrower has taken the fortuitous events at his charge.

The liability weighing on the borrower provided for in the preceding paragraph does not apply when the thing is the object of joint use by the lender and the borrower or when the lender has reserved the possibility of using the loaned thing.

###### Article 2096

The borrower cannot retain the thing by compensation for what the lender owes him.

###### Article 2097

If several have jointly borrowed the same thing, they are jointly and severally liable to the lender.

###### Section III: Obligations of the one who lends for use

###### Article 2098

The lender may only take back the loaned thing after the agreed term, or, in the absence of such provision, only after it has served the use for which it was borrowed.

He is required to reimburse the sums engaged by the borrower under the conditions of Article 2094, second paragraph.

###### Article 2099

Nevertheless, if, during the agreed period or before the borrower's need has ceased, the lender experiences a pressing and unforeseen need for his thing, the judge may, depending on the circumstances, compel the borrower to return it to him without waiting.

###### Article 2100

When the loaned thing has defects such that it risks causing harm to the one who uses it, the lender is liable as soon as he knew of the defects and did not warn the borrower.

##### Chapitre II: Loan for consumption

###### Section I: Nature of the loan for consumption

###### Article 2101

The loan for consumption is a contract by which one of the parties delivers to the other a certain quantity of things that are consumed by use, on the condition that the latter returns as much of the same kind and quality.

###### Article 2102

By the effect of this loan, the borrower becomes the owner of the loaned thing.

If it perishes, it is he who, regardless of the cause of this fact, suffers the loss, except for his recourse against the one by whose fault it occurred

###### Article 2103

One cannot give as a loan for consumption things that, although of the same species, differ in the individual, such as animals: then it is a loan for use.

###### Article 2104

The obligation resulting from a loan of money is always only of the sum stated in the contract.

If there has been an increase or decrease in currency before the time of payment, the debtor must return the loaned sum, and must only return that sum in the currency having legal tender at the time of payment. This rule does not apply if the loan was made in bullion or commodities, in which cases the debtor must always return the same quantity and quality, and must only return that regardless of the variation in value that may have affected the property.

###### Section II: Obligations of the lender

###### Article 2105

In the loan for consumption, the lender is subject to the liability established by Article 2100 for the loan for use.

###### Article 2106

The lender cannot reclaim the loaned things before the agreed term.

###### Article 2107

If no term has been set for restitution, the judge may grant the borrower a period depending on the circumstances.

###### Article 2108

If it has only been agreed that the borrower would pay when he could, or when he has the means, the judge shall set a term of payment for him depending on the circumstances.

###### Section III: Obligations of the borrower

###### Article 2109

The borrower is required to return the loaned things, in the same quantity and quality, and at the agreed term. If he is unable to satisfy this on that date, he must pay the value:

- on the day and at the place of repayment when the contract has provided for the time and place of restitution;
- on the day and at the place where the loan was made.

###### Article 2110

If the borrower does not return the loaned things or their value at the agreed term and failing that, from the formal notice addressed to him, he owes interest from the day of the summons or judicial claim.

##### Chapitre III: Interest-bearing loan

###### Article 2111

The stipulation of interest is authorized both for the loan of money, commodities, and other movable things.

###### Article 2112

If the borrower has paid interest when it was not stipulated, he cannot obtain reimbursement. Nor can he credit it against the principal.

###### Article 2113

Interest is legal or conventional. Legal interest is set by law. Conventional interest may exceed that of the law, whenever the law does not prohibit it.

The rate of conventional interest must be set in writing. Failing that, the loan is granted on a gratuitous basis and interest at the legal rate only runs from the formal notice to return the principal.

###### Article 2114

The receipt for the principal given without reservation of interest presumes payment thereof and effects discharge.

###### Article 2115

One may also provide that, in consideration for making capital available, which the lender undertakes not to demand, the borrower undertakes to pay him a periodic annuity.

In this case, the loan takes the name of constitution of annuity.

It may also be constituted, on a purely gratuitous basis, by gift inter vivos or by will. It must then be clothed in the forms required by law.

###### Article 2116

This annuity may be constituted in two ways, in perpetuity or for life.

###### Article 2117

The annuity constituted in perpetuity is redeemable. This possibility of redemption is imprescriptible and implicit in these kinds of contracts.

The parties may only agree that redemption will not be made before a certain period. This period takes the form:

- either of a waiting period, which will be set by the parties for a maximum duration of ten years, from the loan;
- or of a notice period, which the debtor must give to the creditor when he notifies him of his intention to redeem.

###### Article 2118

The debtor of a perpetual annuity may be compelled to redeem: 1° If he ceases to fulfill his obligations for two years;

2° If he fails to provide the lender with the securities promised by the contract.

###### Article 2119

The capital of the perpetual annuity also becomes due in the event of bankruptcy of the debtor.

###### Article 2120

The rules concerning life annuities are established in the title On Aleatory Contracts.

#### Title XIII: On Deposit

Chapter I: On the Two Types of Deposits

###### Article 2121

Deposit is an act by which a person receives the property of another, subject to keeping it and returning it in kind.

###### Article 2122

There are two types of deposit: deposit properly so called and sequestration.

##### Chapter II: On Deposit Properly So Called

###### Section I: On the Nature and Essence of the Contract of Deposit

###### Article 2123

Deposit properly so called is an essentially gratuitous contract.

###### Article 2124

It can have as its object only movable property.

###### Article 2125

It is perfected only by the actual or constructive delivery of the deposited property.

Constructive delivery suffices when the depositary is already in possession, under some other title, of the property which one agrees to leave with him as a deposit.

###### Article 2126

Deposit is voluntary or necessary.

###### Section II: On Voluntary Deposit

###### Article 2127

Voluntary deposit is formed by the reciprocal consent of the person who makes the deposit and the person who receives it.

Voluntary deposit presupposes persons capable of contracting. Nevertheless, if a person capable of contracting accepts a deposit made by an incapable person, he is bound by all the obligations of a true depositary; he may be sued by the tutor or administrator of the person who made the deposit.

Conversely, if the deposit was made by a capable person to an incapable person, the person who made the deposit has only the action for revendication of the deposited property, as long as it exists in the hands of the depositary, or the action for restitution up to the amount that has turned to the profit of the latter.

###### Article 2128

Voluntary deposit can only be validly made by the owner of the deposited property, or with his express or tacit consent.

###### Article 2129

Voluntary deposit must be proved in writing. Proof by witness is not admissible when the value of the deposited property exceeds 20,000 FD.

###### Article 2130

When the deposit, being above the amount provided for in the preceding article, is not proved in writing, the person who is sued as depositary is believed on his declaration, whether as to the fact of the deposit itself, or as to the property which was its object, or as to the fact of its restitution.

###### Section III: On the Obligations of the Depositary

###### Article 2131

The depositary must exercise, in the safekeeping of the deposited property, the same care that he exercises in the safekeeping of property that belongs to him.

This obligation must be applied with greater rigor:

1° If the depositary offered himself to receive the deposit;

2° If he stipulated a salary for the safekeeping of the deposit;

3° If the deposit was made solely for the benefit of the depositary;

4° If it was expressly agreed that the depositary would be liable for any kind of fault.

###### Article 2132

The depositary is not liable, in any case, for accidents of force majeure, unless he has been placed in default to return the deposited property.

###### Article 2133

He may not use the deposited property without the express or presumed permission of the depositor.

###### Article 2134

He must not seek to know what the property deposited with him is if it was entrusted to him in a closed container or under a sealed envelope.

###### Article 2135

When the deposited property is a specific thing, the depositary must return the very thing he received. In the contrary case, he must return a thing of the same kind, and identical in quantity and quality.

###### Article 2136

The depositary returns the deposited property in the state in which it is at the time of restitution. Deteriorations that did not occur through his act are at the expense of the depositor.

###### Article 2137

If the deposited property happens to disappear as a result of a case of force majeure, the depositary who has received a price or something in its place must return what he received in exchange.

###### Article 2138

The heir of the depositary, who has sold in good faith the property of which he was unaware of the deposit, is only bound to return the price he received, or to assign his action against the purchaser, if he has not received the price.

###### Article 2139

If the deposited property has produced fruits which have been collected by the depositary, he is obliged to return them. He owes no interest on money deposited, except from the day on which he was placed in default to make restitution.

###### Article 2140

The depositary must return the deposited property only to the person who entrusted it to him, or to the person in whose name the deposit was made, or to the person who was designated to receive it.

###### Article 2141

He may not require from the person who made the deposit proof that he was the owner of the deposited property. Nevertheless, if he discovers that the property was stolen, and who its true owner is, he must notify the latter of the deposit that was made with him with a demand to claim it within a fixed and sufficient period. If the person to whom the notification was made neglects to claim the deposit, the depositary is validly discharged by returning it to the person from whom he received it.

###### Article 2142

In case of death of the person who made the deposit, the deposited property can be returned only to his heir. If there are several heirs, it must be returned to each of them for their share and portion. If the deposited property is indivisible, the heirs must agree among themselves to receive it.

###### Article 2143

If the person who made the deposit has been divested of his powers of administration, for example when an adult depositor is struck with incapacity, the deposit can be returned only to the person who has the administration of the depositor's property.

###### Article 2144

If the deposit was made by a tutor or an administrator, in one of those capacities, it can be returned only to the person whom that tutor or administrator represented, if their management or administration has ended.

###### Article 2145

If the contract of deposit designates the place in which restitution must be made, the depositary is bound to bring the deposited property there. If there are transportation costs, they are at the expense of the depositor.

If the contract does not designate the place of restitution, it must be made in the very place of the deposit.

###### Article 2146

The deposit must be returned to the depositor as soon as he claims it, even if the contract had fixed a specified period for restitution; unless there exists, in the hands of the depositary, a seizure or an opposition to the restitution and removal of the deposited property.

###### Article 2147

The depositary who misappropriates the property entrusted to him or who, through his fault, cannot return the deposited property must pay its value, at the choice of the depositor, either on the day of the deposit or on the day the judge rules, without prejudice to damages that may be awarded.

###### Article 2148

All obligations of the depositary cease if he comes to discover and prove that he is himself the owner of the deposited property.

###### Section IV: On the Obligations of the Depositor

###### Article 2149

The depositor must reimburse the depositary for the expenses he incurred for the preservation of the deposited property, and indemnify him for all losses that the deposit may have caused him.

###### Article 2150

The depositary may retain the deposited thing until full payment of what is owed to him by reason of the deposit.

###### Section V: Of necessary deposit

###### Article 2151

Necessary deposit arises from the constraint suffered by a person, by reason of an unforeseen event, for example, a fire, a ruin, a pillage, or a shipwreck, to deposit his effects in the hands of a third party to ensure their safekeeping.

Except for special provisions, necessary deposit is governed by all the rules previously stated.

###### Article 2152

Proof by witnesses may be received for necessary deposit, even when it concerns a value exceeding the amount provided for in Article 2129.

###### Article 2153

Hotel deposit is assimilated to necessary deposit: innkeepers or hoteliers are responsible, as depositaries, for the clothing, luggage and various objects brought into their establishment by the traveler who lodges with them.

They are responsible for the theft or damage of the traveler's effects, whether the theft was committed or the damage was caused by their employees, or by third parties coming and going in the hotel or any establishment assimilated to a hotel.

When an object, whatever its nature or value, has been deposited in their hands or when they have refused to receive it without legitimate reason, their liability in case of theft or deterioration is complete, notwithstanding any clause to the contrary. In all other cases, the damages owed to the traveler are, to the exclusion of any lower contractual limitation, limited to the equivalent of twenty times the rental price of the lodging per day, unless the traveler demonstrates that the damage he suffered results from a fault of the person providing him accommodation or persons for whom the latter must answer.

They are not, however, responsible for thefts committed with armed force or other cases of force majeure.

##### Chapter III: Of sequestration

###### Article 2154

Sequestration is conventional or judicial.

###### Section I: Of conventional sequestration

###### Article 2155

Conventional sequestration is the deposit made by one or more persons, of a contentious thing, in the hands of a third party who undertakes to return it, after the dispute is concluded, to the person who shall be judged to be entitled to obtain it.

###### Article 2156

Sequestration need not be gratuitous.

When it is gratuitous, it is subject to the rules of deposit properly so called, provided that: 1° Sequestration may have as its object not only movable effects, but also immovables. 2° The depositary charged with the sequestration may not be discharged before the dispute is concluded, except with the consent of all interested parties, or for a cause judged legitimate such as a long absence or a failing state of health, and obtain, if applicable, the designation of a replacement.

###### Section II: Of sequestration or "judicial deposit"

###### Article 2157

The court may order sequestration:

1° Of movables seized from a debtor;

2° Of an immovable or a movable thing whose ownership or possession is disputed between two or more persons;

3° Of things, according to what he owes, that a debtor offers for his release.

###### Article 2158

The establishment of a judicial keeper produces, between the seizing party and the keeper, reciprocal obligations:

1° The keeper must:

- exercise, for the preservation of the seized effects, the care of a good father of a family;
- produce said effects, either to discharge the seizing party for the sale, or to the party against whom the executions have been made, in case of release from the seizure.

2° The seizing party must pay the keeper the salary determined by the judge.

###### Article 2159

Judicial sequestration is given, either to a person agreed upon among the interested parties, or to a person appointed ex officio by the judge.

In both cases, the person to whom the thing has been entrusted is subject to all the obligations that conventional sequestration entails.

#### Title XIV: Of aleatory contracts

Chapter I: Of gaming and wagering

###### Article 2160

The law grants no action for a gaming debt or for the payment of a wager.

###### Article 2161

However, the loser may never recover what he has voluntarily paid, unless there has been, on the part of the winner, fraud, trickery or swindling.

##### Chapter II: Of the life annuity contract

###### Section I: Of the conditions required for the validity of the contract

###### Article 2162

An annuity is a claim the object of which is a periodic income obtained by a person, called the annuitant, from another person, the debtor of the annuity; when it is for life, the annuity is paid throughout the lifetime of its beneficiary.

###### Article 2163

The annuity may be constituted for valuable consideration, in return for a sum of money, or for an appreciable movable thing, or for an immovable.

###### Article 2164

It may also be constituted, as a purely gratuitous title, by gift inter vivos or by will. It must then be vested with the forms required by law. Such is especially the case for annuities constituted by way of gift-partition.

When it is constituted as a purely gratuitous title, the annuity is reducible if it exceeds what one is permitted to dispose of; it is null if it is for the benefit of a person incapable of receiving.

###### Article 2165

The annuity may be constituted either on the head of the person who provides the price, or on the head of a third party, although the price of the annuity is provided in that case by another person.

It may also be constituted on one or several heads.

###### Article 2166

When an annuity is constituted on the head of a third party, although it has the characteristics of a liberality, it is not subject to the forms required for gifts; except to be reduced if it exceeds what one is permitted to dispose of or to be annulled if it is made for the benefit of a person incapable of receiving. In life annuity constitution contracts, the clause by which the purchaser stipulates that after his death, the annuity shall be continued to a third party during the latter's lifetime, is valid, although that third party has not been a party to the contract.

When, constituted by spouses or one of them, the annuity is stipulated reversible for the benefit of the surviving spouse, the reversibility clause may have the characteristics of a liberality or those of an act for valuable consideration. In the latter case, the compensation or indemnity owed by the beneficiary of the reversion to the community or to the succession of the predeceased is equal to the value of the reversion of the annuity. Except for the contrary will of the spouses, the reversion is presumed to have been granted as a gratuitous title.

###### Article 2167

Any life annuity contract, created on the head of a person who was dead on the day of the contract, produces no effect.

The same applies to the contract by which the annuity was created on the head of a person suffering from the illness from which he died within twenty days of the date of the contract.

###### Article 2168

A life annuity may be constituted at such rate as the contracting parties see fit to fix.

###### Section II: Of the effects of the contract between the contracting parties

###### Article 2169

He for whose benefit the life annuity has been constituted in return for a price may demand the termination of the contract, if the debtor of the annuity does not give him the securities that may have been stipulated for its performance.

###### Article 2170

The mere failure to pay the arrears of the annuity does not authorize the person in whose favor it is constituted to demand reimbursement of the capital, or to recover the property alienated by him: he has only the right to seize and have sold the property of his debtor and to have ordered or agreed, from the proceeds of the sale, the use of a sufficient sum for the service of the arrears.

###### Article 2171

The debtor of an annuity cannot free himself from payment of the annuity by offering to reimburse the capital and renouncing recovery of arrears paid: he is bound to pay the annuity during the entire life of the person or persons on whose life the annuity was established, whatever the duration of the life of such persons, and however burdensome the payment of the annuity may have become.

###### Article 2172

A life annuity is acquired by the owner only in proportion to the number of days he has lived. Nevertheless, if it has been agreed that it would be paid in advance, the installment that was due to be paid is acquired from the day on which payment was due to be made.

###### Article 2173

A life annuity may only be stipulated as unseizable when it has been established gratuitously.

###### Article 2174

The holder of a life annuity may only claim arrears by providing proof of his existence, or that of the person on whose life it was established.

#### Titre XV: Of mandate

Chapitre Ier: Of the nature and form of mandate

###### Article 2175

A mandate, or power of attorney, is an act by which a person called the principal gives to another, the agent, the power to do something for the principal and in his name.

The contract is only formed by the acceptance of the agent.

###### Article 2176

The mandate may be given by authentic act or by private written instrument, even by letter. It may also be given verbally; but testimonial evidence thereof is only admissible in accordance with the title Of obligations.

The acceptance of the mandate may be only tacit, and result from the execution given to it by the agent.

###### Article 2177

The mandate is gratuitous, unless otherwise agreed.

###### Article 2178

It is special when it is given for one matter or certain matters only; it is general when it is given for all the matters of the principal.

When it is general, the mandate only permits acts of administration.

If it concerns alienating or mortgaging, or any other act of ownership, the mandate must be express.

###### Article 2179

The agent may not do anything beyond what is stated in his mandate.

The power to settle does not include the power to submit to arbitration.

###### Article 2180

In case of absence, excess or misuse of power by the agent, the rules of article 1274 are applicable.

###### Article 2181

An unemancipated minor may be chosen as agent; but the principal shall only have an action against him according to the general rules relating to the obligations of minors.

##### Chapitre II: Of the obligations of the agent

###### Article 2182

The agent is bound to perform the mandate as long as he remains charged with it, and is liable for damages that could result from its non-performance.

He is likewise bound to complete the matter commenced at the death of the principal, if there is peril in delay.

###### Article 2183

The agent is liable not only for fraud, but also for faults he commits in his management. Nevertheless, liability relating to faults is applied less rigorously to one whose mandate is gratuitous than to one who receives remuneration.

###### Article 2184

Every agent is bound to render account of his management, and to account to the principal for everything he has received by virtue of his power of attorney, even in the case where what he has received is not due to the principal.

###### Article 2185

The agent is liable for the person he has substituted in the management:

1° when he has not received the power to substitute someone;

2° when this power has been conferred on him without designation of a person, but the person he has chosen was notoriously incapable or insolvent.

In all cases, the principal may act directly against the person whom the agent has substituted.

###### Article 2186

When there are several attorneys-in-fact or agents established by the same act, there is only solidarity between them insofar as it is expressed.

###### Article 2187

The agent owes interest on sums that he has used for his own use from the date of such use; and on those for which he is a debtor by reason of his mission, from the day he is put in default.

###### Article 2188

The agent who has given to the party with whom he contracts in that capacity sufficient knowledge of his powers is not bound by any warranty for what has been done beyond them, if he has not personally submitted thereto.

##### Chapitre III: Of the obligations of the principal

###### Article 2189

The principal is bound to perform the commitments contracted by the agent, in accordance with the power that has been given to him.

He is only bound by what may have been done beyond, insofar as he has ratified it expressly or tacitly.

###### Article 2190

The principal must reimburse to the agent the advances and expenses that the latter has made for the execution of the mandate, and pay him his remuneration when it has been promised.

If there is no fault attributable to the agent, the principal may not dispense with making these reimbursements and payment, even in the case where the matter he hoped to conclude has not succeeded, nor have the amount of expenses and advances reduced on the pretext that they could have been less.

###### Article 2191

Unless otherwise agreed, the principal must also indemnify the agent for losses that the latter has suffered on the occasion of his management, without imprudence attributable to him.

###### Article 2192

Advances made by the agent bear interest against the principal, from the date of the advances established.

These interests are due by the principal from the day the advances were made, and not from the day they were established by judicial decision or from the day of the demand for payment.

###### Article 2193

When the agent has been appointed by several persons for a common matter, each of them is held solidarily towards him for all the effects of the mandate.

##### Chapitre IV: Of the different ways in which the mandate ends

###### Article 2194

The mandate ends notably:

1° By the revocation of the agent;

2° By the renunciation by the latter of the mandate;

3° By the death, guardianship of adults or bankruptcy, either of the principal or of the agent.

###### Article 2195

The principal may revoke his power of attorney when he sees fit and compel, if need be, the agent to return to him the instrument containing the power of attorney. This restitution must occur without delay, as soon as the agent is required to do so by the principal.

The appointment of a new agent for the same matter constitutes revocation of the first, from the day it has been notified to the latter.

In all cases, from the revocation, the rendering of accounts becomes immediately due.

###### Article 2196

Revocation notified to the agent alone is presumed unknown to third parties who have dealt in ignorance of this revocation, except for the principal to prove that, taking into account the circumstances, the third party should have had knowledge thereof.

###### Article 2197

The agent may renounce the mandate, by notifying the principal of his renunciation.

Nevertheless, if this renunciation prejudices the principal, he must be indemnified by the agent, unless the latter finds himself in the impossibility of continuing the mandate without himself suffering considerable prejudice.

###### Article 2198

If the agent is unaware of the death of the principal or one of the other causes that terminate the mandate, what he has done in this ignorance is valid.

###### Article 2199

In the above cases, the commitments of the agent are performed with regard to third parties who are in good faith.

###### Article 2200

In case of death of the agent, his heirs must give notice thereof to the principal, and provide, in the meantime, for what the circumstances require for the interest of the latter.

#### Titre XVI: Of certain assigned estates

Chapitre Ier: Of the foundation

###### Article 2201

A foundation results from an act by which a person allocates, in an irrevocable manner, all or part of their property to a purpose of social utility having a lasting character.

The foundation may not have as its essential object the realization of a profit or the operation of a business.

###### Article 2202

The property of the foundation constitutes either an autonomous patrimony distinct from that of the settlor and any other person, or the patrimony of a legal person.

In the first case, the foundation is governed by the provisions of this title relating to the social utility trust, subject to the provisions of the law; in the second case, it is governed by the laws applicable to legal persons of its kind.

###### Article 2203

The foundation created by trust is established by donation or by will, according to the rules governing these acts.

###### Article 2204

Unless otherwise stipulated in the constitutive act of the foundation, the property that forms the initial patrimony of the foundation created by trust, or the property that is subrogated or added to it, must be preserved and allow the pursued purpose to be achieved either by the distribution of the revenues alone that derive from it, or by a use that does not significantly modify the composition of the patrimony.

##### Chapitre II : Trusts

###### Section I : The Nature of the Trust and its Constitution

###### § 1. The Nature of the Trust

###### Article 2205

A trust results from an act by which one or more persons, called the settlor, transfer from their patrimony property, rights or security interests, or a set of property, rights or security interests, present or future, to one or more other patrimonies that they constitute for a determined purpose for the benefit of one or more beneficiaries, and that a trustee undertakes, by the fact of their acceptance, to hold and administer.

###### Article 2206

The trust patrimony, formed of the property referred to in the preceding article and transferred in trust, constitutes an autonomous patrimony dedicated to a purpose and distinct from that of the settlor, the trustee or the beneficiary, over which none of them has a real right. In particular, the opening of judicial reorganization or liquidation proceedings, personal bankruptcy and fraudulent bankruptcy, or equivalent proceedings abroad concerning the trustee does not affect the trust patrimony.

Without prejudice to the rights of the settlor's creditors holding a right of pursuit attached to a security interest published prior to the trust contract and except in cases of fraud against the rights of the settlor's creditors, the trust patrimony may only be seized by holders of claims arising from the preservation or management of that patrimony.

In case of insufficiency of the trust patrimony, the obligation for trust liabilities is limited to the trust patrimony alone.

###### Article 2207

A trust is established by contract, for consideration or gratuitously, by will or by law. It may also, when the law so authorizes, be established by judgment.

###### Article 2208

A trust is constituted upon acceptance by the trustee or, if there are several, by one of them. The settlor may revoke the trust contract as long as it has not been accepted by the beneficiary; after acceptance by the beneficiary, the contract may only be modified or revoked with their consent or by judicial decision.

When the trust is established by will, the effects of acceptance retroact to the day of death.

###### Article 2209

Acceptance of the trust divests the settlor of the property, charges the trustee with ensuring their allocation and the administration of the trust patrimony, and makes certain the beneficiary's right.

###### § 2. The Trust Contract

###### Article 2210

The trust contract determines, on pain of nullity:

1° The property, rights or security interests transferred. If they are future, they must be determinable; 2° The duration of the transfer, which may not exceed ninety-nine years from the signing of the contract;

3° The identity of the settlor or settlors;

4° The identity of the trustee or trustees;

5° The identity of the beneficiary or beneficiaries or, failing that, the principles or rules allowing their designation; 6° The mission of the trustee or trustees and the extent of their powers of administration and disposition. The trust contract also defines the conditions under which the trustee accounts for their mission to the settlor. However, when during the execution of the contract the settlor is subject to a guardianship measure, the trustee, as soon as they are informed, accounts for their mission to the guardian at the latter's request at least once a year, without prejudice to the periodicity set by the contract. When during the execution of the contract the settlor is subject to a curatorship measure, the trustee accounts for their mission, under the same conditions, to the settlor and their curator.

###### Article 2211

When the trust contract provides that the settlor retains the use or enjoyment of a business or commercial real property transferred into the trust patrimony, the agreement concluded for this purpose is not subject to chapters 2 and 4 of title I of book II of the commercial code, unless otherwise stipulated.

###### Article 2212

The assignment of claims made within the framework of a trust is enforceable against third parties on the date of the trust contract or the amendment that records it. It only becomes enforceable against the debtor of the assigned claim by notification made to them by the assignor or the trustee.

###### Article 2213

On pain of nullity, the trust contract and its amendments are registered in a public register, within one month from their date, with the register of immovable security interests.

When they relate to immovables or real rights in immovables, they are additionally published in the Land Register. The trustee is, in case of default by the settlor, subject to the rules relating to the exercise of mortgage rights as set forth by this code.

The transmission of rights resulting from the trust contract and, if the beneficiary is not designated in the trust contract, their subsequent designation must, on pain of nullity, give rise to a written act registered under the same conditions.

###### Article 2214

A national register of trusts is established and maintained by the Central Bank of Djibouti.

###### Section II : The Various Types of Trusts

###### Article 2215

Trusts are constituted for personal purposes, or for purposes of private or social utility. They may, to the extent that a notation indicates that it is a trust, be identified under the name of the settlor, the trustee or the beneficiary or, if they are constituted for purposes of private or social utility, under a name that designates their object.

###### Article 2216

A personal trust is constituted gratuitously, with the aim of providing a benefit to a determined person or one who may be so determined.

###### Article 2217

A trust for private utility is one that has as its object the construction, maintenance or conservation of tangible property, or the use of property allocated to a determined use, either for the indirect benefit of a person or in their memory, or for another purpose of a private nature.

###### Article 2218

Also for private utility is a trust constituted for consideration with the aim, in particular, of allowing the realization of a profit by means of placements or investments, of providing for retirement or of providing another benefit to the settlor or to persons they designate, to members of a company or association, to employees or to security holders.

###### Article 2219

A trust established by contract for consideration may also have as its object the guarantee of the performance of an obligation.

###### Article 2220

The social purpose trust is one that is established for a purpose of general interest, particularly of a cultural, educational, philanthropic, religious or scientific nature.

Its essential purpose is not to make a profit or to operate a business.

###### Article 2221

A personal trust established for the benefit of several persons successively may not include more than two orders of beneficiaries of fruits and income, in addition to that of the beneficiary of the capital.

Accruals, among the co-beneficiaries of the fruits and income of the same order.

###### Article 2222

The right of the first order beneficiary opens at the latest upon expiration of the ninety-nine years following the establishment of the trust, even if a longer term has been stipulated. That of the beneficiaries of subsequent orders may open subsequently, but for the benefit of only those beneficiaries who have the required capacity to receive upon expiration of the ninety-nine years following the establishment of the trust.

Legal persons may never be beneficiaries for a period exceeding ninety-nine years, even if a longer term has been stipulated.

###### Article 2223

A private or social purpose trust may be perpetual.

###### Section III: Administration of the trust

###### § 1. Designation and office of the trustee

###### Article 2224

Only banking or financial institutions, investment firms, and insurance companies may have the capacity of trustees. Members of the legal profession may also have the capacity of trustee.

The settlor or the beneficiary may be a trustee, but must act jointly with a trustee who is neither settlor nor beneficiary.

###### Article 2225

The settlor may appoint one or more trustees or provide for the manner of their appointment or replacement.

In the absence of contractual stipulations providing for the conditions of replacement or if it is impossible to provide for the replacement of a trustee, the court may, at the request of an interested party and after notice given to the persons it indicates, proceed with the replacement. It may also, when the conditions of the administration require it, appoint one or more other trustees.

When the trustee fails in his duties or endangers the interests entrusted to him, or if he is subject to safeguard or judicial reorganization proceedings, the settlor, the beneficiary or the third party designated pursuant to Article 2234 may apply to the court for the appointment of an interim trustee or request the replacement of the trustee. The judicial decision granting the application shall automatically divest the original trustee and vest his replacement.

###### Article 2226

The trustee has the complete and exclusive control and administration of the trust estate and the documents relating to the property composing it are drawn up in his name; he exercises all rights relating to the estate and may take any measure appropriate to ensure its allocation.

When the trustee acts on behalf of the trust, he must expressly mention it. In his relations with third parties, the trustee is deemed to have the most extensive powers over the trust estate, unless it is shown that the third parties were aware of any limitations affecting his powers.

###### § 2. The beneficiary and his rights

###### Article 2227

The settlor or the trustee may be the beneficiary or one of the beneficiaries of the trust contract.

###### Article 2228

The beneficiary of a trust established gratuitously must have the required capacity to receive by gift or by will at the opening of his right.

The beneficiary of a trust must, in order to receive, fulfill the conditions required by the constitutive instrument.

###### Article 2229

The settlor may reserve the right to receive the fruits and income or, as the case may be, the capital of a trust, even if established gratuitously, or to participate in the advantages it provides.

###### Article 2230

The settlor may reserve or confer upon the trustee or a third party the power to elect the beneficiaries or to determine their share.

In the case of a social purpose trust, the trustee's power to elect the beneficiaries and determine their share is presumed. In the case of a personal or private purpose trust, the power to elect may be exercised by the trustee or the third party only if the category of persons from among whom they must choose the beneficiary is clearly determined in the constitutive instrument.

The person who has the power to elect the beneficiaries or to determine their share exercises it as he sees fit; he may modify or revoke his decision for the needs of the trust. The person who exercises the power may not do so for his own benefit.

###### Article 2231

During the term of the trust, the beneficiary has the right to require:

1° According to the periodicity set by the contract, the report by the trustee on his mission. The third party designated pursuant to Article 2234 has the same power.

2° According to the constitutive instrument, either the provision of a benefit granted to him, or the payment of the fruits and income and the capital or only one of them.

###### Article 2232

The beneficiary of a trust established gratuitously is presumed to have accepted the right granted to him and may dispose of it.

He may also renounce it at any time. The renunciation must be made by notarial deed if he is a beneficiary of a personal or private purpose trust.

###### Article 2233

In the case of a plurality of beneficiaries, when one of them renounces his right or the latter becomes without effect, that right passes, in proportion to the shares of each, to the co-beneficiaries of the fruits and income or of the capital, depending on whether he himself is a beneficiary of the fruits and income or of the capital.

If he is the sole beneficiary of the fruits and income in his order, the right of the renouncing party passes, in proportion to the shares of each, to the beneficiaries of the fruits and income of the second order or, failing that, to the beneficiaries of the capital.

###### § 3. Measures of supervision and control

###### Article 2234

Unless otherwise stipulated in the trust contract, the settlor may, at any time, designate a third party responsible for ensuring the preservation of his interests in the context of the performance of the contract and who may have the powers that the law grants to the settlor.

When the settlor is a natural person, he may not renounce this power.

###### Article 2235

The administration of the trust is subject to the supervision of the settlor or his heirs, if deceased, and of the beneficiary, even if contingent. It is also subject to that of the third party designated by the settlor according to Article 2234.

Furthermore, in the cases provided for by law, the administration of private or social purpose trusts is subject, according to their object and purpose, to the supervision of the persons and bodies designated by law.

###### Article 2236

Upon establishment of a private or social purpose trust subject to the supervision of a person or body designated by law, the trustee must file with that person or body a declaration indicating, in particular, the nature and object of the trust, its duration, and the name and address of the trustee.

He must, at the request of the person or body, allow the examination of the trust files and provide any account, report or information requested of him.

###### Article 2237

The rights of the beneficiary of a personal trust are exercised, if he is not yet conceived, by the person who, having been designated by the settlor to act as curator, accepts this office or, failing that, by the person appointed by the court at the request of the trustee or any interested person.

In the case of a trust for private purposes of which no person, even determinable or contingent, can be a beneficiary, the rights that this paragraph grants to the beneficiary may be exercised by the public prosecutor.

###### Article 2238

The settlor, the beneficiary or another interested person may, notwithstanding any provision to the contrary, take action against the trustee to compel him to perform his obligations or to do an act necessary for the trust, to enjoin him from any act harmful to the trust or to obtain his removal. He may also attack acts done by the trustee in fraud of the trust patrimony or the rights of the beneficiary.

###### Article 2239

The court may authorize the settlor, the beneficiary or another interested person to take legal action in place of the trustee, when the latter, without sufficient cause, refuses to act, neglects to do so or is prevented from doing so.

###### Article 2240

The trustee, the settlor and the beneficiary are, if they participate therein, solidarily liable for acts performed in fraud of the rights of the creditors of the settlor or of the trust patrimony.

###### Section IV: Of the modification and termination of the trust

###### § 1. Of the modification of the trust

###### Article 2241

Any person may increase the trust patrimony by transferring property to it by contract or by will and by following, for such increases, the rules specific to the constitution of a trust. He does not thereby acquire the rights of a settlor.

The transferred property is merged into the trust patrimony and is administered in accordance with the provisions of the constitutive act and those of this chapter.

###### Article 2242

When a trust has ceased to respond to the original will of the settlor, in particular when the court finds the occurrence of unforeseeable circumstances which make the pursuit of the purpose of the trust too onerous or the impossibility of achieving that purpose, that court may, at the request of an interested person, terminate the trust.

If the trust still responds to the will of the settlor, but new measures would better respect his will or would favor the accomplishment of the trust, the court may modify the provisions of the constitutive act.

In all situations referred to in the preceding paragraphs, notice of the application must be given to the settlor and to the trustee and, where applicable, to the beneficiary, to the liquidator of the settlor's succession or to the heirs, and to any other person or body designated by law whenever the trust is subject to their supervision. These persons must be heard by the court if they so request.

###### § 2. Of the termination of the trust

###### Article 2243

The trust terminates by:

1° the lapse of the right of all beneficiaries, both of capital and of fruits and revenues;

2° the renunciation of the trust by all the beneficiaries, except for stipulations of the contract providing the conditions under which it continues;

3° the arrival of the term or the occurrence of the condition if one is provided;

4° the fact that the purpose of the trust has been achieved or by the impossibility established by the court of achieving it.

###### Article 2244

The trustee must, at the end of the trust, deliver the property to those who are entitled to it.

In the absence of a beneficiary, the property remaining at the end of the trust devolves by operation of law to the settlor or to his heirs.

###### Article 2245

The property of the trust for social purposes which terminates due to the impossibility of accomplishing it returns to the settlor. If he is deceased, such property devolves to a trust, to a legal person or to any other group of persons having a purpose as close as possible to that of the trust. The designation is made by the court, upon the recommendation of the trustee. The court also takes the advice of the person or body designated by law, if the trust was subject to their supervision.

#### Title XVII: Of transactions

###### Article 2246

A transaction is a contract by which the parties, by mutual concessions, settle a dispute that has arisen, or prevent a dispute from arising.

This contract must be in writing.

###### Article 2247

To enter into a transaction, one must have the capacity to dispose of the objects included in the transaction. The tutor may only enter into a transaction for the minor or the major under tutorship in accordance with Article 604 of the Title Of Minority, Tutorship and Emancipation; and he may only enter into a transaction with the minor who has become of age, on the tutorship account, in accordance with Article 609 of the same title.

Municipalities and public institutions may only enter into transactions with the express authorization of the President of the Republic.

###### Article 2248

One may enter into a transaction on the civil interest resulting from an offence. The transaction does not prevent prosecution by the public prosecutor.

###### Article 2249

A stipulation of a penalty clause may be added to a transaction against the person who fails to perform it.

###### Article 2250

Transactions are limited to their object: the renunciation made therein of all rights, actions and claims is understood only as relating to the dispute which gave rise to it.

###### Article 2251

Transactions settle only the disputes included therein, whether the parties have manifested their intention by special or general expressions, or whether that intention is recognized by a necessary consequence of what is expressed.

###### Article 2252

If a person who had entered into a transaction on a right he had in his own capacity, and has thus abandoned it in part, subsequently acquires a similar right by virtue of another person, he is not, as to the newly acquired right, bound by the previous transaction.

###### Article 2253

A transaction entered into by one of the interested parties does not bind the other interested parties and cannot be invoked by them.

###### Article 2254

A transaction prevents the institution or continuation between the parties of a legal action having the same object. The judge may raise on his own motion this ground of inadmissibility derived from the existence of a transaction.

A transaction may not be challenged on grounds of error of law, nor on grounds of lesion.

###### Article 2255

Nevertheless, a transaction may be annulled when there is error as to the person or as to the object of the dispute.

It may be annulled in all cases where there is fraud or duress.

###### Article 2256

An action for annulment also lies against a transaction when it was entered into in execution of a void title, except if the parties, when they have the power to do so, have expressly confirmed the cause of nullity.

###### Article 2257

A transaction entered into on documents which have since been recognized as false is entirely null.

###### Article 2258

A transaction on a lawsuit terminated by a judgment that has become res judicata, of which the parties or one of them had no knowledge, is null.

If the judgment unknown to the parties was subject to appeal, the transaction is valid.

###### Article 2259

When the parties have settled generally on all matters they could have had between them, titles that were then unknown to them, and that were subsequently discovered, are not a ground for annulment, unless they were withheld by the act of one of the parties.

But the settlement would be null if it related only to an object on which it would be established, by newly discovered titles, that one of the parties had no right.

###### Article 2260

Calculation error in a settlement must be corrected.

#### Titre XVIII: Arbitration

###### Article 2261

Arbitration is governed by the provisions of articles L.710-1 et seq. of the code of civil procedure.

#### Titre XIX: Security Interests

###### Article 2262

Whoever has bound himself personally is required to fulfill his commitment on all his movable and immovable property, present and future.

###### Article 2263

The debtor's property may be seized even when it is held by third parties.

Seizure is carried out according to the rules specific to the nature of each of them.

###### Article 2264

Property referred to in articles L.511-4 to L.511-6 of the code of civil procedure cannot be seized. Furthermore, any individual entrepreneur who is a natural person may render unseizable the rights he holds in the immovable property forming his principal residence, to shelter his family home from a failure of his business. The unsseizability is effected by a declaration before a notary which, to be enforceable against third parties, must be the subject of publication in a newspaper authorized to receive legal publications.

###### Article 2265

Seized property is unavailable.

Leases granted by the person whose property is seized are, whatever their duration, unenforceable against the pursuing creditors. The same rules apply to property seized, mortgaged or pledged on a conservatory basis.

###### Article 2266

The debtor's property is the common security of his creditors; and the proceeds are distributed among them by contribution, unless there are legitimate causes of preference among the creditors.

###### Article 2267

With respect to real security interests, the legitimate causes of preference are privileges and mortgages.

Sous-Titre I: Personal Security Interests

##### Chapitre I: Suretyship

###### Section I: Nature and Extent of Suretyship

###### Article 2268

Civil suretyship is a contract by which the surety undertakes toward the creditor to perform the debtor's obligation if the debtor does not satisfy it himself.

###### Article 2269

Suretyship can exist only on a valid obligation.

However, it is possible to provide suretyship, with full knowledge, for an obligation, even though it could be annulled by an exception purely personal to the obligor; for example, the commitments of an incapable person. The confirmation by the debtor of an obligation tainted by relative nullity does not, however, bind the surety, except express waiver by the surety of such nullity.

The lack of authority of the representative to bind the legal person as principal debtor may be invoked by its surety under the conditions provided in the preceding paragraph.

###### Article 2270

The surety's commitment cannot be contracted on more onerous conditions than the principal obligation, nor exceed what is owed by the debtor at the time of proceedings.

The principal debtor cannot aggravate the surety's commitment by an agreement subsequent to the suretyship.

Suretyship that exceeds the debt, or that is contracted under more onerous conditions, is not null; it is reduced to the extent of the principal obligation.

The surety's commitment may be contracted for only part of the debt, and on less onerous conditions.

###### Article 2271

A suretyship may be contracted without the debtor's order and even without his knowledge.

One may also become surety, not only for the principal debtor, but also for the one who has provided suretyship for him.

###### Article 2272

Suretyship is not presumed, whatever the nature of the guaranteed obligation.

It must be express, and one cannot extend it beyond the limits within which it was contracted. Suretyship must be recorded in an instrument bearing the surety's signature and the mention of the maximum amount guaranteed in both words and figures. In case of difference, the suretyship is valid for the amount expressed in words.

The surety who does not know how or cannot write affixes his fingerprint in the presence of a witness who attests in the suretyship instrument his identity, his presence and that the nature and effects of the instrument have been specified to the surety.

The provisions of this article also apply to suretyship required by law.

###### Article 2273

Suretyship of an obligation may extend, in addition to the principal and within the limit of the maximum amount guaranteed, to the accessories of the debt and to the costs of recovering the claim, including those subsequent to the notice given to the surety provided that this commitment results from a handwritten mention by the surety in accordance with the provisions of the preceding article.

The instrument constituting the principal obligation must be attached to the suretyship agreement.

###### Art.2274

General suretyship of the principal debtor's debts, in the form of suretyship for all commitments, for the debit balance of a current account, or in any other form, is understood, except express contrary clause, only as guarantee of direct contractual debts.

It must be concluded, on pain of relative nullity, for a maximum amount freely determined between the parties, including the principal and all accessories.

General suretyship may be renewed when the maximum amount is reached. The renewal must be express; any contrary clause is deemed unwritten.

It may be revoked, at any time, by the surety before the maximum guaranteed amount has been reached. All commitments of the guaranteed debtor arising before the revocation remain guaranteed by the surety. Except contrary clause, general suretyship does not guarantee the principal debtor's debts prior to the date of the suretyship.

###### Article 2275

The debts incumbent on the deceased in the capacity of surety remain, like all other debts, chargeable to his successors.

However, only debts arising before the surety's death are transmitted to his successors. There remain, however, chargeable to them the debts arising before the death or universal transmission, whatever the time of their maturity.

###### Article 2276

The debtor required to provide a surety must present one who has the capacity to contract, who has sufficient property to answer for the object of the obligation, and whose domicile is within the jurisdiction where it must be given, unless dispensed by the creditor or by the competent court. The debtor who cannot find a surety may replace it with any real security giving the same guarantees to the creditor.

###### Article 2277

The solvency of a civil surety is estimated only with regard to his landed property, except in commercial matters, or when the debt is small.

No regard is had to litigious immovable property, or whose discussion would become too difficult by the remoteness of their location.

###### Article 2278

When the surety received by the creditor, voluntarily or in court, subsequently becomes insolvent, the debtor must provide another or provide a real security giving the same guarantees to the creditor.

This rule is excepted only in the case where the surety was given by virtue of an agreement by which the creditor required a specific person as surety.

###### Section II: On the effect of suretyship

###### § 1. On the effect of suretyship between the creditor and the surety

###### Article 2279

The creditor must notify the surety of any default by the debtor, forfeiture or extension of term, indicating the amount remaining due by him in principal, interest and costs as of the date of default, forfeiture or extension of term.

In case of extension of term granted to the principal debtor, the surety is entitled to refuse the benefit of this extension and to pursue the debtor to force payment or obtain a guarantee or a conservatory measure.

In case of forfeiture of term that affects the principal debtor, it does not automatically extend to the surety who cannot be required to pay except at the maturity date fixed at the time when the surety was provided. Any contrary clause is unwritten. However, the surety incurs forfeiture of term if, after formal notice, it does not satisfy its own obligations at the fixed maturity date.

###### Article 2280
