Civil suretyship is simple, unless otherwise provided by law or conventional stipulation of solidarity. The joint and several surety is bound to perform the principal obligation under the same conditions as a joint and several debtor subject to the particular provisions of this code.

Unless otherwise provided by law or stipulation, the simple surety, unlike the judicial surety and the joint and several surety, has the benefit of discussion and division.

However, the creditor may only pursue the surety, whether simple, joint and several or judicial, by joining the principal debtor as a party.

###### Article 2281

The creditor may not bring legal action against the surety except after a formal demand for payment addressed to the debtor and which remained without effect.

The surety is only bound to pay the creditor if the principal debtor does not perform his obligation. It is bound in the same manner as the principal debtor.

###### Article 2282

Any surety may raise against the creditor all exceptions belonging to the principal debtor, which are inherent to the debt and tend to reduce, extinguish or defer the debt, subject to contrary legislative provisions. But the surety may not raise against the creditor exceptions that are purely personal to the debtor.

The simple or joint and several surety is discharged when subrogation to the rights and guarantees of the creditor can no longer operate in its favor, by act of the creditor. Any contrary clause is deemed unwritten. If the act imputed to the creditor only limits this subrogation, the surety is discharged to the extent of the insufficiency of the preserved guarantee.

###### Article 2283

The surety who, upon first proceedings brought against it, requests the benefit of discussion must indicate to the creditor the property of the principal debtor that can be immediately seized on national territory and, if the creditor so requests, advance sufficient sums to conduct the discussion.

###### Article 2284

Whenever the surety has made the indication of property authorized by the preceding article, and has provided sufficient sums for discussion, the creditor is, up to the amount of the property indicated, liable to the surety for the insolvency of the principal debtor arising from failure to pursue.

###### Article 2285

If there are several sureties for the same debtor and the same debt, unless there is a stipulation of solidarity between them or waiver by them of this benefit, each of them may, upon first proceedings by the creditor, request division of the debt among the solvent sureties on the day when the exception is invoked.

The surety is not liable for the insolvencies of other sureties that occurred after the division.

The creditor who voluntarily divides his action when he could have avoided it, cannot revoke this division and bears the insolvency of the sureties pursued without being able to transfer it to the other sureties.

###### § 2. On the effect of suretyship between the debtor and the surety

###### Article 2286

As soon as it is pursued, the surety must notify the principal debtor or join him as a party before paying the debt to the pursuing creditor.

If the surety has paid without having notified or joined the principal debtor as a party, it loses its recourse against him if, at the time of payment by it or subsequent to this payment, the debtor had the means to have the debt declared extinguished or if he had paid in ignorance of the payment by the surety. Nevertheless, the surety retains its action for restitution against the pursuing creditor.

###### Article 2287

The surety who has paid has recourse against the principal debtor, even if the suretyship was given without the debtor's knowledge.

This recourse applies both to the principal and to interest and costs; nevertheless, the surety has recourse only for costs incurred by it since it notified the principal debtor of the proceedings brought against it.

It also has recourse for damages and interest, if applicable in case of prejudice it would have suffered due to the creditor's proceedings.

###### Article 2288

The surety who has paid the debt is subrogated to all the rights and guarantees of the pursuing creditor against the debtor.

If there are several principal debtors jointly and severally liable for the same debt, the surety is subrogated against each of them for all that it has paid, even if it only guaranteed one of them. If the debtors are joint, it must divide its recourses.

###### Article 2289

The surety, even before having paid, may act against the debtor to be indemnified by him, or request preservation of its rights in the patrimony of the latter:

1° As soon as it is pursued in court for payment;

2° When the debtor has ceased payments;

3° When the debtor has not discharged it within the agreed period;

4° When the debt has become due by the expiry of the term under which it was contracted.

###### § 3. On the effect of suretyship between the various sureties

###### Article 2290

When several persons have guaranteed the same debtor for the same debt, the surety who has discharged the debt has recourse against the other sureties, each for its share and portion; But this recourse only applies when the surety has paid in one of the cases stated in the preceding article.

###### Section III: On the extinction of suretyship

###### Article 2291

The obligation resulting from suretyship is extinguished by the same causes as under the general law of contracts.

Dation in payment definitively releases the surety, even if the creditor is subsequently evicted from the thing accepted by him. Any contrary clause is deemed unwritten.

Novation of the principal obligation by change of object or cause releases the surety unless it accepts to transfer its guarantee to the new debt. Any contrary clause stipulated before the novation is deemed unwritten.

###### Article 2292

The surety's commitment is extinguished independently of the principal obligation:

- when, in proceedings brought against it, the surety raises set-off for a personal claim against the pursuing creditor;
- when the creditor has consented to a release of debt to the surety alone;
- when confusion occurs between the person of the creditor and the surety;
- when the creditor has voluntarily accepted immovable property or any effect in payment of the principal debt, even if subsequently the creditor were to be evicted from it;
- for debts arising after the death of the surety;
- in the case of Article 2282.

###### Article 2293

The simple extension of time granted by the creditor to the principal debtor, or the modification of the securities with which the principal obligation is provided into new equivalent securities, does not discharge the surety, who may, in this case, pursue the debtor to compel payment.

##### Chapitre II : De la lettre de garantie ou « garantie autonome »

###### Article 2294

A letter of guarantee or independent guarantee is the necessarily written undertaking by which the guarantor binds himself, in consideration of an obligation undertaken by a third party ordering party, to pay a sum either on first demand or according to agreed terms.

Such a contract may not be entered into, on pain of nullity, by natural persons; and may not, for legal persons, be stipulated for a purpose unrelated to the commercial or professional activity of the borrower. In this case, the letter of guarantee is governed by articles L.2281-201 and following of the Commercial Code.

##### Chapitre III : De la lettre d'intention

###### Article 2295

The letter of intent is the undertaking to do or not to do having as its object the support provided to a debtor in the performance of his obligation toward his creditor.

Sous-Titre II : Les sûretés réelles

##### Chapitre I : Dispositions générales

###### Article 2296

Any security interest in rem may be created, registered, managed and enforced for the account of the creditors of the guaranteed obligation by a person whom they designate for this purpose in the instrument recording such obligation.

###### Article 2297

A privilege is a right that the nature of the claim gives to a creditor to be preferred over other creditors, even mortgagees. It may be over movables or over immovables.

Among privileged creditors, preference is determined by the different natures of the privileges. When they are of the same rank, privileged creditors are paid proportionally.

###### Article 2298

The privilege, in respect of the rights of the Public Treasury and the order in which it is exercised, are governed by the laws concerning them.

The Public Treasury may not however obtain a privilege to the prejudice of rights previously acquired by third parties.

###### Article 2299

Privileges, like securities, may be over movables or over immovables.

##### Chapitre II : Des sûretés sur les meubles

###### Article 2300

Security interests in movables comprise: the right of retention, the pledge, privileges and ownership retained or transferred as security.

###### Section I : Du droit de rétention

###### Article 2301

The creditor who lawfully holds a property of the debtor may retain it until complete payment of what is owed to him, independently of any other security.

When the same property is the subject of several successive pledges without dispossession, the rank of creditors is determined by the order of their registration. When a property pledged without dispossession is subsequently the subject of a pledge with dispossession, the right of preference of the prior pledgee is opposable to the subsequent pledgee when it is duly published notwithstanding the right of retention of the latter.

###### Article 2302

The right of retention may only be exercised:

- before any seizure;
- if the claim is certain, liquidated and due;
- if there exists a connection between the birth of the claim and the thing retained.

###### Section II : Du nantissement

###### Article 2303

The pledge is a contract by which a debtor delivers a thing to his creditor as security for the debt.

Pledges without dispossession relating to: membership rights and securities; the business; professional equipment; stocks of raw materials and goods, are governed by the provisions of the Commercial Code.

The pledge of a movable thing is called a gage. That of an immovable thing is called an immovable gage.

###### Article 2304

Heavy equipment purchased by an individual may be the subject of a pledge for the benefit of the seller, the third party having guaranteed the purchaser's commitments to the seller, or any person having lent the sums necessary for the purchase.

Such a security is only opposable to third parties if it is registered in the Register of Movable Securities.

###### Article 2305

The gage is a contract by which a debtor delivers a thing or a set of things of a movable nature to his creditor as security for the debt.

The secured claims may be present, future or contingent; in the latter two cases, they must be determinable and not be tainted with nullity.

The gage confers upon the creditor the right to be paid from the thing that is its object, by privilege and in preference to other creditors.

###### Article 2306

The gage may be granted by the debtor or by a third party; in the latter case, the creditor has recourse only against the property assigned as security.

Except for a gage granted by a third party, the gage of another's thing is null and may give rise to damages when the creditor was unaware that the thing belonged to another. If the thing does not belong to the grantor, the pledgee in good faith may oppose the owner's claim under the conditions provided for a possessor in good faith.

###### Article 2307

Any movable property, corporeal or incorporeal, is capable of being given as a gage.

Movable securities subject to publicity are the subject of registration, at the initiative of the creditor, in the Register of Movable Securities.

###### Article 2308

The parties may agree to the substitution during the performance of the contract of the pledged thing by another thing.

The gage may also relate to sums or securities deposited as security by civil servants, ministerial officers or any other person to guarantee abuses for which they could be liable and loans granted for the constitution of such security.

###### Article 2309

The gage contract provided with dispossession produces effect only if the pledged thing is effectively delivered to the creditor or to a third party agreed upon between the parties.

The promise to pledge, particularly of future things, obliges the promisor to deliver the thing under the agreed conditions.

###### Article 2310

When it is without dispossession of the debtor, the gage is opposable to third parties by the publicity given to it. This is effected at the diligence of the creditor in the Register of Movable Securities.

###### Article 2311

The gage contract is only opposable to third parties if it is evidenced by a writing, authentic or under private signature, duly registered, and containing indication of the sum owed as well as the species, nature and quantity of the movable property given as a gage, except for derogation provided by law.

The drafting of the instrument in writing and its registration are nevertheless required only in matters exceeding the value of 100,000 FD.

The gage is also opposable to third parties by the dispossession into the hands of the creditor or of an agreed third party of the property that is its object.

If the gage is constituted over an incorporeal movable, such as a movable claim, the instrument, registered, is served on the debtor of the claim given as a gage.

###### Article 2312

The debtor who pledges their claim against a named third party must deliver to the pledgee creditor their title of claim and notify their own debtor of the transfer of their claim in this capacity; failing this, the pledgee creditor may proceed with this notification.

This pledge is realized by the demand for payment that the pledgee creditor addresses to the transferred debtor. The latter may raise against the pledgee creditor the defenses based on their personal relations with their own creditor as well as the defenses they may have against the pledgee creditor. It is otherwise if the transferred debtor has made a written commitment to pay the pledgee creditor directly, in which case they cannot raise against the pledgee creditor the defenses based on their personal relations with their own creditor.

The creditor of the transferred debtor remains liable, jointly and severally with the latter, for payment of the pledged claim.

The pledgee creditor who has obtained payment must account for it to their own debtor.

###### Article 2313

In other areas, if there are no specific legal provisions or contractual stipulations defining the methods of pledging the intangible property given as security, the delivery to the creditor of the title that establishes the existence of the right effects dispossession of the pledgor.

###### Article 2314

The deposit or consignment of sums, instruments or securities, ordered judicially as security or as a conservatory measure, entails special allocation and privilege under article 2305 paragraph 3.

###### Article 2315

The pledgee creditor retains or has retained the pledged thing by the agreed third party until full payment, in principal, interest and costs, of the debt for which the pledge was constituted.

If there arise on the part of the same debtor to the same creditor, one or more other debts contracted subsequent to the pledging, and becoming due before payment of the first debt, the creditor may retain or have retained the pledged thing until complete payment of all debts, even in the absence of any stipulation to that effect.

###### Article 2316

The privilege subsists on the pledge only insofar as the pledge has been placed and has remained in the possession of the creditor, or of a third party agreed upon between the parties.

But if they have been dispossessed against their will, the creditor may claim the pledged thing as a possessor in good faith.

###### Article 2317

Until the expropriation of the debtor, if applicable, the pledgor remains owner of the pledge, which is, in the hand of the creditor, only a deposit securing the latter's privilege.

###### Article 2318

The creditor or the agreed third party must watch over the thing and ensure its preservation, as must a remunerated depositary. They are liable for the loss or deterioration of the pledge that would have occurred through their negligence. They may not, unless otherwise stipulated, use the pledged thing or collect its fruits. If they are authorized to collect the fruits, they must apply them, unless otherwise provided, to what is owed to them in interest and principal. When the pledged thing is a claim, the provisions of article 2320 are applied. If the thing threatens to perish, the creditor or the agreed third party may, upon authorization, as the case may be, of the Civil Chamber or the Commercial Chamber of the Court of First Instance, sell it and the effects of the pledge are then transferred to the price.

The agreed third party and, if applicable, the bad faith acquirer of the pledged thing are jointly and severally liable with the pledgee creditor for the non-performance of these obligations.

The pledging of a consumable thing authorizes the creditor or the agreed third party to return an equivalent thing.

When the pledge has as its object fungible things, the creditor or the agreed third party may only alienate them if the agreement so provides, with the obligation to replace them with the same quantity of equivalent things. In the absence of a stipulation to this effect, they must keep them separate from things of the same nature that belong to them. Failing for the creditor or the agreed third party to do so, the pledgor may claim the restitution of the pledged property, without prejudice to damages, if the creditor or the agreed third party does not fulfill their obligation to preserve the pledge. When the agreement exempts the creditor from the obligation to separate the pledged property from their things of the same nature, they acquire ownership thereof with the obligation to return the same quantity of equivalent things.

###### Article 2319

For their part, when they have fully paid them the principal, interest and costs, the debtor must take into account to the creditor the useful and necessary expenses that the latter has incurred for the preservation of the pledge.

###### Article 2320

When the thing given as pledge is a claim:

- if the maturity of the claim given as pledge is prior to the maturity of the secured claim, the pledgee creditor is entitled to collect the amount in principal and interest, unless otherwise provided;
- if the maturity of the secured claim is prior to the maturity of the claim given as pledge, the pledgee creditor is required to wait for the maturity of the latter to collect the amount.

In both cases, the pledgee creditor collects the amount of the pledged claim subject to being accountable, in the capacity of mandatory, for the surplus collected in favor of the pledgor.

Moreover, unless otherwise agreed, if this claim bears interest, the creditor applies this interest to what may be owed to them in interest and principal.

If the debt for security of which the claim has been given as pledge does not itself bear interest, the application is made to the principal of the debt.

###### Article 2321

In default of payment at maturity, the pledgee creditor may, eight days after a simple notification made to the debtor and to the third party who holds the thing delivered as pledge, if there is one, have the pledged thing proceed to public sale.

The sale is made by bailiff at least eight days after publication of a notice in a newspaper authorized to receive legal notices mentioning the date, time and place of the sale, the place where the objects can be viewed, the reserve price or prices, the nature of the object and the costs. The creditor may also seize, as the case may be, the Civil Chamber or the Commercial Chamber of the Court of First Instance to request that the pledge be allocated to them or sold to a third party up to the amount of their claim and according to valuation following market rates or expert opinion.

Any clause that would authorize the creditor to appropriate the pledge or dispose of it without the above formalities is deemed unwritten.

###### Article 2322

In case of sale or loss or destruction of the pledged thing, the pledgee creditor has a privilege over the price of the thing sold or over the insurance indemnity for the amount of the secured claim in principal, interest and costs.

They exercise their right of preference in accordance with article 2331 of this code. If there are several pledgee creditors, they are ranked in the order of registration of successive pledges or, in the absence of registration, in the order of constitution.

###### Article 2323

The pledge is indivisible notwithstanding the divisibility of the debt towards the heirs of the debtor or those of the creditor.

The heir of the debtor who has paid their portion of the debt cannot request the restitution of their portion in the pledge, even if it is divisible by nature, as long as the debt is not entirely discharged. Reciprocally, the heir of the creditor who has received their share of the claim cannot return the pledge, even if it is divisible, to the prejudice of those of their co-heirs who are not paid.

###### Article 2324

The commercial pledge falls under the provisions of the commercial code.

###### Article 2325

A pledge over a registered motor vehicle or registered trailer is governed by this article and by articles 2326 to 2329 below.

This pledge is enforceable against third parties by the declaration thereof made to the Mining Service. This declaration is entered in a special register with counterfoil and mentions the creation of the pledge over which the vehicle or trailer is the object, the name of the owner of the property and that of the creditor, and the date of registration of the contract.

A receipt of this declaration is issued to the pledgee creditor, repeating literally the mentions appearing on the counterfoil. By possession of this receipt, the pledgee creditor is deemed to have retained the vehicle or trailer in his possession.

###### Article 2326

In the case of a pledge over a new vehicle or trailer, the registration of the pledge by the seller, assignee of debt, discounter or lender of money for the purchase made, must be effected within a period of three months from the issue of the receipt of declaration of entry into service of the vehicle.

###### Article 2327

The cancellation of the pledge mention may be requested either by the creditor or by the debtor. When it is done by the creditor, indication of the cancellation is entered on the receipt issued to him. In this case, the debtor may request to obtain a cancellation certificate. When it is done by the debtor, the latter must prove the extinction of the guaranteed debt or produce the deed giving release of the registration. A cancellation certificate is then issued to him.

###### Article 2328

In the event of default of payment of the guaranteed debt, the creditor may have the court order the sale of the pledged property. This sale takes place according to the procedures provided by enforcement proceedings without the pledge agreement being able to derogate therefrom.

The creditor may also have the court order that the property shall remain with him in payment. When the value of the property exceeds the amount of the guaranteed debt, the sum equal to the difference is paid to the debtor or, if there are other pledgee creditors, is deposited.

###### Article 2329

It may be agreed, upon the creation of the pledge or subsequently, that in the event of non-performance of the guaranteed obligation the creditor shall become owner of the pledged property.

The value of the property is determined on the day of transfer by an expert appointed amicably or judicially. Any contrary clause is deemed unwritten.

When this value exceeds the amount of the guaranteed debt, the sum equal to the difference is paid to the debtor or, if there are other pledgee creditors, is deposited.

###### Section III : Des privilèges sur les meubles

###### Article 2330

Privileges are either general, or particular over certain movables.

###### § 1. Des privilèges généraux sur les meubles

###### Article 2331

Claims privileged over all movables are those expressed below, and are exercised in the following order, without formality of publicity:

1° Court costs;

2° Funeral expenses;

3° Any expenses of the last illness preceding the seizure of property, whatever its outcome, concurrently among those to whom they are owed;

4° Without prejudice to the possible application of the provisions of articles 152 to 155 of the labour code, privileges for wages, which cover:

- sums owed to workers and apprentices for performance and termination of their contract during the last six months preceding the death of the debtor, the seizure of property or the judicial decision opening collective proceedings;
- allowances owed for paid leave;
- severance allowances owed;

5° Provisions of subsistence made to the debtor and his family during the last year;

6° Sums owed to authors of intellectual, literary and artistic works for the last three years preceding the death of the debtor, the seizure of property or the judicial decision opening collective proceedings;

7° Up to a limit of one million Djibouti Francs, sums which the debtor owes in respect of tax and customs claims and to the National Social Security Fund.

###### Article 2332

It is recalled that, in accordance with article 2298, the privilege, by reason of the rights of the Public Treasury and the order in which it is exercised, are regulated by the laws concerning them. The same applies to contribution claims of the National Social Security Fund.

Special texts creating general privileges must specify the rank thereof by determining it in relation to the provisions of this article. Failing that, the rank of these privileges is the last of that established by this article.

###### § 2. Des privilèges sur certains meubles

###### Article 2333

Creditors holding special privileges have, over the movables assigned to them as a basis by law, a right of preference.

This right of preference is also exercised, by subrogation, over the insurance indemnity for property that has perished or disappeared, as long as it is not paid.

###### Article 2334

Claims privileged over certain movables are, without prejudice to special texts establishing others, those:

1° Of the lessor of immovable property, who has a privilege over the fruits and revenues of the year, and over the price of everything that furnishes the leased property.

This privilege guarantees, in addition to the damages that could be awarded to him, the claims of the lessor against the lessee for the twelve months elapsed preceding the seizure and for the twelve months to fall due after it.

The lessee or any person who, by fraudulent manoeuvres, deprives the lessor of his privilege totally or partially, commits a criminal offence punished by the penalties for breach of trust.

The owner may seize the movables that furnish his house or his farm, when they have been removed without his consent, and he retains his privilege over them, provided that he has claimed them in the seizure deed; however, the lessor who thus claims the movables removed without his consent must reimburse the purchaser the price they cost him.

2° Of the pledgee creditor, over the pledge he realizes;

3° Of the person who has incurred expenses or provided services for the preservation of the thing;

4° Of the seller, who has, over the movable sold, a privilege to guarantee payment of the unpaid price, if it is still in the possession of the debtor or over the price still owed by the sub-purchaser.

5° The hotel keeper for his supplies, over the effects of the traveller which have been transported to his hotel;

6° The carrier, for carriage costs and ancillary expenses, over the thing transported;

7° Holders of claims resulting from abuses and malfeasance committed by public officials in the exercise of their functions, over the funds of their security and over the interest that may be owed thereon;

8° Holders of claims arising from an accident for the benefit of third parties injured by this accident or their successors in title, over the indemnity of which the civil liability insurer acknowledges itself or has been judicially recognized as debtor by reason of the insurance contract.

No payment made to the insured shall be liberating as long as the privileged creditors have not been paid off.

###### Section V : La propriété retenue ou cédée à titre de garantie

###### § 1. De la propriété retenue à titre de garantie

###### Article 2335

Ownership of property may be retained as security by the effect of a retention of title clause. The effect of a retention of title clause is to suspend the transfer effect of a contract until full payment of the obligation which constitutes the consideration therefor.

The ownership thus reserved is accessory to the claim whose payment it guarantees.

###### Article 2336

Retention of title must necessarily be agreed in writing.

###### Article 2337

Reserved ownership of a fungible good may be exercised, up to the amount of the debt remaining due, over goods of the same nature and of the same quality held by the debtor or on his behalf.

###### Article 2338

The incorporation of a movable subject to retention of title into another property does not impede the creditor's rights when these properties can be separated without suffering damage.

###### Article 2339

In the event of failure to pay in full at maturity, the creditor may request the restitution of the property in order to recover the right to dispose of it.

The value of the property recovered is applied, as payment, to the balance of the secured debt. Where the value of the property recovered exceeds the amount of the secured debt still due, the creditor owes the debtor a sum equal to the difference.

###### Article 2340

The right of ownership transfers to the debtor's claim against the sub-purchaser or to the insurance indemnity subrogated to the property.

###### § 2. De la propriété cédée à titre de garantie

###### Article 2341

Ownership of movable property or of a right may be transferred as security for an obligation by virtue of a fiducie contract entered into pursuant to articles 2205 to 2245.

###### Article 2342

In the case of a fiducie concluded as security, the contract must mention, on pain of nullity, in addition to the provisions set out in article 2210, the secured debt and the estimated value of the property or right transferred to the fiduciary estate.

###### Article 2343

In the event of failure to pay the secured debt and unless otherwise stipulated in the fiducie contract, the fiduciary, when he is the creditor, acquires free disposal of the property or right transferred as security. Where the fiduciary is not the creditor, the latter may require him to hand over the property, which he may then freely dispose of, or, if the fiducie contract so provides, to sell the property or right transferred and hand over all or part of the price.

The value of the property or right transferred is determined by an expert appointed amicably or judicially, unless the property is a sum of money. Any clause to the contrary is deemed unwritten.

###### Article 2344

If the beneficiary of the fiducie has acquired free disposal of the property or right transferred pursuant to article 2343, he shall pay the settlor, where the value mentioned in the last paragraph of that article exceeds the amount of the secured debt, a sum equal to the difference between that value and the amount of the debt, subject to prior payment of debts arising from the conservation or management of the fiduciary estate.

Subject to the same reservation, if the fiduciary proceeds to sell the property or right transferred pursuant to the fiducie contract, he shall return to the settlor the portion of the proceeds of such sale exceeding, as the case may be, the value of the secured debt.

###### Article 2345

The ownership transferred pursuant to article 2341 may be subsequently assigned as security for debts other than those mentioned in the constitutive instrument provided that the latter expressly so provides. The settlor may offer it as security, not only to the original creditor, but also to a new creditor, even though the former has not been paid. Where the settlor is a natural person, the fiduciary estate may then be assigned as security for a new debt only within the limit of its value estimated on the day of the recharge.

On pain of nullity, the agreement established according to the provisions of article 2342 is registered in the form provided for in article 2213. The date of registration determines, as between them, the rank of the creditors. The provisions of this article are of public policy and any clause contrary thereto is deemed unwritten.

##### Chapitre III : Des sûretés sur les immeubles

###### Article 2346

Securities on immovables are: privileges, the immovable pledge (or antichresis), and mortgages.

Ownership of the immovable may also be retained or transferred as security.

###### Section I : Du gage immobilier ou « antichrèse »

###### Article 2347

The immovable pledge, or antichresis, is the assignment, by the debtor or by a third party for the debtor, of an immovable as security for an obligation; it entails dispossession of the person who constitutes it.

The immovable pledge is established only in writing.

By this contract the creditor acquires only the right to collect the fruits of the immovable, subject to applying them annually to the interest, if any is owed to him, and then to the principal of his debt. For this purpose, he may, without losing possession of the property, lease the immovable, either to a third party or to the debtor himself.

###### Article 2348

The creditor is obliged, unless otherwise agreed, to pay the contributions and annual charges on the immovable that he holds as immovable pledge.

He must also, on pain of damages, provide for the upkeep and useful and necessary repairs of the immovable, and may deduct for this purpose, from the fruits, all expenses relating to these various matters. He may, at any time, relieve himself of this obligation by returning the property to its owner.

###### Article 2349

The debtor may not claim the enjoyment of the immovable that he has handed over as immovable pledge before the full discharge of his debt.

###### Article 2350

The creditor does not become owner of the immovable by the mere failure to pay at the agreed term; any clause to the contrary is null.

The creditor, in the event of failure to pay at the agreed term, may on the other hand pursue the expropriation of his debtor by legal means.

###### Article 2351

The provisions of article 2323 apply to the immovable pledge.

###### Article 2352

Nothing provided in this chapter prejudices the rights that third parties might have over the estate of the immovable handed over as immovable pledge. Indeed, the immovable pledge being only an assignment of the fruits as they fall due or are collected, third parties may acquire and exercise their rights over the pledged immovable.

If the creditor, holding this title, has privileges or mortgages on the estate legally established and preserved, he exercises them in his order and like any other creditor.

###### Article 2353

The rights of the creditor holding an immovable pledge right are extinguished notably:

1° By the extinction of the principal obligation;

2° By the early restitution of the immovable to its owner.

###### Section II: Real Property Privileges

###### § 1. Special Privileges on Real Property

###### Article 2354

Privileged creditors on real property are:

1° The vendor, on the property sold, for payment of the price;

If there are several successive sales for which the price is owed in whole or in part, the first vendor is preferred to the second, the second to the third, and so on;

2° Those who have provided funds for the acquisition of real property, provided that it is authentically established, by the loan agreement, that the sum was intended for this use and, by the vendor's receipt, that this payment was made from the borrowed funds;

3° The coheirs, on the real property of the estate, for the guarantee of partitions made between them, and of balancing payments or returns of lots;

4° The architects, contractors and artisans who have built, rebuilt or repaired buildings, canals or any other works whatsoever, provided however that, by an expert appointed ex officio by the court of first instance in whose jurisdiction the buildings are located, a report has been drawn up beforehand, for the purpose of establishing the condition of the premises in relation to the works which the owner shall declare his intention to carry out, and that the works have been, within six months at most of their completion, accepted by an expert equally appointed ex officio. But the amount of the privilege cannot exceed the values established by the second report, and it is reduced to the added value existing at the time of the alienation of the property and resulting from the works that have been carried out thereon;

5° Those who have lent the funds to pay or reimburse the workers, enjoy the same privilege, provided that this use is authentically established by the loan agreement, and by the workers' receipt, as has been stated above for those who have lent the funds for the acquisition of real property;

6° The creditors of the deceased and the legatees of sums of money on the real property of the estate, as well as the personal creditors of the heir on the latter's real property, for the guarantee of the rights they hold under article 1028.

###### Article 2355

The privileges enumerated in articles 2331 and 2354 of the civil code, with the exception however of the privilege for court costs, incurred for the realization of the property and the distribution of the price, grant a right of preference to the beneficiaries called to exercise them on the real property estate only over unsecured creditors.

###### § 2. General Privileges on Real Property

###### Article 2356

The privileges that extend to movable and real property are those set forth in article 2331.

###### Article 2357

When, in the absence of movable property, the privileged creditors set forth in the preceding article come forward to be paid from the price of real property in competition with other privileged creditors on the property, payments are made in the following order:

1° The court costs and others set forth in article 2331;

2° The claims designated in article 2354.

###### § 3. How Real Property Privileges Are Preserved

###### Article 2358

As between creditors, privileges produce effect with regard to real property only insofar as they are made public by registration in the registers of the mortgage registrar, in the manner determined by law, and from the date of such registration, subject only to the following exceptions.

###### Article 2359

The claims enumerated in article 2331 are excepted from the formality of registration.

###### Article 2360

If their privilege is established by a notarial deed to be published in the land register:

1° The privileged vendor preserves his privilege by the transcription of the instrument that transferred ownership to the purchaser, and which establishes that all or part of the price is owed to him; for which purpose, the transcription of the contract made by the purchaser shall constitute registration for the vendor and for the lender who has provided him with the sums paid, and who shall be subrogated to the vendor's rights by the same contract. In this case, the mortgage registrar shall nevertheless be required, on pain of all damages and interest toward third parties, to register ex officio in his register, the claims resulting from the instrument transferring ownership, both in favor of the vendor and in favor of the lenders, who may also have made, if it has not been done, the transcription of the sales contract, for the purpose of acquiring registration of what is owed to them on the price. 2° The coheir or copartitioner preserves his privilege on the property of each lot or on the property sold by licitation for the balancing payment and return of lots or for the price of the licitation, by the registration made at his diligence, within sixty days, from the date of the partition deed or the adjudication by licitation; during which time no mortgage may take place on the property charged with the balancing payment or adjudicated by licitation, to the prejudice of the creditor of the balancing payment or of the price.

###### Article 2361

The architects, contractors, masons and other workers employed to build, rebuild or repair buildings, canals, or other works, and those who have, to pay and reimburse them, lent the sums whose use has been established preserve by the double registration made:

1° Of the report establishing the condition of the premises;

2° Of the acceptance report, their privilege as of the date of registration of the first report.

###### Article 2362

The creditors and legatees who request the separation of the deceased's estate, in accordance with article 665 in the title On Successions, preserve, with regard to the creditors of the heirs or representatives of the deceased, their privilege on the real property of the estate, by the registrations made on each of these properties, within six months from the opening of the succession.

Before the expiration of this period, no mortgage may be established with effect on these properties by the heirs or representatives to the prejudice of these creditors or legatees.

###### Article 2363

The assignees of these various privileged claims exercise all the same rights as the assignors in their stead.

###### Article 2364

All privileged claims subject to the formality of registration, with regard to which the conditions prescribed above for preserving the privilege have not been fulfilled, do not nevertheless cease to be secured by mortgage, but the mortgage dates, with regard to third parties, only from the time of the registrations that should have been made as will be explained hereinafter.

###### Section III: Mortgages

###### Article 2365

The provisions of Law No. 177/AN/91/2ème L on the organization of land ownership are applicable, in a general manner and subject to the provisions that follow, to registered real property and to the real rights relating thereto.

###### Article 2366

A mortgage is a real right over real property assigned to the discharge of an obligation.

It is, by its nature, indivisible, and subsists in its entirety over all the assigned properties, over each one and over each portion of these properties.

It follows them into whatever hands they pass.

###### Article 2367

A mortgage takes place only in the cases and according to the forms authorized by law.

###### Article 2368

Only the following are susceptible to mortgages:

1° Parcels of land whether built upon or not that are in commerce and with them, their accessories deemed to be immovable;

2° The usufruct of the same properties, during the time of its duration;

3° The rights of emphyteusis, during the time of its duration, and of superficies, established on the same properties. Movable property does not follow through mortgage.

Ships and seagoing vessels are subject to the provisions specific to them.

###### Article 2369

A mortgage is either legal, judicial, or conventional.

A legal mortgage is one that results from the law.

A judicial mortgage is one that results from judgments or judicial acts. A mortgage may likewise result from judgments rendered in foreign countries, if they have been declared enforceable by a Djiboutian court, subject to special laws or treaties. Similarly, arbitral decisions give rise to a mortgage only insofar as they are vested with the exequatur.

A conventional mortgage is one that results from contracts and other juridical acts. It is granted by notarial deed; the transfer and release of the mortgage take place in the same forms.

###### Article 2370

A conventional mortgage may be granted only by those who have the capacity to alienate the immovable properties they subject to it. The property of minors, adults under guardianship, and that of absentees as long as possession is granted only provisionally, may be mortgaged only for the causes and in the forms established by law, or by virtue of judgments; those who have only a right over the immovable property suspended by a condition, or resolvable in certain cases, or subject to rescission, may grant only a mortgage subject to the same conditions or to the same rescission.

The authentic instrument specifically declares the nature and location of each of the immovable properties currently belonging to the debtor, over which he grants the mortgage securing the debt.

###### Article 2371

Future property cannot be mortgaged.

Nevertheless, if the present and unencumbered property of the debtor is insufficient for the security of the debt, he may, by acknowledging this insufficiency, consent that each of the properties he subsequently acquires be specifically allocated thereto as acquisitions are made.

###### Article 2372

If the immovable property or immovable properties currently subject to the mortgage perish or suffer damage in such a manner that they become insufficient for the security of the creditor, the latter may obtain a supplementary mortgage or, failing that, pursue his reimbursement forthwith.

###### Article 2373

A conventional mortgage is valid only insofar as the sum for which it is granted is certain and determined by the deed: if the debt resulting from the obligation is conditional as to its existence, or undetermined in its value, the creditor may require the registration of which mention will be made hereinafter, only up to an estimated value expressly declared by him, and which the debtor shall have the right to have reduced, if appropriate.

###### Article 2374

Mortgages and privileges that have given rise to registration are extinguished:

1° By the extinction of the obligation of which they constitute the security;

2° By the creditor's renunciation of his right;

3° By the completion of the procedure for purging mortgages by the third-party holder upon forced expropriation or upon expropriation for reasons of public utility, in accordance with the requirements of Article 51 of Law No. 177/AN/91/2ème L on the organization of land ownership.

###### Section IV: Immovable property transferred as security

###### Article 2375

The provisions of this chapter are not applicable to fiducies constituted as security by legal persons.

###### Article 2376

Ownership of an immovable property may be transferred as security for an obligation by virtue of a fiducie contract concluded in application of Articles 2205 to 2245.

###### Article 2377

In case of a fiducie concluded as security, the contract mentions, on pain of nullity, in addition to the provisions set forth in Article 2210, the debt secured and the estimated value of the immovable property transferred to the fiduciary estate.

###### Article 2378

In the absence of payment of the secured debt and unless otherwise stipulated in the fiducie contract, the fiduciary, when he is the creditor, acquires free disposal of the property transferred as security. When the fiduciary is not the creditor, the latter may require of him the delivery of the property, which he may then freely dispose of, or, if the agreement so provides, the sale of the property and the delivery of all or part of the price.

The value of the property is determined by an expert appointed amicably or judicially. Any clause to the contrary is deemed unwritten.

###### Article 2379

If the beneficiary of the fiducie has acquired free disposal of the property in application of Article 2378, he pays to the settlor, when the value mentioned in the last paragraph of that article exceeds the amount of the secured debt, a sum equal to the difference between that value and the amount of the debt, subject to prior payment of debts arising from the conservation or management of the fiduciary estate. Subject to the same reservation, if the fiduciary proceeds to the sale of the property in application of the fiducie contract, he restores to the settlor the portion of the proceeds of that sale exceeding, where appropriate, the value of the secured debt.

###### Article 2380

The property transferred in application of Article 2376 may be subsequently allocated to the security of debts other than those mentioned in the constitutive act provided that it expressly so provides. The settlor may offer it as security, not only to the original creditor, but also to a new creditor, even though the former has not been paid. When the settlor is a natural person, the fiduciary estate may then be allocated as security for a new debt only within the limit of its value estimated on the day of the recharge.

On pain of nullity, the agreement established according to the provisions of Article 2377 is published in the form provided for in Article 2213. The date of publication determines, among them, the rank of creditors.

The provisions of this article are of public order and any clause contrary thereto is deemed unwritten.

#### TITRE XX: Real property revendication and forced sale of immovable properties

###### Article 2381

The action for revendication of an immovable property and the forced sale of immovable properties is pursued in compliance with the provisions of the code of civil procedure and those of Law No. 177/AN/91/2ème L on the organization of land ownership.

#### Titre XXI: Prescription

Chapitre Ier: General provisions

###### Article 2382

Prescription is a means of acquiring or being released by a certain lapse of time, and under the conditions determined by law.

The periods of foreclosure are not, except for contrary provisions provided by law, governed by this title.

The provisions of this title do not preclude the application of special rules provided by other texts or special laws.

###### Article 2383

Extinctive prescription is a mode of extinction of a right resulting from the inaction of its holder for a time defined by law.

It is subject to the law governing the right that it affects.

###### Article 2384

Acquisitive prescription is a means of acquiring property or a right by the effect of possession, when the law authorizes such an effect.

###### Article 2385

Prescription may in no case constitute a mode of acquisition of real rights over immovable properties or of release from charges encumbering the same immovable properties.

###### Article 2386

In movable matters, possession may produce an acquisitive effect of right under the conditions set forth in Article 686 et seq.

###### Article 2387

One may not, in advance, renounce prescription; one may renounce prescription acquired. Renunciation of prescription is express or tacit; tacit renunciation results from an act that presupposes the abandonment of the acquired right.

One who cannot exercise his rights by himself may not renounce alone the acquired prescription.

###### Article 2388

Except in case of waiver, prescription may be raised at any stage of proceedings, even before the court of appeal. Creditors, or any other person having an interest in the prescription being acquired, may raise it, even if the debtor or owner has stated that they waive it.

Judges cannot of their own motion raise the defense arising from prescription.

###### Article 2389

Payment made to extinguish a debt cannot be reclaimed solely on the ground that the prescription period had expired.

###### Article 2390

The State, public establishments and municipalities are subject to the same prescriptions as private individuals, and may likewise raise them.

###### Article 2391

However, the following are imprescriptible, subject to the provisions that govern them:

1° Property belonging to the public domain within the meaning of the law (specifically referred to here are Law No. 171/AN/91/2nd L establishing and organizing the public domain and Law No. 173/AN/91/2nd L organizing the private domain of the State);

2° Things that are not in commerce;

3° In accordance with Article 674, the right of ownership as well as the rights and actions that are attributes of the right of ownership, such as for example the right to acquire co-ownership of a wall, the right to use running water of which one is a riparian owner, the right to claim a right of way for the owner of a landlocked property, the right to enclose, or the right to request partition.

##### Chapitre II : Causes that prevent movable prescription

###### Article 2392

One cannot oneself change the cause and principle of one's possession, so that one prescribes according to the obligation one has undertaken. Thus, those who possess for another never acquire by prescription, whatever the period of time may be. Such is the case, for example, of the depositary or the usufructuary, and of all others who hold the owner's thing precariously, cannot acquire it by prescription.

The heirs of those who held the thing for someone by such precarious titles cannot acquire by prescription either.

###### Article 2393

It is otherwise in case of interversion of title, namely when the person whom the owner designates as precarious holder considers that his holding has been changed into possession or ownership.

###### Article 2394

Those to whom the thing has been transferred by a precarious holder by a title transferring ownership may nevertheless acquire it by prescription when the conditions of possession are met.

##### Chapitre III : The running of prescription

###### Section I : General provisions

###### Article 2395

Prescription runs against all persons, unless they fall within some exception established by law.

###### Article 2396

Prescription is counted by days, and not by hours. It is acquired when the last day of the term is completed.

###### Article 2397

When a new law extends the duration of a prescription period or a forfeiture period, it has no effect on a prescription or forfeiture already acquired. Subject to any transitional provisions it may provide, such a law applies immediately to the situation when the prescription period or the forfeiture period had not expired on the date of its entry into force; the period already elapsed is then taken into account.

If the new law reduces the duration of a prescription period or a forfeiture period, this new period runs from the day of entry into force of this new law, without the total duration being able to exceed the duration provided by the prior law.

###### Article 2398

The prescription period may be interrupted or suspended according to the causes that the law indicates. The interruption of prescription erases the period already acquired and starts a new period running. This new period is of the same duration as the old one.

The suspension of prescription temporarily stops its running without erasing the period already elapsed.

###### Section II : The ordinary period and certain particular periods

###### Article 2399

Except where otherwise provided:

1° Personal or movable actions are barred by prescription after three years from the day on which the holder of a right knew or should have known the facts enabling him to exercise it;

2° Real property actions are barred by prescription after thirty years from the day on which the holder of a right knew or should have known the facts enabling him to exercise it.

3° The prescription period is:

- a. 10 years in case of bodily injury for the victim, from the date of consolidation of the injury;
- b. 10 years for ecological damage;
- c. 20 years in case of harm related to an act of torture or barbarity, or violence or sexual assault against minors.
- d. Architects, contractors and other persons bound to the project owner by a contract for work are discharged from the guarantee of works they have made or directed after ten years if they are major works, after two years for minor works.
- e. The action of bailiffs, for the remuneration of acts they serve and commissions they execute; the action of notaries for payment of their acts; the action of doctors, surgeons, dental surgeons, midwives and pharmacists, for their visits, operations and medicines, are barred by prescription after two years.
- f. The action of lawyers, for payment of their costs and fees, is barred by prescription after two years, from the judgment of proceedings or the conciliation of parties, or from the revocation of said lawyers.

With regard to matters not concluded, they cannot make claims for their costs and fees going back more than five years.

g. Prescription, in the above cases, takes place, even though there has been continuation of supplies, deliveries, services and works.

It only ceases to run when there has been a settled account, acknowledgment or obligation, or a summons in court that has not lapsed.

h. Nevertheless, those against whom these prescriptions are raised may refer the oath to those who raise them, on the question of whether the thing has actually been paid.

The oath may be referred to widows and heirs, or to their guardians, if they are minors, so that they must declare whether they do not know that the thing is due.

i. Judges, bailiffs as well as persons who have represented or assisted the parties are discharged from the documents five years after the judgment or the cessation of their involvement.

j. The action of workers for payment of wages, accessories of wages, bonuses and allowances of any nature as well as, more generally, any sum due by the employer to the worker, and that for the provision of benefits in kind and possibly their reimbursement, are barred by prescription after one year. Prescription runs from the date from which the wage is due. It is suspended or interrupted under the conditions provided by Section III below.

###### Article 2400

All actions, both real and personal, are barred by prescription after thirty years, without the person who alleges this prescription being obliged to produce a title or being subject to the exception derived from bad faith.

The thirty-year extinctive prescription established by the preceding paragraph is not applicable to cases where the law provides for a shorter period, when it starts running from the day of knowledge of the fact, act or event.

###### Section III: Causes that interrupt or suspend prescription

###### § 1. Causes that interrupt the running of prescription

###### Article 2401

Prescription is interrupted:

1° When the possessor is deprived for more than one year of the enjoyment of the thing, either by the claimed owner or even by a third party;

2° By the acknowledgment that the debtor or possessor makes of the right of the one against whom he was prescribing.

###### Article 2402

A legal claim, even in summary proceedings, a demand or a seizure, served on the person whom one wishes to prevent from prescribing, also interrupts the prescription period as well as the foreclosure period. The same applies when the legal claim is brought before an incompetent court, or when the summons is void due to a defect in form.

The interruption resulting from the legal claim produces its effects until the extinction of the proceedings.

###### Article 2403

The interruption is regarded as null and void:

- if the claimant withdraws his claim;
- if he allows the proceedings to lapse;
- or if his claim is definitively rejected.

###### Article 2404

The formal demand made to one of the joint and several debtors by a legal claim, or by an act of forced execution, or the acknowledgment by the debtor of the right of the one against whom he was prescribing, interrupts prescription against all the others, even against their heirs.

On the other hand, the formal demand made to one of the heirs of a joint and several debtor, or the acknowledgment of that heir, does not interrupt prescription with regard to the other co-heirs, even in the case of a mortgage debt, if the obligation is divisible. This formal demand or this acknowledgment interrupts prescription, with regard to the other co-debtors, only for the share for which that heir is liable.

To interrupt prescription for the whole, with regard to the other co-debtors, the formal demand must be made to all the heirs of the deceased debtor, or the acknowledgment of all those heirs is required.

###### Article 2405

The formal demand made to the principal debtor, or his acknowledgment, interrupts prescription against the surety.

###### § 2. Causes that suspend the running of prescription

###### Article 2406

By exception to Article 2395, prescription does not run against a person who cannot validly act, by reason of an impediment resulting from the law, from the agreement, or from force majeure.

###### Article 2407

Prescription does not run against unemancipated minors and adults under guardianship, except in cases determined by law.

Thus and by exception, there run against unemancipated minors and adults under guardianship, subject to their recourse against their guardians: prescriptions relating to the payment or recovery of salaries, annuity arrears, maintenance payments, rents, rental charges, interest on loaned sums and, generally, actions for payment of anything that is payable by years or at shorter periodic terms.

###### Article 2408

Prescription does not run between spouses, one against the other.

###### Article 2409

Prescription does not run:

- with regard to a claim that depends on a condition, until the condition occurs;
- with regard to an action for warranty, until the eviction takes place;
- with regard to a claim at a fixed date, until that date has arrived.

###### Article 2410

Prescription does not run against the beneficiary heir, with regard to the claims he has against the estate.

On the other hand, it runs against a vacant estate, even in the case where it is not provided with a curator.

###### Article 2411

When the law grants a person a period for delay, the prescription of the property and rights concerned is suspended during this legally granted time.

Article final

General transitional provisions

All texts contrary to the provisions of this code are repealed, except when they create texts derogating from common law, in consideration of their domain.

References to provisions repealed, amended or moved by this code and contained in provisions of any nature, legislative or regulatory, are replaced by references to provisions having the same object.

Contracts and other legal acts that were entered into under the previous code are valid if they complied with the conditions then required.

Prescriptions commenced at the time of publication of this code are governed in accordance with the former texts. Nevertheless, prescriptions then commenced, and for which more than thirty years would still be required, according to the former laws, from the same time, shall be completed by this period of thirty years, all subject to Article 2400, paragraph 2.

This law shall be executed upon its promulgation.
